`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/ARCHITECTURE.md`:

```md
# NavKit: how it is built

This page is for developers who will change NavKit's code. To run NavKit, read [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md)
and [README.md](README.md). The format of the navigation file and the builder's stages are described in
[KYNAPSE_SPEC.md](../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/research/KYNAPSE_SPEC.md).

## Overview

NavKit turns one level of a game into navigation data for soldiers. That data is walkable areas, the boundaries
between them, and a route graph. NavKit lives in three folders. This folder, the **big-endian kit**, holds the BF1943
pipeline: the driver `navkit.py`, the window `navkitGUI.pyw` and the `tools\*1943.py` modules, which read your Xbox 360
copy of BF1943. [`bf1943-auto-navkit-common`](../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/README.md) holds the modules both kits use,
one copy of each: the builder package `navbuild`, the walkability rules, the samples format, the `.hpd` reader and
writer, the Havok reader and the level-object rules. [`bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian`](../bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian/README.md)
is OPFOR's BFBC2 NavKit, which builds with the same shared modules. The kits read the game data through `core/bfbc2core`:
`game1943` (your copy and its bundles), `level1943`, `terrain`, `water` and `dbx`. They hand their builds on through
`navdata` (reads a `.hpd`) and `rsnv` (the navigation runtime's file).

A BF1943 run has these steps:
1. **prepare** reads the level from the bundles.
2. **sample** measures its collision offline, at 0.8 m everywhere and at 0.2 m in the detailed sectors.
3. **build** makes the `.hpd`.
4. **check** tests its structure and its routes.
5. **export** writes the build as an RSNV file for our runtime, rsnav (in project-opfor-bf1943).

Two more tools work on a build: one makes the vehicle worlds and one audits the build against the level. Every step
records what it was made from in the level's `navkit.json`. A later step refuses work that comes from another
generation (another preparation, sampling run or build).

## Data flow

Everything is written under `work\levels\<level>\` (`BF1943_WORK` overrides `<suite>\work`; `navkitjson1943.paths`).
The game copy is only read.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    GAME["BF1943 copy, dist/xenon bundles<br/>(read only; core game1943)"]
    PREP["prepare: navkit.py prepare<br/>levelobjects1943, core terrain + water"]
    OBJ["objects/<br/>objects.json, *_tris.npy, all_tris.npy,<br/>object_boxes.json, ladders.json, soldier_spawns.json,<br/>heightfield.res, water_mesh.res"]
    SAMP["sample: navkit.py sample<br/>navsample1943 (4 runs), detailed1943"]
    SMP["samples/<br/>samples.bin, samples_high.bin (0.8 m)<br/>samples_02.bin, samples_02_high.bin (0.2 m)"]
    BUILD["build: navkit.py build<br/>jumplinks1943, then navbuild.build<br/>with soldier1943.SETTINGS"]
    HPD["navkit/<br/>LEVEL.hpd, LEVEL.cells.npz,<br/>jump_links.json, build.log"]
    CHECK["check: navkit.py check<br/>hpdcheck, routecheck1943"]
    CK["navkit/check.txt, check.json"]
    EXP["navexport1943"]
    RSNV["navkit/LEVEL.rsnv<br/>(failed check: LEVEL.failed.rsnv)"]
    VEH["navexport_vehicles1943<br/>groundnav1943, seanav1943, airnav1943,<br/>rsnvgrid1943, vehicleclasses1943"]
    VOUT["vehicles/ (ground collision, samples)<br/>navkit/LEVEL.jeep, .tank, .lcvp, .plane .rsnv,<br/>LEVEL.transfers.json, LEVEL.vehicles.json"]
    AUD["navaudit1943 masks, audit"]
    AOUT["audit/masks/*.npz, audit.json, audit.md"]
    STAMP[("navkit/navkit.json<br/>settings and stamps")]
    RT["rsnav (project-opfor-bf1943)"]

    GAME --> PREP --> OBJ
    OBJ --> SAMP --> SMP
    OBJ --> BUILD
    SMP --> BUILD --> HPD
    HPD --> CHECK --> CK
    HPD --> EXP --> RSNV
    GAME --> EXP
    RSNV --> VEH --> VOUT
    GAME --> VEH
    HPD --> AUD
    SMP --> AUD --> AOUT
    RSNV --> RT
    VOUT --> RT
    PREP -.-> STAMP
    SAMP -.-> STAMP
    BUILD -.-> STAMP
    CHECK -.-> STAMP
    EXP -.-> STAMP
    VEH -.-> STAMP
```

What each step reads and writes:

| Step | Reads | Writes | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| prepare | the level's bundles and `levels-common-00.fbrb` (`game1943.Game`) | empties `objects\` first, then writes the object files, `heightfield.res` and `water_mesh.res`; then a new `navkit.json` with the sea level and sector offsets | `navkit.prepare`, `levelobjects1943.main` |
| sample | `objects\all_tris.npy`, `heightfield.res` | two 0.8 m runs (the soldier's step, and a 0.6 m step for stairs), then the detailed sectors (`detailed1943.choose`), then two 0.2 m runs over those sectors. Each run is a `navsample1943.py` child process, two at a time (`run_parallel`) | `navkit.sample` |
| build | the object files, the samples, the water mesh | `jump_links.json` first, then `<level>.hpd` and `<level>.cells.npz` (`navbuild.write`), then `build.log` | `navkit.build`, `jumplinks1943.level_links`, `navbuild.build` |
| check | `<level>.hpd`, the level's spawns and flags | `check.txt`, `check.json` | `navkit.check`, `hpdcheck.check`, `routecheck1943.check` |
| export | the checked build, `cells.npz`, `jump_links.json`, `ladders.json`, the prepared height field, the vehicle entries (`core vehicles1943`) | `<level>.rsnv` (or `.be.rsnv`) through `core rsnv` | `navexport1943.py` |
| vehicle worlds | `<level>.rsnv` (read only), the prepared copy | a world per class, the transfers, the checks | `navexport_vehicles1943.py` |
| audit | the checked build, the samples | the masks, then the reports | `navaudit1943.py`, `navaudit1943_checks` |

## The builder (`navbuild`)

`navbuild.build(samples, forbid_tris, xoff, zoff, out, ..., detailed=..., settings=...)` builds a `.hpd` from the
samples and the object files:
- `stages.stage` builds one grid. `inputs.stage_level` gathers the walkable surfaces (`navwalk.walkable`) into a `Level`
  that carries the `Settings` and the stage's `Grid`. `areas` traces the sectors, tiles, areas and their boundaries.
  `graph` makes each sector's route graph.
- With `detailed`, `merge.merge_detailed` builds the detailed sectors at 0.2 m and merges them with the 0.8 m build.
  `seams` then joins the two grids where they meet.
- `write.write_file` writes the `.hpd` and `<level>.cells.npz`, each area's cells and ground heights. The RSNV exporter
  reads the cells file.

The constants in `navbuild/config.py` are documented defaults, and nothing changes them at run time. A build's rules
come in as one frozen `Settings` object:
- `navbuild.BFBC2` holds NavKit's defaults.
- `soldier1943.SETTINGS` holds BF1943's soldier and the rules BF1943's levels needed: `area_cliff`, `border_seam_line`,
  the seam links, `seam_gap_nodes`, `column_sectors_cm=True` (whole-centimetre sector lines, 2026-11-05) and
  `normal_links_own_grid=True` (links between 0.8 m sectors use the 0.8 m slope rule in builds with detailed sectors,
  2026-11-05; off for BFBC2 until measured with `navregress.py`).

What a build collects as it runs is kept in its `BuildState`. The common README's
[builder table](../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/README.md#the-builder-package-toolsnavbuild) gives every module in the package.

## Module map

| File | Responsibility | Key entry points |
|---|---|---|
| `navkit.py` | the BF1943 driver: the steps and their stamps | `prepare`, `sample`, `build`, `check`, `stamp`, `invalidate`, `preparation_id`, `main` |
| `navkitGUI.pyw` | the window; runs `navkit.py <step>` as a child process | `App` |
| `tools/navkitjson1943.py` | `navkit.json`: the lock, atomic writes, hashes, which build may be read | `paths`, `read`, `update`, `write`, `build_refusal`, `prepared_heightfield`, `same_file` |
| `tools/soldier1943.py` | BF1943's soldier and its builder `Settings` | `SETTINGS`, `STEP`, `WATER_DEPTH`, `sea_level` |
| `tools/levelobjects1943.py` | object placements and collision from the bundles | `main` |
| `tools/navsample1943.py` | the offline sampler (writes navsample format v1) | command line |
| `tools/detailed1943.py` | which sectors are built at 0.2 m | `choose` |
| `tools/jumplinks1943.py` | jump links on ships, in the `ladders.json` format | `level_links` |
| `tools/routecheck1943.py` | every spawn on the network, a route between every pair of flags | `check`, `report` |
| `tools/navexport1943.py` | `.hpd` to RSNV, and the `exported` stamp | `stamp_export`, `check`, `EXPORTER_VERSION` |
| `tools/navexport_vehicles1943.py`, `groundnav1943.py`, `seanav1943.py`, `airnav1943.py`, `rsnvgrid1943.py` | the vehicle worlds and their writer | `write_world` (rsnvgrid1943) |
| `tools/vehicleclasses1943.py` | the vehicle classes and the `vehicles` stamps | `CLASSES`, `inputs`, `record`, `soldier_world` |
| `tools/navaudit1943.py`, `tools/navaudit1943_checks/` | the audit, one module per check | `run` |
| `tools/rsnvtool.py`, `tools/enclosure_probe1943.py` | inspection only: never write a build or an export | command lines |
| `../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/navbuild/` | the builder | `build`, `Settings`, `BFBC2`, `BuildError`, `read_cells` |
| `../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/` | `navwalk`, `navsample`, `hpdtool`, `kymesh`, `hpdcheck`, `hkpack`, `havok461`, `levelobjects`, `detailed`, `navdiff`, `navedits`, `hpdview` | see [its README](../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/README.md#layout) |
| `../core/bfbc2core/` | `game1943`, `level1943`, `terrain`, `water`, `navdata`, `rsnv`, `rsnvtrip`, `vehicles1943` | see [core's README](../core/README.md) |

A script finds these folders through the suite's bootstrap. The BF1943 tools call
`suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)`, and the shared folders are always on the path
([core/suitepath.py](../core/suitepath.py)).

## The stamps in `navkit.json`

| Key | Written by | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `preparation` and its inputs (`level`, `game`, `sea_level`, `sector_offsets`, `objects_sha256`) | prepare (a new file each time) | the digest of the preparation; every later stamp carries it |
| `samples` `0.8` and `0.2`, `detailed_sectors`, `sampled` | sample | the preparation, the game copy and a random `id` for each pass; the 0.2 m pass also holds its sectors |
| `built`, `build_from` | build | the preparation, the ids of the passes it read, `hpd_sha256`, `jump_links_sha256` |
| `checked` | check | the time, then `ok` or `FAILED` |
| `exported` | navexport1943, for `<level>.rsnv` only | the build's `hpd_sha256` and the export's own `sha256` |
| `vehicles` `collision`, `samples`, `worlds` | vehicleclasses1943 `record` | the preparation, the class's parameter digest, the soldier world's SHA-256, or `absent` with a reason |

## Key invariants

- **One preparation.** prepare deletes `navkit.json` and empties `objects\`, so no file from an earlier preparation
  is hashed into the new one. Every later stamp names `preparation`. Steps run before the new preparation stay on disk,
  but nothing reads them. `navkit.invalidate` drops the stamps that follow a step. A new build also drops `exported`
  and the vehicle `worlds`.
- **Identity by content, not time.** The `built` and `time` fields keep only the minute. Builds are told apart by
  `hpd_sha256`, sampling passes by `id`, and the soldier world by its file's SHA-256. The game folder is compared as a
  file (`navkitjson1943.same_file`), so another spelling of the same path still matches.
- **A long step is stamped only if its inputs did not change while it ran.** Each step's `done` function runs inside
  `navkitjson1943.update`, which does a fresh read, the change and an atomic replace. The update holds an OS lock on
  `navkit.json.lock` (`msvcrt.locking`, or `fcntl.flock` on other systems) and gives up after 30 s. If the preparation
  or a pass the step read changed meanwhile, the step raises and stamps nothing (`navkit.stamp`, the guarded `done`
  functions).
- **Consumers read only the checked build of the current preparation.** `nj.build_refusal` checks this for the export
  and the audit. The export writes a build whose check failed only to `.failed.rsnv`, exits 1 and stamps nothing. The
  vehicle builders need the `exported` stamp, and `vehicleclasses1943.soldier_world` checks it. The audit's masks carry
  the SHA-256 of their samples and build.
- **The prepared height field.** The export, the audit and the jump links read `objects\heightfield.res`, checked
  against `objects_sha256`, and refuse a game copy whose height field has changed since
  (`nj.prepared_heightfield`).
- **Settings come in as arguments.** No module edits another module's constants. A rule that differs between the
  games is a `Settings` field whose default keeps BFBC2's behaviour. After the 2026-10-31 merge, both kits' builds
  were byte for byte as before (the common README says what was checked).
- **One copy of each shared module.** No module name is in two of the suite's path folders, and `tests/test_repo.py`
  enforces it.

## How BF1943 and BFBC2 differ

| | BF1943 (this folder) | BFBC2 (`bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian`) |
|---|---|---|
| Driver | `navkit.py`, `navkitGUI.pyw` | `navkit_le.py` (with `navkit_le_project.py`), `navkitGUI_le.pyw` |
| Level objects | `levelobjects1943.py`: binary DBX and Havok 4.6.1, read straight from the bundles | `levelobjects.py` (shared): an unpacked, XML-converted level, read through `core xmlinst` |
| Samples | computed offline by `navsample1943.py` from the height field and `all_tris.npy` | measured in game through OPFOR's `[dev] navsample` |
| Settings | `soldier1943.SETTINGS`, `step=soldier1943.STEP`, `max_water_depth=soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH` | `navbuild.BFBC2` (the default `settings`) |
| Detailed sectors | `detailed1943.choose` (uses `NeedsDetailedPathfinding` itself) | `detailed.py` |
| Output | an RSNV export for our runtime; nothing is installed in the game | `pathdata.hpd` installed into the OPFOR game copy (`install`, `restore`) |
| Work folder | `<suite>\work\levels\<level>\` | `work\` inside the Project OPFOR folder |
| Stamps | the generation stamps above | the level's settings only (`box`, `y`, `xoff`, `zoff`, ...); its guards are in its README's robustness sections |

## Tests

They run with `python -B run_tests.py quick` or `bf1943`. Most use made-up data. Script tests are listed in
`run_tests.py`; pytest-style files are found by the runner.

| Guards | Files |
|---|---|
| the steps' stamps and refusals | `tests/test_navkit_stages.py`, `test_vehicle_stages.py`, `test_navkit_review.py`, `test_navkit_review2.py`, `test_navkit_review3.py`, `test_vehicleclasses_stamps.py` |
| the sampler, objects, jump links, route check | `test_sampler1943.py`, `test_levelobjects_made_up.py`, `test_jumplinks1943.py`, `test_jumplinks_made_up.py`, `test_routecheck1943.py`, `test_enclosure_probe.py` |
| 0.8 m / 0.2 m seams under BF1943's settings | `test_mixed_seam.py` |
| export and vehicle worlds | `test_navexport_made_up.py`, `test_navexport_vehicles_made_up.py`, `test_vehicle_builders_made_up.py`, `test_vehicles_nav1943.py`, `test_rsnvgrid_world.py`, `test_rsnvtool.py`, `test_rsnvtool_inprocess.py` |
| the audit | `test_navaudit_checks.py`, `test_fuzz_samples1943.py` |
| shared rules and readers | `../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tests/` (water, headroom, lips, portals, bridges, `test_navbuild_edges.py` under `BFBC2`, `test_formats.py`, `test_fuzz_navkit.py`) |
| core formats | `../core/tests/test_rsnv.py`, `test_navdata_offset.py`, `test_water_mesh.py`, `test_level1943_made_up.py`, `test_game1943_bundles.py`, `test_fuzz_core.py` |
| your copy (bf1943 tier) | `test_levelobjects1943.py`, `test_navexport1943.py`, `../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tests/test_havok461.py`, `../tests/test_bf1943_tools.py navkit` and `probe` |
| the BFBC2 driver | `../bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian/tests/` |

## Where to start

**Change a builder rule for BF1943 only.**
1. Add a field to `navbuild/config.py` `Settings` whose default is today's behaviour, so `BFBC2` builds don't change.
2. Read the field from `level.settings` in the module that applies the rule (`areas`, `graph`, `seams`, `inputs`).
3. Set it in `soldier1943.SETTINGS`.
4. Add a rule test in `bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tests` and check `test_mixed_seam.py`.
5. Rebuild and audit the four maps, because their builds will change.

**Add a step or an output that depends on a build.**
1. Read `navkitjson1943.py` first.
2. Refuse stale inputs with `build_refusal` (or a check like it), and stamp through `update` with a guarded change.
3. If an earlier step must drop the new stamp, add it to `navkit.invalidate`.
4. Copy the style of `test_navkit_stages.py` and `test_navkit_review2.py`: they replace the long steps with stand-ins
   and check every refusal.

**Change what an RSNV file holds.**
1. Change `core/bfbc2core/rsnv.py` (the layout, `load`, `World.validate`).
2. Then change its writers: `navexport1943.py` (raise `EXPORTER_VERSION`) and `rsnvgrid1943.py`, and the inspector
   `rsnvtool.py`.
3. The C runtime, rsnav in project-opfor-bf1943, matches `rsnv.search` and `validate` exactly, so change it in step.
4. Tests: `core/tests/test_rsnv.py`, `test_navexport_made_up.py`, `test_rsnvgrid_world.py`.

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/QUICKSTART.md`:

```md
# NavKit Quickstart (BF1943)

NavKit makes a navigation build for a level of your Battlefield 1943 copy: walkable ground, areas, portals and a
route graph, saved as `<level>.hpd`. The build is the input of our own navigation runtime for bots; BF1943 has no
Kynapse runtime, so nothing is installed in the game. This page shows how to make one from start to finish.

To learn how it works inside, read [README.md](README.md) and the [specification](../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/research/KYNAPSE_SPEC.md).

## Before you start

You need:

1. **A BF1943 game folder** from `bf1943-xenia-kit` (its `output\title\dist\xenon` folder, made from your own
   package). NavKit finds it by itself. If yours is elsewhere, set the environment variable `BF1943_GAME` to it,
   or add `--game <folder>` to every command.
2. **Python 3** from [python.org](https://www.python.org/). When you install it, tick "Add python.exe to PATH".
3. **numpy.** Open a command prompt and run:

   ```
   pip install numpy
   ```

   **Show in 3D** opens the Navigation Studio, which also needs `moderngl`, `glfw` and `imgui-bundle`.

NavKit does not start the game. The game folder is only read.

## The easy way: the NavKit window

Double-click **`navkitGUI.pyw`** in the `bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian` folder. The window has a level list at the
top, then the steps, and a log of what NavKit is doing at the bottom.

1. **Pick a level** in the *Level* list, for example `wake_island_s`.
2. Click **1. Prepare.** NavKit reads the level's objects, collision, flags, ladders, terrain and water from the
   bundles, and sets the sea level and sector offsets.
3. Click **2. Sample.** NavKit computes the collision samples from the level's data: twice at 0.8 m, then twice
   at 0.2 m in the detailed sectors (buildings and other places with floors above floors, which NavKit finds by
   itself). This is the long step: about 30 minutes on Wake Island.
4. Click **3. Build.** NavKit makes `<level>.hpd` with BF1943's soldier, its ladders, and jump links from ships'
   decks down to their AA gun platforms and between a carrier's floors a ledge apart. About 15 minutes on Wake Island.
5. Click **4. Check.** NavKit checks the file's structure and its routes (see [Reading the check](#reading-the-check)).
6. Click **Show in 3D** to open the build in the Navigation Studio.

**Run all (1-4)** does steps 1 to 4 in a row. A tick next to a step means it has been done for that level (a cross:
the check failed). **Cancel** ends the running step and the samplers it started. **Open output folder** shows that
level's files.

## The same steps from a command prompt

Run these from the `bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian` folder:

```
python navkit.py levels                    your copy's levels, and what has been done for each
python navkit.py prepare wake_island_s
python navkit.py sample  wake_island_s     --pitch 0.8 or --pitch 0.2: only that pass
python navkit.py build   wake_island_s
python navkit.py check   wake_island_s     exit code 1 when the check fails
python navkit.py status  wake_island_s     what has been done for a level
python navkit.py all     wake_island_s     prepare, sample, build and check in one go
```

The 0.2 m pass needs the 0.8 m pass first. If the 0.2 m samples are missing, Build builds the detailed sectors at
0.8 m and says so.

## Reading the check

Check runs two checks:

- **structure** (`tools\hpdcheck.py`): the rules a navigation file must keep. It prints "every check passes" or
  the rules that fail, with an example.
- **routes** (`tools\routecheck1943.py`): every soldier spawn of each base and flag is joined to the route graph
  (the nearest node within 15 m across and 4 m in height), and a route is looked for between every pair of flags.
  It fails when there was nothing to check: no soldier spawn, a flag without spawns while the others have them, or
  fewer than two flags (Coral Sea's flags have no soldier spawns: its carriers are checked, and a note says so).

For Wake Island's build of 2026-10-29 (round 5) it reports 12,779 nodes, 45,278 edges and 64 islands; the main network
has 11,420 nodes; 16 of 16 ladders are linked from the main network; all 10 flag pairs are routed; the structure check
passes. (The ladder count does not include the jump links to the carriers' AA guns and ledges, which are in
`jump_links.json`.) Build also writes `<level>.cells.npz` beside the build: its areas' own cells and heights, which
the exporter reads.

A spawn that is not on the main network is listed with the size of its island. A base on a carrier is its own
network (the sea divides it); that is expected and listed apart. The check fails when a flag's spawn is off the
main network or a flag pair has no route.

The full report is in `check.txt`, and the same in `check.json`.

## Auditing a build

The check covers flags, spawns and routes. For a fuller test of a build against its level, run the audit from the
variant's folder (the masks take about 30 minutes per level, once per build; an audit then about a minute):

```
python tools\navaudit1943.py masks wake_island_s     the build's walkable surfaces, and once per rule turned off
python tools\navaudit1943.py audit wake_island_s     the checks: work\levels\wake_island_s\audit\audit.md
```

`masks --variants base` makes only the build's own mask (about 6 minutes on Wake Island); the audit then leaves out
where each rule fired. The audit lists every capture area, spawn, vehicle spawn, mounted gun and repair station that
is not on walkable ground of its own floor - a vehicle: no walkable ground within its own entry radius of one of its
entry points, from the vehicle's data (with the sample columns there and why each surface is or is not walkable),
routes from every infantry spawn to every capture area and back, every island and what kind it is (a
carrier deck is a vehicle-only zone, not a fault), the file's consistency and the places the route graph does not
cross, and more. Run the masks again after every build: they belong to one build.

## Exporting for the navigation runtime

```
python tools\navexport1943.py wake_island_s --check     work\levels\wake_island_s\navkit\wake_island_s.rsnv
python tools\navexport1943.py wake_island_s --big-endian   wake_island_s.be.rsnv, for experiments in Xenia
```

`--check` reads the file back and compares it with the build. Export again after every build (under a minute on Wake Island).
The exporter takes only the checked build of the level's current preparation: after `prepare` or `sample` again, the
old `<level>.hpd` stays on disk but is refused until you build and check again; so is a build whose
`jump_links.json` was written again since (by `tools\jumplinks1943.py` run on its own). A build whose check failed is
exported for inspection to `<level>.failed.rsnv` (unless `--out` says where), with a warning and exit code 1:
`<level>.rsnv` stays as it was. When it writes `<level>.rsnv` (by default, or `--out` naming that file) it stamps `navkit.json` with what it
exported (`exported`: the file's SHA-256 and the build's, the `.hpd`'s SHA-256), which the vehicle worlds check.

To look inside an export (read-only):

```
python tools\rsnvtool.py info wake_island_s          sections, counts, edge kinds, tight edges, islands
python tools\rsnvtool.py validate wake_island_s      exit code 1 on a problem
python tools\rsnvtool.py --help                      the other commands: locate, los, route, pockets, tight, cells, walk, picture, diff
```

## Vehicle worlds

After the soldier export, one command builds and checks the worlds of the jeeps, tanks, landing craft and planes:

```
python tools\navexport_vehicles1943.py wake_island_s                 every class; samples the ground vehicles if their samples are missing or stale
python tools\navexport_vehicles1943.py wake_island_s --sample        sample the ground vehicles again first
python tools\navexport_vehicles1943.py wake_island_s --check-only    only the checks, on the worlds already written
```

`--classes jeep,tank` builds only those classes. The ground vehicles' sampling is the long part (about 11-13 minutes
per class on a map). It reads `<level>.rsnv` and never changes it. The exit code is 1 when a check fails; the checks
are in `<level>.vehicles.json`.

Each vehicle step records what it was made from in `navkit.json` (`vehicles`: the collision, each class's samples and
world, with the preparation, the game copy, the class's parameters and the soldier world). Ground samples of another
preparation or other sampling parameters (radius, step, height, pitch) are made again; a world needs the export of the
current soldier build (every builder fails without `<level>.rsnv`); the level's spawns come from the game copy it was
prepared from. A class the level has none of (no spawns; for the landing craft also no water, whatever the soldier
export) is recorded as absent, and the check accepts that; a class asked for whose world is missing, or of another
preparation, class parameters or soldier world, fails the check (one not asked for is a note). A new `prepare` drops
every vehicle stamp, a new soldier `sample` or `build` drops the worlds'.

## Where the files go

All of these are in the suite's work folder (`<suite>\work`; the environment variable `BF1943_WORK` sets another):

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `work\levels\<level>\objects\` | the level's objects and collision (`levelobjects1943.py`'s files), `heightfield.res`, `water_mesh.res` |
| `work\levels\<level>\samples\` | the collision samples (`samples*.bin`) and their logs |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\navkit.json` | the settings Prepare chose (sea level, sector offsets, detailed sectors) and the steps done |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.hpd` | **the result** |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\build.log` | the build's log |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\check.txt`, `check.json` | the check report |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\jump_links.json` | the jump links Build made (ships' AA gun platforms and carrier ledges) |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.cells.npz` | the build's area cells and ground heights, read by the exporter |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.rsnv` | the export for the navigation runtime (`.be.rsnv`: big-endian) |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.failed.rsnv` | the export of a build whose check failed, to look at only |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\navkit.json.lock` | the lock the steps take while they write `navkit.json` (it stays; leave it) |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.jeep.rsnv`, `.tank.rsnv`, `.lcvp.rsnv`, `.plane.rsnv` | the vehicle worlds |
| `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.transfers.json`, `<level>.vehicles.json` | the vehicle worlds' transfers and checks |
| `work\levels\<level>\vehicles\` | the ground vehicles' collision, samples and logs |
| `work\levels\<level>\audit\` | the audit's masks (`masks\`) and report (`audit.json`, `audit.md`) |

NavKit never changes your game folder.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to do |
|---|---|
| "... is not a BF1943 game folder" / no game folder found | Run `bf1943-xenia-kit` first, or point `BF1943_GAME` or `--game` at a `dist\xenon` folder with a `levels\` folder. |
| "...: not a level of ..." | Use a name `navkit.py levels` lists, such as `wake_island_s`. |
| "not prepared yet" / "not sampled yet" / "not built yet" | Run the step before it. |
| A step failed in the window | The window shows its last lines; the whole output is in the log above it. |

## How NavKit stays clean

NavKit is written from a published specification of the file format. It contains no code from the original
licensed generator and never runs it. All game data comes from your own copy. See
[README.md](README.md#rules-clean-room-approach).

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/README.md`:

```md
# BF1943 NavKit (big-endian)

> **This variant reads big-endian data:** BF1943's Xbox 360 levels (terrain heightfields; Havok 4.6.1 packfiles). It began as a copy of `bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian` on 2026-10-23. OPFOR's changes reach it through that variant, not directly.

> **2026-10-31: the modules both variants use are one copy in [`bf1943-auto-navkit-common`](../bf1943-auto-navkit-common/README.md)** (the builder `navbuild`, now a package, `navwalk`, `navsample`, `navedits`, `hpdtool`, `kymesh`, `hpdcheck`, `hpdview`, `hkpack`, `havok461`, `levelobjects`, `detailed`, `navdiff`; the spec `KYNAPSE_SPEC.md`; the rule tests), merged with the little-endian copies. This variant keeps its BF1943 tools (`*1943.py`, `rsnvtool.py`) and builds with `soldier1943.SETTINGS`; every BF1943 build and RSNV export comes out byte for byte as before (all four maps rebuilt and exported, 2026-10-31). Below, `tools\<shared module>` means the common folder's.

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** (2026-10-24) - `navkit.py` and `navkitGUI.pyw` are the
BF1943 pipeline: from a level of your BF1943 copy to a checked navigation build, and `tools\navaudit1943.py`
audits a build against its level. **To use it, start with [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md).** How NavKit is built
(the pipeline, the `navkit.json` stamps, the shared modules, BF1943 against BFBC2): [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

```
python navkit.py levels                   the copy's levels, and what has been done for each
python navkit.py prepare wake_island_s    objects, collision, flags, ladders, terrain and water from the bundles
python navkit.py sample  wake_island_s    the collision samples, computed offline (--pitch 0.8 or 0.2: that pass only)
python navkit.py build   wake_island_s    the navigation build with BF1943's soldier
python navkit.py check   wake_island_s    structure (hpdcheck.py) and routes (routecheck1943.py)
python navkit.py all     wake_island_s    prepare, sample, build, check
python navkit.py status  wake_island_s    what has been done for a level
```

Option: `--game <dist\xenon folder>` (default: `BF1943_GAME`, else `bf1943-xenia-kit`'s output).

- **Nothing is started in the game.** The game copy is only read; everything is computed from the level's data.
  There is no `install` or `restore`: BF1943 has no Kynapse runtime. The build is the input of our own navigation
  runtime (a per-level graph queried with A*; operation-rising-sun
  `research/evidence/navigation-runtime-options.json`).
- **Files** go under the suite's work folder (`BF1943_WORK` overrides `<suite>\work`):
  `work\levels\<level>\objects\` (`levelobjects1943.py`'s files, `heightfield.res`, `water_mesh.res`),
  `samples\` (`samples*.bin` and their logs), `navkit\` (`navkit.json` settings, `<level>.hpd`, `<level>.cells.npz`,
  `build.log`, `check.txt` / `check.json`, `jump_links.json`; the exports `<level>.rsnv` and the vehicle worlds),
  `vehicles\` (the ground vehicles' collision, samples and logs), `audit\` (the audit's masks, `audit.json` and
  `audit.md`).
- **Steps.** *prepare* reads the level's objects and collision (`tools\levelobjects1943.py`), its height field and
  water, and sets the sea level and sector offsets. *sample* computes the collision samples offline
  (`tools\navsample1943.py`): two runs at 0.8 m (BF1943's soldier, and a 0.6 m step for stairs), the detailed
  sectors (`tools\detailed1943.py`), then two runs at 0.2 m over them. *build* runs `navbuild` (the package in `..\bf1943-auto-navkit-common\tools\navbuild\`) with
  BF1943's soldier (`tools\soldier1943.py`): 0.8 m everywhere, the detailed sectors at 0.2 m, water, spawn seeds,
  ladder links, jump links to ships' AA gun platforms (`tools\jumplinks1943.py`), and a shared node wherever the
  two grids' ground meets a mixed-pitch seam with no node joining it (`seam_gap_nodes` in `soldier1943.SETTINGS`). *check* runs `tools\hpdcheck.py` and `tools\routecheck1943.py` (new): every spawn and flag joined
  to the route graph, and a route between every pair of flags; it fails when there was nothing to check (no
  soldier spawn, a flag without spawns while others have them, fewer than two flags; 2026-10-30). A Wake Island run
  takes about 45 minutes on 8 cores, most of it the 0.2 m sampling.
- **Stamps** (`navkit.json`, 2026-10-30). Each step records what it was made from and refuses another generation's
  work: *prepare* stores the game folder, every objects file's SHA-256 and their digest (`preparation`), and drops
  the later stamps; each sampling pass stores that digest and the game (`samples`: `0.8`, and `0.2` with its
  sectors) and drops the stamps after it; *build* needs the current preparation's 0.8 m pass (the 0.2 m samples
  only when theirs too) and records them (`build_from`); *check* needs that build. A `--game` other than the
  preparation's is refused, and so is a `--pitch` other than 0.8 or 0.2. Levels prepared before 2026-10-30 have no
  digest: prepare and sample them again. The audit and the RSNV export read the game copy the level was prepared
  from.
- **The window** (`navkitGUI.pyw`): a level list, the steps Prepare, Sample, Build and Check with a mark for each
  step done, **Run all (1-4)**, **Cancel** (ends the running step and its samplers), **Show in 3D** (opens the
  Navigation Studio on the build) and **Open output folder**.
- **Wake Island, today's build (2026-10-29, round 5):** 12,779 nodes, 45,278 edges, 64 islands; the main network has 11,420
  nodes; 16 of 16 ladders linked from the main network, the 4 carrier AA guns and 21 carrier ledges by jump links; all 10 flag pairs
  routed; `hpdcheck` passes.
- **The audit** (`tools\navaudit1943.py`, new 2026-10-24; operation-rising-sun `research/NAVMESH_AUDIT.md`):
  `navaudit1943.py masks <level>` recomputes the build's walkable surfaces exactly as the build does (and once per
  rule with the rule off: headroom, lips, water, ladders); `navaudit1943.py audit <level>` then checks the build
  against the level's own data - every capture area, spawn, mounted gun and repair station on an area of its own floor,
  every vehicle with walkable ground within its own EntryRadius of an entry point (the vehicle's
  PlayerEntryComponentData; `VEHICLE_REACH`, 4 m from the spawn, only where a blueprint gives none), routes from every infantry spawn to every capture area and back, islands classified (main,
  vehicle-only zone, separate landmass, raised surface, gap candidate), file consistency and crossings (touching
  ground on two islands, tested on the samples), 0.8 m against 0.2 m, the wading band, where each rule fired and its
  near-misses, and the playable area. Where it lists a column's surfaces, a terrain surface carries its ground
  material (core `materialmap1943.py`, the level's terrain material map). The checks are in
  the package `tools\navaudit1943_checks` (a module per check). Reports: `work\levels\<level>\audit\audit.{json,md}`.
- **The export for our navigation runtime** (`tools\navexport1943.py`, new 2026-10-24): `navexport1943.py <level>
  [--big-endian] [--check]` writes `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.rsnv` (`.be.rsnv` big-endian), the build in
  the runtime's own format (core `rsnv.py`): the route graph with integer costs (1/16 m) and edge kinds (walk, ladder
  up and down, jump), each area's walkable cells and their heights (a height grid of 1 m blocks at 0.2 m pitch, one
  block per cell at 0.8 m; exporter 1.1, 2026-10-25), a grid to find the areas near a point, the islands, and the
  build's hash. Exporter 1.2 flags tight walk edges, those with no line of sight either way over the cells
  (`rsnv.World.los`, the runtime's rule). `--check` reads the file back and compares it with the build.
  **Exporter 1.3 (2026-10-26)** takes each area's cells and ground heights from the build itself: `navbuild` writes
  `<level>.cells.npz` beside `<level>.hpd` (every area's cells and heights, and the build's SHA-256). Before, heights
  were estimated from the nearest outline point, 0.3 m or more off on 11 % of Coral Sea's 0.8 m cells (`--compare`
  reports the old rasterisation's differences). With it, and the runtime's quarter-cell line-of-sight rule, tight edges
  fell from 1.6-4 % to 0.16-0.33 % of the walk edges and pockets from 5.5-36.5 % to 0.4-1.0 % of each main network;
  0 nodes outside an area on all four maps. LADR holds only ladder and jump records the build linked (a
  `jump_links.json` newer than the build gave records with no node, which rsnav refuses). Details: operation-rising-sun
  `research/NAVMESH_AUDIT.md`, update 2026-10-26.
- **2026-10-26 build rules:** ships' ledges (`jumplinks1943.SHIP_LEDGES`: jump links between a carrier's floors a
  ledge apart, its deck-edge galleries 0.58 m and gun tubs 0.84 m under the deck; Wake 21, Iwo Jima 21, Coral Sea 41
  links) and border nodes on the seam line (`navbuild.BORDER_SEAM_LINE`, on in `soldier1943.SETTINGS`: ground that
  reaches a sector seam but not the border line one sample beyond gets a shared node; two of Coral Sea's three seam
  breaks closed).
- **2026-10-26, round 2:** areas hold no cliff (`navbuild.AREA_CLIFF`: a surface beside a cell of its area more than
  1 m and a 45-degree slope plus the step away in height starts its own area - a bridge deck beside the ground under
  it); `join_groups` floods up to 2 m past a sector's window into sectors of the same pitch (`JOIN_MARGIN`); the
  exporter gives an area 0.4 m height blocks, then one per cell, where its 1 m grid is more than 0.25 m off at one of
  its cells (`HEIGHT_TOL`); a seam's coincident nodes are merged (`merge_coincident_border`). Tight walk edges
  150/88/124/158 -> 8/40/26/96, pockets 0.2 % or less of each main network; exports 4.2-5.5 MB.
- **2026-10-26, round 3 (exporter 1.4):** beside a mixed (0.2/0.8 m) seam, the 0.8 m graph gets walk edges where the
  0.2 m samples join ground its own step rule cannot (`SEAM_FINE_LINKS`: Coral Sea's last seam break, a 0.53 m lip
  beside the South Base bunker, closed); a sector's window grows 1 m past a mixed seam so both grids' cells overlap there
  (`MIXED_OVERLAP`; no nodes on the grown cells); exporter 1.4 rounds every edge cost up to 16 x its length and writes
  the search heuristic's scale in the header (0.999 on all four maps: the heuristic is admissible), and lists an area in
  every 4 m bucket its cells reach. Tight walk edges 8/40/26/96 -> 8/10/14/30 (Wake, Guadalcanal, Iwo Jima, Coral Sea); pockets 0.24/0.05/0.20/0.00 %
  of each main network; exports 4.3-5.5 MB.
- **2026-10-29, round 4:** every tight pair traced (`rsnvtool.py tight`, `cells`). Line of sight starts on the floor
  nearest the start's height (`rsnv.LOS_START_NEAREST`: 11 of 31 pairs had started a floor below their node on stairs)
  and tests a change of area against the ground it has followed (`LOS_FOLLOWED`); `AREA_CLIFF` 1.0 -> 0.6 m (no two
  side-by-side cells of one area beyond the 0.2 m step rule). Tight walk edges 8/10/14/30 -> 8/6/6/28; pockets
  0.24/0.05/0.20/0.00 % -> 0.04/0.03/0.01/0.00 %; exports 4.2-5.4 MB. What is left, case by case: operation-rising-sun
  `research/NAVMESH_AUDIT.md` item 7.
- **2026-10-29, round 5:** `AREA_CLIFF_REACH` 2 (no two cells of an area two apart across an empty cell beyond a 45-degree
  slope plus the step: Iwo Jima's floor strip one empty row from the floor 1.56 m above it) and `SEAM_FAR_LINKS` (0.8 m
  pieces two columns apart beside a mixed seam joined where one piece of 0.2 m ground carries the build's own line:
  Iwo Jima's last seam break closed; Iwo Jima 2 links, Coral Sea 3). Tight walk edges 8/6/6/28 -> 6/6/4/26; pockets
  0.04/0.04/0.00/0.00 %; no seam break left; `rsnvtool.py walk` added. NAVMESH_AUDIT.md item 8.

**Vehicle navigation (new 2026-10-26).** One RSNV world per vehicle class beside the soldier's, read by rsnav like
any other world: `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.jeep.rsnv`, `.tank.rsnv`, `.lcvp.rsnv`, `.plane.rsnv`, plus
`<level>.transfers.json` (every transfer, resolved against the current soldier world) and `<level>.vehicles.json` (the
checks). `tools\navexport_vehicles1943.py <level> [--sample] [--classes ...] [--check-only]` builds and checks them
all; it only reads `<level>.rsnv`. Labels: [O] from the data, [E] estimate, [H] hypothesis, [U] unknown.

- **Stamps (2026-10-30).** The vehicle collision was made again only when its file was missing, the ground samples on
  disk were reused whatever they were made from, the builders read the default game copy's spawns, a missing world
  passed the check, and a level without water (sea level None) raised TypeError. Now every vehicle step stamps
  `navkit.json` (`vehicles`: `collision`, `samples` and `worlds` per class; the preparation's digest, the game copy, the
  class's parameters' digest, a world also the soldier world's SHA-256; `vehicleclasses1943.py`), samples or worlds
  of another generation are made again or refused, the builders read the prepared copy, a class absent from the level
  (its data: no spawns, no water) is stamped absent while a requested world missing fails the check, and a level
  without water gets `soldier1943.sea_level` (10 m under its lowest terrain: no ground under water, as in its build)
  for the ground and plane worlds and no landing-craft world. `navexport1943.py` exports only the checked build of
  the current preparation and stamps the export (`exported`). After review: a build is told apart by its `.hpd`'s
  SHA-256 (`build_from` `hpd_sha256`, also in `exported`; `built` keeps only the minute); the samples' parameter digest
  covers only what the sampler reads; the soldier world and the game copy are compared by file identity; every step
  writes `navkit.json` by a fresh read-modify-write of its own keys (`tools\navkitjson1943.py`), so the long soldier
  steps keep the vehicle stamps written while they ran; jump links and the audit take `soldier1943.sea_level` too.
  Second review (2026-10-30): `navkit.json` is written by replacing it whole (a temporary file) under
  a lock on `navkit.json.lock` (30 s wait, then an error in words), and a missing or damaged file is an error in
  words; *prepare* empties `objects\` first; each sampling pass has an `id`
  and the build records the ids it used (`build_from` `samples_08_id`, `samples_02_id`), so a 0.2 m pass made while
  the build ran leaves it unstamped; the build's jump links read `samples_02.bin` only when the build uses that pass;
  the audit (`navaudit1943.py masks` and `audit`) takes only the checked build of the current preparation and makes
  again a mask of other samples or another build; `navexport1943.py` still exports a build whose check failed (to
  look at) but does not stamp it as the soldier world and exits 1, and the vehicle builders refuse such a build;
  `navkit.py` and `routecheck1943.py` parse their arguments with argparse (`--pitch=0.2`, options anywhere, unknown
  arguments refused). Tests: `tests\test_vehicle_stages.py`, `tests\test_navkit_stages.py`, `tests\test_navkit_review.py`.
  Second review, second pass (2026-10-30): the lock is an OS lock (`msvcrt.locking`; `fcntl.flock` elsewhere) on
  `navkit.json.lock`, a file that stays in place: the system releases it when its process ends, so a killed step
  leaves nothing behind and no lock is ever removed by its age (the age rule let two steps hold it at once, and a
  left-over lock file it could not delete made every step spin forever); every wait ends after 30 s with an error
  naming the file; a level without its `navkit\` folder is "not prepared". A vehicle world is stamped only while its
  soldier world is still the export of the current, passed build (`vehicleclasses1943.record` refuses one finished
  after the soldier was built again), and `navexport_vehicles1943.py`'s check reports a `<level>.rsnv` that is not
  the current export. The build stamps its `jump_links.json` (`build_from` `jump_links_sha256`): the export and the
  audit refuse the build when that file was written again since (a build stamped before this has none: build and
  check again), and `jumplinks1943.py` with another `--game` than the prepared copy refuses to write it (`--json`
  elsewhere is allowed). An export of a build whose check failed goes to `<level>.failed.rsnv` (`.be.failed.rsnv`)
  unless `--out` names a file, so `<level>.rsnv` stays as it was. Test: `tests\test_navkit_review2.py`.
  The user's review (2026-10-30): a vehicle world's stamp (`vehicles` `worlds` per class) also holds the world file's
  own SHA-256 (`sha256`), and META the class parameters' digest (`params`); the vehicle check refuses a file that is
  not the one its builder wrote and a world whose header and META name another level (level id, META level), class
  (META class, layer) or parameters (header radius, META params) - a valid world of another level with radius 99 in
  the jeep world's place had passed (a world stamped before this has no `sha256`: build it again). The soldier export,
  the audit and the jump links take the height field the level was prepared with (`objects\heightfield.res`, checked
  against `objects_sha256`), and refuse a game copy whose height field changed since (they reread the game's).
  `rsnvtool.py pockets`: the pieces are weakly connected components (an edge joins its ends whichever way it runs),
  disjoint; they followed outgoing edges only and could overlap on one-way edges. It also prints the share of the
  largest piece outside its strongly connected core (one-way edges). Every soldier export of 2026-10-25 to 10-30 in
  `work` has no one-way kept edge, so the pocket shares recorded then are unchanged. Test: `tests\test_navkit_review3.py`.

- **Classes** (`tools\vehicleclasses1943.py`, which reads and prints the blueprints and collision): sizes [O] from each
  vehicle's `*_havok.res` box; slope from `WheelConfigData SlopeGripMaxAngle` (jeeps 25 deg [O]; tanks 25..52 [O],
  40 used [E]); top gear speed [O] (unit km/h [H]); entry radius and exit points [O]. Jeep: radius 1.5 m (half-width
  1.06 [O] + 0.45 [E]), height 2.0, step 0.3 [E], ford 0.8 [E]. Tank: radius 1.8, height 2.9, step 0.6 [E], ford 1.2
  [E]. LCVP: radius 2.5, draft 0.9 [E], bow ramp 5.5 m ahead [O]. Plane: clearance 25 m, cruise 60 m above the floor
  [E]. Not in the data: steering angle, step height, the entries' AIData (dangling references) [U].
- **Ground** (`tools\groundnav1943.py prepare|sample|build|all <level> [jeep|tank]`): the collision without ExcludeFromPathfinding
  objects and dynamic props (fences, palms, wire, sandbags, crates - pushed through [H]), sampled by
  `navsample1943.py` with the class's disc, step and height on the soldier's 0.8 m grid (about 11-13 min per class
  and map); drivable = not blocked, slope, ford depth, not on ForbidPathfinding objects, continuous ground under the
  disc; links by the step rule; components touching a ground-vehicle spawn kept; nodes every 6.4 m at the cell
  farthest from the undrivable, edges by a straight grid line, graph pieces joined along the grid's shortest path.
  NavKit's `.hpd` builder is not used: its rules are fitted to the soldier and DICE's BFBC2 data.
- **Landing craft** (`tools\seanav1943.py <level>`): 2 m sea grid, depth = sea level - terrain [O], blocked by collision
  crossing the waterline band; nodes every 10 m; deck lanes from each carrier craft along its own heading to the
  deck's end (the craft face the sterns [O]; leaving that way [H]) and a one-way DROP edge to the water; landing zones
  every 25 m of beach whose bow point unloads onto the soldier main island, nearest of any island and with no
  ForbidPathfinding collision between (Iwo Jima's no-go strip is never used; checked).
- **Planes** (`tools\airnav1943.py <level>`, a first version): 16 m altitude-floor grid (terrain and every object's top,
  grown by 25 m), a cruise surface 60 m above it that climbs at most 7 deg, nodes every 64 m; take-off lanes along the
  spawn headings (decks, airfields) with a JUMP edge (climb-out) and a DROP edge (landing approach); parachute DROP
  transfers over every base, flag and non-carrier soldier island (Coral Sea's islets).
- **Writer 1.2 (2026-10-29): admissible costs.** As the soldier exporter 1.4: each drive edge costs 16 x its length
  between the float32 node positions, rounded up (a given cost, a deck drop's horizontal run, no less), and the header
  carries the heuristic scale (`rsnv.heuristic_scale`: 0.999 on every vehicle world), so `rsnv.search` and rsnav's
  search never overestimate on vehicle worlds either. The heading-aware planner keeps its own weighted heuristic (x1.25,
  by design: a local, bounded search over its own primitive costs).
- **Unload points (2026-10-29):** a landing zone's alight transfer stores a soldier cell beside the craft's bow from
  which a main-island node is in sight (100 of 104 zones on Wake, 58 of 62 on Iwo Jima; the rest the node itself), and
  `rsnvtrip.resolve` / `rsn_transfer_soldier_node` resolve alight and drop transfers to the nearest node within 6 m in
  line of sight of that point (`rsnv.World.los` / `rsn_los`, 32 tried at most) when the stored node has moved: a
  rebuilt soldier world moves its nodes, the point stays [O: the cells; H: that a soldier steps off the ramp there].
- **Take-off lanes checked (2026-10-26):** every lane is tested against the collision on rsnav's flight-test obstacle
  grid (4 m cells, all objects): the centre line +-2 m clear from its start to 40 m past its end, the deck or field
  under the roll to lift-off (85 m). A blocked spawn heading is turned (up to 20 deg; then any heading: a turn on the
  ground), started up to 16 m ahead (out of a hangar) or shortened (to 75 m), in that order; each lane's meta records
  its offset, start, length, clearance and the highest obstacle within the half wingspan, with [O] / [H]. Changed: 7
  of 23 (Guadalcanal 1533, 1535, 1536; Iwo Jima 1986, 2219; Coral Sea 640, 648); Guadalcanal 1581's roll leaves its
  hilltop at 58 m (kept, flagged). The flight test takes off from all 23.
- **Transfers** (OFFM): board (1: entry point, EntryRadius, aux = soldier node), alight (2) and drop (4: the soldier
  node), launch (3: the deck end). `core\bfbc2core\rsnvtrip.py` resolves them again against the soldier world in use
  and plans walk -> ride -> walk (rsnav's `rsn_trip_plan` gives the same answer).
- **Writer:** `tools\rsnvgrid1943.py` (areas per 100 m sector by flood fill, one cell per column; bitmaps, per-cell
  heights, buckets, portals, islands, tight edges by `rsnv.World.los`). Writer 1.1 (2026-10-26): a cell on a 100 m
  sector edge goes to the sector it starts (before, i x 0.8 m rounding lost a one-cell column on every sector edge to the
  bucket lookup).
- **Heading-aware planning** (`core\bfbc2core\rsnvhybrid.py`, 2026-10-26): the reference of rsnav's `rsn_hybrid_plan`, a
  lattice hybrid A* over (cell, 16 headings, direction) with motion primitives per kind (car 4.5 m, boat 8 m turning
  radius [E], reversing at a cost; tanks pivot); rsnav's C tables are generated from it. Used locally by the drivers:
  jeeps 120 / 120, tanks 120 / 120, landing craft 96 / 96 routes in the kinematic simulation (rsnav README).
- **Tests:** `tests\test_vehicles_nav1943.py` (quick tier, made-up data); rsnav's `tests\test_vehicles.py` on the real
  worlds.
- **Built (2026-10-26) [M]:** jeep 3,263 / 4,178 / 3,012 nodes (Wake / Guadalcanal / Iwo Jima; 0.08-0.11 km2
  drivable, 1.0-1.5 MB); tank 5,252 / 5,697 / 4,191 (0.12-0.17 km2, 1.4-1.9 MB); LCVP 24,870 nodes, 104 landing zones,
  8 deck lanes on Wake, 15,093 / 63 / 8 on Iwo Jima (Guadalcanal and Coral Sea have no craft); plane about 1,000 nodes
  per map, 5-8 take-off lanes, 10-71 drops. Every check of `navexport_vehicles1943.py` passes on all four maps; every
  carrier deck reaches every flag by the craft (Wake 10/10, Iwo Jima 20/20 trips). The soldier export changes under
  these files without harm: transfers carry positions and are resolved again.

**Looking inside an export** (`tools\rsnvtool.py`, new 2026-10-26; read-only; `<level>` is a level name or an
`.rsnv` path; `--class jeep|tank|lcvp|plane` reads a vehicle world; tested by `tests\test_rsnvtool.py`):

| Command | What it gives |
|---|---|
| `info <level>` | sections, counts, edge kinds, tight edges, islands, the exporter and its sources' hashes |
| `validate <level>` | consistency (exit 1 on a problem) |
| `locate <level> X Y Z` | the walkable cell and nearest node under a point |
| `los <level> X,Y,Z X,Y,Z` | line of sight by the runtime's rule |
| `route <level> FROM TO [--soldier] [--png]` | a search between nodes or points, as rsnav finds it |
| `pockets <level>` | the main network's pieces without tight edges (weakly connected, disjoint), the largest pockets with positions, and the share outside the largest piece's strongly connected core |
| `tight <level> [--samples] [--json F]` | every tight walk edge (new 2026-10-29): its ends' areas (sector, pitch, layer, cell, ground), the first failing line-of-sight sample each way with the rule that refuses it (`rsnv.World.los`'s trace) and by how much, the other areas with ground there, and a cause (`hole`, `step`, `lean`, `cell`, `climb`, `end`); `--samples` adds the build's own samples and kept surfaces at that sample (the audit's base masks) |
| `cells <level> --at X,Z --y Y [--radius R] [--samples] [--line A B]` | text maps around a point (new 2026-10-29), 0.2 m a character: each area's walkable cells, the build's samples on both grids (kept / not kept), a line drawn over them |
| `walk <level> A B [--reach R]` | the build's own kept samples along a line (new 2026-10-29, round 5; A, B nodes or points), on both grids: the surface followed column by column, the largest step and where, the gaps, how far the end lies off B - what a straight walk over the kept surfaces meets, to set against line of sight |
| `picture <level> --at X,Z [--radius R] [--y Y] [--route FROM TO]` | a top-down PNG: cells; edges (tight red, ladders orange, jumps cyan); a route in yellow |
| `diff <a> <b>` | what changed between two exports |

**Reading BF1943.** `hkpack.py` (`bf1943-auto-navkit-common\tools`) reads Havok 4.6.1 packfiles (byte order from
the file's layout rules, 20-byte class-member records); BF1943's packfiles carry no `__types__`, so class layouts are
given by `havok461.py` there (checked by its `tests\test_havok461.py` on all 807 meshes of Wake Island's 97 Havok
files).
`tools\levelobjects1943.py` reads object placements and collision straight from the bundles (meshes and
`hkConvexVerticesShape` boxes; `hkBoxShape` and `hkConvexTranslateShape` are not read yet and are reported), and
writes `ladders.json` from the placed objects whose blueprint has a `LadderEntityData` (Wake Island: 16). Core's
`terrain.py` and `water.py` detect the byte order.

**BF1943's soldier.** `tools\soldier1943.py` holds the soldier's physics (`DefaultSoldierPhysics`: radius 0.35 m,
step 0.3 m plus a 0.07 m tolerance, height 1.8 m, 45 deg, water depth 1.4 m), and its `SETTINGS` (a
`navbuild.Settings`, which `navkit.py build` passes to `navbuild.build`) holds the NavKit settings that follow from it
over the BFBC2 defaults (`navbuild.BFBC2`): slope limit, the detailed zones' link step (0.37 m), node height (0.9 m),
and the headroom band (0.5-1.8 m); the water depth goes in as `build(max_water_depth=...)`. They also switch on
BF1943's build rules (`ladder_all_ground`, and the seam and area rules of the 2026-10-26 entries above). Nothing
rewrites NavKit's module constants at run time (`configure()` did until 2026-10-31). NavKit's other values were fitted
to DICE's BFBC2 path data and are not checked on BF1943. Since the two variants' builders were merged (2026-10-31),
`seam_gap_nodes` says what this variant's copy always did (the little-endian copy never had it). Since 2026-11 BF1943
takes NavKit's whole-centimetre sector rule (`column_sectors_cm`; until then a column's float position, which put a
column on a sector line in the sector before it and gave Guadalcanal a one-row sector of its own; `detailed1943.py`
counts stacked floors by the same rule, and chooses the same sectors), and `normal_links_own_grid`: after the merge
with the detailed zones, the neighbour links between two 0.8 m sectors by the 0.8 m step rule (the 0.2 m rule NavKit
still defaults to left 44 of Guadalcanal's 199 and 84 of Coral Sea's 410 such border portals unlinked).

**Tools in this variant:** `detailed1943.py`, `levelobjects1943.py`, `navsample1943.py`, `routecheck1943.py`,
`soldier1943.py`, `jumplinks1943.py`, `navaudit1943.py` with `navaudit1943_checks` (a package), `navexport1943.py`,
`rsnvtool.py`, `enclosure_probe1943.py`, `vehicleclasses1943.py`, `groundnav1943.py`, `seanav1943.py`,
`airnav1943.py`, `rsnvgrid1943.py`, `navexport_vehicles1943.py`, `navkitjson1943.py` (navkit.json and its stamps,
shared by `navkit.py` and the tools) (`enclosure_probe1943.py <level> <x> <y> <z> [radius] [--png out.png]`: why a
spot is cut off from the network). The modules it shares with the little-endian variant are in
`bf1943-auto-navkit-common\tools` (one copy since 2026-10-31): `navbuild` (a package), `navwalk.py`, `navsample.py`,
`navedits.py`, `hpdtool.py`, `kymesh.py`, `hpdcheck.py`, `hpdview.py`, `hkpack.py`, `havok461.py`,
`levelobjects.py`, `detailed.py`, `navdiff.py`. Not in this variant: `graphstats`, `sample_all`, `navwater`,
`navlinks`, `navtraversal`, `navboundary`, `navcompare`, `navparity`, `navregress`, `ordercheck` and `ladders.py`.
They remain in `bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian`, which stays OPFOR's BFBC2 NavKit.

**Layout of this variant:**

```
QUICKSTART.md        how to build a BF1943 level's navigation, step by step
navkitGUI.pyw        the NavKit window (Tkinter): the steps as buttons
navkit.py            driver: levels / prepare / sample / build / check / all / status
tools\               this variant's NavKit tools (Python 3 + numpy); the shared ones (navbuild, navwalk, navsample,
                     hpdtool, kymesh, hpdcheck, hpdview, hkpack, havok461, levelobjects, detailed, navedits, navdiff)
                     and the spec (KYNAPSE_SPEC.md) are in ..\bf1943-auto-navkit-common
  levelobjects1943.py  BF1943: object placements, collision, flags and ladders straight from the level's bundles
  navsample1943.py     BF1943: collision samples computed offline (terrain + collision)
  detailed1943.py      BF1943: which sectors are built at 0.2 m (detailed.py's rule on BF1943 data)
  soldier1943.py       BF1943's soldier and the NavKit settings that follow from it (navbuild.Settings)
  navkitjson1943.py    a level's navkit.json (settings and stamps): read, fresh read-modify-write; SHA-256, file identity
  routecheck1943.py    BF1943: spawns and flags on the route graph, routes between every pair of flags
  jumplinks1943.py     BF1943: jump links from ships' decks to their AA gun platforms, and between a carrier's floors
                       a ledge apart (SHIP_LEDGES) (ladder records of kind 'jump'); a raised-floor rule
                       (RAISED_FLOORS) is kept but off - see operation-rising-sun NAVMESH_AUDIT.md
  navaudit1943.py      BF1943: the audit - the build's walkable masks, then the checks
  navaudit1943_checks\ BF1943: the audit's checks, a package of a module per check (required positions,
                       reachability, consistency, resolution, layers, water, rules, playable area; __init__ lists them)
  navexport1943.py     BF1943: the build exported for our navigation runtime (<level>.rsnv, core rsnv.py)
  rsnvtool.py          BF1943: look inside an RSNV export - info, validate, locate, los, route, pockets, picture, diff
  vehicleclasses1943.py  BF1943: the vehicle classes (jeep, tank, lcvp, plane) from the blueprints and collision
  groundnav1943.py     BF1943: jeep and tank worlds (<level>.jeep.rsnv, <level>.tank.rsnv)
  seanav1943.py        BF1943: the landing craft's world (<level>.lcvp.rsnv)
  airnav1943.py        BF1943: the planes' world (<level>.plane.rsnv), a first version
  rsnvgrid1943.py      BF1943: the vehicle worlds' RSNV writer (cells on a grid -> an RSNV world)
  navexport_vehicles1943.py  BF1943: builds and checks every vehicle world of a level, and its transfers
  enclosure_probe1943.py  BF1943: why a spot is cut off (flood fill over the 0.2 m samples, the blocking objects, a map)
tests\               the sampler, rsnvtool, jump links, mixed-pitch seams (BF1943's settings), the steps and their
                     stamps, vehicle navigation, Wake Island's objects and the RSNV export (the rule tests and the
                     Havok 4.6.1 test are the common folder's)
```

What follows is OPFOR's NavKit description, which this variant shares. Its commands, steps and tools are the
little-endian variant's (`bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian`), not this variant's: where it names tools this
variant no longer has (`ladders.py`, `navregress.py`, `navparity.py` and the others listed above) or OPFOR's in-game
sampler, FbrbTool and DbxEdit, those are BFBC2's pipeline. Standalone tooling to create AI navigation data
(`pathdata.hpd`) for Battlefield: Bad Company 2 levels – including multiplayer maps that never shipped with any – so
the game's own AI can move on them. Developed for Project OPFOR and published for other modders as
`bfbc2-auto-navkit`, the automated navigation-data generator of the BFBC2 suite. For BF1943, use this variant's
[QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md); BFBC2's is the little-endian variant's.

## Why

BC2's AI uses Autodesk Kynapse. The game ships the Kynapse *runtime* (which loads `pathdata.hpd`)
under DICE's runtime licence, but the *generator* that DICE used to create that data is a separately
licensed developer tool: the copy that is still inside the game executable stops with a FLEXnet
licence error. NavKit replaces it with independent code.

## Rules (clean-room approach)

1. **Research** (`research\`): the Kynapse map builder in BFBC2Game.exe and the `.hpd` files are
   reverse engineered for interoperability. Results are written up as a *specification* – file
   formats, data structures, units, what each build stage produces. Licence checks are only located
   and documented as the boundary; they are not analysed in order to defeat them and nothing in this
   project bypasses them.
2. **Implementation** (`src\`): written from the specification with our own code and open-source
   libraries (e.g. recastnavigation, zlib licence). No Kynapse code is copied or translated
   line-by-line, no Kynapse binaries are shipped, and the tool never runs Kynapse code.
3. Game data (levels, collision meshes) always comes from the user's own installation.
4. Geometry is sampled through the **game engine's own physics queries** (DICE code, via Project
   OPFOR's `[dev] navsample` option) or read from the level's own data files – never through Kynapse.
   Observations of the original generator are limited to its boundary with DICE's code (the point
   queries it makes, the files it writes) and its output data.
5. The private folder `research\kynapse mapbuilder research\` is git-ignored and never published.

## Layout

This variant's layout is at the top of this README; OPFOR's full BFBC2 layout is in the little-endian variant's README.

## Detailed zones, ladders and walkability rules (2026-10-21 / 22)

All 15 levels with DICE path data, rebuilt and measured on PC ground (`navregress.py`, run `regression_det_v6`,
2026-10-23, now the default reference `regression`): **ground 98.2 %** of DICE's, **extra ground 8.3 %**,
**connectivity 98.5** (of the routes DICE's data allows, the share NavKit's allows), over-connection 15.3 % (routes
only NavKit's allows: open slopes, stairs, steps and ladders - see below). **Every area boundary is closed** on all 15
builds (0 open areas; before the exact bridge tracing below, 1.7 - 3.1 % of the areas on sp_004_b / sp_01 were open,
DICE has none).

- **Exact bridge tracing (`navbuild.BRIDGE_UNION`, 2026-10-23):** an area's 45-degree bridges are the exact union of
  the quarter cells they cut, traced as one outline, in place of clipping each bridge on its own (`clip_bridges`,
  which left gaps where bridges met: open boundaries, and walkable ground in no area). Ground 98.12 -> 98.22 %,
  extra 8.36 -> 8.31; checked by `tests\test_bridge_union.py` (600 random patterns; the old method fails 107) and by
  `hpdcheck.py` on every regression build.

- **The default pipeline:** `navkit.py sample` (and `all`, and the window's buttons) samples the level at 0.8 m, chooses
  its detailed zones from the level alone, then samples those at 0.2 m (`DETAILED_BUDGET_MS` = 400 ms of sampling per
  frame: a 0.2 m run is ten times the columns and must end before a round, or a campaign level with an idle player,
  does). A run whose level ends first is reported, not waited out. `navkit.py build` builds the detailed sectors at
  0.2 and merges them with the normal build.
- **Detailed zones (pitch 0.2):** chosen by `tools\detailed.py` without DICE's data - sectors near an object whose
  blueprint sets `NeedsDetailedPathfinding`, and sectors with 100+ stacked-floor columns in the 0.8 m samples (93 % of
  DICE's choice on 14 levels). Built with 6 x 6 tiles, link step 0.3 m, a Gabriel-pruned route graph and coverage
  nodes every 4 m.
- **Ladder links:** `navkit.py prepare` writes `ladders.json` (BFBC2: `tools\ladders.py`; in this variant
  `tools\levelobjects1943.py`, from the objects whose blueprint has a `LadderEntityData`: placed ladders and their
  collision boxes, a buried foot raised to the terrain); the build seeds the far end of a ladder whose near end is walkable and links a node at each end.
  DICE's path data has none; the game puts any soldier who walks into a ladder on it.
- **Walkability rules added 2026-10-22** (`tools\navwalk.py`, each with a switch and its measurements in the code):
  - `LIP_WIDTH`: at 0.2 m, a band of up to two samples steeper than 40 deg between walkable ground (a lip the 0.8 m
    step rule stepped over) is walkable; `LIP_OBJECT_RISE`: the same on objects when the band is within 0.3 m of the
    floor on both sides (door sills, thresholds) - steeper than 55 deg only between flat floors (`LIP_OBJECT_FLAT`
    15 deg: a rock mesh meeting sloped terrain is no sill). sp_007's north strip, sp_009's aircraft aisles (sp_009
    connectivity 90.9 -> 100).
  - `DYNAMIC_FLOOR`, `DYNAMIC_ABSENT_HEADROOM`: dynamic props (and `PdtWhenAlive` doors) are absent for path data -
    the floor under a prop lying on it counts, and neither the prop nor rays grazing its vertical faces count as a
    ceiling. sp_003_b's monastery gate, sp_009's aircraft doors.
  - `ROOF_PRUNE`: roof islands nothing reaches are dropped - an island with no soldier spawn, AI order position or
    ladder end, mostly on objects with ground 2 m or more below, and no reached ground within 2 m at its own height.
    Ground-level islands stay (DICE keeps those). sp_008 extra ground 29.5 -> 22.7 %, sp_01 12.2 -> 9.6 %.
  - Not adopted: a slope test from heights instead of normals (`STEEP_TERRAIN`, off - DICE cuts at 40 deg by the
    normal: 15 % of 40-45 deg terrain covered), pruning islands by size or by combat area (DICE keeps small islands
    and ground outside its combat areas).
- **Collision of assets named `<name>_Havok_Havok.res`** (`levelobjects.havok_index`): indexed under the blueprint's
  name; before, such an object had no collision in NavKit (sp_009's animated aircraft door stayed solid).
- **navparity** clips DICE's reference to the level's terrain (ground beyond it does not exist on PC), leaves out
  DICE's route nodes with no PC ground within 1 m of their height (`stale_nodes`, column *stale_reference_nodes*:
  data built before late geometry - sp_03's only valley-to-plateau links run under a cliff mesh added afterwards),
  matches nodes within 1 m of height, and reports ground reached by ladder as its own column (*ladder %*), not as
  extra ground.
- **"Up" border portals** (a border portal whose direction is (0, 1, 0)): about half of DICE's border portals
  (50-58 % on sp_004_b, sp_01, ONS_MP_002), none of NavKit's. Not a kind of portal: they lie where DICE's ordinary
  ones lie (the sector margin, along the line), the neighbour sector's area is across them as for the others (100 %),
  and along one border line consecutive pieces of the same geometry alternate between (1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0); the
  y slot also holds 0.38, 0.92, 0.71 and -2.0. A default or left-over value in DICE's generator; NavKit writes the
  outward direction, and its files route across sector borders in game. (DICE also splits border portals per 0.8 m
  cell - 3-4x NavKit's count, the same geometry.)
- **Anomalies against DICE** (Navigation Studio's overlay counts, 15 levels, 2026-10-22 - DICE / NavKit): soldier
  spawns on islands under 25 nodes 147 / 72, AI orders without a route node 768 / 686, sliver areas 77,996 /
  62,708, lonely route nodes 5,081 / 10,011, islands under 25 nodes 5,684 / 6,390. NavKit has fewer of the two that
  stop bots; more lonely nodes, and more slivers on levels with many detailed sectors (clutter at 0.2 m).
  - *Lonely nodes* (no other node within 12 m) are node spacing, not junk: on sp_006 2,634 of NavKit's 2,638 are on
    islands of 25+ nodes - normal sectors get route nodes only at area centres and portals. Proposed: coverage nodes
    in normal sectors too (`NODE_COVER`, about 8-10 m), tuned by regression.
  - *Sliver areas* (under 5 cells, no portal) are mostly 0.2 m clutter (sp_006: 7,712 of 9,060 in detailed zones;
    DICE 1,160): one-area islands nothing routes onto. Proposed: drop isolated areas of a few 0.2 m cells unless a
    spawn, order or ladder anchors them.
  - *Border-to-border duplicate nodes* (two border nodes at one spot joined by a zero-length edge): none any more -
    sp_01, sp_004_b and ONS_MP_002 have 0, as DICE's (shared corner nodes, 2026-10-20).
- **Missing ground** (DICE's walkable ground NavKit lacks, about 1.9 %; five levels classified, 2026-10-23): 74-97 %
  of it is a rim beside NavKit's ground. By what NavKit's samples show there: terrain steeper than 40 deg 56 % (DICE's
  areas reach a cell past where the samples turn steep), walkable but not kept 22 % (on sp_01: DICE's own small
  unreached islands of 2-23 nodes 64 %, cells outside their own unclosed outline 22 % - fixed by `BRIDGE_UNION`),
  no surface at DICE's height 17 % (half of it under objects - on ONS_MP_002 vegetation; making vegetation passable
  was tried and dropped: about 0.1 % of DICE's ground to gain, and both versions lost ground), no room 3.5 %.
- **Closed area boundaries** (`navbuild.BRIDGE_UNION`, 2026-10-23): DICE's files have no area whose outline, portals
  and border portals leave an open end; NavKit's had them in 1.7-3.1 % of areas (sp_004_b, sp_01), all at cell
  corners where a 45-degree bridge piece ends - overlapping bridges were clipped asymmetrically, and an area's cells
  fell outside its own outline. The bridges' outline is now the exact union of the half-cells they cover.
- **M-COM targets on the Onslaught maps** (2026-10-23): 14 of the 15 AI attack orders that sit on an M-COM
  (`mpobjective`, within 3 m; ONS_MP_002 7 of 8, ONS_MP_004 6 of 6) are on no area in NavKit's file - DICE's console
  file has ground at all 15, its layout having no object there. The M-COM is `ForbidPathfinding` (its top is not
  floor - DICE's campaign files carve all 24 of theirs); the hole at its centre is its collision (no room for the
  soldier), not the flag, so clearing the flag would not help. The game's destination query fails there and units
  stop short. Planned: keep the floor under an AI order point that lies on a forbidden object, out to the walkable
  ground around it (the order point unchanged - as in DICE's console file, with which bots reach and arm M-COMs).
  No campaign order sits on an M-COM.
- **Destruction:** path data describes the intact level (DICE's and NavKit's). Objects carry `DisablePathfinding`:
  `PdtNever` (32,854 placed objects on the 15 levels), `PdtWhenAlive` (729: doors, gates, scripted walls - absent for
  path data; NavKit honours it), `PdtWhenDestroyed` (556: houses, factories, walkways, rope bridges - inferred: the
  runtime switches their path data off once destroyed), `PdtWhenPartDestroyed` (13); level settings
  `DestructibleLocalPathfindingParts`, `PathObjectCount`, `MaxLocalPathfindingObjects` point to runtime handling.
  Not yet checked that the switch-off works on NavKit's files (a play-test item). Openings made by destruction are
  not routes in either; precomputed "breach links" for OPFOR's bot layer are on the TODO list (OPFOR
  `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md`).
- **Still open:** sp_003_b (connectivity 93.3: a rocky gully whose rough terrain fails the slope test at 0.2 m almost
  everywhere); soldier spawns on small islands where NavKit has more than DICE (sp_008_b, sp_02, sp_003_b, sp_006,
  sp_01, a few each); ONS_MP_002's power-line pylons and a cliff top that roof pruning keeps (they stand beside each
  other at one height); the M-COM target rule (above); lonely nodes and slivers (above); vehicle path data; and play
  tests of the current builds (ladder links and destroyed houses included).

## Plan and status (2026-10-23)

1. **`.hpd` format – done.** Header, sector table, per-sector graph and runtime mesh fully decoded
   (spec §4); `hpdtool.py` parses every campaign file.
2. **Byte-exact rewrite – done.** `hpdtool.py roundtrip` / `meshtrip` re-emit every shipped file and
   all 7,944 sector meshes identically.
3. **Builder behaviour – done.** Spec §3: stages, the sampling grid, area cuts, graph rules,
   auto-seeding, the walkability rules (§3.7), structures and doors (§3.8), and the rules found on the
   other campaign levels (§3.9).
4. **Generator – runs on all 13 campaign levels and the Onslaught maps (`navbuild`, the shared package).**
   - Full pipeline: walkable surfaces from two in-game sampling runs (normal and high capsule) plus the
     level's objects (`levelobjects.py`), 100 m sectors (level `SectorOffsets`; without one, DICE's rule:
     one sector below the path data's lowest extent), 3 × 3 tiles of 50
     samples, single-layer 8-connected areas, outlines with 45° bridges, portals (B), border portals (C),
     neighbour links, route network (area, portal and shared border nodes; walkable edges up to 15 m;
     groups joined through string-pulled waypoints; no lone nodes), written as `pathdata.hpd`. Seeds:
     sector perimeter lines and soldier spawn points.
   - Rules added 2026-10-17 to 10-19 (details and measurements: spec §4.5):
     - **areas** are whole pieces of a tile joined by DICE's raw 0.6 m terrain step (`AREA_LINK`); no
       20 m bisection;
     - **edge sectors** (on the sector grid's minimum X / Z) start their tiles and their rectangle at
       their own edge (`EDGE_SECTOR_TILES`, `EDGE_SECTOR_RULE`);
     - on a level with DICE path data the ground is **bounded to DICE's extent** (`CLIP_TO_REFERENCE` -
       a bound for comparison, not a rule found in the level data; a new map keeps its sampling box);
     - **portals** stand on both of their areas; a piece whose target sees that side as its own interior
       becomes outline (`SYMMETRIC_PORTALS`, `ONE_WAY_PORTALS`);
     - **soldiers** standing in the level while it was sampled are not in the path data
       (`navwalk.CHARACTERS_ABSENT`);
     - each area's **height range** follows DICE's convention: lowest ground to highest ground + 1.52 m.
   - **In game:** sp_01's file loads and the AI walks on it (play test 2026-10-15). sp_004_b (play tests
     2026-10-19, same launch as DICE's file, only the `.hpd` differing): the file loads, the pathfinder
     finds paths (394 of 400 requests), but **the friendly squad does not follow them**, where with DICE's
     file it does. After a found path the game checks whether its last point equals the requested destination
     exactly, and further checks decide whether it is followed (`DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md` in Project OPFOR);
     measuring how NavKit's paths end, and which check they fail, is the next step. Leaving the level with NavKit's file also crashes at shutdown (a Kynapse block released after its memory manager was
     destroyed; not with DICE's file) - a separate open bug.
   - Accuracy against DICE's files (`ordercheck.py`: AI order / patrol positions on the areas, and the
     pairwise route check), 2026-10-15:

| Level | DICE-covered order positions also on NavKit's areas | Pairwise route check | Main route network (NavKit / DICE) |

| sp_01 | 618 / 633 (97.6 %) | 89.5 % | 639 / 607 |
| sp_02 | 241 / 260 (92.7 %) | 84.2 % | 313 / 362 |
| sp_03 | 343 / 353 (97.2 %) | 92.4 % | 374 / 232 |
