```py
        'all': save('all_tris.npy', [tris for _, tris in placed]),
        'forbid': save('forbid_tris.npy', [tris for p, tris in placed if flag(p, 0) and not flag(p, 1)]),
        'dynamic': save('dynamic_tris.npy', [tris for p, tris in placed if dynamic(p)]),
        'stairs': save('stair_tris.npy',
                       [tris for p, tris in placed if stair_like.search(p['bp'].rsplit('/', 1)[-1])]),
        'exclude': save('exclude_tris.npy', [tris for p, tris in placed if flag(p, 1)]),
        'exclude_foot': save('exclude_footprint_tris.npy', [footprint(p, tris) for p, tris in placed if flag(p, 1)]),
    }

    def object_box(index: int, placement: Placement, tris: Triangles) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """object_boxes.json's record of a placement with collision."""
        lo, hi = tris.reshape(-1, 3).min(0), tris.reshape(-1, 3).max(0)
        return {'index': index, 'bp': placement['bp'],
                'destructible': bool(placement['flags'] and placement['flags'][6]),
                'detailed': bool(placement['flags'] and placement['flags'][5]),
                'min': lo.round(2).tolist(), 'max': hi.round(2).tolist(),
                'footprint': round(float(np.prod(hi[[0, 2]] - lo[[0, 2]])), 1)}
    boxes = [object_box(index, placement, tris) for index, (placement, tris) in enumerate(placed)]
    hf_data = game.data(f'terrains/{level}/{level}.heightfield-000.res')
    hf = terrain.read(hf_data) if hf_data else None
    ladders = []
    for placement, tris in placed:
        if flag(placement, 7):
            lo, hi = tris.reshape(-1, 3).min(0), tris.reshape(-1, 3).max(0)
            box_lo = float(lo[1])
            if hf is not None:                        # the foot: where the ladder leaves the ground
                lo[1] = max(lo[1], float(hf.height((lo[0] + hi[0]) / 2, (lo[2] + hi[2]) / 2)))
            if hi[1] - lo[1] >= LADDER_MIN_HEIGHT:
                ladders.append({'bp': placement['bp'], 'lo': [round(float(v), 3) for v in lo],
                                'hi': [round(float(v), 3) for v in hi], 'box_lo_y': round(box_lo, 3)})
    for name, value in (('objects.json', objs), ('group_instances.json', groups), ('soldier_spawns.json', spawns),
                        ('order_points.json', orders), ('object_boxes.json', boxes), ('ladders.json', ladders)):
        with open(os.path.join(out, name), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            json.dump(value, f)
    print(f'{level}: {len(objs)} placed objects, {len(groups)} group members, {len(placed)} with collision')
    print('triangles: ' + ', '.join(f'{k} {v}' for k, v in counts.items()))
    print(f'ladders: {len(ladders)}')
    for why, bps in sorted(missing.items()):
        print(f'{why}: {len(bps)} blueprints, e.g. {sorted(bps)[:4]}')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('levelobjects1943', gui=False)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943.py`:

```py
r"""NavKit (big-endian): an audit of a BF1943 navigation build against its own level - the level's required positions
(capture areas, soldier and vehicle spawns, repair stations, AA guns), the build's internal consistency, and the
samples it was built from. Nothing here changes a build; every input is hashed into the report.

  navaudit1943.py masks <level> [--variants base,headroom,lips,water,ladders] [--stage normal|detailed|both]
      the build's walkable surfaces, recomputed exactly as navbuild.stage computes them (the check: the base run's
      count equals build.log's "walkable kept"), and once per rule with that rule turned off - the surfaces each rule
      changed. Written to work/levels/<level>/audit/masks/<stage>_<variant>.npz, with the SHA-256 of the samples and
      the build they were made from: a mask of other samples or another build is made again (and the audit refuses
      it), and only the checked build of the level's current preparation is audited (navkitjson1943.build_refusal).
      The detailed stage only when the build used a current 0.2 m pass. One variant (both stages, most of it
      the detailed stage) takes about 6 min on Wake Island and 2-3 GB of memory, all five about 30 min per level:
      run them one at a time.
  navaudit1943.py audit <level> [--json out.json]
      the checks (needs the masks' base runs; the rule-off runs for the rule section): work/levels/<level>/audit/
      audit.json and audit.md.

Settings the audit adds (not in the game's data, not in NavKit): OBJECTIVE_REACH, FLOOR_DY, LAYER_WINDOW (below),
and navaudit1943_checks' (its config.py) BOAT_REACH, VEHICLE_REACH, MOUNT_DROP, AIRBORNE and USABLE_SHARE.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
import navkitjson1943 as nj  # noqa: E402
import navsample  # noqa: E402
import soldier1943  # noqa: E402
from bfbc2core import game1943  # noqa: E402

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from navsample import Samples

type Log = Callable[[str], object]
type BoolArray = npt.NDArray[np.bool]

OBJECTIVE_REACH = 2.0     # m (horizontal): a required position passes when walkable ground on its own floor is this close.
                          # NavKit has no such value and the runtime's locate() takes its distance as a parameter
                          # (NAVIGATION_RUNTIME_DESIGN.md); 2 m is a soldier's arm's length plus his radius, chosen here
FLOOR_DY = 0.6            # m: a nav cell is on a position's floor when its ground is within this of the floor's height
LAYER_WINDOW = 3.0        # m: surfaces this far above or below a position's floor are its layers (check 5)
# each variant's rule turned off: navwalk.walkable's arguments, or an input left out
VARIANTS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    'base': {},
    'headroom': {'headroom_band': None},
    'lips': {'lip_width': 0},
    'water': {'water': None},
    'ladders': {'ladders': None},
}
WALKABLE_ARGS = ('headroom_band', 'lip_width')


sha256 = nj.sha256                 # (navkitjson1943: one chunked SHA-256 for every tool)


def load_samples(path: str) -> 'Samples':
    """A navsample version-1 file (navsample1943's output) as navsample.Samples, read with numpy: the same arrays
    navsample.load gives (normals / 127 as float32), in a fraction of its time and memory; as it does, an interrupted
    run keeps its finished columns. ValueError for a file that is not one (2026-10-31 fuzzing: struct.error on a cut
    header, a 2^31-column header that made tables of 16 GiB and more; review: an IndexError where a run stopped
    inside a column's records: navsample.load keeps the finished columns there, this read past the end)."""
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    if len(data) < navsample.HEADER.size:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: not a version-1 navsample file ({len(data)} bytes, shorter than its header)')
    magic, version, pitch, min_x, min_z, nx, nz, y_top, y_bottom, radius, cap_bottom, cap_top, ray_radius, _ = \
        navsample.HEADER.unpack_from(data, 0)
    if magic != b'ONS1' or version != 1:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: not a version-1 navsample file')
    if nx < 1 or nz < 1 or nx * nz > navsample.MAX_COLUMNS:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: a grid of {nx} x {nz} columns (at least 1 x 1, at most {navsample.MAX_COLUMNS})')
    column_count = nx * nz
    raw = np.frombuffer(data, np.uint8)
    pos = navsample.HEADER.size
    column_pos = np.empty(column_count, np.int64)      # each column's count byte
    counts = np.empty(column_count, np.int64)
    c = 0
    while c < column_count and pos < len(data):    # each column: a count byte, then 8-byte records
        n = data[pos]
        column_pos[c], counts[c] = pos, n
        pos += 1 + 8 * n
        c += 1
    if pos > len(data):                           # the run stopped inside the last column's records: as navsample.load,
        c -= 1                                    # keep the finished columns only
        pos = int(column_pos[c])
    counts[c:] = 0
    column_pos[c:] = pos
    start = np.zeros(column_count + 1, np.int64)
    np.cumsum(counts, out=start[1:])
    total = int(start[-1])
    within = np.arange(total, dtype=np.int64) - np.repeat(start[:-1], counts)   # each record's index in its column
    record_pos = np.repeat(column_pos + 1, counts) + 8 * within
    del within
    y = np.empty(total, np.float32)
    normal = np.empty((total, 3), np.float32)
    flags = np.empty(total, np.uint8)
    for first in range(0, total, 1 << 22):         # 4 M records at a time
        chunk = record_pos[first:first + (1 << 22)]
        records = raw[chunk[:, None] + np.arange(8)]
        y[first:first + len(chunk)] = records[:, :4].copy().view('<f4')[:, 0]
        normal[first:first + len(chunk)] = records[:, 4:7].view(np.int8) / np.float32(127.0)
        flags[first:first + len(chunk)] = records[:, 7]
    return navsample.Samples(pitch, min_x, min_z, nx, nz, y_top, y_bottom, radius, cap_bottom, cap_top, ray_radius,
                             start, y, normal, flags, None)


def current_build(lv: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """navkit.json, refused (NavKitError) unless the build on disk is the checked build of the current preparation
    (2026-10-30 review: the audit and its masks read whatever <level>.hpd was on disk)."""
    st = nj.read(lv)
    hpd = level_paths(lv)['hpd']
    why = nj.build_refusal(st, lv, hpd if os.path.isfile(hpd) else None)
    if why:
        raise nj.NavKitError(why)
    if not os.path.isfile(hpd):
        raise nj.NavKitError(f'{lv}: no build (missing {hpd}): navkit.py build {lv}')
    return st


def detailed_current(st: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether the build was made from a current 0.2 m pass (navkit.json's build_from names one)."""
    build_from = st.get('build_from') or {}
    return bool(build_from.get('samples_02_id') or build_from.get('samples_02'))


class Hashes:
    """The SHA-256 of a level's samples and build, each read once."""

    def __init__(self, lv: str) -> None:
        self.p: dict[str, str] = level_paths(lv)
        self.done: dict[str, str] = {}      # path -> its SHA-256

    def __call__(self, name: str) -> str:
        """The SHA-256 of 'hpd' (the build) or of a samples file by name."""
        path = self.p['hpd'] if name == 'hpd' else os.path.join(self.p['samples'], name)
        if path not in self.done:
            self.done[path] = sha256(path)
        return self.done[path]


def mask_stale(path: str, src: str, hashes: Hashes) -> str | None:
    """Why a mask file is not of the current samples and build (None when it is)."""
    try:
        mask_file = np.load(path)
        have = (str(mask_file['samples_sha256']), str(mask_file['hpd_sha256']))
    except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
        return f'{path}: unreadable ({e})'
    if have[0] != hashes(src):
        return f'{path}: made from other samples than {src}'
    if have[1] != hashes('hpd'):
        return f'{path}: made for another build'
    return None


def level_paths(lv: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The level's work folder and its parts: root, objects, samples, navkit, audit, hpd, settings."""
    root = game1943.level_work(lv)
    return {'root': root, 'objects': os.path.join(root, 'objects'), 'samples': os.path.join(root, 'samples'),
            'navkit': os.path.join(root, 'navkit'), 'audit': os.path.join(root, 'audit'),
            'hpd': os.path.join(root, 'navkit', f'{lv}.hpd'), 'settings': os.path.join(root, 'navkit', 'navkit.json')}


def stage_keep(lv: str, which: str, variant: str = 'base',
               normal_keep: 'tuple[Samples, BoolArray] | None' = None, log: Log = print
               ) -> 'tuple[Samples, BoolArray]':
    """The kept walkable surfaces (bool per surface) of one stage of a build, as navbuild.stage computes them for
    navkit.py build: which = 'normal' (the 0.8 m run) or 'detailed' (the 0.2 m run, seeded from the normal stage's
    kept ground in the detailed sectors - normal_keep). Mirrors navbuild.build / merge_detailed / stage up to
    navwalk.walkable, with the variant's rule turned off. Returns (samples, keep)."""
    import navbuild
    import navwalk
    from bfbc2core import water as water_mod
    paths = level_paths(lv)
    st = nj.read(lv)
    objects, samples_dir = paths['objects'], paths['samples']
    settings = soldier1943.SETTINGS                 # what navkit.py build passes
    opts = dict(VARIANTS[variant])
    # navwalk's rules as the build has them, the variant's turned off (until 2026-10-31 the module constants were
    # rewritten for the run and restored after it)
    rules: dict[str, Any] = {'headroom_band': settings.headroom_band, 'lip_width': navwalk.LIP_WIDTH}
    rules.update((k, opts.pop(k)) for k in WALKABLE_ARGS if k in opts)
    s = load_samples(os.path.join(samples_dir, 'samples.bin' if which == 'normal' else 'samples_02.bin'))
    high = load_samples(os.path.join(samples_dir, 'samples_high.bin' if which == 'normal' else 'samples_02_high.bin'))
    with open(os.path.join(objects, 'soldier_spawns.json'), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        seeds = json.load(f)
    with open(os.path.join(objects, 'ladders.json'), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        ladders = json.load(f)
    jumps_path = os.path.join(paths['navkit'], 'jump_links.json')      # navkit.py build adds them (jumplinks1943)
    if os.path.isfile(jumps_path):
        with open(jumps_path, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            ladders += json.load(f)
    if 'ladders' in opts:
        ladders = opts['ladders']
    water_path = os.path.join(objects, 'water_mesh.res')
    has_mesh = soldier1943.has_water(st) and os.path.isfile(water_path)
    mesh = water_mod.read_mesh(water_path) if has_mesh else None
    if 'water' in opts:
        mesh = None
    hand = {}                                       # navwalk.walkable's hand-made rules: deep water
    if mesh is not None:
        hand['force_unwalkable'] = navbuild.deep_water(s, mesh, soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH)
    seed_points = []
    if which == 'detailed':
        xoff, zoff = st['sector_offsets']
        dset = {(int(k[:2], 16), int(k[2:], 16)) for k in st.get('detailed_sectors') or ()}
        # the detailed stage is seeded from the normal one: masks() passes normal_keep
        normal_s, normal_kept = cast('tuple[Samples, BoolArray]', normal_keep)
        col = np.repeat(np.arange(normal_s.nx * normal_s.nz), np.diff(normal_s.start))
        for k in np.nonzero(normal_kept)[0]:
            c = col[k]
            x = normal_s.min_x + (c % normal_s.nx) * normal_s.pitch
            z = normal_s.min_z + (c // normal_s.nx) * normal_s.pitch
            if (int(math.floor(x / 100.0)) - xoff, int(math.floor(z / 100.0)) - zoff) in dset:
                seed_points.append((x, float(normal_s.y[k]), z))
    tris = np.load(os.path.join(objects, 'forbid_tris.npy'))
    dynamic = np.load(os.path.join(objects, 'dynamic_tris.npy'))
    exclude = np.load(os.path.join(objects, 'exclude_tris.npy'))
    exclude_footprint = np.load(os.path.join(objects, 'exclude_footprint_tris.npy'))
    t0 = time.time()
    # with return_gradients and return_stairs: (keep, gradient x, gradient z, stairs)
    keep, _gx, _gz, _stair = cast('tuple[BoolArray, Any, Any, Any]', navwalk.walkable(
        s, tris, slope=settings.slope_max, step=soldier1943.STEP, dynamic_tris=dynamic, high_capsule=high,
        return_gradients=True, return_stairs=True, narrow_capsule=None, stair_tris=None, exclude_tris=exclude,
        exclude_footprint_tris=exclude_footprint, extra_seeds=list(seeds) + seed_points, soldier_points=seeds,
        ladders=ladders, **hand, anchors=list(seeds) + seed_points, **rules))
    log(f'{lv} {which} {variant}: {len(s.y)} surfaces, {int(keep.sum())} walkable kept ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    return s, keep


def masks(lv: str, variants: Sequence[str], stages: Sequence[str], log: Log = print) -> None:
    """The masks of the checked build of the current preparation; a mask file there of other samples or another build
    is made again (2026-10-30 review: any file there was kept)."""
    st = current_build(lv)
    paths = level_paths(lv)
    out = os.path.join(paths['audit'], 'masks')
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    samples_dir = paths['samples']
    hashes = Hashes(lv)
    if 'detailed' in stages and not detailed_current(st):
        log(f'{lv}: the build has no 0.2 m samples of this preparation (its detailed sectors are built at 0.8 m): no '
            f'detailed masks')
        stages = [stage for stage in stages if stage != 'detailed']
    normal_base = None                              # (samples, keep) of the normal stage's base run
    for which in stages:
        src = 'samples.bin' if which == 'normal' else 'samples_02.bin'
        for variant in variants:
            path = os.path.join(out, f'{which}_{variant}.npz')
            if os.path.isfile(path):
                why = mask_stale(path, src, hashes)
                if why is None:
                    log(f'{path}: kept from an earlier run (of these samples and this build)')
                    continue
                log(f'{why}: made again')
            normal = None
            if which == 'detailed':
                if normal_base is None:
                    base_path = os.path.join(out, 'normal_base.npz')
                    base_current = os.path.isfile(base_path) and mask_stale(base_path, 'samples.bin', hashes) is None
                    base_file = np.load(base_path) if base_current else None
                    normal_s = load_samples(os.path.join(samples_dir, 'samples.bin'))
                    if base_file is not None:
                        normal_kept = base_file['keep']
                    else:
                        normal_kept = stage_keep(lv, 'normal', 'base', log=log)[1]
                    normal_base = (normal_s, normal_kept)
                normal = normal_base
            s, keep = stage_keep(lv, which, variant, normal_keep=normal, log=log)
            if which == 'normal' and variant == 'base':
                normal_base = (s, keep)
            np.savez_compressed(path, keep=keep, surfaces=len(s.y), samples=src,
                                samples_sha256=hashes(src), hpd_sha256=hashes('hpd'))
            log(f'wrote {path}')
            del s, keep


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='navaudit1943.py', description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='cmd', required=True)
    masks_cmd = sub.add_parser('masks')
    masks_cmd.add_argument('level')
    masks_cmd.add_argument('--variants', default=','.join(VARIANTS))
    masks_cmd.add_argument('--stage', default='both', choices=['normal', 'detailed', 'both'])
    audit_cmd = sub.add_parser('audit')
    audit_cmd.add_argument('level')
    audit_cmd.add_argument('--json')
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    if args.cmd == 'masks':
        chosen = [v for v in args.variants.split(',') if v]
        bad = [v for v in chosen if v not in VARIANTS]
        if bad:
            raise SystemExit(f'unknown variant(s) {bad}; known: {", ".join(VARIANTS)}')
        masks(args.level, chosen, ['normal', 'detailed'] if args.stage == 'both' else [args.stage])
    else:
        import navaudit1943_checks
        navaudit1943_checks.run(args.level, json_out=args.json)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('navaudit1943', gui=False)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/__init__.py`:

```py
"""The checks of navaudit1943.py (audit): a BF1943 build against its level's own data and its own consistency.

  1 required positions   capture areas (HotZone outlines), bases, soldier spawns and alternates, vehicle spawns
                         (ground, boats, aircraft, AA guns and mounted MGs), repair stations: walkable ground of the
                         build on the position's own floor within OBJECTIVE_REACH; a vehicle: walkable ground within
                         its own EntryRadius of one of its entry points (the blueprint's PlayerEntryComponentData),
                         else within VEHICLE_REACH (BOAT_REACH for a boat in the water); a base's marker is reported
                         only; the walkable share of each capture area
  2 reachability         every infantry spawn to every capture area and back on the route graph; every island
                         classified (main, vehicle-only zone, separate landmass, raised surface, gap candidate)
  3 file consistency     hpdcheck; portals two-way; border portals paired; one node per position; border-node owners;
                         crossings (touching ground of one floor on two islands)
  4 resolution           0.8 m and 0.2 m walkable ground compared in the detailed sectors
  5 layers               every surface within LAYER_WINDOW of each required position's floor: kept or not, and why
  6 water and shore      the wading band down to WATER_DEPTH; walkable ground under deeper water; jetties and piers
  7 rules                where each rule changed the kept ground (the rule-off masks), and near-misses within 20 %
  8 playable area        walkable ground inside and outside the combat area

The package (navaudit1943_checks.py until 2026-10-31, split along its checks; every name it had is here as
navaudit1943_checks.<name>, and run() stays here, so a test that replaces navaudit1943_checks.load is what run calls):
  config.py       the vehicle classes and the audit's own settings (BOAT_REACH, VEHICLE_REACH, MOUNT_DROP, AIRBORNE,
                  USABLE_SHARE, NEAR, CLUSTER_CELL)
  geometry.py     geometry helpers: polygons, distances, labelling, clusters
  grids.py        the level: one grid's samples and masks (Grid), why a surface is not kept, the build's graph (Nav)
  loading.py      load: the level, its build and masks (C); lookups by position
  positions.py    1 + 5: the required positions, their checks and layers, the capture areas' walkable share
  islands.py      2: the landmass, the islands' classes and reachability
  filecheck.py    3: file consistency and crossings
  pitches.py      4: resolution, 0.8 m against 0.2 m
  shore.py        6: water and shore
  rulemasks.py    7: where each rule changed the kept ground, near-misses, ladders
  combatarea.py   8: the playable area
  report.py       audit.md (markdown) and the JSON encoder
  __init__.py     run: every check, audit.json and audit.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast

import navaudit1943  # noqa: E402
import soldier1943  # noqa: E402

# the package's modules, re-exported: every name the module had
from .config import (  # noqa: F401
    AIRBORNE, AIRCRAFT, BOAT_REACH, BOATS, CLUSTER_CELL, GROUND, MOUNT_DROP, NEAR, PIER_RX, STATIONARY, USABLE_SHARE,
    VEHICLE_REACH)
from .geometry import clusters_xz, in_poly, label, poly_area, seg_dist  # noqa: F401
from .grids import Grid, Nav, why_not  # noqa: F401
from .loading import grid_at, load, objects_at, sector_of  # noqa: F401
from .positions import (  # noqa: F401
    capture_share, check_position, fine_entry, floor_of, nearest_cell_3d, required_positions, vehicle_entries)
from .islands import classify_islands, landmass, landmass_at, reachability, sea_level, vehicle_link  # noqa: F401
from .filecheck import consistency, crossings  # noqa: F401
from .pitches import ground_heights, resolution  # noqa: F401
from .shore import water_checks  # noqa: F401
from .rulemasks import _near, ladder_report, rules, step_near  # noqa: F401
from .combatarea import playable  # noqa: F401
from .report import _cols, _fmt, _json, markdown  # noqa: F401

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from navaudit1943 import Log


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ run

def run(lv: str, json_out: str | None = None, log: 'Log' = print) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every check on a level's checked build: writes audit.json (json_out, else the level's audit folder) and
    audit.md beside it, and returns the report."""
    t0 = time.time()
    ctx = load(lv, log)
    positions = required_positions(ctx)
    for position in positions:
        if position.get('capture_area') is not None:
            position['_poly'] = position['capture_area']
    checked = []
    for position in positions:
        res = check_position(ctx, position)
        if position['kind'] in ('flag', 'base', 'repair station', 'hot zone without a flag'):
            res['capture_share'] = capture_share(ctx, position)
        if position['kind'] == 'repair station' and res.get('capture_share'):
            # a repair station is its outline (vehicles are repaired inside it); its entity's point can sit above the
            # ground (Guadalcanal: 4.4 m) - reported, not the test
            share = cast('dict[str, Any]', res['capture_share'])     # checked just above
            res['marker_status'], res['marker_reason'] = res['status'], res.get('reason')
            res['status'] = share['status']
            res['reason'] = (f"outline {share['share']:.0%} walkable ({share['share_of']})"
                             if share['share'] is not None else 'outline: no ground')
        res['_poly'] = position.get('_poly')
        checked.append(res)
    log(f'{lv}: 1 positions ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    land = landmass(ctx)
    islands = classify_islands(ctx, land, checked)
    reach = reachability(ctx, checked)
    log(f'{lv}: 2 reachability ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    file_consistency = consistency(ctx)
    file_consistency['crossings'] = crossings(ctx)
    log(f'{lv}: 3 consistency ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    pitch_comparison = resolution(ctx)
    log(f'{lv}: 4 resolution ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    water = water_checks(ctx)
    log(f'{lv}: 6 water ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    rule_report = rules(ctx, checked)
    log(f'{lv}: 7 rules ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    play = playable(ctx)
    log(f'{lv}: 8 playable area ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    for res in checked:
        res.pop('_poly', None)
    soldier = {'radius': soldier1943.RADIUS, 'step': soldier1943.STEP, 'height': soldier1943.HEIGHT,
               'slope_max': soldier1943.SLOPE_MAX, 'water_depth': soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH}
    settings = {'OBJECTIVE_REACH': navaudit1943.OBJECTIVE_REACH, 'FLOOR_DY': navaudit1943.FLOOR_DY,
                'LAYER_WINDOW': navaudit1943.LAYER_WINDOW, 'BOAT_REACH': BOAT_REACH, 'USABLE_SHARE': USABLE_SHARE,
                'soldier': soldier}
    # the positions at the origin: required_positions (above) set them
    placeholders = ctx['placeholders']  # pyright: ignore[reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess]
    report = {'level': lv, 'date': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p'), 'inputs': ctx['inputs'],
              'settings': settings,
              'masks': {which: sorted(grid.variants) for which, grid in ctx['grids'].items()},
              'placeholders at the origin (not checked)': placeholders,
              '1 positions': checked, '2 reachability': reach, '2 islands': islands, '3 consistency': file_consistency,
              '4 resolution': pitch_comparison, '6 water': water, '7 rules': rule_report, '8 playable area': play}
    path = json_out or os.path.join(ctx['p']['audit'], 'audit.json')
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        json.dump(report, f, indent=1, default=_json)
    md = os.path.splitext(path)[0] + '.md'
    with open(md, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write(markdown(json.loads(json.dumps(report, default=_json))))
    log(f'{lv}: wrote {path} and {md} ({time.time() - t0:.0f} s)')
    return report

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/combatarea.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks, check 8: walkable ground inside and outside the combat area.

From the level's combat-area outlines (CombatAreaTriggerEntityData) and the build's 0.8 m cells: the land inside,
the share of it the build (and its main network) walks, and the walkable ground outside, clustered with its islands
and objects.
"""
import collections
import math
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

import soldier1943  # noqa: E402

from .geometry import clusters_xz, in_poly, poly_area
from .islands import sea_level
from .loading import objects_at

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .loading import AuditContext


def _cell_keys(x: npt.NDArray[np.floating], z: npt.NDArray[np.floating]) -> set[tuple[int, int]]:
    """The 0.8 m grid columns of points (x, z)."""
    return set(zip(np.round(x / 0.8).astype(int).tolist(), np.round(z / 0.8).astype(int).tolist()))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 8: playable area

def playable(ctx: 'AuditContext') -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The combat areas' land and walkable ground, and the walkable ground outside them."""
    lvl = ctx['lvl']
    nav_index = ctx['nav']
    nav = nav_index.nav
    combat = [(shape.kind, shape.points) for shape in lvl.shapes
              if lvl.entities[shape.entity].short_type == 'CombatAreaTriggerEntityData']
    areas = [points for kind, points in combat if kind == 'area']
    outer = [points for kind, points in combat if kind == 'outer area']
    out: dict[str, Any] = {'combat areas': len(areas), 'outer areas': len(outer)}
    if not areas:
        return out
    x, z = nav.cell_xz[:, 0], nav.cell_xz[:, 1]
    inside = np.zeros(len(x), bool)
    for poly in areas:
        inside |= in_poly(x, z, poly)
    hf = ctx['hf']
    lvl_sea = sea_level(ctx)
    # land a soldier can stand on: terrain at most WATER_DEPTH under the sea, on the build's own 0.8 m cell grid; the
    # walkable share counts each such column once (stacked floors and object tops are reported apart)
    land = set()
    for poly in areas:
        columns_x = np.arange(math.floor(poly[:, 0].min() / 0.8), math.ceil(poly[:, 0].max() / 0.8) + 1) * 0.8
        columns_z = np.arange(math.floor(poly[:, 2].min() / 0.8), math.ceil(poly[:, 2].max() / 0.8) + 1) * 0.8
        grid_x, grid_z = np.meshgrid(columns_x, columns_z)
        grid_x, grid_z = grid_x.ravel(), grid_z.ravel()
        ins = in_poly(grid_x, grid_z, poly) & (hf.height(grid_x, grid_z) >= lvl_sea - soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH)
        land.update(_cell_keys(grid_x[ins], grid_z[ins]))
    terrain_y = hf.height(x, z)
    on_ground = inside & (np.abs(nav.cell_y - terrain_y) < 0.3)
    walk_cols = _cell_keys(x[on_ground], z[on_ground])
    cells_isl = np.array([area.island for area in nav.areas])[nav.cell_area]
    main_cols = _cell_keys(x[on_ground & (cells_isl == nav_index.main)], z[on_ground & (cells_isl == nav_index.main)])
    out.update({
        'combat area m2': [round(poly_area(poly), 0) for poly in areas],
        'outer area m2': [round(poly_area(poly), 0) for poly in outer],
        'land inside (terrain down to the wading depth), m2': round(len(land) * 0.64, 0),
        'walkable ground inside (one per column), m2': round(len(walk_cols & land) * 0.64, 0),
        'main network ground inside, m2': round(len(main_cols & land) * 0.64, 0),
        'walkable share of the land inside': round(len(walk_cols & land) / len(land), 3) if land else None,
        'main network share of the land inside': round(len(main_cols & land) / len(land), 3) if land else None,
        'walkable on objects and stacked floors inside, m2': round(float((inside & ~on_ground).sum()) * 0.64, 0),
        'walkable outside, m2': round(float((~inside).sum()) * 0.64, 0),
        'walkable outside, clusters': clusters_xz(x[~inside], z[~inside], top=15),
    })
    if areas and outer and max(poly_area(poly) for poly in areas) < 0.05 * max(poly_area(poly) for poly in outer):
        out['note'] = ("the combat areas are small outlines inside the outer area (Coral Sea: four of about 11,500 m2, "
                       "at the carriers) - not the playable boundary; what they mean is not known")
    for cluster in out['walkable outside, clusters']:
        cx, cz = cluster['centre']
        sel = (~inside) & (np.abs(x - cx) < 50) & (np.abs(z - cz) < 50)
        if sel.any():
            cluster['islands'] = {int(k): int(v) for k, v in collections.Counter(cells_isl[sel]).most_common(3)}
            cluster['objects'] = objects_at(ctx, cx, float(np.median(nav.cell_y[sel])), cz, grow=5.0)
    return out

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/config.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks: the vehicle classes and the audit's own settings (not in the game's data, not in NavKit)."""
import re


GROUND = {'willys-mb', 'kurogane', 'm4-sherman', 'type97-chiha'}
BOATS = {'lcvp-landingcraft'}
AIRCRAFT = {'corsair', 'zero_fighter'}
STATIONARY = {'aa_bofors', '30cal_tripod', '30cal_windowmount'}
BOAT_REACH = 6.0          # m: an LCVP in the water is boarded from ground this close (it is about 11 m long)
VEHICLE_REACH = 4.0       # m (3-D, spawn point to walkable ground): the fallback for a vehicle whose blueprint gives no
                          # entry point (a vehicle is judged first by its PlayerEntryComponentData's EntryRadius, see
                          # vehicle_entries): half a vehicle plus a step, chosen here. Mounted guns without entry
                          # points use OBJECTIVE_REACH: the gunner stands at the gun
MOUNT_DROP = 2.0          # m: a mounted gun's gunner stands on a floor up to this far below the gun's spawn point
AIRBORNE = 3.0           # m: a spawn this far above its floor is in the air, not on the ground
USABLE_SHARE = 0.25       # a capture area with less of its land on the main network than this is listed
NEAR = 0.2                # near-miss band: within 20 % of a threshold
CLUSTER_CELL = 2.0        # m: rule-firing and difference clusters are grouped on this grid
PIER_RX = re.compile(r'pier|jetty|dock|landing_?stage|boardwalk|bridge', re.I)
```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/filecheck.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks, check 3: file consistency and crossings.

consistency reads the build's .hpd (hpdtool, kymesh) for one-way portals, nodes sharing a position, self-loop edges
and border-node owners, with hpdcheck's findings; crossings finds where touching walkable ground of one floor lies on
two islands and tests each place on the kept samples (a real break, or not joined on the ground).
"""
import collections
import math
from collections import deque
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast

import numpy as np

import soldier1943  # noqa: E402

from .loading import grid_at

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .loading import AuditContext


def _rounded_ends(portal: Any) -> set[tuple[float, float]]:
    """A portal's two ends on xz, rounded to 1 cm: the key a portal and its way back share."""
    return {(round(portal.p0[0], 2), round(portal.p0[2], 2)), (round(portal.p1[0], 2), round(portal.p1[2], 2))}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 3: consistency

def consistency(ctx: 'AuditContext') -> dict[str, Any]:
    """hpdcheck's findings, one-way portals, nodes sharing a position, self-loop edges and border-node owners."""
    import hpdcheck
    import hpdtool
    import kymesh
    paths = ctx['p']
    out: dict[str, Any] = {'hpdcheck': hpdcheck.check(paths['hpd'])}
    hpd = hpdtool.parse(open(paths['hpd'], 'rb').read())
    one_way, dup_nodes, self_loops = [], [], []
    owners = collections.defaultdict(list)          # border id -> [(sector, owns it: bit 16 clear)]
    for sector in hpd.sectors:
        mesh = kymesh.parse_mesh(sector.mesh)
        for area_index, area in enumerate(mesh.areas):
            for portal in area.portals:
                target = mesh.areas[portal.target] if 0 <= portal.target < len(mesh.areas) else None
                key = _rounded_ends(portal)
                back = target is not None and any(other.target == area_index and _rounded_ends(other) == key
                                                   for other in target.portals)
                if not back:
                    p0, p1 = portal.p0, portal.p1
                    one_way.append(f'sector {sector.id:04x} area {area_index} -> {portal.target} at '
                                   f'({p0[0]:.1f}, {p0[1]:.1f}, {p0[2]:.1f})-({p1[0]:.1f}, {p1[2]:.1f})')
        seen = collections.defaultdict(list)        # rounded position -> node ids
        for node in sector.nodes:
            seen[tuple(round(v, 3) for v in node.pos)].append(node.id & 0xFFFFFFFF)
            if node.id & 0x80000000:
                owners[node.id & 0xFFFFFFFF].append((sector.id, not (node.c >> 16) & 1))
        for pos, ids in seen.items():
            if len(set(ids)) > 1:
                dup_nodes.append(f'sector {sector.id:04x}: {len(ids)} nodes at {pos}')
        for edge in sector.edges:
            if edge.src == edge.dst:
                self_loops.append(f'sector {sector.id:04x}: edge {edge.src} -> itself')
    # border portals are not matched piece by piece: see crossings (each side splits them its own way)
    owner_counts = collections.Counter(sum(1 for _sector, owns in copies if owns) for copies in owners.values())
    owners_per_id = {str(k): v for k, v in sorted(owner_counts.items())}
    out.update({
        'portals one-way': one_way,
        'nodes sharing a position': dup_nodes, 'self-loop edges': self_loops,
        'border node owners (copies without bit 16, per border id)': owners_per_id,
        'border nodes': len(owners),
    })
    return out


def crossings(ctx: 'AuditContext') -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Where walkable ground of one floor touches another area, can the route graph get across? Build cells side by
    side (0.8 m, within the step) in different areas whose areas lie on different islands; each such place is then
    tested on the kept samples: a flood under the build's own step (0.37 m on 0.2 m grids, LINK_STEP 0.6 m on 0.8 m)
    from the smaller island's nodes that reaches ground under the other island's nodes is a real break (a seam or
    portal the graph does not cross); otherwise the two sides are not joined on the ground either (a pocket the 0.8 m
    seeds kept that the 0.2 m samples wall off, or the reader giving a node-less area a neighbour's island).
    The exact-match count of unpaired border portals (consistency) is no test: each side places its border portals 1.2
    (0.8 m) or 0.3 m (0.2 m) inside its own edge and splits them differently - DICE's files show 21-32 % uncovered."""
    nav_index = ctx['nav']
    nav = nav_index.nav
    area_isl = np.array([area.island for area in nav.areas])
    area_sec = np.array([area.sector for area in nav.areas])
    cells_at = collections.defaultdict(list)        # 0.8 m grid position -> cells
    for k, (x, z) in enumerate(nav.cell_xz):
        cells_at[(int(round(x / 0.8)), int(round(z / 0.8)))].append(k)
    # (island, island) -> the touching cell pairs: how many, whether across a sector seam, where
    groups: collections.defaultdict[tuple[int, ...], dict[str, Any]] = collections.defaultdict(
        lambda: {'pairs': 0, 'seam': False, 'xyz': []})
    for (i, j), cells in cells_at.items():
        for di, dj in ((1, 0), (0, 1)):
            for k in cells:
                for m in cells_at.get((i + di, j + dj), ()):
                    island_a, island_b = area_isl[nav.cell_area[k]], area_isl[nav.cell_area[m]]
                    if island_a == island_b or abs(nav.cell_y[k] - nav.cell_y[m]) > soldier1943.STEP:
                        continue
                    group = groups[tuple(sorted((int(island_a), int(island_b))))]
                    group['pairs'] += 1
                    group['seam'] |= bool(area_sec[nav.cell_area[k]] != area_sec[nav.cell_area[m]])
                    group['xyz'].append((float(nav.cell_xz[k, 0]), float(nav.cell_y[k]), float(nav.cell_xz[k, 1])))
    ground = nav_index.node_ground
    out = []
    for isl, group in groups.items():
        centre = np.mean(group['xyz'], 0)
        small, big = sorted(isl, key=lambda i: nav.islands[i].nodes)
        grid = grid_at(ctx, centre[0], centre[2])
        s, keep = grid.s, grid.keep
        step = soldier1943.STEP if s.pitch < 0.5 else 0.6

        def surf(x: float, y: float, z: float) -> int | None:
            """The kept surface of the column at (x, z) nearest y, within 0.5 m."""
            column = grid.col(x, z)
            if column is None:
                return None
            near_y = [k for k in grid.surfaces(column) if keep[k] and abs(s.y[k] - y) < 0.5]
            return min(near_y, key=lambda k: abs(s.y[k] - y)) if near_y else None

        def near(island: int) -> list[np.intp]:
            """The island's route nodes within 30 m of the place."""
            return [k for k in np.nonzero(nav.node_island == island)[0]
                    if math.hypot(nav.node_pos[k, 0] - centre[0], nav.node_pos[k, 2] - centre[2]) < 30]
        starts = {surf(nav.node_pos[k, 0], ground[k], nav.node_pos[k, 2]) for k in near(small)} - {None}
        goals = {surf(nav.node_pos[k, 0], ground[k], nav.node_pos[k, 2]) for k in near(big)} - {None}
        seen, queue, hit = set(starts), deque(starts), False
        col_of = grid.col_of()
        while queue and not hit:
            k = queue.popleft()
            column = cast(int, col_of[k])           # one surface's column
            i, j = column % s.nx, column // s.nx
            for di in (-1, 0, 1):
                for dj in (-1, 0, 1):
                    ni, nj = i + di, j + dj
                    if not (di or dj) or not (0 <= ni < s.nx and 0 <= nj < s.nz):
                        continue
                    if math.hypot(s.min_x + ni * s.pitch - centre[0], s.min_z + nj * s.pitch - centre[2]) > 30:
                        continue
                    for n in grid.surfaces(nj * s.nx + ni):
                        if keep[n] and n not in seen and abs(s.y[n] - s.y[k]) <= step:
                            seen.add(n)
                            queue.append(n)
                            hit |= n in goals
        out.append({'centre': [round(float(v), 1) for v in centre], 'cell_pairs': group['pairs'],
                    'across_a_seam': group['seam'], 'grid': grid.label, 'islands': [int(i) for i in isl],
                    'island_nodes': [nav.islands[i].nodes for i in isl], 'main': nav_index.main in isl,
                    'verdict': 'real break' if hit else 'not joined on the ground'})
    out.sort(key=lambda record: (record['verdict'] != 'real break', -min(record['island_nodes'])))
    return out

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/geometry.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks: geometry helpers (polygons, distances, labelling, clusters).

Inputs are numpy arrays of world positions on the horizontal plane (x, z); outputs are masks, distances, labels and
the cluster records the report lists.
"""
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

from .config import CLUSTER_CELL

type FloatArray = npt.NDArray[np.float64]
type Cluster = dict[str, Any]       # {'centre': [x, z], 'points', 'cells', 'bbox': [x0, z0, x1, z1]}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ geometry helpers

def in_poly(px: npt.ArrayLike, pz: npt.ArrayLike, poly: npt.NDArray[np.floating]) -> npt.NDArray[np.bool]:
    """Even-odd point-in-polygon on xz for arrays of points; poly (n, >=2) with x, z in columns 0 and -1."""
    px, pz = np.asarray(px, float), np.asarray(pz, float)
    x, z = poly[:, 0], poly[:, -1]
    x_next, z_next = np.roll(x, -1), np.roll(z, -1)
    out = np.zeros(px.shape, bool)
    # each edge (xa, za) -> (xb, zb); a horizontal edge crosses no ray
    for xa, za, xb, zb in zip(x, z, x_next, z_next):
        if za == zb:
            continue
        straddles = (za > pz) != (zb > pz)
        x_cross = xa + (pz - za) * (xb - xa) / (zb - za)
        out ^= straddles & (px < x_cross)
    return out


def poly_area(poly: npt.NDArray[np.floating]) -> float:
    """The polygon's area on xz (the shoelace formula); x, z in columns 0 and -1."""
    x, z = poly[:, 0], poly[:, -1]
    return 0.5 * abs(float(np.dot(x, np.roll(z, -1)) - np.dot(z, np.roll(x, -1))))


def seg_dist(px: float, pz: float, a: FloatArray, b: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
    """Distances from (px, pz) to segments a -> b ((n, 2) arrays on xz)."""
    d = b - a                              # each segment's direction
    length_sq = (d ** 2).sum(1)
    # t: the nearest point's position along each segment, 0 at a and 1 at b
    t = np.clip(((px - a[:, 0]) * d[:, 0] + (pz - a[:, 1]) * d[:, 1]) / np.maximum(length_sq, 1e-12), 0, 1)
    return np.hypot(a[:, 0] + t * d[:, 0] - px, a[:, 1] + t * d[:, 1] - pz)


def label(mask: npt.NDArray[np.bool]) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.int_], int]:
    """8-connected components of a 2-D bool array: (labels with -1 off the mask, count). Label propagation with
    pointer jumping; no scipy here."""
    h, w = mask.shape
    labels = np.where(mask, np.arange(h * w).reshape(h, w), h * w)
    big = h * w                            # the label of cells off the mask
    for _ in range(100000):
        lowest = labels.copy()
        padded = np.pad(labels, 1, constant_values=big)
        for dj in (-1, 0, 1):
            for di in (-1, 0, 1):
                if di or dj:
                    np.minimum(lowest, padded[1 + dj:1 + dj + h, 1 + di:1 + di + w], out=lowest)
        lowest = np.where(mask, lowest, big)
        flat = lowest.ravel()
        # pointer jumping: follow each label to its own label's label
        for _ in range(4):
            ok = flat < big
            flat[ok] = flat[flat[ok]]
        lowest = flat.reshape(h, w)
        if np.array_equal(lowest, labels):
            break
        labels = lowest
    roots, inverse = np.unique(labels[mask], return_inverse=True)
    out = np.full((h, w), -1, int)
    out[mask] = inverse
    return out, len(roots)


def clusters_xz(x: npt.ArrayLike, z: npt.ArrayLike, weight: object = None, cell: float = CLUSTER_CELL,
                top: int | None = None) -> list[Cluster]:
    """Points grouped into 8-connected clusters on a cell grid: [{'centre', 'cells', 'points', 'bbox'}], largest
    first. (weight is not used.)"""
    x, z = np.asarray(x, float), np.asarray(z, float)
    if not len(x):
        return []
    i = np.floor(x / cell).astype(int)
    j = np.floor(z / cell).astype(int)
    i0, j0 = i.min(), j.min()
    width, height = i.max() - i0 + 1, j.max() - j0 + 1
    mask = np.zeros((height, width), bool)
    mask[j - j0, i - i0] = True
    labels, count = label(mask)
    point_label = labels[j - j0, i - i0]
    points = np.bincount(point_label, minlength=count)
    sum_x, sum_z = np.bincount(point_label, x, count), np.bincount(point_label, z, count)
    cells = np.bincount(labels[labels >= 0], minlength=count)
    lo_x, lo_z = np.full(count, np.inf), np.full(count, np.inf)
    hi_x, hi_z = np.full(count, -np.inf), np.full(count, -np.inf)
    np.minimum.at(lo_x, point_label, x)
    np.minimum.at(lo_z, point_label, z)
    np.maximum.at(hi_x, point_label, x)
    np.maximum.at(hi_z, point_label, z)
    order = np.argsort(-points, kind='stable')
    if top:
        order = order[:top]
    return [{'centre': [round(float(sum_x[k] / points[k]), 1), round(float(sum_z[k] / points[k]), 1)],
             'points': int(points[k]), 'cells': int(cells[k]),
             'bbox': [round(float(lo_x[k]), 1), round(float(lo_z[k]), 1),
                      round(float(hi_x[k]), 1), round(float(hi_z[k]), 1)]} for k in order]

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/grids.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks: the level - one grid's samples and masks (Grid), why a surface is not kept, the build's
graph (Nav).

Grid wraps one sampling run (navsample.Samples) with the build's kept mask, the terrain and the water over every
column; Nav wraps the build as navdata reads it (areas with exact outlines, cells, route graph) for the checks'
lookups: the area near a point, the route node near a point, what a node reaches.
"""
import collections
import math
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast, overload

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

import navaudit1943  # noqa: E402
import soldier1943  # noqa: E402

from .geometry import seg_dist

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from bfbc2core.materialmap1943 import MaterialMap
    from bfbc2core.navdata import NavData
    from bfbc2core.terrain import Heightfield
    from navsample import Samples

type BoolArray = npt.NDArray[np.bool]
type Index = int | np.integer[Any]        # a column or surface index, plain or numpy
type WaterMesh = tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float32], npt.NDArray[np.uint32]]   # (vertices, triangles)
type BuildCells = list[tuple[int, float, npt.NDArray[np.int32], npt.NDArray[np.int32], npt.NDArray[np.float32]]]
type AreaHit = tuple[float, int, float]     # (distance, area index, the area's ground height there)
type SurfaceRecord = dict[str, Any]         # one surface of Grid.describe's column


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ the level

class Grid:
    """One sampling run with its kept mask: surfaces per column, the build's verdict, water over every column."""

    def __init__(self, s: 'Samples', keep: BoolArray, hf: 'Heightfield', water: WaterMesh | None,
                 label_: str) -> None:
        import navbuild
        self.s, self.keep, self.hf, self.label = s, keep, hf, label_
        if water is not None:
            self.top = navbuild.water_tops(s, water[0], water[1]).astype(np.float32)
        else:
            self.top = np.full(s.nx * s.nz, -np.inf, np.float32)
        self.variants: dict[str, BoolArray] = {}        # rule name -> the kept mask with that rule off

    def col(self, x: float, z: float) -> int | None:
        """The column nearest (x, z), None off the grid."""
        s = self.s
        i, j = int(round((x - s.min_x) / s.pitch)), int(round((z - s.min_z) / s.pitch))
        if not (0 <= i < s.nx and 0 <= j < s.nz):
            return None
        return j * s.nx + i

    def centre(self, c: Index) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """Column c's (x, z)."""
        s = self.s
        return s.min_x + (c % s.nx) * s.pitch, s.min_z + (c // s.nx) * s.pitch

    def surfaces(self, c: Index) -> range:
        """Column c's surface indices, top down."""
        return range(self.s.start[c], self.s.start[c + 1])

    def col_of(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.int_]:
        """Every surface's column (computed once)."""
        if not hasattr(self, '_col_of'):
            self._col_of = np.repeat(np.arange(self.s.nx * self.s.nz), np.diff(self.s.start))
        return self._col_of

    def describe(self, c: Index, lo: float = -1e9, hi: float = 1e9, mm: 'MaterialMap | None' = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The column's surfaces between heights lo and hi, top down: the sample columns of the report."""
        s = self.s
        x, z = self.centre(c)
        terrain_y = float(self.hf.height(x, z))
        water_top = float(self.top[c])
        indices = list(self.surfaces(c))
        out = []
        for position, n in enumerate(indices):
            y = float(s.y[n])
            if not (lo <= y <= hi):
                continue
            above = float(s.y[indices[position - 1]]) if position > 0 else None     # surfaces are stored top down
            slope_deg = math.degrees(math.acos(max(-1.0, min(1.0, float(s.normal[n, 1])))))
            on_terrain = abs(y - terrain_y) < 0.06
            surface = {'y': round(y, 2), 'slope_deg': round(slope_deg, 1), 'blocked': bool(s.flags[n] & 1),
                       'kept': bool(self.keep[n]), 'clearance': None if above is None else round(above - y, 2),
                       'terrain': on_terrain,
                       'below_terrain': round(terrain_y - y, 2) if y < terrain_y - 0.06 else 0.0,
                       'water_depth': round(water_top - y, 2) if water_top > -1e30 and water_top > y else 0.0}
            if on_terrain and mm is not None:
                surface['material'] = mm.name_at(x, z)[0]
            changed_by = [rule for rule, rule_keep in self.variants.items() if rule_keep[n] != self.keep[n]]
            if changed_by:
                surface['rules'] = {rule: ('removed it' if self.variants[rule][n] else 'added it')
                                    for rule in changed_by}
            surface['why_not'] = None if surface['kept'] else why_not(surface)
            out.append(surface)
        return {'grid': self.label, 'column': [round(x, 2), round(z, 2)], 'terrain_y': round(terrain_y, 2),
                'water_top': None if water_top < -1e30 else round(water_top, 2), 'surfaces': out}


def why_not(surface: SurfaceRecord) -> list[str]:
    """Why a surface of Grid.describe was not kept: the surface tests it fails, else the flood's."""
    reasons = []
    if surface['blocked']:
        reasons.append('capsule blocked')
    if surface['slope_deg'] > soldier1943.SLOPE_MAX + 0.6:
        reasons.append(f'steeper than {soldier1943.SLOPE_MAX:g} deg')
    if surface['clearance'] is not None and 0.5 <= surface['clearance'] < soldier1943.HEIGHT:
        reasons.append('headroom under 1.8 m')
    if surface['water_depth'] > soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH:
        reasons.append('deeper than 1.4 m under water')
    if surface['below_terrain'] > 0.5:
        reasons.append('more than 0.5 m under the terrain')
    for rule, what in (surface.get('rules') or {}).items():
        if what == 'removed it':
            reasons.append(f'{rule} rule removed it')
    return reasons or ['passes the surface tests; not reached by the flood from the seeds (or an object rule: forbid, '
                       'exclude, dynamic)']


class Nav:
    """The build: areas with exact outlines (point in area, distance to area), cells, route graph."""

    def __init__(self, nav: 'NavData', exact: BuildCells | None = None) -> None:
        self.nav = nav
        # the build's own cells (navbuild's <level>.cells.npz) per area: x, z, ground height - exact, where the
        # reader's cells (navdata, 0.8 m, heights from the nearest outline point) can be metres off on rock and slopes
        # (Coral Sea's South Base flag, 2026-10-26)
        self.exact: list[tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float64], npt.NDArray[np.float64], npt.NDArray[np.float64]]] | None
        self.exact = None
        if exact is not None and len(exact) == len(nav.areas):
            self.exact = [(np.asarray(cell_i, float) * pitch, np.asarray(cell_j, float) * pitch,
                           np.asarray(cell_y, float))
                          for _sector, pitch, cell_i, cell_j, cell_y in exact]
        # per area: its outline, portal and border segments ((n, 2, 3) array) and their box (x0, z0, x1, z1)
        self.segs: list[npt.NDArray[np.float64]] = []
        self.box: list[tuple[float, float, float, float] | None] = []
        for area in nav.areas:
            segments = []
            for line in area.outline:
                line = np.asarray(line, float)
                for k in range(len(line) - 1):
                    segments.append((line[k], line[k + 1]))
            for p0, p1, *_ in area.portals:
                segments.append((np.asarray(p0, float), np.asarray(p1, float)))
            for p0, p1 in area.borders:
                segments.append((np.asarray(p0, float), np.asarray(p1, float)))
            seg_array = np.array(segments, float).reshape(-1, 2, 3) if segments else np.zeros((0, 2, 3))
            self.segs.append(seg_array)
            if len(seg_array):
                self.box.append((seg_array[:, :, 0].min(), seg_array[:, :, 2].min(),
                                 seg_array[:, :, 0].max(), seg_array[:, :, 2].max()))
            else:
                self.box.append(None)
        # areas by 10 m bucket of their box
        self.bucket: collections.defaultdict[tuple[int, int], list[int]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for k, box in enumerate(self.box):
            if box is None:
                continue
            for i in range(int(box[0] // 10), int(box[2] // 10) + 1):
                for j in range(int(box[1] // 10), int(box[3] // 10) + 1):
                    self.bucket[(i, j)].append(k)
        # the reader's cells by 0.8 m grid position
        self.cell_key: collections.defaultdict[tuple[int, int], list[int]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
        cell = 0.8
        for n, (x, z) in enumerate(nav.cell_xz):
            self.cell_key[(int(round(x / cell)), int(round(z / cell)))].append(n)
        main = max(range(len(nav.islands)), key=lambda i: nav.islands[i].nodes) if nav.islands else -1
        self.main = main
        # the route graph as compressed rows: node u's successors are fwd_dst[fwd_start[u]:fwd_start[u + 1]]
        node_count = len(nav.node_pos)
        edges = nav.edges
        order = np.argsort(edges[:, 0], kind='stable')
        self.fwd_dst = edges[order, 1]
        self.fwd_start = np.searchsorted(edges[order, 0], np.arange(node_count + 1))
        order = np.argsort(edges[:, 1], kind='stable')
        self.bwd_dst = edges[order, 0]
        self.bwd_start = np.searchsorted(edges[order, 1], np.arange(node_count + 1))
        self.node_ground = nav.node_pos[:, 1] - soldier1943.HEIGHT / 2

    def area_height(self, k: int, x: float, z: float) -> float:
        """The area's ground height near (x, z): its nearest cell's (the build's own cells where the build has its
        cells file, else the reader's 0.8 m cells), else its nearest outline point's."""
        if self.exact is not None and len(self.exact[k][0]):
            cell_x, cell_z, cell_y = self.exact[k]
            return float(cell_y[int(np.argmin((cell_x - x) ** 2 + (cell_z - z) ** 2))])
        best = None                                         # (squared distance, height)
        for di in range(-3, 4):
            for dj in range(-3, 4):
                for n in self.cell_key.get((int(round(x / 0.8)) + di, int(round(z / 0.8)) + dj), ()):
                    if self.nav.cell_area[n] == k:
                        dist_sq = (self.nav.cell_xz[n, 0] - x) ** 2 + (self.nav.cell_xz[n, 1] - z) ** 2
                        if best is None or dist_sq < best[0]:
                            best = (dist_sq, float(self.nav.cell_y[n]))
        if best is not None:
            return best[1]
        points = self.segs[k].reshape(-1, 3)
        nearest = np.argmin((points[:, 0] - x) ** 2 + (points[:, 2] - z) ** 2)
        return float(points[nearest, 1]) - soldier1943.HEIGHT / 2

    def candidates(self, x: float, z: float, r: float) -> set[int]:
        """The areas whose 10 m buckets lie within r of (x, z)."""
        out = set()
        for i in range(int((x - r) // 10), int((x + r) // 10) + 1):
            for j in range(int((z - r) // 10), int((z + r) // 10) + 1):
                out.update(self.bucket.get((i, j), ()))
        return out

    def locate(self, x: float, z: float, floor_y: float, r: float = 30.0,
               dy: float | None = None) -> tuple[AreaHit | None, AreaHit | None]:
        """Areas near (x, z): the nearest on the floor (|area ground - floor_y| <= dy) and the nearest on any floor.
        Distance 0 inside the area's outline."""
        dy = navaudit1943.FLOOR_DY if dy is None else dy
        same = any_floor = None
        for k in self.candidates(x, z, r):
            segments = self.segs[k]
            # an area without segments has no box, and so no bucket: candidates() never gives it
            box = cast('tuple[float, float, float, float]', self.box[k])
            if x < box[0] - r or x > box[2] + r or z < box[1] - r or z > box[3] + r:
                continue
            seg_a, seg_b = segments[:, 0][:, [0, 2]], segments[:, 1][:, [0, 2]]   # each segment's ends on xz
            straddles = (seg_a[:, 1] > z) != (seg_b[:, 1] > z)
            with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
                x_cross = seg_a[:, 0] + (z - seg_a[:, 1]) * (seg_b[:, 0] - seg_a[:, 0]) / (seg_b[:, 1] - seg_a[:, 1])
            inside = bool(np.count_nonzero(straddles & (x < x_cross)) % 2)
            distance = 0.0 if inside else float(seg_dist(x, z, seg_a, seg_b).min())
            if distance > r:
                continue
            ground = self.area_height(k, x, z)
            hit = (distance, k, ground)
            if any_floor is None or (distance, abs(ground - floor_y)) < (any_floor[0], abs(any_floor[2] - floor_y)):
                any_floor = hit
            if abs(ground - floor_y) <= dy and (same is None or distance < same[0]):
                same = hit
        return same, any_floor

    @overload
    def area_info(self, rec: AreaHit, floor_y: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
    @overload
    def area_info(self, rec: None, floor_y: float | None = None) -> None: ...
    @overload
    def area_info(self, rec: AreaHit | None, floor_y: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None: ...

    def area_info(self, rec: AreaHit | None, floor_y: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        """The report's record of an area locate() found (None for none)."""
        if rec is None:
            return None
        distance, k, ground = rec
        area = self.nav.areas[k]
        island = area.island
        return {'distance': round(distance, 2), 'area': k, 'sector': f'{area.sector:04x}', 'layer': area.layer,
                'pitch': round(area.pitch, 2), 'ground_y': round(ground, 2),
                'dy': None if floor_y is None else round(ground - floor_y, 2), 'island': island,
                'island_nodes': self.nav.islands[island].nodes if island >= 0 else None, 'main': island == self.main}

    def join(self, x: float, z: float, ground_y: float, island: int | None = None, r: float = 15.0,
             dy: float = 2.0) -> int | None:
        """The nearest route node on the ground's floor (and on the island, when given)."""
        nodes = self.nav.node_pos
        distance = np.hypot(nodes[:, 0] - x, nodes[:, 2] - z)
        ok = (distance <= r) & (np.abs(self.node_ground - ground_y) <= dy)
        if island is not None:
            on_island = ok & (self.nav.node_island == island)
            if on_island.any():
                ok = on_island
        if not ok.any():
            return None
        return int(np.argmin(np.where(ok, distance, np.inf)))

    def reach(self, start: int, backward: bool = False) -> BoolArray:
        """The nodes reachable from start (along the edges, or against them with backward)."""
        node_count = len(self.nav.node_pos)
        seen = np.zeros(node_count, bool)
        seen[start] = True
        row_start, successors = (self.bwd_start, self.bwd_dst) if backward else (self.fwd_start, self.fwd_dst)
        stack = [start]
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            for nxt in successors[row_start[node]:row_start[node + 1]]:
                if not seen[nxt]:
                    seen[nxt] = True
                    stack.append(int(nxt))
        return seen

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/islands.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks, check 2: the landmass, the islands' classes and reachability.

landmass labels the land a soldier can wade to; classify_islands names each island of the build (main, vehicle-only
zone, separate landmass, raised surface, gap candidate) from where its cells lie; reachability floods the route graph
from every infantry spawn to every capture area and back.
"""
import collections
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

import navaudit1943  # noqa: E402
import soldier1943  # noqa: E402

from .config import BOAT_REACH
from .geometry import in_poly, label
from .loading import objects_at

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .loading import AuditContext
    from .positions import CheckResult

type Landmass = tuple[npt.NDArray[np.int_], float, float, float]    # (label grid, x0, z0, cell)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 2: reachability

def landmass(ctx: 'AuditContext', cell: float = 4.0) -> Landmass:
    """Land a soldier can wade to: terrain at most WATER_DEPTH under the water, labelled into connected pieces on a
    4 m grid. Returns (label grid, x0, z0, cell)."""
    hf = ctx['hf']
    x0, z0 = float(hf.min[0]), float(hf.min[2])
    n = int((hf.max[0] - hf.min[0]) / cell)
    grid_x, grid_z = np.meshgrid(x0 + (np.arange(n) + 0.5) * cell, z0 + (np.arange(n) + 0.5) * cell)
    terrain_y = hf.height(grid_x, grid_z)
    level = sea_level(ctx)
    land = terrain_y >= level - soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH
    labels, _count = label(land)
    return labels, x0, z0, cell


def sea_level(ctx: 'AuditContext') -> float:
    """The water mesh's median height; without one, navkit.json's (soldier1943.sea_level)."""
    water = ctx['water']
    if water is None or not len(water[0]):
        # no water mesh: navkit.json's sea level, or without water the exporters' (2026-10-30: float(None) raised, then
        # -1e9 put the audit's sea elsewhere than the export's)
        return soldier1943.sea_level(ctx['st'], ctx['hf'])
    return float(np.median(water[0][:, 1]))


def landmass_at(landmass_: Landmass, x: npt.ArrayLike, z: npt.ArrayLike) -> npt.NDArray[np.int_]:
    """The landmass label at each (x, z)."""
    labels, x0, z0, cell = landmass_
    i = np.clip(((np.asarray(x) - x0) / cell).astype(int), 0, labels.shape[1] - 1)
    j = np.clip(((np.asarray(z) - z0) / cell).astype(int), 0, labels.shape[0] - 1)
    return labels[j, i]


def classify_islands(ctx: 'AuditContext', landmass_: Landmass, positions: list['CheckResult']) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Every island of the build with its kind (main, vehicle-only zone, separate landmass, raised surface, gap
    candidate), its extent and the required positions on it."""
    nav_index = ctx['nav']
    nav = nav_index.nav
    hf = ctx['hf']
    cells_isl = np.array([area.island for area in nav.areas])[nav.cell_area]
    cell_terrain = hf.height(nav.cell_xz[:, 0], nav.cell_xz[:, 1])
    cell_landmass = landmass_at(landmass_, nav.cell_xz[:, 0], nav.cell_xz[:, 1])
    main_landmass = collections.Counter(cell_landmass[cells_isl == nav_index.main]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    level = sea_level(ctx)
    required = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for position in positions:
        area = position.get('nearest_same_floor')
        reach = max(navaudit1943.OBJECTIVE_REACH, BOAT_REACH if position.get('afloat') else 0)
        if area and area['distance'] <= reach and area['island'] >= 0:
            required[area['island']].append(f"{position['kind']}: {position['name']}")
    node_pos = nav.node_pos
    node_terrain = hf.height(node_pos[:, 0], node_pos[:, 2])
    node_landmass = landmass_at(landmass_, node_pos[:, 0], node_pos[:, 2])
    out = []
    for k, island in enumerate(nav.islands):
        sel = cells_isl == k
        if sel.any():
            xs, zs, ys = nav.cell_xz[sel, 0], nav.cell_xz[sel, 1], nav.cell_y[sel]
            terrain_y, landmass_label = cell_terrain[sel], cell_landmass[sel]
        else:
            # areas too narrow to hold a 0.8 m cell: the island's route nodes stand for it
            nodes = nav.node_island == k
            xs, zs, ys = node_pos[nodes, 0], node_pos[nodes, 2], nav_index.node_ground[nodes]
            terrain_y, landmass_label = node_terrain[nodes], node_landmass[nodes]
        above_terrain = ys - terrain_y
        on_main_land = float((landmass_label == main_landmass).mean())
        over_water = float((terrain_y < level - soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH).mean())
        raised = float((above_terrain > 1.5).mean())
        record: dict[str, Any] = dict(island=k, nodes=island.nodes, cells=int(sel.sum()),
                                      area_m2=round(float(sel.sum()) * 0.64, 0),
                                      centre=[round(float(xs.mean()), 1), round(float(ys.mean()), 1),
                                              round(float(zs.mean()), 1)],
                                      bbox=[round(float(xs.min()), 1), round(float(zs.min()), 1),
                                            round(float(xs.max()), 1), round(float(zs.max()), 1)],
                                      on_main_landmass=round(on_main_land, 2), over_deep_water=round(over_water, 2),
                                      raised_share=round(raised, 2),
                                      mean_height_above_terrain=round(float(above_terrain.mean()), 1),
                                      required=required.get(k, []))
        cx, cy, cz = record['centre']
        record['objects'] = objects_at(ctx, cx, cy, cz, grow=2.0)
        if k == nav_index.main:
            record['kind'] = 'main'
        elif over_water > 0.5:
            record['kind'] = 'vehicle-only zone'
            record['linked_by'] = vehicle_link(ctx, record, positions)
        elif on_main_land < 0.5:
            record['kind'] = 'separate landmass (reef or islet: boat, or swimming)'
            record['linked_by'] = vehicle_link(ctx, record, positions)
        elif raised > 0.8 and not record['required']:
            record['kind'] = 'raised surface, no access'
        else:
            record['kind'] = 'gap candidate'
        out.append(record)
    return out


def vehicle_link(ctx: 'AuditContext', isl: dict[str, Any], positions: list['CheckResult']) -> list[str]:
    """What would join a vehicle-only zone to the rest: the vehicle spawns on or beside it."""
    x0, z0, x1, z1 = isl['bbox']
    spawns = [spawn for spawn in positions if spawn['kind'] == 'vehicle spawn'
              and x0 - 10 <= spawn['position'][0] <= x1 + 10 and z0 - 10 <= spawn['position'][2] <= z1 + 10]
    kinds = collections.Counter(position.get('class') for position in spawns)
    out = []
    if kinds.get('boat'):
        out.append(f"boat (landing craft spawns: {kinds['boat']})")
    if kinds.get('aircraft'):
        out.append(f"plane (aircraft spawns: {kinds['aircraft']})")
    if not out:
        out.append('no vehicle spawn on it: a boat landing or a parachute drop from a plane')
    return out


def reachability(ctx: 'AuditContext', positions: list['CheckResult']) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Every infantry spawn joined to the route graph, and whether it reaches each flag's capture area and back."""
    nav = ctx['nav']
    flags = [position for position in positions if position['kind'] == 'flag']
    targets = {}                        # flag name -> the route nodes in its capture area
    for flag in flags:
        poly = flag.get('_poly')
        nodes = nav.nav.node_pos
        if poly is not None:
            ins = in_poly(nodes[:, 0], nodes[:, 2], poly)
        else:
            radius = max(flag.get('capture_radius') or 0, 5.0)
            ins = np.hypot(nodes[:, 0] - flag['position'][0], nodes[:, 2] - flag['position'][2]) <= radius
        targets[flag['name']] = np.nonzero(ins)[0]
    rows = []
    for position in positions:
        if position['kind'] != 'soldier spawn':
            continue
        area = position.get('nearest_same_floor')
        if position.get('floor_y') is None:
            rows.append(dict(spawn=position['name'], joined=False, reason='no floor'))
            continue
        x, _, z = position['position']
        node = nav.join(x, z, position['floor_y'], island=area['island'] if area else None)
        if node is None:
            rows.append(dict(spawn=position['name'], objective=position.get('objective'), joined=False,
                             reason='no route node within 15 m on its floor'))
            continue
        forward, backward = nav.reach(node), nav.reach(node, backward=True)
        res = dict(spawn=position['name'], objective=position.get('objective'), joined=True, node=node,
                   island=int(nav.nav.node_island[node]), main=int(nav.nav.node_island[node]) == nav.main,
                   to={}, back={})
        for name, target in targets.items():
            res['to'][name] = bool(len(target) and forward[target].any())
            res['back'][name] = bool(len(target) and backward[target].any())
        rows.append(res)
    return {'targets': {k: int(len(v)) for k, v in targets.items()}, 'spawns': rows}

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/navaudit1943_checks/loading.py`:

```py
"""navaudit1943_checks: loading a level, its build and masks; lookups by position.

load() reads a level's checked build (<level>.hpd and its cells file), its samples and the masks navaudit1943.py
masks made, the level's entities and spawn map from the game copy, and its object boxes; it returns the audit's
level context (AuditContext, a dict), which every check takes as `ctx`. Every mask must be of the samples and
build on disk.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import time
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, NotRequired, TypedDict, cast

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

import navaudit1943  # noqa: E402
import navkitjson1943 as nj  # noqa: E402
import navbuild  # noqa: E402  (bf1943-auto-navkit-common, a shared folder)
import soldier1943  # noqa: E402
from bfbc2core import game1943, materialmap1943, terrain  # noqa: E402

from .grids import Grid, Nav

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from bfbc2core.level import Entity, Level
    from bfbc2core.materialmap1943 import MaterialMap
    from bfbc2core.terrain import Heightfield

    from .grids import WaterMesh

    class AuditContext(TypedDict):
        """The audit's level context: what load() read, and what the checks add as they go."""
        lv: str                                     # the level's name
        p: dict[str, str]                           # navaudit1943.level_paths
        st: dict[str, Any]                          # navkit.json
        game: str                                   # the game copy's folder
        g: game1943.Game                            # the level's bundles
        hf: Heightfield
        mm: MaterialMap | None
        nav: Nav                                    # the build
        lvl: Level                                  # the level's entities and outlines
        map: dict[str, Any]                         # bf1943-spawn-map's objectives and spawns
        water: WaterMesh | None
        entity_by_guid: dict[str, Entity]           # lower-case GUID -> entity
        grids: dict[str, Grid]                      # 'normal' (0.8 m) and, with a current 0.2 m pass, 'detailed'
        xoff: int                                   # navkit.json's sector offsets
        zoff: int
        dset: set[tuple[int, int]]                  # navkit.json's detailed sectors
        dset_built: set[tuple[int, int]]            # the sectors the build has 0.2 m areas in
        boxes: list[dict[str, Any]]                 # object_boxes.json
        inputs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]           # every input's path, size and SHA-256
        placeholders: NotRequired[list[dict[str, Any]]]     # required_positions: the positions at the origin
        _cell_island: NotRequired[npt.NDArray[Any]]         # nearest_cell_3d: each cell's island
        # vehicle_entries: per vehicle blueprint, its entry points (local point, radius, seat order)
        _entries: NotRequired[dict[str, list[tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float64], float, int]]]]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ loading

def load(lv: str, log: 'navaudit1943.Log' = print) -> 'AuditContext':
    """The audit's level context of a level's checked build (NavKitError without one, or with a stale mask)."""
    import spawnmap
    from bfbc2core import level1943, navdata
    from bfbc2core import water as water_mod
    paths = navaudit1943.level_paths(lv)
    st = navaudit1943.current_build(lv)     # the checked build of the current preparation only (2026-10-30 review)
    game = game1943.find_game(st.get('game'))         # the copy the level was prepared from (2026-10-30: the default)
    level_game = game1943.Game(game, lv)
    hf_name = f'terrains/{lv}/{lv}.heightfield-000.res'
    game_hf = nj.game_heightfield(st, lv, level_game.data(hf_name))   # refused when the copy has none (2026-11-01)
    hf = terrain.read(nj.prepared_heightfield(st, lv, game_hf))    # the prepared one (second review)
    mm = materialmap1943.for_level(level_game, lv, hf)
    started = time.time()
    # BF1943 builds store nodes and outlines half the soldier's height (0.9 m) up
    nav = navdata.load(paths['hpd'], hf, cache_dir=os.path.join(paths['audit'], 'cache'),
                       y_offset=soldier1943.SETTINGS.y_offset)
    log(f'{lv}: build read ({time.time() - started:.0f} s): {len(nav.areas)} areas, {len(nav.node_pos)} nodes')
    exact = navbuild.read_cells(paths['hpd'])
    log(f'{lv}: ' + ('cells file of the build read (area heights exact)' if exact is not None else
                     'no cells file for this build: area heights from the reader cells'))
    lvl = level1943.load(lv, game=game, log=lambda *a: None)
    level_map = spawnmap.spawn_map(game, lv)
    water_path = os.path.join(paths['objects'], 'water_mesh.res')
    has_mesh = soldier1943.has_water(st) and os.path.isfile(water_path)
    water = water_mod.read_mesh(water_path) if has_mesh else None
    masks = os.path.join(paths['audit'], 'masks')
    grids = {}
    hashes = navaudit1943.Hashes(lv)
    # every mask must be of the samples and build on disk (their SHA-256, stored in it): 2026-10-30 review, a base mask
    # was checked only by its surface count and the rule-off masks not at all
    for which, src in (('normal', 'samples.bin'), ('detailed', 'samples_02.bin')):
        if which == 'detailed' and not navaudit1943.detailed_current(st):
            log(f'{lv}: the build has no 0.2 m samples of this preparation: no detailed grid')
            continue
        path = os.path.join(masks, f'{which}_base.npz')
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            log(f'{lv}: no {which} base mask ({path}): navaudit1943.py masks {lv}')
            continue
        why = navaudit1943.mask_stale(path, src, hashes)
        if why:
            raise nj.NavKitError(f'{why}: make the masks again (navaudit1943.py masks {lv})')
        base_mask = np.load(path)
        s = navaudit1943.load_samples(os.path.join(paths['samples'], src))
        if int(base_mask['surfaces']) != len(s.y):
            raise nj.NavKitError(f'{path}: made from another sampling run ({int(base_mask["surfaces"])} surfaces, '
                                 f'now {len(s.y)})')
        grid = Grid(s, base_mask['keep'], hf, water, '0.2 m' if which == 'detailed' else '0.8 m')
        for variant in navaudit1943.VARIANTS:
            variant_path = os.path.join(masks, f'{which}_{variant}.npz')
            if variant != 'base' and os.path.isfile(variant_path):
                why = navaudit1943.mask_stale(variant_path, src, hashes)
                if why:
                    log(f'{why}: left out (navaudit1943.py masks {lv} --variants {variant})')
                    continue
                grid.variants[variant] = np.load(variant_path)['keep']
        grids[which] = grid
    if 'normal' not in grids:
        raise nj.NavKitError(f'{lv}: no normal base mask of this build: navaudit1943.py masks {lv}')
```
