`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/seanav1943.py`:

```py
r"""NavKit (big-endian): navigation for BF1943's landing craft (LCVP) - a sea grid with its route graph, the carrier
launch lanes and the beach landing zones, exported to RSNV as its own world (<level>.lcvp.rsnv), with the
transfers to and from the soldier world (<level>.rsnv).

  seanav1943.py <level> [--soldier <level.rsnv>]

What it builds (parameters: vehicleclasses1943.CLASSES['lcvp']):
  - the sea grid: 2 m cells over the land, the carriers and the craft spawns plus a 250 m margin; a cell's depth is
    the sea level (navkit.json) less the terrain height (core terrain.py) [O]; a cell is blocked by collision
    (all_tris.npy, every object) that crosses the waterline band (sea - draft - 0.3 .. sea + 2 m): carriers, wrecks,
    piers, rocks [O]; the boat's centre may stand where the water is at least the draft deep, no collision lies within
    the radius and no ground shallower than the draft lies within the half-width;
  - route nodes: one per 4 x 4 cell block (8 m) at the cell farthest from shore and collision, edges between nodes of
    neighbouring blocks (including knight moves) with a straight line over navigable cells, pieces of one water
    body joined along the grid's shortest path (groundnav1943.join_pieces' rule on cells);
  - launch lanes: a craft spawned on a carrier deck (higher than sea + 5 m) drives forward along its own heading on
    the deck [O: the Wake and Iwo Jima craft face the carriers' sterns] until the deck ends; a lane of cells at deck
    height (3 cells wide), a node at the spawn and one at the deck's end, and a one-way DROP edge from there to the
    sea node where the craft lands (the deck end + half the craft's length + 2 m, at sea level). That a craft leaves
    the deck this way is [H]: the level shows lcvp_shell objects ("invisible boat wall", destructible) around each
    deck craft [O]; an in-game look is needed;
  - landing zones: navigable cells within the bow distance (5.5 m [O], the exit points at the ramp) of beach ground
    (depth at most beach_depth, no collision), one per 25 m of shore; each zone's ALIGHT transfer goes to the
    soldier node nearest its bow point, which must lie on the soldier world's main island and be the nearest of any
    island (Iwo Jima's no-go strip behind the ForbidPathfinding boardwalk is its own island: zones there are
    dropped), with no ForbidPathfinding collision between the bow and that node;
  - transfers (OFFM): BOARD_VEHICLE at each craft spawn (the soldier-side point: the driver's entry point, radius
    EntryRadius 8 m [O]; aux: the soldier node nearest it); ALIGHT_ZONE at each landing node (the soldier node's
    position; aux: its index); LCVP_LAUNCH at each lane's deck end (the drop point; yaw: the heading).
"""
import argparse
import collections
import math
import os
import sys
import time
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
import rsnvgrid1943  # noqa: E402
import soldier1943  # noqa: E402
import navkitjson1943 as nj  # noqa: E402
import vehicleclasses1943 as vc  # noqa: E402
from bfbc2core import game1943, rsnv, rsnvtrip, terrain  # noqa: E402

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from bfbc2core.level import Level

type Log = Callable[[str], object]
type Triangles = npt.NDArray[np.floating[Any]]  # (n, 3 corners, x y z)
type CellMask = npt.NDArray[np.bool_]           # per sea-grid cell (nz, nx): bool
type Edge = tuple[int, int, int, float | None, bool]    # rsnvgrid1943.write_world's: (a, b, kind, cost m, both ways)
type Point = Sequence[float] | npt.NDArray[np.float64]     # (x, y, z)
type Edges = set[tuple[int, int]]               # undirected sea-graph edges (a, b) between cells, a < b

MARGIN = 250.0               # m of sea around the land, carriers and craft spawns
BAND_BELOW = 0.3             # m under the draft: collision there still touches the hull
BAND_ABOVE = 2.0             # m over the sea level: collision there touches the hull
ZONE_SPACING = 25.0          # m between landing zones along a shore
ALIGHT_REACH = 12.0          # m from the bow point to the soldier node a zone unloads onto
FORBID_CLEAR = 1.5           # m: no ForbidPathfinding collision this close to the bow -> soldier node line
DECK_MIN = 5.0               # m over the sea: a craft spawn this high is on a deck
DECK_GAP = 6.0               # m without deck along a lane: the deck has ended
LAUNCH_GAP = 2.0             # m past the deck end + half the craft's length: where it lands in the water
OFFM_ALIGHT_ZONE, OFFM_LCVP_LAUNCH = rsnvgrid1943.OFFM_ALIGHT_ZONE, 3      # design 1.3's OFFM kinds


def paths(lv: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    work = game1943.level_work(lv)
    return {'work': work, 'objects': os.path.join(work, 'objects'), 'navkit': os.path.join(work, 'navkit'),
            'rsnv': os.path.join(work, 'navkit', f'{lv}.lcvp.rsnv'),
            'soldier': os.path.join(work, 'navkit', f'{lv}.rsnv')}


def craft_spawns(lv: str, game: str | None = None) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], 'Level']:
    """The level's landing craft spawns (vehicle name, team, position, heading, entry points) and the level."""
    from bfbc2core import level1943, vehicles1943
    level = level1943.load(lv, game=game, log=lambda *a: None)
    game_level = game1943.Game(game1943.find_game(game), lv)
    out = []
    for entity in level.entities:
        if entity.category != 'vehicle spawn' or entity.position is None:
            continue
        part = vehicles1943.vehicle_partition(entity)
        name = part.rsplit('/', 1)[-1] if part else ''
        if vehicles1943.vehicle_class(name) != 'boat':
            continue
        matrix = np.asarray(entity.matrix, float)
        forward = matrix[2, :3]
        out.append({'vehicle': name, 'team': entity.team, 'pos': [float(v) for v in entity.position],
                    'fwd': (forward / max(np.linalg.norm(forward[[0, 2]]), 1e-9)).tolist(),
                    'yaw': math.atan2(forward[0], forward[2]),
                    'entries': vehicles1943.entry_points(game_level, entity), 'index': entity.index})
    return out, level


def rasterise_band(T: Triangles, lo: float, hi: float, x0: float, z0: float, nx: int, nz: int,
                   pitch: float) -> tuple[CellMask, int]:
    """Bool (nz, nx): cells whose centre lies under a triangle crossing the height band [lo, hi] (a triangle smaller
    than a cell marks the cell of its centroid). T: triangles (n, 3 corners, xyz)."""
    import navsample1943
    tri_ylo, tri_yhi = T[:, :, 1].min(1), T[:, :, 1].max(1)
    T = T[(tri_ylo <= hi) & (tri_yhi >= lo)].astype(np.float64)
    out = np.zeros((nz, nx), bool)
    if not len(T):
        return out, 0
    centroid = T.mean(1)
    cent_i = np.round((centroid[:, 0] - x0) / pitch).astype(np.int64)
    cent_j = np.round((centroid[:, 2] - z0) / pitch).astype(np.int64)
    on_grid = (cent_i >= 0) & (cent_j >= 0) & (cent_i < nx) & (cent_j < nz)
    out[cent_j[on_grid], cent_i[on_grid]] = True
    # triangles two cells or more across: every cell centre under them
    lo_i = np.floor((T[:, :, 0].min(1) - x0) / pitch).astype(np.int64)
    hi_i = np.ceil((T[:, :, 0].max(1) - x0) / pitch).astype(np.int64)
    lo_j = np.floor((T[:, :, 2].min(1) - z0) / pitch).astype(np.int64)
    hi_j = np.ceil((T[:, :, 2].max(1) - z0) / pitch).astype(np.int64)
    big = np.nonzero((hi_i - lo_i >= 2) | (hi_j - lo_j >= 2))[0]
    for tri in big.tolist():
        i0, i1 = max(lo_i[tri], 0), min(hi_i[tri], nx - 1)
        j0, j1 = max(lo_j[tri], 0), min(hi_j[tri], nz - 1)
        if i1 < i0 or j1 < j0:
            continue
        cols_i, cols_j = np.meshgrid(np.arange(i0, i1 + 1), np.arange(j0, j1 + 1))     # the cells under its box
        cols_i, cols_j = cols_i.ravel(), cols_j.ravel()
        _u, _v, _w, under = navsample1943.inside(T[tri:tri + 1, :, [0, 2]], x0 + cols_i * pitch, z0 + cols_j * pitch)
        out[cols_j[under[0]], cols_i[under[0]]] = True
    return out, len(T)


def dilate(mask: CellMask, cells: float) -> CellMask:
    """Bool mask grown by a disc of `cells` radius."""
    out = mask.copy()
    reach = int(math.ceil(cells))
    nz, nx = mask.shape
    for dj in range(-reach, reach + 1):
        for di in range(-reach, reach + 1):
            if (di or dj) and di * di + dj * dj <= cells * cells + 1e-9:
                # the grid shifted by (di, dj): out[r, c] takes src[r, c]
                src = mask[max(0, -dj):nz - max(0, dj), max(0, -di):nx - max(0, di)]
                out[max(0, dj):nz + min(0, dj), max(0, di):nx + min(0, di)] |= src
    return out


def distance_field(mask: CellMask, cap: int) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
    """Chessboard distance (cells) from each True cell to the nearest False, capped."""
    dist = np.where(mask, cap, 0).astype(np.int64)
    inside = mask.copy()
    for ring in range(1, cap):
        # erode by one cell: a cell stays inside when its four neighbours are inside
        eroded = inside.copy()
        eroded[1:, :] &= inside[:-1, :]
        eroded[:-1, :] &= inside[1:, :]
        eroded[:, 1:] &= inside[:, :-1]
        eroded[:, :-1] &= inside[:, 1:]
        dist = np.where(inside & ~eroded, np.minimum(dist, ring), dist)
        inside = eroded
        if not inside.any():
            break
    return dist


def cell_line(nav: CellMask, a: tuple[int, int], b: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
    """Whether the straight line between cells a (i, j) and b crosses only navigable cells (4-connected steps)."""
    (ia, ja), (ib, jb) = a, b
    steps = max(abs(ib - ia), abs(jb - ja))
    if steps == 0:
        return bool(nav[ja, ia])
    prev_i, prev_j = ia, ja
    for step in range(1, steps + 1):
        to_i = int(round(ia + (ib - ia) * step / steps))
        to_j = int(round(ja + (jb - ja) * step / steps))
        # a diagonal step passes through either side cell
        if to_i != prev_i and to_j != prev_j and not (nav[prev_j, to_i] or nav[to_j, prev_i]):
            return False
        if not nav[to_j, to_i]:
            return False
        prev_i, prev_j = to_i, to_j
    return True


def build(lv: str, soldier_path: str | None = None, game: str | None = None,
          log: Log = print) -> tuple[str | None, dict[str, Any]]:
    """The LCVP world: (rsnv path, stats), or (None, stats) when the level has none (no water, no craft spawns: stamped
    absent). Reads the level from the game copy it was prepared from (2026-10-30: game=None read the default copy)."""
    files = paths(lv)
    started = time.time()
    st = nj.read(lv)
    game = vc.prepared_game(st, game, lv)
    want = vc.inputs(st, lv, 'lcvp')
    if not soldier1943.has_water(st):            # prepare found no water mesh (2026-10-30: float(None) raised)
        # absent whatever the soldier world: the level's data says so (2026-10-30: a current soldier export was needed)
        why = 'no water on the level (navkit.py prepare found no water mesh)'
        log(f'{lv}: {why}: no LCVP world')
        vc.absent(lv, 'lcvp', want, files['rsnv'], why, log)
        return None, {'spawns': 0, 'note': why}
    soldier_path = soldier_path or files['soldier']
    want['soldier'] = vc.soldier_world(st, lv, soldier_path)
    vc.drop(lv, 'worlds', 'lcvp')
    pitch = vc.value('lcvp', 'pitch')
    draft = vc.value('lcvp', 'draft')
    radius = vc.value('lcvp', 'radius')
    half_w = vc.value('lcvp', 'half_width')
    beach = vc.value('lcvp', 'beach_depth')
    bow = vc.value('lcvp', 'bow')
    hf_path = os.path.join(files['objects'], 'heightfield.res')
    hf = terrain.read(hf_path)
    sea = soldier1943.sea_level(st, hf)
    spawns, _level = craft_spawns(lv, game)
    soldier = rsnv.load(soldier_path)
    if not spawns:
        log(f'{lv}: no landing craft spawns: no LCVP world')
        vc.absent(lv, 'lcvp', want, files['rsnv'], 'no landing craft spawns on the level', log)
        return None, {'spawns': 0}
    # the box: land, carriers (objects holding soldier spawns), craft spawns
    land = hf.heights > sea - draft
    land_j, land_i = np.nonzero(land)
    cell_x, cell_z = hf.cell
    lo = np.array([hf.min[0] + land_i.min() * cell_x, hf.min[2] + land_j.min() * cell_z])
    hi = np.array([hf.min[0] + (land_i.max() + 1) * cell_x, hf.min[2] + (land_j.max() + 1) * cell_z])
    must_hold = np.array([spawn['pos'] for spawn in spawns])[:, [0, 2]]     # x, z the box must hold
    if soldier.islands:
        on_carrier = [node for node in range(len(soldier.node_pos))
                      if soldier.islands[int(soldier.node_island[node])][2] & rsnv.ISLD_CARRIER]
        carrier_nodes = soldier.node_pos[on_carrier]
    else:
        carrier_nodes = np.zeros((0, 3))
    if len(carrier_nodes):
        must_hold = np.concatenate([must_hold, carrier_nodes[:, [0, 2]]])
    lo, hi = np.minimum(lo, must_hold.min(0)) - MARGIN, np.maximum(hi, must_hold.max(0)) + MARGIN
    lo = np.maximum(lo, [hf.min[0], hf.min[2]])
    hi = np.minimum(hi, [hf.max[0] - pitch, hf.max[2] - pitch])
    x0, z0 = math.floor(lo[0] / pitch) * pitch, math.floor(lo[1] / pitch) * pitch
    nx, nz = int((hi[0] - x0) / pitch) + 1, int((hi[1] - z0) / pitch) + 1
    I, J = np.meshgrid(np.arange(nx), np.arange(nz))            # the sea grid's cell indices, (nz, nx)
    X, Z = x0 + I * pitch, z0 + J * pitch                       # ... and their centres
    depth = sea - hf.height(X, Z)
    tris = np.load(os.path.join(files['objects'], 'all_tris.npy'))      # collision triangles (n, 3 corners, xyz)
    blocked, n_band = rasterise_band(tris, sea - draft - BAND_BELOW, sea + BAND_ABOVE, x0, z0, nx, nz, pitch)
    log(f'{lv}: sea grid {nx} x {nz} cells of {pitch} m (x {x0:.0f}..{x0 + nx * pitch:.0f}, z {z0:.0f}..'
        f'{z0 + nz * pitch:.0f}); {n_band} triangles cross the waterline band, {int(blocked.sum())} cells blocked')
    water = depth >= draft
    shallow_ground = ~water
    nav = water & ~dilate(blocked, radius / pitch) & ~dilate(shallow_ground, half_w / pitch)
    # the boat's own water bodies: keep those a craft spawn or a launch reaches
    beach_cells = (depth <= beach) & (depth > -1.0) & ~dilate(blocked, 1.0 / pitch)
    log(f'  navigable {int(nav.sum())} cells ({nav.sum() * pitch * pitch / 1e6:.2f} km2), '
        f'beach {int(beach_cells.sum())}')
    # launch lanes
    lanes = []
    deck_spawns = [spawn for spawn in spawns if spawn['pos'][1] - sea >= DECK_MIN]
    if deck_spawns:
        deck_xz = np.array([spawn['pos'] for spawn in deck_spawns])[:, [0, 2]]
        tri_centres = tris[:, :, [0, 2]].mean(1)
        near = np.zeros(len(tris), bool)
        for spawn_xz in deck_xz:
            near |= np.hypot(tri_centres[:, 0] - spawn_xz[0], tri_centres[:, 1] - spawn_xz[1]) < 400.0
        deck_tris = tris[near & (tris[:, :, 1].max(1) >= sea + DECK_MIN - 3.0)]
        for spawn in deck_spawns:
            lane = launch_lane(spawn, deck_tris, sea, pitch, log)
            if lane is not None:
                lanes.append(lane)
    log(f'  {len(lanes)} launch lanes (deck lengths {[lane["length"] for lane in lanes]})')
    # graph over sea cells
    nav_idx = np.full((nz, nx), -1, np.int64)
    nav_cells = np.nonzero(nav.ravel())[0]
    nav_idx.ravel()[nav_cells] = np.arange(len(nav_cells))
    links = rsnvgrid1943.grid_links(nav_idx)
    sea_set = rsnvgrid1943.CellSet(pitch, x0, z0, I.ravel()[nav_cells], J.ravel()[nav_cells],
                                   np.full(len(nav_cells), sea), links, name=f'{lv} sea')
    # components of the navigable water (straight links), to keep the craft's water bodies
    pairs = np.array([(k, n) for (k, _di, _dj), n in links.items()], np.int64).reshape(-1, 2)
    import groundnav1943
    water_body = groundnav1943.components(len(nav_cells), pairs)
    sea_i = sea_set.i
    sea_j = sea_set.j

    def nearest_cell(x: float, z: float, maxd: float = 60.0) -> tuple[int | None, float]:
        """(sea cell nearest (x, z), its distance), the cell None when farther than maxd."""
        dist2 = (x0 + sea_i * pitch - x) ** 2 + (z0 + sea_j * pitch - z) ** 2
        k = int(np.argmin(dist2))
        dist = math.sqrt(float(dist2[k]))
        return (k, dist) if dist2[k] <= maxd * maxd else (None, dist)
    kept_bodies = set()
    for lane in lanes:
        k, dist = nearest_cell(lane['land'][0], lane['land'][2])
        lane['water_cell'] = k
        lane['water_dist'] = round(dist, 1)
        if k is not None:
            kept_bodies.add(int(water_body[k]))
    for spawn in spawns:
        if spawn['pos'][1] - sea < DECK_MIN:
            k, dist = nearest_cell(spawn['pos'][0], spawn['pos'][2], 20.0)
            spawn['water_cell'] = k
            if k is not None:
                kept_bodies.add(int(water_body[k]))
    kept = np.isin(water_body, list(kept_bodies))
    log(f'  kept {len(kept_bodies)} water bodies, {int(kept.sum())} cells ({kept.sum() * pitch * pitch / 1e6:.2f} km2)')
    kept_nav = np.zeros_like(nav)
    kept_nav[sea_set.j[kept], sea_set.i[kept]] = True
    # rebuild the set on the kept cells
    nav_idx = np.full((nz, nx), -1, np.int64)
    kept_nav_cells = np.nonzero(kept_nav.ravel())[0]
    nav_idx.ravel()[kept_nav_cells] = np.arange(len(kept_nav_cells))
    links = rsnvgrid1943.grid_links(nav_idx)
    sea_set = rsnvgrid1943.CellSet(pitch, x0, z0, I.ravel()[kept_nav_cells], J.ravel()[kept_nav_cells],
                                   np.full(len(kept_nav_cells), sea), links, name=f'{lv} sea')
    old_to_new = {int(old): int(nav_idx.ravel()[nav_cells[old]]) for old in np.nonzero(kept)[0].tolist()}
    for lane in lanes:
        lane['water_cell'] = old_to_new.get(lane['water_cell']) if lane['water_cell'] is not None else None
    for spawn in spawns:
        if spawn.get('water_cell') is not None:
            spawn['water_cell'] = old_to_new.get(spawn['water_cell'])
    # route nodes: per 4 x 4 block the cell farthest from the shore
    clearance = distance_field(kept_nav, 12)
    spacing = int(vc.value('lcvp', 'node_spacing'))
    cell_i, cell_j = sea_set.i, sea_set.j
    block_i, block_j = cell_i // spacing, cell_j // spacing
    off_centre = ((cell_i - (block_i * spacing + spacing / 2 - 0.5)) ** 2
                  + (cell_j - (block_j * spacing + spacing / 2 - 0.5)) ** 2)
    # per block (block_i, block_j): the most clearance first, then the nearest the block's centre
    order = np.lexsort((off_centre, -clearance[cell_j, cell_i], block_j, block_i))
    block = np.stack([block_i[order], block_j[order]], 1)
    first_in_block = np.ones(len(order), bool)
    first_in_block[1:] = np.any(block[1:] != block[:-1], axis=1)
    node_cells = order[first_in_block].tolist()
    node_of_block = {(int(bi), int(bj)): k for (bi, bj), k in zip(block[first_in_block].tolist(), node_cells)}
    edges = set()
    for (bi, bj), k in node_of_block.items():
        for di, dj in ((1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, -1)):
            other = node_of_block.get((bi + di, bj + dj))
            if other is not None and cell_line(kept_nav, (int(cell_i[k]), int(cell_j[k])),
                                               (int(cell_i[other]), int(cell_j[other]))):
                edges.add((min(k, other), max(k, other)))
    log(f'  {len(node_cells)} sea nodes, {len(edges)} edges')
    # extra nodes: craft water cells, lane landings, landing zones
    extra = set()
    for lane in lanes:
        if lane['water_cell'] is not None:
            extra.add(lane['water_cell'])
    for spawn in spawns:
        if spawn.get('water_cell') is not None:
            extra.add(spawn['water_cell'])
    zones = landing_zones(lv, sea_set, kept_nav, depth, beach_cells, soldier, bow, pitch, x0, z0, log)
    for zone in zones:
        extra.add(zone['cell'])
    node_cells, edges = connect_extra(sea_set, kept_nav, node_cells, edges, extra)
    node_cells, edges = join_cell_pieces(sea_set, kept_nav, node_cells, edges, log)
    # deck lanes: a cell set per lane (3 cells wide at deck height), a node at each end
    lane_sets = []
    for lane in lanes:
        spawn = lane['spawn']
        cells = {}                                      # (i, j) -> deck height
        start = np.array(spawn['pos'], float)
        fwd = np.array(spawn['fwd'], float)
        fwd[1] = 0
        fwd /= np.linalg.norm(fwd)
        side = np.array([fwd[2], 0.0, -fwd[0]])
        dist = float(np.linalg.norm((np.array(lane['deck_end']) - start)[[0, 2]]))
        for along in np.arange(0.0, dist + 1e-6, pitch / 2):
            for offset in (-pitch, 0.0, pitch):
                point = start + fwd * along + side * offset
                cell_i = int(round((point[0] - x0) / pitch))
                cell_j = int(round((point[2] - z0) / pitch))
                cells.setdefault((cell_i, cell_j), start[1])
        lane_cells = sorted(cells)
        cell_index = {cell: k for k, cell in enumerate(lane_cells)}
        lane_links = {}
        for (cell_i, cell_j), k in cell_index.items():
            for di, dj in rsnvgrid1943.STRAIGHT:
                n = cell_index.get((cell_i + di, cell_j + dj))
                if n is not None:
                    lane_links[(k, di, dj)] = n
        lane_set = rsnvgrid1943.CellSet(pitch, x0, z0, [cell[0] for cell in lane_cells],
                                        [cell[1] for cell in lane_cells], [cells[cell] for cell in lane_cells],
                                        lane_links, name=f'lane {spawn["index"]}')
        start_cell = (int(round((start[0] - x0) / pitch)), int(round((start[2] - z0) / pitch)))
        deck_end = np.array(lane['deck_end'])
        end_cell = (int(round((deck_end[0] - x0) / pitch)), int(round((deck_end[2] - z0) / pitch)))
        if end_cell in cell_index:
            end_k = cell_index[end_cell]
        else:                                           # the lane cell nearest the deck end
            end_k = min(cell_index.items(),
                        key=lambda item: (item[0][0] - end_cell[0]) ** 2 + (item[0][1] - end_cell[1]) ** 2)[1]
        lane['cells'] = (cell_index[start_cell], end_k)
        lane_sets.append(lane_set)
    # all nodes: sea set 0, lanes 1..
    sets = [sea_set] + lane_sets
    node_list = [(0, k) for k in node_cells]
    node_of_cell = {k: n for n, k in enumerate(node_cells)}
    edge_list: list[Edge] = [(node_of_cell[a], node_of_cell[b], rsnv.EDGE_WALK, None, True) for a, b in sorted(edges)]
    offm = []
    lane_info = []
    for lane_no, lane in enumerate(lanes):
        deck_node = len(node_list)
        node_list.append((lane_no + 1, lane['cells'][0]))
        end_node = len(node_list)
        node_list.append((lane_no + 1, lane['cells'][1]))
        # forward only: the craft does not drive back up
        edge_list.append((deck_node, end_node, rsnv.EDGE_WALK, None, False))
        if lane['water_cell'] is not None:
            water_node = node_of_cell[lane['water_cell']]
            deck_end = np.array(lane['deck_end'])
            water_xz = sea_set.xz(lane['water_cell'])
            drop_run = float(math.hypot(water_xz[0] - deck_end[0], water_xz[1] - deck_end[2]))
            edge_list.append((end_node, water_node, rsnv.EDGE_DROP, drop_run, False))
            offm.append((OFFM_LCVP_LAUNCH, team_mask(lane['spawn']['team']), vc.CLASS_IDS['lcvp'], end_node,
                         float(lane['land'][0]), float(lane['land'][1]), float(lane['land'][2]),
                         float(lane['spawn']['yaw']), float(vc.value('lcvp', 'half_length')), water_node))
        lane['nodes'] = (deck_node, end_node)
        lane_info.append({'spawn': lane['spawn']['index'], 'team': lane['spawn']['team'], 'deck node': deck_node,
                          'deck end node': end_node, 'water node': node_of_cell.get(lane['water_cell']),
                          'deck length': lane['length'], 'landing point': [round(v, 2) for v in lane['land']],
                          'snap to water': lane['water_dist']})
    # boarding transfers: every craft spawn
    board = []
    for spawn in spawns:
        lane = next((candidate for candidate in lanes if candidate['spawn'] is spawn), None)
        if lane is not None:
            node = lane['nodes'][0]
        elif spawn.get('water_cell') is not None:
            node = node_of_cell[spawn['water_cell']]
        else:
            node = None
        entry = next((candidate for candidate in spawn['entries'] if candidate.get('order', 0) == 0), None)  # driver's
        if not entry:
            entry = {'point': spawn['pos'], 'radius': vc.value('lcvp', 'radius') + 4.0}
        soldier_n = soldier_node(soldier, entry['point'], entry['radius'] + 2.0)
        offm.append((rsnv.OFFM_BOARD_VEHICLE, team_mask(spawn['team']), vc.CLASS_IDS['lcvp'],
                     node if node is not None else 0xFFFFFFFF, *[float(v) for v in entry['point']],
                     float(spawn['yaw']), float(entry['radius']), soldier_n if soldier_n is not None else 0xFFFFFFFF))
        board.append({'spawn': spawn['index'], 'team': spawn['team'], 'pos': [round(v, 2) for v in spawn['pos']],
                      'node': node, 'entry': [round(v, 2) for v in entry['point']], 'radius': entry['radius'],
                      'soldier node': soldier_n,
                      'soldier island': int(soldier.node_island[soldier_n]) if soldier_n is not None else None,
                      'on deck': lane is not None})
    # alight transfers
    for zone in zones:
        node = node_of_cell[zone['cell']]
        unload = zone['unload']
        offm.append((OFFM_ALIGHT_ZONE, 3, vc.CLASS_IDS['lcvp'], node, float(unload[0]), float(unload[1]),
                     float(unload[2]), float(zone['yaw']), float(zone['reach']), int(zone['soldier'])))
        zone['node'] = node
    flags_of_node = [0] * len(node_list)
    for zone in zones:
        flags_of_node[zone['node']] |= rsnv.NAUX_SHALLOW               # a landing node: the craft grounds here
    sources = (('soldier rsnv', soldier_path), ('all_tris.npy', os.path.join(files['objects'], 'all_tris.npy')),
               ('heightfield.res', hf_path), ('navkit.json', os.path.join(files['navkit'], 'navkit.json')))
    meta = {'sources': {name: {'path': path, 'sha256': rsnvgrid1943.sha256(path)} for name, path in sources
                        if os.path.isfile(path)},
            'class parameters': {key: list(entry) if isinstance(entry, tuple) else entry
                                 for key, entry in vc.CLASSES['lcvp'].items()},
            'grid': {'pitch': pitch, 'x0': x0, 'z0': z0, 'nx': nx, 'nz': nz}, 'lanes': lane_info, 'boarding': board,
            'landing zones': [{key: (round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for key, v in zone.items()
                               if key != 'cell'} for zone in zones]}
    header = {'sea_level': sea, 'radius': radius, 'height': vc.value('lcvp', 'height'), 'step': 0.5,
              'water_depth': draft, 'sha256': meta['sources']['soldier rsnv']['sha256']}
    stats = rsnvgrid1943.write_world(lv, 'lcvp', sets, node_list, edge_list, offm, files['rsnv'], st['sector_offsets'],
                                     header, meta, node_flags=flags_of_node, log=log)
    vc.record(lv, 'worlds', dict(want, sha256=nj.sha256(files['rsnv'])), 'lcvp', soldier_path=soldier_path)
    stats.update({'lanes': len(lanes), 'landing zones': len(zones), 'boarding': len(board),
                  'seconds': round(time.time() - started, 1)})
    log(f'{lv}: LCVP world {files["rsnv"]}: {stats["nodes"]} nodes, {len(lanes)} lanes, {len(zones)} landing zones, '
        f'{len(board)} boarding points ({stats["seconds"]:.0f} s)')
    return files['rsnv'], stats


def launch_lane(spawn: dict[str, Any], deck_tris: Triangles, sea: float, pitch: float,
                log: Log) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """The launch lane of a craft spawned on a deck: forward along its heading until the deck ends (DECK_GAP without
    deck); its deck end, landing point and length, or None (no deck end within 300 m)."""
    fwd = np.array(spawn['fwd'], float)
    fwd[1] = 0.0
    fwd /= np.linalg.norm(fwd)
    start = np.array(spawn['pos'], float)
    deck_y = start[1]
    end = None
    along = 0.0
    last_deck = 0.0
    while along < 300.0:
        point = start + fwd * along
        # collision top within 1.5 m below the craft and 1 m above it, at the lane point or 1 m around it (the
        # craft's cradle leaves holes in the deck's collision under it)
        if any(deck_tops(deck_tris, point[0] + ox, point[2] + oz, deck_y - 1.5, deck_y + 1.0) is not None
               for ox, oz in ((0, 0), (1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))):
            last_deck = along
        elif along - last_deck > DECK_GAP:
            end = last_deck + pitch
            break
        along += pitch
    if end is None:
        log(f'  craft {spawn["index"]} at {np.round(start, 1).tolist()}: no deck end within 300 m, no launch lane')
        return None
    deck_end = start + fwd * max(end - pitch, 0.0)
    land_pt = start + fwd * (end + vc.value('lcvp', 'half_length') + LAUNCH_GAP)
    return {'spawn': spawn, 'deck_end': deck_end.tolist(),
            'land': [float(land_pt[0]), sea, float(land_pt[2])], 'length': round(end, 1)}


def team_mask(team: int | None) -> int:
    """The OFFM team mask of a spawn's team (1, 2; anything else: both)."""
    masks: dict[int | None, int] = {1: 1, 2: 2}
    return masks.get(team, 3)


# deck_tops' per-triangle boxes of the triangle array it was last given: {id(T): (box lo, box hi, y lo, y hi)}
_tops_cache: dict[int, tuple[npt.NDArray[Any], ...]] = {}


def deck_tops(T: Triangles, x: float, z: float, ylo: float, yhi: float) -> float | None:
    """The highest collision surface at (x, z) between ylo and yhi, or None. T: triangles (n, 3 corners, xyz)."""
    key = id(T)
    if key not in _tops_cache:
        _tops_cache.clear()
        _tops_cache[key] = (T[:, :, [0, 2]].min(1), T[:, :, [0, 2]].max(1), T[:, :, 1].min(1), T[:, :, 1].max(1))
    box_lo, box_hi, tri_ylo, tri_yhi = _tops_cache[key]       # per triangle: x-z box and height range
    candidates = np.nonzero((box_lo[:, 0] <= x) & (box_hi[:, 0] >= x) & (box_lo[:, 1] <= z) & (box_hi[:, 1] >= z)
                            & (tri_yhi >= ylo) & (tri_ylo <= yhi))[0]
    best = None
    for tri in candidates.tolist():
        # its corners a, b, c in x-z, and the barycentric (u, w) of (x, z) in them: edges v0, v1, the point v2
        a, b, c = (T[tri, 0, [0, 2]].astype(float), T[tri, 1, [0, 2]].astype(float), T[tri, 2, [0, 2]].astype(float))
        v0, v1, v2 = b - a, c - a, np.array([x, z]) - a
        det = v0[0] * v1[1] - v0[1] * v1[0]
        if abs(det) < 1e-9:
            continue
        u = (v2[0] * v1[1] - v2[1] * v1[0]) / det
        w = (v0[0] * v2[1] - v0[1] * v2[0]) / det
        if u >= -1e-6 and w >= -1e-6 and u + w <= 1 + 1e-6:
            y = float(T[tri, 0, 1] + u * (T[tri, 1, 1] - T[tri, 0, 1]) + w * (T[tri, 2, 1] - T[tri, 0, 1]))
            if ylo <= y <= yhi and (best is None or y > best):
                best = y
    return best


def soldier_node(S: rsnv.World, p: Point, reach: float, dy: float = 3.5) -> int | None:
    """rsnvgrid1943.soldier_node: the rule the runtime resolves a transfer with again. S: the soldier world."""
    return rsnvgrid1943.soldier_node(S, p, reach, dy)


def landing_zones(lv: str, cs: 'rsnvgrid1943.CellSet', nav: CellMask, depth: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
                  beach_cells: CellMask, soldier: rsnv.World, bow: float, pitch: float, x0: float, z0: float,
                  log: Log) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Landing zones: navigable cells within the bow distance of beach ground, one per ZONE_SPACING, unloading onto
    the soldier main island (see the module's description). cs: the sea cells; nav: the navigable cells."""
    near_beach = dilate(beach_cells, (bow + 0.5) / pitch)
    candidates = np.nonzero(near_beach[cs.j, cs.i])[0]
    if not len(candidates):
        return []
    forbid_path = os.path.join(game1943.level_work(lv), 'objects', 'forbid_tris.npy')
    forbid_tris = np.load(forbid_path) if os.path.isfile(forbid_path) else np.zeros((0, 3, 3), np.float32)
    forbid_centres = forbid_tris.mean(1) if len(forbid_tris) else np.zeros((0, 3))
    beach_j, beach_i = np.nonzero(beach_cells)
    beach_x, beach_z = x0 + beach_i * pitch, z0 + beach_j * pitch
    main = 0
    carrier_islands = {island_no for island_no, island in enumerate(soldier.islands)
                       if island[2] & rsnv.ISLD_CARRIER}
    zones: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    rejected: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    taken: list[tuple[float, float]] = []            # the zones' cell centres (x, z)
    # nearest first to the shore: shallower water first
    candidate_depth = depth[cs.j[candidates], cs.i[candidates]]
    for k in candidates[np.argsort(candidate_depth, kind='stable')].tolist():
        x, z = cs.xz(k)
        if any((x - taken_x) ** 2 + (z - taken_z) ** 2 < ZONE_SPACING ** 2 for taken_x, taken_z in taken):
            continue
        beach_dist2 = (beach_x - x) ** 2 + (beach_z - z) ** 2
        nearest_beach = int(np.argmin(beach_dist2))
        dirx, dirz = beach_x[nearest_beach] - x, beach_z[nearest_beach] - z
        length = math.hypot(dirx, dirz)
        if length < 1e-6:
            continue
        dirx, dirz = dirx / length, dirz / length
        bow_xz = (x + dirx * bow, z + dirz * bow)
        node_dist = np.hypot(soldier.node_pos[:, 0] - bow_xz[0], soldier.node_pos[:, 2] - bow_xz[1])
        node_dist = np.where(np.abs(soldier.node_pos[:, 1] - cs.y[k]) <= 3.0, node_dist, np.inf)
        soldier_n = int(np.argmin(node_dist))
        if not np.isfinite(node_dist[soldier_n]) or node_dist[soldier_n] > ALIGHT_REACH:
            rejected['no soldier ground within reach'] += 1
            continue
        island = int(soldier.node_island[soldier_n])
        if island != main or island in carrier_islands:
            rejected['nearest soldier ground not the main island'] += 1
            continue
        soldier_pos = soldier.node_pos[soldier_n]
        if len(forbid_centres):
            # ForbidPathfinding collision near the bow -> soldier node line: each triangle centre's distance to it
            # (the line from a, the bow, along v to the soldier node; t: each centre's place along it, 0..1)
            ax, az = bow_xz[0], bow_xz[1]
            vx, vz = float(soldier_pos[0]) - ax, float(soldier_pos[2]) - az
            length2 = max(vx * vx + vz * vz, 1e-9)
            t = np.clip(((forbid_centres[:, 0] - ax) * vx + (forbid_centres[:, 2] - az) * vz) / length2, 0, 1)
            line_dist = np.hypot(forbid_centres[:, 0] - (ax + t * vx), forbid_centres[:, 2] - (az + t * vz))
            if (line_dist <= FORBID_CLEAR).any():
                rejected['ForbidPathfinding collision between bow and soldier ground'] += 1
                continue
        # the unload point: the soldier cell nearest the bow point (the craft's ramp reach) from which a main-island
        # node is in sight (rsnvtrip.in_sight_node, the runtime's rule) - a point on the soldier world's cells, which
        # stays put when the soldier world is rebuilt; else the node's own position
        unload, unload_node = None, None
        located = soldier.locate(bow_xz[0], float(soldier_pos[1]), bow_xz[1], max_dist=ALIGHT_REACH, dy=3.0)
        if located is not None:
            area = soldier.areas[located[0]]
            cell_x, cell_z = area.x0 + located[1][0] * area.pitch, area.z0 + located[1][1] * area.pitch
            cell_y = soldier.ground(area, cell_x, cell_z)
            unload_node = rsnvtrip.in_sight_node(soldier, cell_x, cell_y, cell_z)
            if unload_node is not None and int(soldier.node_island[unload_node]) == main:
                unload = (float(cell_x), float(cell_y), float(cell_z))
        if unload is None:
            unload, unload_node = (float(soldier_pos[0]), float(soldier_pos[1]), float(soldier_pos[2])), soldier_n
            how = 'the soldier node itself'
        else:
            how = 'a soldier cell by the bow, a main-island node in sight'
        taken.append((x, z))
        zones.append({'cell': k, 'pos': [x, float(cs.y[k]), z], 'bow': [bow_xz[0], bow_xz[1]],
                      'yaw': math.atan2(dirx, dirz), 'soldier': unload_node,
                      'soldier pos': [float(v) for v in soldier.node_pos[unload_node]], 'unload': list(unload),
                      'unload is': how, 'reach': float(math.hypot(unload[0] - x, unload[2] - z)),
                      'depth': float(depth[cs.j[k], cs.i[k]])})
    log(f'  {len(zones)} landing zones; rejected candidates: {dict(rejected)}')
    return zones


def connect_extra(cs: 'rsnvgrid1943.CellSet', nav: CellMask, node_cells: Iterable[int], edges: Edges,
                  extra: Iterable[int]) -> tuple[list[int], Edges]:
    """Adds the extra cells as nodes, each linked to every node within 2 blocks it has a straight line to."""
    node_cells = list(node_cells)
    have = set(node_cells)
    node_ij = np.stack([cs.i[node_cells], cs.j[node_cells]], 1)
    for k in sorted(extra):
        if k in have:
            continue
        cell = (int(cs.i[k]), int(cs.j[k]))
        dist = np.abs(node_ij - cell).max(1)
        near = np.nonzero(dist <= 10)[0]
        for nearby in near[np.argsort(dist[near], kind='stable')].tolist():
            other = node_cells[nearby]
            if cell_line(nav, cell, (int(cs.i[other]), int(cs.j[other]))):
                edges.add((min(k, other), max(k, other)))
        node_cells.append(k)
        have.add(k)
        node_ij = np.concatenate([node_ij, [cell]])
    return node_cells, edges


def join_cell_pieces(cs: 'rsnvgrid1943.CellSet', nav: CellMask, node_cells: list[int], edges: Edges,
                     log: Log) -> tuple[list[int], Edges]:
    """Pieces of the sea graph on one water body joined along the grid's shortest path (as groundnav1943)."""
    import groundnav1943
    links = cs.links
    table = {}
    for (k, di, dj), n in links.items():
        table[(k, di, dj)] = n
    pairs = np.array([(k, n) for (k, _di, _dj), n in links.items()], np.int64).reshape(-1, 2)
    body_of_cell = groundnav1943.components(cs.n, pairs)

    class G:
        i: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
        j: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
    grid = G()                                          # what join_pieces reads of a ground grid: i, j
    grid.i, grid.j = cs.i, cs.j

    def line(ka: int, kb: int) -> list[int] | None:
        return [ka, kb] if cell_line(nav, (int(cs.i[ka]), int(cs.j[ka])), (int(cs.i[kb]), int(cs.j[kb]))) else None
    saved = groundnav1943.grid_line
    groundnav1943.grid_line = lambda _g, _t, a, b: line(a, b)
    try:
        nodes, edges = groundnav1943.join_pieces(grid, None, table, body_of_cell, node_cells, edges, log)
    finally:
        groundnav1943.grid_line = saved
    return nodes, edges


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='seanav1943.py', description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('level')
    parser.add_argument('--soldier', help='the soldier world (default work\\levels\\<level>\\navkit\\<level>.rsnv)')
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    files = paths(args.level)
    soldier = args.soldier or files['soldier']
    if not os.path.isfile(soldier):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{args.level}: no soldier world (missing {soldier}): '
                                f'run navexport1943.py {args.level}')
    build(args.level, soldier)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('seanav1943', gui=False)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/tools/soldier1943.py`:

```py
"""NavKit (big-endian): BF1943's soldier, and the NavKit settings that follow from it.

NavKit's defaults come from BFBC2: some are BFBC2's soldier, some were fitted to DICE's BFBC2 path data
(navbuild.BFBC2). For BF1943 the soldier's values come from the game (Objects/Soldiers/Common/DefaultSoldierPhysics:
CharacterPhysicsData and the Stand pose; BFBC2's soldier has the same values), and SETTINGS holds the NavKit settings
that depend on them, with the rules BF1943's levels needed. The BF1943 tools pass them where they are used:

  import soldier1943
  navbuild.build(..., step=soldier1943.STEP, max_water_depth=soldier1943.WATER_DEPTH, settings=soldier1943.SETTINGS)
  detailed.stacked_columns(samples, xoff, zoff, slope_max=soldier1943.SLOPE_MAX,
                           cm_sectors=soldier1943.SETTINGS.column_sectors_cm)

(Until 2026-10-31 configure() wrote these into navbuild's, navwalk's and detailed's module constants, and a build
was BF1943's only when it had run first.)
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import navbuild  # bf1943-auto-navkit-common's (one copy for both NavKit variants since 2026-10-31)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from bfbc2core.terrain import Heightfield

RADIUS = 0.35                   # PhysicalRadius
STEP_HEIGHT = 0.3               # StepHeight
STEP_TOLERANCE = 0.07           # the soldier climbs a little more than StepHeight: in game he walks into Wake's beach
                                # bunker (mil_bunker_t01v01) over a 0.33 m lip at its door (2026-10-23). The real limit
                                # is not measured; 0.07 keeps a small margin over what was seen.
STEP = STEP_HEIGHT + STEP_TOLERANCE
HEIGHT = 1.8                    # Height (Stand; Crouch 1.15)
SLOPE_MAX = 45.0                # MaxAscendAngle (deg)
WATER_DEPTH = 1.4               # WaterDepthLimit (m): pass as navbuild.build(max_water_depth=...), a default argument
NO_WATER_BELOW = 10.0           # m: a level without water gets its sea this far under its lowest terrain (sea_level)


def has_water(settings: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Whether navkit.py prepare found water on the level (navkit.json's sea_level is None without)."""
    return settings.get('sea_level') is not None


def sea_level(settings: Mapping[str, Any], heightfield: 'Heightfield') -> float:
    """The water height every tool computes with (navexport1943, jumplinks1943, groundnav1943, airnav1943, seanav1943,
    navaudit1943_checks): navkit.json's sea_level, or for a level without water (navkit.py prepare found no water mesh:
    None) NO_WATER_BELOW under the lowest terrain, so no ground counts as under water and the build, which had no water
    either, agrees. (Before 2026-10-30 the soldier export took 0, which puts water over any ground below 0 m, the
    vehicle builders and the jump links raised TypeError on None, and the audit took -1e9.)"""
    if has_water(settings):
        return float(settings['sea_level'])
    return float(heightfield.heights.min()) - NO_WATER_BELOW


def sea_level_args(settings: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """navsample1943's --sea-level (it bounds the sampled box by the land); none without water: the whole height field."""
    return ['--sea-level', str(settings['sea_level'])] if has_water(settings) else []


SETTINGS = navbuild.Settings(
    slope_max=SLOPE_MAX,                # BFBC2 NavKit: 40 (detailed.stacked_columns takes SLOPE_MAX too)
    # nodes and outlines stand half the soldier's height above the ground (EntityHeight / 2; BFBC2 NavKit: 1.9 / 2)
    y_offset=HEIGHT / 2,
    # NavKit's band (0.5, 2.0) is fitted to DICE's BFBC2 data; the soldier stands 1.8 m, and navsample1943's capsule
    # test already blocks less headroom. The 2.0 end removed open ground at Wake's airfield bunker door (1.94 m).
    headroom_band=(0.5, HEIGHT),
    # the height step that links straight neighbours in a detailed zone (one 0.2 m cell); NavKit's 0.3 is DICE's
    # one-cell steps (p99 0.31): below the soldier's step, a lip he climbs would not link
    detailed_link_step=STEP,
    # a ladder links to each piece of ground beside its ends, not only the nearest surface (Wake's towers: the floor
    # enclosed by the frame is nearer the foot than the ground outside, from which the ladder is climbed)
    ladder_all_ground=True,
    # shared border nodes also on the seam line itself, for ground that reaches the seam but not the border line one
    # sample beyond (Coral Sea's three seam breaks, 2026-10-26)
    border_seam_line=True,
    # an area holds no cliff between plan-neighbouring cells (a bridge deck beside the ground under it): the RSNV height
    # grid cannot hold one (2026-10-26: 66 of Wake Island's 75 remaining tight edges lay in such areas). 0.6 m from
    # 2026-10-29 (was 1.0): a 0.2 m cell's 45-degree rise plus the step is 0.57 m straight, 0.65 m diagonal (the rule's
    # other term), so cells further apart are no walk; 34-44 areas per map held such pairs 0.6-1.0 m apart (Coral Sea
    # area 3133: 78.45 beside 79.41), the height grid read them as a ramp, and 5 of the 22 remaining tight pairs met one
    area_cliff=0.6,
    # and between cells two apart across a cell the area does not hold (2026-10-29, round 5): the per-cell height grid
    # carried a floor across the empty cell to the floor 1.56 m below it (Iwo Jima (-92.0, 20.7, -17.4): kept 0.2 m
    # ground at 20.72-20.75 m along the edge, a strip at 19.16 m one empty row away in the same area)
    area_cliff_reach=2,
    # join_groups floods 2 m past a sector's window: ground joined to the rest of its sector only round a corner of
    # the neighbour sector (Coral Sea's last seam break, 2026-10-26)
    join_margin=2.0,
    # beside a mixed seam, the 0.8 m graph is told where the 0.2 m samples join ground its step rule cannot (a lip the
    # coarse grid does not resolve: Coral Sea's last seam break, 2026-10-26)
    seam_fine_links=True,
    # ... and where that 0.2 m ground joins 0.8 m pieces two columns apart across columns the 0.8 m grid kept nothing in
    # (Iwo Jima's last seam break, 2026-10-29)
    seam_far_links=True,
    # a sector's window grows 1 m past a mixed seam, so both grids' cells overlap there (2026-10-26)
    mixed_overlap=1.0,
    # a shared node wherever kept ground meets a mixed seam on both grids and no carried node joins it (2026-10-24:
    # Wake Island's Japanese carrier, Coral Sea's islets); a module constant on in the big-endian copy until
    # 2026-10-31, a setting since the two copies were merged (the little-endian copy, BFBC2's, never had it)
    seam_gap_nodes=True,
    # a column's sector from whole centimetres, as NavKit's default (navbuild.COLUMN_SECTORS_CM; 2026-11). The float
    # position BF1943's builds took until then put a column on a sector line in the sector before it: Guadalcanal's
    # one row on z = -400.0 made a sector of its own (0c06: one area, 2 nodes, 12 cells 0c07 holds too). The rebuild
    # changed nothing else on the four maps: the same detailed sectors, routes, islands, tight edges and pockets
    column_sectors_cm=True,
    # after the merge, the links between two normal sectors by the 0.8 m grid's own step rule, not the 0.2 m grid's
    # (navbuild.NORMAL_LINKS_OWN_GRID; 2026-11: the 0.2 m rule left 44 of Guadalcanal's 199 and 84 of Coral Sea's 410
    # normal-to-normal border portals without a neighbour link)
    normal_links_own_grid=True,
)
```

```py
r"""NavKit (big-endian): BF1943's vehicle classes as the vehicle navigation needs them - size and movement limits read
from the vehicles' own blueprints and collision, and the navigation parameters that follow from them.

  vehicleclasses1943.py [--game <dist\xenon>] [--json <out.json>]     prints the table (and writes it as JSON)

  import vehicleclasses1943 as vc
  vc.CLASSES['jeep']                 # the navigation parameters of a class (radius, height, step, slope, ...)
  vc.read(game)                      # {vehicle name: what its blueprint and collision give}

estimate with its basis, [H] a hypothesis, [U] not known. BFBC2 is a lead only: its vehicle graphs used one radius,
2.5 m, for every vehicle (KYNAPSE_SPEC 4.3).

What the data gives (read 2026-10-26, Wake Island's bundles; every MP level shares levels-common-00.fbrb):
  - size: the collision's bounding box (the vehicle's *_havok.res: meshes and convex shapes) [O];
  - wheels and tracks: wheel positions (WheelComponentData Transform), radius and spring (WheelConfigData) [O];

        'radius': (25.0, '[E] clearance kept from terrain and objects in flight'),
        'cruise_agl': (60.0, '[E] cruise height over the altitude floor (design 4.2)'),
        'speed': (130 / 3.6, '[O] last forward gear 130 (km/h [H]); flight speed itself [U]'),
        'takeoff_run': (120.0, '[E] the carrier decks are 235 m [O]; the take-off roll is not in the data [U]'),
        'turn_radius': (150.0, '[E] at cruise speed'),
        'pitch': (16.0, 'altitude-floor grid cell (m)'),
        'node_spacing': (4, 'cells between route nodes (64 m)'),
    },
}
CLASS_IDS = {'jeep': 1, 'tank': 2, 'lcvp': 3, 'plane': 4}       # the RSNV layer / OFFM vehicle class of each file


def value(cls: str, key: str) -> Any:
    """A class's navigation parameter (CLASSES[cls][key] without its label)."""
    return CLASSES[cls][key][0]


# ---- what each vehicle step was made from (navkit.json 'vehicles') -------------------------------------------------
# 2026-10-30: the vehicle collision was made again only when its file was missing, and the samples reused whatever was
# on disk, so a new preparation (another game copy, other objects) kept the old collision and samples. Each step now
# stamps navkit.json: 'vehicles': {'collision': stamp, 'samples': {class: stamp}, 'worlds': {class: stamp}}, every
# stamp the preparation's digest and game folder ('preparation', 'game'), a class's also the digest of its parameters
# ('params': for the samples only those the sampler reads, SAMPLING_PARAMS; for a world every one), a world's also the
# SHA-256 of the soldier world it was built on ('soldier'), or 'absent' with why when the level has no such world (no
# spawns of the class, no water). navkit.py prepare writes a new navkit.json (every stamp goes); a soldier sampling or
# build drops the worlds' stamps (navkit.invalidate); the next step needs its input's stamp to be current, and refuses
# or makes it again. Every write is a fresh read-modify-write (navkitjson1943.update).

class StaleError(RuntimeError):
    """A vehicle step's input is of another preparation, game copy, class parameters or soldier world."""


SAMPLING_PARAMS = ('radius', 'step', 'height', 'pitch')   # what navsample1943 is given (groundnav1943.sample_command)


def params_id(cls: str, keys: Container[str] | None = None) -> str:
    """The digest of a class's navigation parameters: every value of CLASSES[cls], or only keys."""
    import hashlib
    values = {key: (entry[0] if isinstance(entry, tuple) else entry) for key, entry in CLASSES[cls].items()
              if keys is None or key in keys}
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(values, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()


def sampling_params_id(cls: str) -> str:
    """The digest of the parameters the class's samples depend on (2026-10-30: every parameter was hashed, so a new
    speed or node spacing sampled again for nothing)."""
    return params_id(cls, SAMPLING_PARAMS)


def inputs(st: 'nj.Settings', lv: str, cls: str | None = None, sampling: bool = False, **extra: Any) -> Stamp:
    """The stamp a vehicle step of the current preparation makes (and the one its next step needs); sampling: the
    class's samples' (their parameters only those the sampler reads)."""
    if not st.get('preparation'):
        raise StaleError(f'{lv}: prepared without a preparation stamp (an older NavKit): prepare again '
                         f'(navkit.py prepare {lv})')
    out = {'preparation': st['preparation'], 'game': st.get('game')}
    if cls is not None:
        out.update({'class': cls, 'params': sampling_params_id(cls) if sampling else params_id(cls)})
    out.update(extra)
    return out


def stamp(st: Mapping[str, Any], kind: str, cls: str | None = None) -> Any:
    """A vehicle step's stamp in navkit.json ('collision'; 'samples' or 'worlds' with a class), or None."""
    of_kind = (st.get('vehicles') or {}).get(kind)
    return (of_kind or {}).get(cls) if cls is not None else of_kind


def current(st: Mapping[str, Any], kind: str, want: Mapping[str, Any], cls: str | None = None) -> bool:
    """Whether the step's stamp in st is want (its time and what it found aside)."""
    have = stamp(st, kind, cls)
    return have is not None and all(have.get(key) == wanted for key, wanted in want.items())


def soldier_changed(st: Mapping[str, Any], lv: str, soldier: str) -> str | None:
    """Why a world built on the soldier world whose SHA-256 is soldier may not be stamped now (None when it may): that
    file must still be the export of the current, passed build (navkit.json 'exported' and 'build_from')."""
    built = st.get('build_from') or {}
    exported = st.get('exported') or {}
    if 'built' not in st or not built.get('hpd_sha256') or exported.get('hpd_sha256') != built['hpd_sha256'] \
            or exported.get('sha256') != soldier or not nj.check_passed(st):
        return (f'{lv}: the soldier world changed while the vehicle world was built (built, checked or exported again): '
                f'it is not stamped; build it again (navexport_vehicles1943.py {lv})')
    return None


def record(lv: str, kind: str, value: Mapping[str, Any], cls: str | None = None,
           soldier_path: str | None = None) -> 'nj.Settings':
    """Stamps a finished step; nothing when navkit.json now holds another preparation (prepared meanwhile). A world
    (a value with 'soldier') built on the default soldier world (soldier_path None or that file, as soldier_world
    tells it) is refused with StaleError, and not stamped, when that file is no longer the export of the current
    build: 2026-10-30 second review, a world finished after the soldier was built again was stamped, and the vehicle
    check took it as current while the old export was still on disk."""
    import time
    value = dict(value, time=time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'))
    refused: list[str] = []
    default_soldier = soldier_path is None or nj.same_file(soldier_path,
                                                           os.path.join(nj.paths(lv)['navkit'], f'{lv}.rsnv'))

    def change(st: 'nj.Settings') -> None:
        if st.get('preparation') != value['preparation']:
            return
        if 'soldier' in value and default_soldier:
            why = soldier_changed(st, lv, value['soldier'])
            if why:
                refused.append(why)
                return
        vehicles = st.setdefault('vehicles', {})
        if cls is None:
            vehicles[kind] = value
        else:
            vehicles.setdefault(kind, {})[cls] = value
    st = nj.update(lv, change)
    if refused:
        raise StaleError(refused[0])
    return st


def drop(lv: str, kind: str, cls: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Removes a step's stamp before it runs: an interrupted run leaves none."""
    def change(st: 'nj.Settings') -> None:
        vehicles = st.get('vehicles') or {}
        if cls is None:
            vehicles.pop(kind, None)
        else:
            (vehicles.get(kind) or {}).pop(cls, None)
    if os.path.isfile(nj.paths(lv)['settings']):
        nj.update(lv, change)


def absent(lv: str, cls: str, want: Mapping[str, Any], path: str, why: str,
           log: Callable[[str], object] = print) -> None:
    """The level has no world of the class (its data says so: no spawns of it, no water): a world file of an earlier
    run goes, and the stamp says why (navexport_vehicles1943.check tells this from a world not built)."""
    if os.path.isfile(path):
        os.remove(path)
        log(f'{lv}: {os.path.basename(path)} of an earlier run removed ({why})')
    record(lv, 'worlds', dict(want, absent=why), cls)


def prepared_game(st: Mapping[str, Any], game: str | None, lv: str) -> str | None:
    """The game copy the level was prepared from; a different one given is refused (navkit.same_game's rule: the
    same folder by identity, navkitjson1943.same_file)."""
    want = st.get('game')
    if game is None:
        return want
    if not nj.same_file(want, game):
        raise StaleError(f'{lv}: prepared from {want}, not {game}: use that copy, or prepare again (navkit.py prepare {lv})')
    return game


def soldier_world(st: Mapping[str, Any], lv: str, path: str) -> str:
    """The SHA-256 of the soldier world a vehicle world is built on. Refused when it is missing, when the soldier build
    is not of the current preparation, or (the default <level>.rsnv, by file identity) when the file is not the export
    of the current build: the export's stamp names the build by its .hpd's SHA-256 (navkit.json 'build_from'
    'hpd_sha256'; 2026-10-30: by its 'built' minute, which a quick rebuild repeats)."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{lv}: no soldier world (missing {path}): export it (navexport1943.py {lv})')
    built = st.get('build_from') or {}
    if built.get('preparation') != st.get('preparation') or 'built' not in st or not built.get('hpd_sha256'):
        raise StaleError(f'{lv}: the soldier build is not of the current preparation: build and export it again '
                         f'(navkit.py build {lv}; navexport1943.py {lv})')
    if not nj.check_passed(st):              # 2026-10-30 review: a build whose check failed was exported and stamped
        raise StaleError(f'{lv}: the soldier build\'s check did not pass ({st.get("checked") or "not checked"}): no '
                         f'vehicle world is built on it (navkit.py check {lv})')
    digest = nj.sha256(path)
    exported = st.get('exported') or {}
    default = os.path.join(nj.paths(lv)['navkit'], f'{lv}.rsnv')
    if nj.same_file(path, default) and (exported.get('sha256') != digest
                                        or exported.get('hpd_sha256') != built['hpd_sha256']):
        raise StaleError(f'{lv}: {path} is not the export of the current build: export again (navexport1943.py {lv})')
    return digest


def _fields(xml: str, name: str) -> list[str]:
    """The text of every <field name="name"> in a partition's XML."""
    return re.findall(r'<field name="' + re.escape(name) + r'">([^<]*)</field>', xml)


def _instances(xml: str, typename: str) -> list[str]:
    """The XML of every instance of a type (its name without the namespace)."""
    return re.findall(r'<instance[^>]*type="[^"]*\.' + typename + r'"[^>]*>.*?</instance>', xml, re.S)


def _translation(inst: str) -> list[float] | None:
    """An instance's Transform translation (x, y, z), or None."""
    match = re.search(r'<complex name="Transform">([^<]*)</complex>', inst)
    if not match:
        return None
    values = [float(t) for t in match.group(1).split('/')]
    return [round(x, 3) for x in values[12:15]] if len(values) == 16 else None


def collision_box(game: 'Game', res: str) -> Box | None:
    """(min, max) of a vehicle's collision (meshes and convex shapes of its *_havok.res), or None."""
    import havok461
    import hkpack
    data = game.data(res)
    if not data:
        return None
    packfile = hkpack.Packfile(data, classes=havok461.CLASSES)
    points = []
    for offset in packfile.objects_of('hkStorageExtendedMeshShapeMeshSubpartStorage'):
        vertices, _triangles = havok461.triangles(packfile, offset)
        if vertices:
            points.append(np.asarray(vertices, float)[:, :3])
    for offset in packfile.objects_of('hkConvexVerticesShape'):
        box, _, _ = havok461.convex_box(packfile, offset)
        if box:
            points.append(np.asarray(box, float).reshape(-1, 3))
    if not points:
        return None
    every = np.concatenate(points)
    return every.min(0).round(3).tolist(), every.max(0).round(3).tolist()


def read(game_dir: str | None = None, level: str = 'wake_island_s') -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """{vehicle: {...}} from the blueprints and collision of your copy (every value [O]); hashes of the inputs."""
    import hashlib
    from bfbc2core import dbx, game1943
    level_game = game1943.Game(game1943.find_game(game_dir), level)
    out: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for name, (cls, part, res) in VEHICLES.items():
        data = level_game.data(part + '.dbx')
        if data is None:
            out[name] = {'class': cls, 'missing': part}
            continue
        xml = dbx.to_xml(data)
        xml = xml if isinstance(xml, str) else xml.decode('utf-8')

        def floats(field: str) -> list[float]:
            return [float(text) for text in _fields(xml, field)]
        wheels: dict[str | int, list[float] | None] = {}     # wheel name (or its number): its local position
        for inst in _instances(xml, 'WheelComponentData'):
            name_match = re.search(r'<field name="Name">([^<]*)<', inst)
            wheels[name_match.group(1) if name_match else len(wheels)] = _translation(inst)
        exits = [_translation(inst) for inst in _instances(xml, 'VehicleExitPointComponentData')]
        entries = []
        for inst in _instances(xml, 'PlayerEntryComponentData') + _instances(xml, 'LandingGearEntryComponentData'):
            name_match = re.search(r'<field name="Name">([^<]*)<', inst)
            radius_match = re.search(r'<field name="EntryRadius">([^<]*)<', inst)
            entries.append({'name': name_match.group(1) if name_match else '', 'local': _translation(inst),
                            'radius': float(radius_match.group(1)) if radius_match else None})
        gears = [[float(speed) for speed in speeds.split('/')]
                 for speeds in re.findall(r'<array name="ForwardGearSpeeds">([^<]*)<', xml)]
        box = collision_box(level_game, res)
        collision_data = level_game.data(res)
        spring_lengths = re.findall(r'<complex name="Spring">\s*<field name="Length">([^<]*)<', xml)
        out[name] = {
            'class': cls, 'blueprint': part + '.dbx', 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
            'collision': res,
            'collision_sha256': hashlib.sha256(collision_data).hexdigest() if collision_data else None,
            'collision_box': box,
            'size': [round(b - a, 3) for a, b in zip(*box)] if box else None,
            'body_mass': floats('BodyMass')[:1],
            'wheel_radius': floats('Radius')[:2] if wheels else [],
            'spring_length': [float(length) for length in spring_lengths],
            'slope_grip_min': floats('SlopeGripMinAngle'), 'slope_grip_max': floats('SlopeGripMaxAngle'),
            'steering_type': [int(text) for text in _fields(xml, 'SteeringType')],
            'forward_gear_speeds': gears, 'top_gear_speed': max((max(speeds) for speeds in gears), default=None),
            'wheels': wheels, 'entries': entries, 'exits': exits,
            'water_jet': 'true' in _fields(xml, 'IsWaterJetEngine'),
            'float_physics': [t for t in ('BoatFloatPhysicsData', 'BoxFloatPhysicsData') if _instances(xml, t)],
        }
        if len(wheels) >= 4:
            wheel_pos = np.array([at for wheel, at in wheels.items() if str(wheel).startswith('Wheel ') and at], float)
            if len(wheel_pos) >= 4:
                out[name]['wheelbase'] = round(float(wheel_pos[:, 2].max() - wheel_pos[:, 2].min()), 3)
                out[name]['track'] = round(float(wheel_pos[:, 0].max() - wheel_pos[:, 0].min()), 3)
    return out


def check(table: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]) -> list[str]:
    """Problems where the [O] parameters of CLASSES disagree with the data read ([] when none)."""
    problems = []
    for cls, params in CLASSES.items():
        # the wider side (x) of the class's collision boxes
        half_width = max((max(-vehicle['collision_box'][0][0], vehicle['collision_box'][1][0])
                          for _name, vehicle in table.items()
                          if vehicle.get('class') == cls and vehicle.get('collision_box')), default=None)
        if half_width is not None and abs(half_width - params['half_width'][0]) > 0.06:
            problems.append(f'{cls}: half-width {params["half_width"][0]} against the collision\'s {half_width:.2f}')
        if cls in ('jeep', 'tank'):
            grip = max((max(vehicle['slope_grip_max']) for vehicle in table.values()
                        if vehicle.get('class') == cls and vehicle.get('slope_grip_max')), default=None)
            if cls == 'jeep' and grip is not None and grip != params['slope'][0]:
                problems.append(f'jeep: slope {params["slope"][0]} against SlopeGripMaxAngle {grip}')
    return problems


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='vehicleclasses1943.py', description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('--game')
    parser.add_argument('--json')
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    table = read(args.game)
    for name, vehicle in table.items():
        print(f'{name:18s} {vehicle["class"]:6s} size {vehicle.get("size")} mass {vehicle.get("body_mass")} slope grip '
              f'{vehicle.get("slope_grip_min")}..{vehicle.get("slope_grip_max")} '
              f'top gear {vehicle.get("top_gear_speed")} wheelbase {vehicle.get("wheelbase")} '
              f'track {vehicle.get("track")} entries {len(vehicle.get("entries", []))} '
              f'exits {len(vehicle.get("exits", []))}')
    for cls, params in CLASSES.items():
        print(f'{cls}: ' + ', '.join(f'{key} {entry[0]:g}' for key, entry in params.items() if key != 'vehicles'))
    problems = check(table)
    for problem in problems:
        print('MISMATCH ' + problem)
    if args.json:
        classes = {cls: {key: (list(entry) if isinstance(entry, tuple) else entry) for key, entry in params.items()}
                   for cls, params in CLASSES.items()}
        with open(args.json, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
            json.dump({'vehicles': table, 'classes': classes}, f, indent=1)
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('vehicleclasses1943', gui=False)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/README.md`:

```md
# NavKit, the modules both variants use (bf1943-auto-navkit-common)

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** (2026-10-31) - the BF1943 pipeline
(`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian`) builds with these modules and BF1943's settings; the BFBC2 pipeline
(`bf1943-auto-navkit-little-endian`) with the same modules and NavKit's defaults.

Until 2026-10-31 each NavKit variant had its own copy of these modules: 14 module names were in both, 10 of the files
the same but for their bootstrap line, the rest forks (the builder, the walkability rules, the `.hpd` reader and the
mesh model, the Havok 4.6.1 reader, the level objects, the samples, the detailed-sector rule), and which copy a
script got depended on the order it named the variants in (`core/suitepath.py`). Now there is one copy of each, in
`tools\`, a shared folder (`suitepath.SHARED`, pyproject's `dev-mode-dirs`): every script and library finds them
without naming a variant, and no module name is in two of the suite's folders (`tests\test_repo.py` checks it).

How NavKit is built, these modules among the rest: the big-endian kit's
[ARCHITECTURE.md](../bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## What was merged, and how both kits get what they had

Each fork was merged into one module that serves both kits through explicit settings. Checked 2026-10-31: the four
BF1943 maps built as `navkit.py build` builds them and exported to RSNV (`.hpd`, `.rsnv` and the `.cells.npz` arrays),
and two BFBC2 levels built as `navregress.py` builds them (sp_009, ONS_MP_004), come out byte for byte as before the
merge.

| Module | Merged from | How the two kits keep their behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `navbuild` (a package) | the big-endian copy (BF1943's rules, the `Settings`), with the little-endian copy's later fixes | `build(settings=...)`: `navbuild.BFBC2` (NavKit's defaults, the little-endian kit's builds) or `soldier1943.SETTINGS` (BF1943). Two rules that were not settings are now: `seam_gap_nodes` (always on in the big-endian copy, never in the little-endian one) and `column_sectors_cm` (a sample column's sector from whole centimetres, the little-endian fix; BF1943's builds kept the float rule until 2026-11, and take the fix since, after a rebuild and an audit). `normal_links_own_grid` (2026-11, on for BF1943): after the merge, links between two 0.8 m sectors by the 0.8 m step rule; NavKit's default keeps the 0.2 m rule every build had until BFBC2's builds are measured with it. The little-endian copy's checks (a sampling run on another grid, no walkable ground, a file that does not read back: `BuildError`), its atomic file write, its detailed pass made again without sectors that have no 0.2 m ground, and its guard against a ladder linked to itself are kept for both; none of them fires on a BF1943 build |
| `navwalk.py` | the big-endian copy (the soldier's headroom band and lip width as arguments, jump-link bands, `ladder_end_options`) | the little-endian copy's `coarse(f, pitch)`, its roof rule's lowest surface over non-empty columns only (it differs only for the last non-empty column when empty ones follow it), and its `score` guard |
| `hpdtool.py`, `kymesh.py` | the little-endian copies | their damaged-file checks (a truncated file, overlapping blocks, a mesh without its trailer, a portal to no area, an area in no tile) |
| `havok461.py` | the little-endian copy | a last triangle stored without its padding word is kept; every one of the 3,721 meshes in your BF1943 copy's 445 Havok files has a whole number of padded triangles, so no BF1943 output changes |
| `levelobjects.py` | the little-endian copy (Havok 4.6.1 collision, `NeedsDetailedPathfinding`) | the big-endian copy's JSON files written through `with` blocks |
| `detailed.py` | the little-endian copy (the flag DICE's zones follow, the sampled-run record, the offsets from `navkit.json`) | the big-endian copy's `slope_max`; `stacked_columns(cm_sectors=...)`, the sector rule as in `navbuild` (`detailed1943.py` passes BF1943's) |
| `navsample.py` | the little-endian copy (`column_sectors`, a run stopped inside a column) | |
| `hkpack.py`, `hpdcheck.py`, `hpdview.py`, `navedits.py` | either: the same | |
| `navdiff.py` | the little-endian kit's only copy | moved here so core's `navdata.py` needs no NavKit variant |

The OPFOR copies' provenance (`provenance/opfor-imports.json`) records the move: `tools\import_opfor.py --update`
leaves these files out of the little-endian kit and reports an OPFOR change to one as a conflict to merge by hand
here.

## The builder package (`tools\navbuild\`)

`navbuild.py` (2,315 lines) split along its stages; `import navbuild` and every name it had (`navbuild.build`,
`navbuild.Settings`, `navbuild.BFBC2`, `navbuild.stage`, `navbuild.read_cells`, the constants, ...) work as before.

| Module | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `__init__.py` | `build()`: the normal stage, the detailed stage and the merge, the file; the package's names re-exported |
| `config.py` | the documented constants (defaults, never changed at run time), `Settings`, `BFBC2`, `BuildError`, `Grid` / `grid_at`, `BuildState`, `JoinScope` |
| `inputs.py` | input assembly: the sampling runs on the stage's grid (`to_pitch`, `same_grid`), the water and extent rules, a column's sector, the walkable surfaces (`Level`), and `stage_level`, which puts them together for a stage |
| `areas.py` | a stage's sectors, tiles and areas, their traced boundaries (portals, border portals, outlines with 45-degree bridges) and the links between sectors |
| `graph.py` | a sector's route graph (nodes, walk edges, joined groups, order and ladder nodes) and its final tables |
| `stages.py` | `stage`: one grid's build, not yet written |
| `seams.py` | links across mixed-pitch seams after the merge: gap nodes, fine and far links |
| `merge.py` | `merge_detailed` (the 0.2 m stage over the detailed sectors, merged with the normal build) and `merge_coincident_border` |
| `write.py` | the `.hpd` file and its `<name>.cells.npz` |
| `__main__.py` | the command line: `python -B -m navbuild <samples.bin> <forbid_tris.npy> <XOffset> <ZOffset> <out.hpd> [...]` (in `tools\`) |

A test that switches a rule sets it in the module that reads it (`navbuild.areas.ONE_WAY_PORTALS`), and one that
replaces a step replaces it where it is called (`navbuild.write_file` for `build`, `navbuild.merge.stage` for the
detailed pass).

## Layout

```
research\KYNAPSE_SPEC.md   the path-data format and the builder's stages (one copy; was in both variants)
research\img\              its pictures
tools\                     the shared modules (on sys.path for every script: suitepath.SHARED)
  navbuild\                the generator: samples + level objects -> a navigation file (pathdata.hpd layout)
  navwalk.py               walkability rules
  navsample.py             the samples file format: read, and compare with a path-data file
  navedits.py              walkability edits as generator inputs
  hpdtool.py               the navigation file: info / sector / roundtrip / coverage / meshtrip
  kymesh.py                per-sector mesh: parse_mesh / write_mesh (byte-exact)
  hpdcheck.py              structure checks (closed boundaries, edges, node order, zero-length edges)
  hpdview.py               render one sector to PNG
  navdiff.py               two navigation files compared layer by layer (core's navdata reads cells with it)
  hkpack.py                Havok binary packfile reader: 5.5 (BFBC2) and 4.6.1 (BF1943), byte order from the file
  havok461.py              class layouts for Havok 4.6.1 packfiles, which have no __types__ section
  levelobjects.py          BFBC2's level objects and the pathfinding-flag rules; the collision index
  detailed.py              the detailed-sector rule (BF1943: the big-endian kit's detailed1943.py applies it)
tests\                     the rule tests (made-up data) of these modules, and the Havok 4.6.1 test (your copy)
```

## Tests

`python -B ..\run_tests.py quick` runs the made-up-data tests here ("NavKit (both variants): ..."): the water,
area-link, portal, headroom, lip, roof, dynamic-prop and character rules, the 45-degree bridges, walkability edits,
the collision index, the builder's edge cases under NavKit's defaults (`test_navbuild_edges.py`) and the readers on
damaged files (`test_formats.py`). `bf1943` adds `test_havok461.py` (Wake Island's Havok files, and the collision
reader on them). The BF1943 settings are tested in the big-endian kit (`test_mixed_seam.py`, the steps and the
export).
```
