`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/hpdcheck.py`:

```py
"""NavKit: structural checks of a pathdata.hpd - what DICE's files always satisfy and the game relies on.

  hpdcheck.py <pathdata.hpd> [...]          exit code 0 when every file passes, 1 otherwise

Checks, per file:
  closed boundaries   every area's outline, portals and border portals meet in pairs at every end point (DICE: no
                      open area; an open one misleads point-in-area tests - navbuild.BRIDGE_UNION)
  edges               every edge's two node indices exist in its sector
  node order          each sector's nodes sorted by unsigned id, border nodes (id flag 80000000h) after the others
                      (the game binary-searches these arrays - navbuild.SORT_NODES_BY_ID)
  zero-length edges   no edge between two different nodes at one position (navbuild.DEDUP_GRAPH_NODES)
Every check holds on DICE's 15 files (13 campaign levels, ONS_MP_002 / 004; 2026-10-23). Not checked: the owner bit
of border nodes (field c bit 16) - DICE's files have border nodes with no owner copy and with two or more.
"""
import os
import sys
from collections import Counter

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import hpdtool  # noqa: E402
import kymesh  # noqa: E402

BORDER = 0x80000000


def check(path: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """{check name: [problem descriptions]} (empty lists: passed)."""
    hpd = hpdtool.parse(open(path, 'rb').read())
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {'closed boundaries': [], 'edges': [], 'node order': [], 'zero-length edges': []}
    for sector in hpd.sectors:
        mesh = kymesh.parse_mesh(sector.mesh)
        for ai, area in enumerate(mesh.areas):
            ends: Counter[tuple[float, float]] = Counter()      # (x, z) of a segment end -> segments ending there
            segs = [(line[k], line[k + 1]) for line in area.outline for k in range(len(line) - 1)]
            segs += ([(portal.p0, portal.p1) for portal in area.portals]
                     + [(border.p0, border.p1) for border in area.border_portals])
            for p0, p1 in segs:
                ends[(round(p0[0], 2), round(p0[2], 2))] += 1
                ends[(round(p1[0], 2), round(p1[2], 2))] += 1
            odd = [point for point, count in ends.items() if count % 2]
            if odd:
                out['closed boundaries'].append(f'sector {sector.id:04x} area {ai}: {len(odd)} open end(s), '
                                                f'e.g. {odd[0]}')
        node_count = len(sector.nodes)
        for edge in sector.edges:
            if not (0 <= edge.src < node_count and 0 <= edge.dst < node_count):
                out['edges'].append(f'sector {sector.id:04x}: edge {edge.src} -> {edge.dst} of {node_count} nodes')
                continue
            src, dst = sector.nodes[edge.src], sector.nodes[edge.dst]
            if src.id != dst.id and tuple(src.pos) == tuple(dst.pos):
                out['zero-length edges'].append(f'sector {sector.id:04x}: nodes {src.id:08x} and {dst.id:08x} at '
                                                f'{tuple(round(v, 2) for v in src.pos)}')
        ids = [node.id & 0xFFFFFFFF for node in sector.nodes]
        key = [((node_id & BORDER) != 0, node_id) for node_id in ids]
        if key != sorted(key):
            out['node order'].append(f'sector {sector.id:04x}: nodes not sorted by id with border nodes last')
    return out


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if any(arg in ('-h', '--help') for arg in argv[1:]):
        print(__doc__)
        return 0
    if len(argv) < 2:
        print(__doc__)
        return 1
    bad = 0
    for path in argv[1:]:
        problems = check(path)
        fails = {name: found for name, found in problems.items() if found}
        bad += bool(fails)
        print(f'{"ok  " if not fails else "FAIL"} {os.path.basename(path)}' +
              ''.join(f'\n       {name}: {len(found)} - {found[0]}' for name, found in fails.items()))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/hpdtool.py`:

```py
"""hpdtool.py - reader/writer for BFBC2 Kynapse navigation data (pathdata.hpd).

Part of BC2 NavKit (see ..\\README.md; written from ..\\research\\KYNAPSE_SPEC.md).

Usage:
    python hpdtool.py info <pathdata.hpd>                 file summary
    python hpdtool.py sector <pathdata.hpd> <index>       one sector: nodes, edges, mesh header
    python hpdtool.py roundtrip <file-or-folder>...       parse + write back, compare byte for byte
    python hpdtool.py coverage <file-or-folder>...        check every byte of every runtime mesh is explained
    python hpdtool.py meshtrip <file-or-folder>...        structured mesh model (kymesh.py) round trip

Sector.mesh holds the raw runtime-mesh record; kymesh.parse_mesh / write_mesh convert it to and
from the structured model (areas, portals, outlines, cells, neighbour links).
"""
import os
import struct
import sys
from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()

MAGIC = b'Kynogon HPD\0'
HEADER_WORDS = 36           # u32 words after the magic (0x0C..0x9B)
HEADER_SIZE = 12 + HEADER_WORDS * 4
TABLE_ENTRY = struct.Struct('<I6f5I')  # 48 bytes
NODE = struct.Struct('<I3fIf3I')       # 36 bytes
EDGE = struct.Struct('<3I')            # 12 bytes
MESH_MARKER = b'KynogonRuntimeMesh'


@dataclass
class Node:
    id: int                  # node id; high bit = border node shared with a neighbouring sector
                             # (same id and position appear in that sector too)
    pos: tuple[float, float, float]  # world position, Y up
    flags: int               # always 0x80000000
    value: float             # DistEdgeMax on the first node of a sector (infantry 15, vehicle 50), else 0
    a: int                   # index of this node's first outgoing edge + 1 (edges are sorted by source)
    b: int                   # low u16: entry of the node list sorted by x; high u16: sorted by y
    c: int                   # low u16: entry of the node list sorted by z; bit 16: border node


@dataclass
class Edge:
    tag: int                 # cost: 0x80000000 | floor(3-D distance between the nodes * 16)
    src: int
    dst: int


@dataclass
class Sector:
    id: int                  # grid coordinates, 0xXXYY
    bounds: tuple[float, ...]  # minX, maxX, minY, maxY, minZ, maxZ
    reserved: int            # always 0 so far
    date: int                # build date YYMMDD, zero-based month (100007 = 2010-01-07)
    time: int                # build time HHMMSScc
    nodes: list[Node] = field(default_factory=list)
    edges: list[Edge] = field(default_factory=list)
    mesh: bytes = b''        # runtime mesh record (starts with "KynogonRuntimeMesh"), raw for now


@dataclass
class HpdFile:
    header: tuple[int, ...]  # the 36 header words (word 2 = sector count, rewritten on save)
    sectors: list[Sector]


def parse(data: bytes) -> HpdFile:
    """The file's header and sectors. Raises ValueError on a file that is not exactly what write() makes of them:
    a truncated file, blocks that overlap, leave gaps or run past the end, or a sector mesh without its trailer."""
    if data[:12] != MAGIC or len(data) < HEADER_SIZE:
        raise ValueError('not a Kynogon HPD file')
    header = struct.unpack_from(f'<{HEADER_WORDS}I', data, 12)
    count = header[2]
    blocks = HEADER_SIZE + count * TABLE_ENTRY.size
    if blocks > len(data):
        raise ValueError(f'truncated: {count} sector entries need {blocks} bytes, the file has {len(data)}')
    sectors: list[Sector] = []
    running = 0
    for i in range(count):
        entry = TABLE_ENTRY.unpack_from(data, HEADER_SIZE + i * TABLE_ENTRY.size)
        sid, bounds, reserved = entry[0], entry[1:7], entry[7]
        size, offset, date, time = entry[8], entry[9], entry[10], entry[11]
        if offset != running:
            raise ValueError(f'sector {i} ({sid:#x}): block at offset {offset}, expected {running} '
                             f'(blocks in table order)')
        start = blocks + offset
        if size < 8 or start + size > len(data):
            raise ValueError(f'sector {i} ({sid:#x}): block of {size} bytes at {start} runs past the end '
                             f'({len(data)} bytes)')
        running += size
        block = data[start:start + size]
        n_nodes, n_edges = struct.unpack_from('<2I', block, 0)
        if 8 + n_nodes * NODE.size + n_edges * EDGE.size > size:
            raise ValueError(f'sector {i} ({sid:#x}): {n_nodes} nodes and {n_edges} edges do not fit its '
                             f'{size}-byte block')
        pos = 8
        nodes: list[Node] = []
        for _ in range(n_nodes):
            values = NODE.unpack_from(block, pos)
            nodes.append(Node(values[0], (values[1], values[2], values[3]), values[4], values[5], values[6],
                              values[7], values[8]))
            pos += NODE.size
        edges: list[Edge] = []
        for _ in range(n_edges):
            edges.append(Edge(*EDGE.unpack_from(block, pos)))
            pos += EDGE.size
        mesh = block[pos:]
        if not mesh.startswith(MESH_MARKER):
            raise ValueError(f'sector {i} ({sid:#x}): runtime mesh not where expected')
        # the mesh ends with its trailer: its own offset, then 0 (mesh_layout)
        if len(mesh) < len(MESH_MARKER) + 8 or \
                struct.unpack_from('<2I', mesh, len(mesh) - 8) != (len(mesh) - 8, 0):
            raise ValueError(f'sector {i} ({sid:#x}): runtime mesh has no trailer (truncated?)')
        sectors.append(Sector(sid, bounds, reserved, date, time, nodes, edges, mesh))
    if blocks + sum(len(_block(sector)) for sector in sectors) != len(data):
        raise ValueError('sector blocks do not cover the file')
    return HpdFile(header, sectors)


MESH_OBJECT_HEADER = 0x50


def mesh_layout(rec: bytes) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int, str]], list[tuple[int, list[tuple[Any, ...]], int | None]],
                                   dict[int, int], list[tuple[int, int, int]], list[int]]:
    """Walk a runtime mesh record (offsets relative to its start) and return a list of
    (start, end, label) regions plus the parsed structure. Raises ValueError on inconsistencies."""
    u32 = lambda at: _at('<I', rec, at)[0]
    regions: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = [(0, 0x50, 'header')]
    nx, nz = u32(0x38), u32(0x3C)
    tiles_off, links_n, links_off = u32(0x44), u32(0x48), u32(0x4C)
    if tiles_off != 0x50:
        raise ValueError(f'tile table at {tiles_off:#x}')
    tile_count = nx * nz
    if 0x50 + 4 * (tile_count + 1) > len(rec):
        raise ValueError(f'a tile table of {nx} x {nz} tiles runs past the end of the mesh')
    regions.append((0x50, 0x50 + (tile_count + 1) * 4, 'tile table'))
    tile_offs = [u32(0x50 + i * 4) for i in range(tile_count + 1)]
    objects: dict[int, int] = {}
    tiles: list[tuple[int, list[tuple[Any, ...]], int | None]] = []
    for tile in range(tile_count):
        tile_at = tile_offs[tile]
        count = u32(tile_at)
        if tile_at + 4 + 12 * count > len(rec):
            raise ValueError(f'tile {tile}: {count} items run past the end of the mesh')
        items = [_at('<Iff', rec, tile_at + 4 + k * 12) for k in range(count)]
        # An empty tile is just its count; otherwise items are followed by an end offset.
        end_ptr = u32(tile_at + 4 + count * 12) if count else None
        regions.append((tile_at, tile_at + (8 + count * 12 if count else 4), f'tile {tile}'))
        for ptr, _, _ in items:
            if ptr not in objects:
                objects[ptr] = _object_end(rec, ptr)
                regions.append((ptr, objects[ptr], f'object @{ptr:#x}'))
        tiles.append((tile_at, items, end_ptr))
    # The extra (last) tile-table entry points at a 4-byte slot the loader never reads; DICE's tool
    # left uninitialised memory there (preserved for exact round trips, zero when generating).
    regions.append((tile_offs[tile_count], tile_offs[tile_count] + 4, 'tile table end slot'))
    # Trailer: the last 8 bytes hold their own offset and 0.
    if u32(len(rec) - 8) != len(rec) - 8 or u32(len(rec) - 4) != 0:
        raise ValueError('mesh trailer not found')
    regions.append((len(rec) - 8, len(rec), 'trailer'))
    links: list[tuple[int, int, int]] = []
    if links_n:
        if links_off + 12 * links_n > len(rec):
            raise ValueError(f'{links_n} neighbour links run past the end of the mesh')
        regions.append((links_off, links_off + links_n * 12, 'link table'))
        for k in range(links_n):
            sid, object_count, list_at = _at('<3I', rec, links_off + k * 12)
            if list_at + 4 * object_count > len(rec):
                raise ValueError(f'link {sid:#x}: a list of {object_count} runs past the end of the mesh')
            regions.append((list_at, list_at + object_count * 4, f'link list {sid:#x}'))
            for j in range(object_count):
                object_at = u32(list_at + j * 4)
                ref_count = u32(object_at + 0xC)
                regions.append((object_at, object_at + 0x10 + ref_count * 4, f'link {sid:#x}/{j}'))
            links.append((sid, object_count, list_at))
    return regions, tiles, objects, links, tile_offs


def _at(fmt: str, rec: bytes, at: int) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
    """struct.unpack_from(fmt, rec, at); ValueError when it runs past the mesh (2026-10-31 fuzzing: struct.error, and
    a negative offset read from the end)."""
    size = struct.calcsize(fmt)
    if at < 0 or at + size > len(rec):
        raise ValueError(f'damaged runtime mesh: {size} bytes at {at:#x} lie outside the {len(rec)}-byte record')
    return struct.unpack_from(fmt, rec, at)


def _object_end(rec: bytes, start: int) -> int:
    """Where the area object at `start` ends: its header, A / B / C records, then its point-list and cell tables."""
    u32 = lambda at: _at('<I', rec, at)[0]
    a_count, b_count, c_count = u32(start + 0x20), u32(start + 0x28), u32(start + 0x30)
    end = start + MESH_OBJECT_HEADER + a_count * 0x20 + b_count * 0x20 + c_count * 0x2C
    for count_off, table_off, stride in ((0x38, 0x3C, 4), (0x40, 0x44, 4), (0x48, 0x4C, 16)):
        count = u32(start + count_off)
        if not count:
            continue
        table = start + u32(start + table_off)
        if table != end:
            raise ValueError(f'object {start:#x}: table {count_off:#x} at {table:#x}, expected {end:#x}')
        first = u32(table)
        last = u32(table + count * stride)
        end = table + (count + 1) * stride + ((last - first) & ~3)
    return end


def mesh_coverage(rec: bytes) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int]], list[tuple[int, int, str]]]:
    """(gaps, overlaps) of the regions mesh_layout explains in the record: (start, end) and (start, end, label)."""
    regions, *_ = mesh_layout(rec)
    regions.sort()
    gaps, overlaps, pos = [], [], 0
    for start, end, label in regions:
        if start > pos:
            gaps.append((pos, start))
        elif start < pos:
            overlaps.append((start, pos, label))
        pos = max(pos, end)
    if pos < len(rec):
        gaps.append((pos, len(rec)))
    return gaps, overlaps


def _block(sector: Sector) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray(struct.pack('<2I', len(sector.nodes), len(sector.edges)))
    for node in sector.nodes:
        out += NODE.pack(node.id, *node.pos, node.flags, node.value, node.a, node.b, node.c)
    for edge in sector.edges:
        out += EDGE.pack(edge.tag, edge.src, edge.dst)
    out += sector.mesh
    return bytes(out)


def write(hpd: HpdFile) -> bytes:
    """The file's bytes (the header's sector count rewritten)."""
    header = list(hpd.header)
    header[2] = len(hpd.sectors)
    out = bytearray(MAGIC + struct.pack(f'<{HEADER_WORDS}I', *header))
    blocks = [_block(sector) for sector in hpd.sectors]
    offset = 0
    for sector, block in zip(hpd.sectors, blocks):
        out += TABLE_ENTRY.pack(sector.id, *sector.bounds, sector.reserved, len(block), offset, sector.date,
                                sector.time)
        offset += len(block)
    for block in blocks:
        out += block
    return bytes(out)


def _files(args: Iterable[str]) -> Iterator[str]:
    """The files named, and every pathdata.hpd under the folders named."""
    for arg in args:
        if os.path.isdir(arg):
            for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(arg):
                for filename in filenames:
                    if filename.lower() == 'pathdata.hpd':
                        yield os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
        else:
            yield arg


def _last_tile_entry(mesh: bytes) -> int:
    """The runtime mesh's last tile-table entry (the end slot's offset)."""
    tiles_x = struct.unpack_from("<I", mesh, 0x38)[0]
    tiles_z = struct.unpack_from("<I", mesh, 0x3C)[0]
    return struct.unpack_from("<I", mesh, 0x50 + tiles_x * tiles_z * 4)[0]


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 3:
        print(__doc__)
        return 1
    cmd = argv[1]
    if cmd == 'info':
        hpd = parse(open(argv[2], 'rb').read())
        nodes = sum(len(sector.nodes) for sector in hpd.sectors)
        edges = sum(len(sector.edges) for sector in hpd.sectors)
        mesh = sum(len(sector.mesh) for sector in hpd.sectors)
        dates = sorted({sector.date for sector in hpd.sectors})
        print(f'{len(hpd.sectors)} sectors, {nodes} graph nodes, {edges} edges, {mesh} bytes of runtime mesh; '
              + (f'build dates {dates[0]}..{dates[-1]}' if dates else 'no build dates (no sectors)'))
        return 0
    if cmd == 'sector':
        hpd = parse(open(argv[2], 'rb').read())
        sector = hpd.sectors[int(argv[3])]
        print(f'sector {sector.id:#06x} bounds {[round(b, 2) for b in sector.bounds]} built {sector.date} '
              f'{sector.time:08d}')
        for node in sector.nodes:
            print(f'  node {node.id:#010x} pos ({node.pos[0]:.2f}, {node.pos[1]:.2f}, {node.pos[2]:.2f}) '
                  f'flags {node.flags:#x} value {node.value:g} a {node.a} b {node.b & 0xFFFF},{node.b >> 16} '
                  f'c {node.c}')
        for edge in sector.edges:
            print(f'  edge {edge.tag:#010x} {edge.src} -> {edge.dst}')
        print(f'  mesh {len(sector.mesh)} bytes: {sector.mesh[:48].hex(" ")}')
        return 0
    if cmd == 'coverage':
        total = clean = 0
        gap_kinds = {}
        for path in _files(argv[2:]):
            hpd = parse(open(path, 'rb').read())
            for sector in hpd.sectors:
                total += 1
                try:
                    gaps, overlaps = mesh_coverage(sector.mesh)
                except (ValueError, struct.error) as ex:
                    print(f'ERROR {path} sector {sector.id:#x}: {ex}')
                    continue
                if not gaps and not overlaps:
                    clean += 1
                else:
                    key = (tuple((end - start) for start, end in gaps[:3]), len(overlaps))
                    gap_kinds[key] = gap_kinds.get(key, 0) + 1
                    if gap_kinds[key] <= 2:
                        desc = [f'{start:#x}:{sector.mesh[start:end].hex(" ")}' for start, end in gaps[:4]]
                        level_folder = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(path)))
                        print(f'{level_folder}/{os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))} '
                              f'sector {sector.id:#x} len {len(sector.mesh):#x} last-tile-entry '
                              f'{_last_tile_entry(sector.mesh):#x}: '
                              f'gaps {desc} overlaps {overlaps[:2]}')
        print(f'coverage: {clean}/{total} meshes fully explained; gap patterns {len(gap_kinds)}')
        return 0
    if cmd == 'meshtrip':
        import kymesh
        total = same = 0
        reasons = {}
        for path in _files(argv[2:]):
            for sector in parse(open(path, 'rb').read()).sectors:
                total += 1
                try:
                    out = kymesh.write_mesh(kymesh.parse_mesh(sector.mesh))
                except Exception as ex:
                    reason = type(ex).__name__ + ': ' + str(ex)[:60]
                    reasons[reason] = reasons.get(reason, 0) + 1
                    continue
                if out == sector.mesh:
                    same += 1
                else:
                    common = min(len(out), len(sector.mesh))
                    first = next((i for i in range(common) if out[i] != sector.mesh[i]), common)
                    word = first // 4 * 4
                    key = f'len {len(out) - len(sector.mesh):+d}, first diff at word {word:#x}'
                    if not reasons:
                        print(f'first mismatch: {path} sector {sector.id:#x}: {key}; '
                              f'orig {sector.mesh[word:word + 16].hex(" ")} new {out[word:word + 16].hex(" ")}')
                    reasons[key] = reasons.get(key, 0) + 1
        print(f'mesh round trip: {same}/{total} identical')
        for reason, count in sorted(reasons.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])[:8]:
            print(f'  {count:6} x {reason}')
        return 0 if same == total else 2
    if cmd == 'roundtrip':
        ok = bad = 0
        for path in _files(argv[2:]):
            data = open(path, 'rb').read()
            try:
                same = write(parse(data)) == data
            except (ValueError, struct.error, IndexError) as ex:      # one damaged file must not end the batch
                same = False
                print(f'ERROR {path}: {ex}')
            ok += same
            bad += not same
            if not same:
                print(f'MISMATCH {path}')
        print(f'round trip: {ok} identical, {bad} different')
        return 0 if bad == 0 else 2
    print(__doc__)
    return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('hpdtool', gui=False)       # a log; an unexpected error explained in words (exit code 1)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/hpdview.py`:

```py
"""hpdview.py - draw one sector of a pathdata.hpd top-down (x right, z up) to a PNG.

Usage: python hpdview.py <pathdata.hpd> <sector index | 0xID> <out.png>

Optional 4th to 7th arguments: minX maxX minZ maxZ zoom window (all four or none).

Colours: grey = tile grid, black = E lines, purple = D lines, cyan = F cells (arrow = row direction),
green = B segments, red = C segments with a horizontal direction (arrow), magenta = C segments with
direction "up", orange = graph nodes, light orange = graph edges.
"""
import struct
import sys

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import hpdtool


def u32(mesh: bytes, offset: int) -> int:
    return struct.unpack_from('<I', mesh, offset)[0]


def f32(mesh: bytes, offset: int) -> float:
    return struct.unpack_from('<f', mesh, offset)[0]


def points_between(mesh: bytes, start: int, end: int) -> list[tuple[float, ...]]:
    """The 3-D points (12 bytes each) from start up to end."""
    return [struct.unpack_from('<3f', mesh, at) for at in range(start, end - 11, 12)]


def segs_from_lists(mesh: bytes, obj: int, count_off: int, table_off: int) -> list[list[tuple[float, ...]]]:
    """D/E lists of the area object at obj: index table of count+1 offsets (relative to the object), data = 3-D
    points."""
    count = u32(mesh, obj + count_off)
    out: list[list[tuple[float, ...]]] = []
    if not count:
        return out
    table = obj + u32(mesh, obj + table_off)
    offsets = [u32(mesh, table + j * 4) for j in range(count + 1)]
    for j in range(count):
        out.append(points_between(mesh, obj + offsets[j], obj + offsets[j + 1]))
    return out


def main() -> int | None:
    if len(sys.argv) < 4 or any(arg in ('-h', '--help') for arg in sys.argv[1:]):
        print(__doc__)
        return 0 if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
    path, which, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    hpd = hpdtool.parse(open(path, 'rb').read())
    if which.startswith('0x'):
        sector = next(candidate for candidate in hpd.sectors if candidate.id == int(which, 16))
    else:
        sector = hpd.sectors[int(which)]
    mesh = sector.mesh
    _, _tiles, objects, _, _ = hpdtool.mesh_layout(mesh)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 12))
    # the tile grid: the sector's bounds and tile counts from the mesh header
    x0, x1, z0, z1 = (f32(mesh, 0x28 + i * 4) for i in range(4))
    nx, nz = u32(mesh, 0x38), u32(mesh, 0x3C)
    for i in range(nx + 1):
        x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * i / nx
        ax.plot([x, x], [z0, z1], color='0.85', lw=0.8)
    for i in range(nz + 1):
        z = z0 + (z1 - z0) * i / nz
        ax.plot([x0, x1], [z, z], color='0.85', lw=0.8)
    for obj in objects:                                  # each area object
        for points in segs_from_lists(mesh, obj, 0x40, 0x44):
            ax.plot([point[0] for point in points], [point[2] for point in points], color='black', lw=0.6)
        for points in segs_from_lists(mesh, obj, 0x38, 0x3C):
            ax.plot([point[0] for point in points], [point[2] for point in points], color='tab:purple', lw=1.6)
        # F cells: 16-byte table entries (point offset, row direction), the points up to the next entry's offset
        cell_count = u32(mesh, obj + 0x48)
        if cell_count:
            table = obj + u32(mesh, obj + 0x4C)
            for j in range(cell_count):
                start = obj + u32(mesh, table + j * 16)
                end = obj + u32(mesh, table + (j + 1) * 16)
                points = points_between(mesh, start, end)
                ax.fill([point[0] for point in points], [point[2] for point in points], color='tab:cyan', alpha=0.6,
                        lw=0)
                direction = struct.unpack_from('<3f', mesh, table + j * 16 + 4)
                centre_x = sum(point[0] for point in points) / len(points)
                centre_z = sum(point[2] for point in points) / len(points)
                ax.arrow(centre_x, centre_z, direction[0] * 0.6, direction[2] * 0.6, head_width=0.2, color='teal',
                         lw=0.5)
        # B segments (0x20 bytes each), then C segments (0x2C bytes each): ends (x, z) at +0, +8 and +12, +20
        b_count = u32(mesh, obj + 0x28)
        records = obj + 0x50
        for k in range(b_count):
            rec = records + k * 0x20
            ax.plot([f32(mesh, rec), f32(mesh, rec + 12)], [f32(mesh, rec + 8), f32(mesh, rec + 20)],
                    color='tab:green', lw=2)
        records += b_count * 0x20
        for k in range(u32(mesh, obj + 0x30)):
            rec = records + k * 0x2C
            up = f32(mesh, rec + 0x24) > 0.5
            ax.plot([f32(mesh, rec), f32(mesh, rec + 12)], [f32(mesh, rec + 8), f32(mesh, rec + 20)],
                    color='tab:red' if not up else 'magenta', lw=2)
            if not up:
                mid_x = (f32(mesh, rec) + f32(mesh, rec + 12)) / 2
                mid_z = (f32(mesh, rec + 8) + f32(mesh, rec + 20)) / 2
                ax.arrow(mid_x, mid_z, f32(mesh, rec + 0x20) * 0.8, f32(mesh, rec + 0x28) * 0.8, head_width=0.25,
                         color='tab:red', lw=0.5)
    for edge in sector.edges:
        src, dst = sector.nodes[edge.src].pos, sector.nodes[edge.dst].pos
        ax.plot([src[0], dst[0]], [src[2], dst[2]], color='moccasin', lw=0.8, zorder=1)
    ax.scatter([node.pos[0] for node in sector.nodes], [node.pos[2] for node in sector.nodes], s=6,
               color='tab:orange', zorder=3)
    if len(sys.argv) >= 8:
        ax.set_xlim(float(sys.argv[4]), float(sys.argv[5]))
        ax.set_ylim(float(sys.argv[6]), float(sys.argv[7]))
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    ax.set_title(f'sector {sector.id:#06x}: {len(objects)} areas, {len(sector.nodes)} nodes, '
                 f'{len(sector.edges)} edges')
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
    print(f'wrote {out}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('hpdview', gui=False)       # a log; an unexpected error explained in words (exit code 1)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main())
```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/kymesh.py`:

```py
"""kymesh.py - structured model of the "KynogonRuntimeMesh" record inside pathdata.hpd sector blocks.

Part of BC2 NavKit; layout as documented in ..\\research\\KYNAPSE_SPEC.md section 4.4/4.5.
parse_mesh(bytes) -> Mesh, write_mesh(Mesh) -> bytes. All offsets in the record are relative to its
start; parse_mesh replaces them with references (object indices etc.) and write_mesh lays the record
out again and recomputes every offset.
"""
import bisect
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Tuple, cast

NULL = 0xFFFFFFFF
MARKER = b'KynogonRuntimeMesh\0\0'
Vec3 = Tuple[float, float, float]


@dataclass
class Portal:                 # B: portal to another area of the same sector
    p0: Vec3
    p1: Vec3
    target: int               # index of the target area (Mesh.areas)


@dataclass
class BorderPortal:           # C: portal on the sector border
    p0: Vec3
    p1: Vec3
    direction: Vec3           # unit vector out of the sector (or "up")
    runtime: tuple[int, int] = (NULL, NULL)   # filled by the game at runtime; NULL in files


@dataclass
class Cell:                   # F: special pitch-sized cell (ledge / height break)
    direction: Vec3
    points: list[Vec3]


@dataclass
class Area:                   # one walkable area inside one tile
    sector_id: int
    tile_x: int
    tile_z: int
    layer: int
    radius: float
    pitch: float
    max_y: float
    min_y: float
    portals: list[Portal] = field(default_factory=list)
    border_portals: list[BorderPortal] = field(default_factory=list)
    d_lines: list[list[Vec3]] = field(default_factory=list)
    outline: list[list[Vec3]] = field(default_factory=list)      # E
    cells: list[Cell] = field(default_factory=list)
    end_row: Vec3 = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)          # floats of the F table's terminating row
    null_offsets: dict[int, int] = field(default_factory=dict)  # raw offset values stored with count 0


@dataclass
class TileItem:
    area: int                 # index into Mesh.areas
    a: float                  # stored per tile item (area min / max height in the samples)
    b: float


@dataclass
class LinkObject:
    header: tuple[int, int, int]
    refs: list[tuple[int, int]]   # (area index, byte offset inside that area object)


@dataclass
class NeighbourLink:
    sector_id: int
    objects: list[LinkObject]


@dataclass
class Mesh:
    version: int
    flags: int
    loaded: int
    sector_id: int
    resolution: float
    pitch: float
    rect: tuple[float, float, float, float]   # minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ
    tiles_x: int
    tiles_z: int
    radius: float
    tiles: list[list[TileItem]]               # tiles_x * tiles_z
    areas: list[Area]
    links: list[NeighbourLink]
    end_slot: bytes                           # 4 bytes the loader never reads (uninitialised in DICE files)
    links_null_offset: int = NULL


def _at(fmt: str, rec: bytes, at: int) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
    """struct.unpack_from(fmt, rec, at); ValueError when it runs past the record (2026-10-31 fuzzing: struct.error,
    and a negative offset read from the end)."""
    size = struct.calcsize(fmt)
    if at < 0 or at + size > len(rec):
        raise ValueError(f'damaged runtime mesh: {size} bytes at {at:#x} lie outside the {len(rec)}-byte record')
    return struct.unpack_from(fmt, rec, at)


def _u32(rec: bytes, at: int) -> int:
    return _at('<I', rec, at)[0]


def _f32(rec: bytes, at: int) -> float:
    return _at('<f', rec, at)[0]


def _v3(rec: bytes, at: int) -> Vec3:
    return _at('<3f', rec, at)


def _points(rec: bytes, start: int, end: int) -> list[Vec3]:
    """The 12-byte points from start to end."""
    return [_v3(rec, at) for at in range(start, end, 12)]


class _Budget:
    """The bytes a record's tables may take together: every table lies in the record, and none overlaps another in a
    file write_mesh makes, so a damaged record whose counts or offsets point many tables at the same bytes is refused
    before it is read many times over (2026-10-31 review, while fuzzing: reading time grew with the square of the
    record's size)."""

    def __init__(self, rec: bytes) -> None:
        self.left = len(rec)

    def take(self, size: int, what: str) -> None:
        self.left -= max(0, size)
        if self.left < 0:
            raise ValueError(f'damaged runtime mesh: {what} would take more bytes than the record has (tables '
                             f'overlap)')


def parse_mesh(rec: bytes) -> Mesh:
    """The record as a Mesh. ValueError for a record that is not one write_mesh could make: cut short, a count or
    offset past its end, tables that overlap, a reference to no area."""
    if not rec.startswith(MARKER):
        raise ValueError('not a KynogonRuntimeMesh record')
    budget = _Budget(rec)
    version, flags = _at('<HH', rec, 0x14)
    loaded, sector_id = _u32(rec, 0x18), _u32(rec, 0x1C)
    resolution, pitch = _f32(rec, 0x20), _f32(rec, 0x24)
    rect = _at('<4f', rec, 0x28)
    tiles_x, tiles_z = _u32(rec, 0x38), _u32(rec, 0x3C)
    radius = _f32(rec, 0x40)
    tile_table, link_count, links_at = _u32(rec, 0x44), _u32(rec, 0x48), _u32(rec, 0x4C)
    tile_count = tiles_x * tiles_z
    budget.take(4 * (tile_count + 1), f'a tile table of {tiles_x} x {tiles_z} tiles')
    tile_offs = [_u32(rec, tile_table + i * 4) for i in range(tile_count + 1)]

    area_index: dict[int, int] = {}           # object offset -> index
    area_offsets: list[int] = []
    tiles_raw: list[list[tuple[Any, ...]]] = []
    for tile in range(tile_count):
        tile_at = tile_offs[tile]
        count = _u32(rec, tile_at)
        budget.take(4 + 12 * count, f'the {count} items of tile {tile}')
        items = [_at('<Iff', rec, tile_at + 4 + k * 12) for k in range(count)]
        for ptr, _, _ in items:
            if ptr not in area_index:
                area_index[ptr] = len(area_offsets)
                area_offsets.append(ptr)
        tiles_raw.append(items)
    tiles = [[TileItem(area_index[ptr], low, high) for ptr, low, high in items] for items in tiles_raw]

    areas: list[Area] = []
    for area_at in area_offsets:
        budget.take(0x50, f'the area at {area_at:#x}')
        header = _at('<4I4f', rec, area_at)
        # the area's tables: count at area_at + key, offset (from the area's start) at area_at + key + 4
        counts = {key: _u32(rec, area_at + key) for key in (0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x48)}
        offsets = {key: _u32(rec, area_at + key + 4) for key in counts}
        null_offsets = {key: offsets[key] for key in counts if counts[key] == 0}
        area = Area(header[0], header[1], header[2], header[3], header[4], header[5], header[6], header[7],
                    null_offsets=null_offsets)
        if counts[0x20]:
            raise ValueError('A records present (never seen before)')
        budget.take(0x20 * counts[0x28] + 0x2C * counts[0x30], f'the portals of the area at {area_at:#x}')
        table_at = area_at + offsets[0x28] if counts[0x28] else None
        for k in range(counts[0x28]):
            record_at = cast(int, table_at) + k * 0x20      # not None: counts[0x28] > 0
            area.portals.append(Portal(_v3(rec, record_at), _v3(rec, record_at + 12),
                                       _u32(rec, record_at + 0x18)))   # target resolved below
        table_at = area_at + offsets[0x30] if counts[0x30] else None
        for k in range(counts[0x30]):
            record_at = cast(int, table_at) + k * 0x2C      # not None: counts[0x30] > 0
            area.border_portals.append(BorderPortal(_v3(rec, record_at), _v3(rec, record_at + 12),
                                                    _v3(rec, record_at + 0x20),
                                                    (_u32(rec, record_at + 0x18), _u32(rec, record_at + 0x1C))))
        for key, target in ((0x38, area.d_lines), (0x40, area.outline)):
            if counts[key]:
                list_table = area_at + offsets[key]
                budget.take(4 * (counts[key] + 1), f'the point lists of the area at {area_at:#x}')
                list_starts = [_u32(rec, list_table + j * 4) for j in range(counts[key] + 1)]
                for j in range(counts[key]):
                    budget.take(list_starts[j + 1] - list_starts[j], f'the points of the area at {area_at:#x}')
                    target.append(_points(rec, area_at + list_starts[j], area_at + list_starts[j + 1]))
        if counts[0x48]:
            cell_table = area_at + offsets[0x48]
            budget.take(16 * (counts[0x48] + 1), f'the cells of the area at {area_at:#x}')
            rows = [_at('<I3f', rec, cell_table + j * 16) for j in range(counts[0x48] + 1)]
            for j in range(counts[0x48]):
                budget.take(rows[j + 1][0] - rows[j][0], f'the cell points of the area at {area_at:#x}')
                area.cells.append(Cell(rows[j][1:], _points(rec, area_at + rows[j][0], area_at + rows[j + 1][0])))
            area.end_row = rows[-1][1:]
        areas.append(area)
    for k, area in enumerate(areas):
        for portal in area.portals:
            if portal.target not in area_index:
                raise ValueError(f'area {k}: portal target {portal.target:#x} is not the start of an area')
            portal.target = area_index[portal.target]

    starts = sorted(area_offsets)
    links: list[NeighbourLink] = []
    budget.take(12 * link_count, f'{link_count} neighbour links')
    for k in range(link_count):
        sid, object_count, list_at = _at('<3I', rec, links_at + k * 12)
        budget.take(4 * object_count, f'the list of link {sid:#x}')
        objs: list[LinkObject] = []
        for j in range(object_count):
            object_at = _u32(rec, list_at + j * 4)
            link_header = _at('<3I', rec, object_at)
            ref_count = _u32(rec, object_at + 0xC)
            budget.take(0x10 + 4 * ref_count, f'link {sid:#x}/{j}')
            refs: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
            for ref in range(ref_count):
                ptr = _u32(rec, object_at + 0x10 + ref * 4)
                after = bisect.bisect_right(starts, ptr)       # the area that starts last at or before ptr
                if not after:
                    raise ValueError(f'link {sid:#x}/{j}: reference {ptr:#x} lies before the first area')
                owner = starts[after - 1]
                refs.append((area_index[owner], ptr - owner))
            objs.append(LinkObject(link_header, refs))
        links.append(NeighbourLink(sid, objs))
    end_slot = rec[tile_offs[tile_count]:tile_offs[tile_count] + 4]
    return Mesh(version, flags, loaded, sector_id, resolution, pitch, rect, tiles_x, tiles_z, radius, tiles, areas,
                links, end_slot, links_at if link_count == 0 else NULL)


def write_mesh(mesh: Mesh) -> bytes:
    """The record's bytes, every offset computed again."""
    # Pass 1: serialise areas without B target fields to learn their sizes; pass 2: lay out and patch.
    bodies = [_area_body(area) for area in mesh.areas]
    out = bytearray(MARKER)
    out += struct.pack('<HHII', mesh.version, mesh.flags, mesh.loaded, mesh.sector_id)
    out += struct.pack('<2f4f2If', mesh.resolution, mesh.pitch, *mesh.rect, mesh.tiles_x, mesh.tiles_z, mesh.radius)
    out += b'\0' * 12                      # tile table offset, link count, link offset (patched below)
    tile_count = mesh.tiles_x * mesh.tiles_z
    tile_table = len(out)
    out += b'\0' * ((tile_count + 1) * 4)
    tile_offs: list[int] = []
    area_at: dict[int, int] = {}           # area index -> its offset in the record
    for items in mesh.tiles:
        tile_at = len(out)
        tile_offs.append(tile_at)
        out += struct.pack('<I', len(items))
        item_pos = len(out)
        out += b'\0' * (len(items) * 12)
        if items:
            out += b'\0' * 4               # end offset, patched below
        for item in items:
            if item.area not in area_at:
                area_at[item.area] = len(out)
                out += bodies[item.area][0]
        for k, item in enumerate(items):
            struct.pack_into('<Iff', out, item_pos + k * 12, area_at[item.area], item.a, item.b)
        if items:
            struct.pack_into('<I', out, item_pos + len(items) * 12, len(out))
    unplaced = [i for i in range(len(mesh.areas)) if i not in area_at]
    if unplaced:
        raise ValueError(f'areas {unplaced[:5]} are in no tile: every area must be listed by a tile to be written')
    end_slot_off = len(out)
    out += mesh.end_slot
    tile_offs.append(end_slot_off)
    for i, tile_at in enumerate(tile_offs):
        struct.pack_into('<I', out, tile_table + i * 4, tile_at)
    # Patch B portal targets (offset and size of the target area).
    sizes = [len(body[0]) for body in bodies]
    for i, (_body, portal_pos) in enumerate(bodies):
        base = area_at[i]
        for k, portal in enumerate(mesh.areas[i].portals):
            struct.pack_into('<II', out, base + portal_pos + k * 0x20 + 0x18, area_at[portal.target],
                             sizes[portal.target])
    # Neighbour links.
    links_off = len(out) if mesh.links else mesh.links_null_offset
    if mesh.links:
        table = len(out)
        out += b'\0' * (len(mesh.links) * 12)
        for k, link in enumerate(mesh.links):
            list_at = len(out)
            out += b'\0' * (len(link.objects) * 4)
            struct.pack_into('<3I', out, table + k * 12, link.sector_id, len(link.objects), list_at)
            for j, obj in enumerate(link.objects):
                struct.pack_into('<I', out, list_at + j * 4, len(out))
                out += struct.pack('<4I', *obj.header, len(obj.refs))
                for ai, rel in obj.refs:
                    out += struct.pack('<I', area_at[ai] + rel)
    struct.pack_into('<3I', out, 0x44, tile_table, len(mesh.links), links_off)
    out += struct.pack('<II', len(out), 0)   # trailer
    return bytes(out)


def _area_body(area: Area) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
    """Bytes of one area object with B target fields zeroed; returns (bytes, offset of the B records)."""
    hdr_size = 0x50
    blob = bytearray()
    offsets: dict[int, int] = {}            # header key -> the table's offset from the area's start
    pos = hdr_size
    portal_pos = pos
    offsets[0x28] = pos if area.portals else area.null_offsets.get(0x28, NULL)
    for portal in area.portals:
        blob += struct.pack('<6fII', *portal.p0, *portal.p1, 0, 0)
    pos = hdr_size + len(blob)
    offsets[0x30] = pos if area.border_portals else area.null_offsets.get(0x30, NULL)
    for border in area.border_portals:
        blob += struct.pack('<6f2I3f', *border.p0, *border.p1, *border.runtime, *border.direction)
    for key, lists in ((0x38, area.d_lines), (0x40, area.outline)):
        if not lists:
            offsets[key] = area.null_offsets.get(key, NULL)
            continue
        table = hdr_size + len(blob)
        offsets[key] = table
        data_start = table + (len(lists) + 1) * 4
        list_starts, next_at = [], data_start
        for points in lists:
            list_starts.append(next_at)
            next_at += len(points) * 12
        list_starts.append(next_at)
        blob += struct.pack(f'<{len(list_starts)}I', *list_starts)
        for points in lists:
            for point in points:
                blob += struct.pack('<3f', *point)
    if area.cells:
        table = hdr_size + len(blob)
        offsets[0x48] = table
        next_at = table + (len(area.cells) + 1) * 16
        for cell in area.cells:
            blob += struct.pack('<I3f', next_at, *cell.direction)
            next_at += len(cell.points) * 12
        blob += struct.pack('<I3f', next_at, *area.end_row)
        for cell in area.cells:
            for point in cell.points:
                blob += struct.pack('<3f', *point)
    else:
        offsets[0x48] = area.null_offsets.get(0x48, NULL)
    offsets[0x20] = area.null_offsets.get(0x20, NULL)
    header = struct.pack('<4I4f', area.sector_id, area.tile_x, area.tile_z, area.layer, area.radius, area.pitch,
                         area.max_y, area.min_y)
    counts = {0x20: 0, 0x28: len(area.portals), 0x30: len(area.border_portals), 0x38: len(area.d_lines),
              0x40: len(area.outline), 0x48: len(area.cells)}
    for key in (0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x48):
        header += struct.pack('<II', counts[key], offsets[key])
    return bytes(header + blob), portal_pos

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/levelobjects.py`:

```py
"""NavKit: object placements and pathfinding flags of a level, from its extracted data.

Reads an unpacked + XML-converted level (FbrbTool unpack of Dist and Package level-00.fbrb, then
DbxEdit xml on both folders) and writes, next to it:
  objects.json       individually placed objects (Entity.ReferenceObjectData): blueprint, flags, matrix
  group_instances.json  instances of static-model groups / forest / middlegrowth (Physics.CompositeHavokAsset:
                     Assets[i] + Transforms[i]), with blueprint flags
  forbid_tris.npy    world-space collision triangles (N x 3 x 3) of every placed object whose blueprint has
                     ForbidPathfinding = true (from the blueprint's <name>_Havok.res packfile)
  stair_tris.npy     collision of staircases and ramps (blueprint names with stair / ramp / steps): floor that
                     does not block its own users' clearance
  dynamic_tris.npy   the same for dynamic (movable / destructible) objects - DynamicModelEntityData blueprints
                     such as crates and barrels - for objects with DisablePathfinding = PdtWhenAlive (doors), and
                     for barrier arms (a forbidden object that is one thin raised bar): path data treats them as absent

Usage: levelobjects.py <level dir> <level name> [extra blueprint dirs ...]
  e.g. levelobjects.py work\\levels\\sp_01 SP_01 work\\audit\\sp_common work\\audit\\mp_common
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import struct
import sys
from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import havok461  # noqa: E402
import hkpack  # noqa: E402
from bfbc2core import xmlinst  # noqa: E402

SEP = chr(92)

# a blueprint's flags (blueprint_flags): ForbidPathfinding, ExcludeFromPathfinding, AllowPathdataSeeds, dynamic,
# DisablePathfinding value, NeedsDetailedPathfinding
type Flags = tuple[bool, bool, bool, bool, str, bool]


def order_points(level_xml: str) -> list[list[float]]:
    """AI order positions of a level: the Transform translation of every AreaGeometryEntityData (the points the
    squad's area / patrol orders send soldiers to; sp_004_b's stairs-top go-to targets are two of them)."""
    points: list[list[float]] = []
    for _typ, _guid, body in xmlinst.instances(level_xml, 'Entity.AreaGeometryEntityData'):
        transform = re.search(r'<complex name="Transform">([^<]*)</complex>', body)
        if transform:
            matrix = [float(value) for value in transform.group(1).split('/')]
            if len(matrix) >= 15 and any(abs(coord) > 1e-3 for coord in matrix[12:15]):
                points.append(matrix[12:15])
    return points


def blueprint_flags(bases: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, Flags]:
    """lower-case blueprint path -> (ForbidPathfinding, ExcludeFromPathfinding, AllowPathdataSeeds, dynamic,
    DisablePathfinding value - e.g. PdtNever / PdtWhenAlive, NeedsDetailedPathfinding). The last (FLAG_DETAILED) is
    what DICE's detailed zones follow (detailed.py; added 2026-10-31 - objects.json from before has five)."""
    flags: dict[str, Flags] = {}
    for base in bases:
        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, '**', '*.xml'), recursive=True):
            text = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
            dynamic = 'type="GameSharedResources.DynamicModelEntityData"' in text
            if 'ForbidPathfinding' not in text and 'NeedsDetailedPathfinding' not in text and not dynamic:
                continue
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, base).replace(SEP, '/').lower()[:-4]
            disable = re.search(r'<field name="DisablePathfinding">([A-Za-z]*)<', text)
            flags.setdefault(rel, ('<field name="ForbidPathfinding">true' in text,
                                   '<field name="ExcludeFromPathfinding">true' in text,
                                   '<field name="AllowPathdataSeeds">true' in text, dynamic,
                                   disable.group(1) if disable else '',
                                   '<field name="NeedsDetailedPathfinding">true' in text))
    return flags


FLAG_DETAILED = 5            # index of NeedsDetailedPathfinding in an object's flags (blueprint_flags)


def mesh_aliases(bases: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """lower-case blueprint path -> blueprint path of its Mesh reference (without _mesh), for blueprints that
    reuse another object's mesh and collision (InvWall_SP03 -> invisiblewall/invwall)."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for base in bases:
        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, '**', '*.xml'), recursive=True):
            text = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
            ref = xmlinst.field_ref(text, 'Mesh')
            if not ref or ref == 'null':
                continue
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, base).replace(SEP, '/').lower()[:-4]
            mesh = ref.rsplit('/', 1)[0].lower()
            out.setdefault(rel, re.sub(r'_mesh$', '', mesh))
    return out


def havok_index(bases: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """lower-case blueprint path -> its collision packfile (<name>_Havok.res; the first base folder that has one)."""
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for base in bases:
        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, '**', '*_havok.res'), recursive=True):
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, base).replace(SEP, '/').lower()[:-len('_havok.res')]
            out.setdefault(rel, path)
            # some assets name their packfile <name>_Havok_Havok.res (sp_009's animated aircraft door,
            # PdtWhenAlive: without its collision the closed door stayed solid and cut the plane's cabins apart;
            # inv_Wall): the blueprint is <name>
            while rel.endswith('_havok'):
                rel = rel[:-len('_havok')]
                out.setdefault(rel, path)
    return out


def triangles16(words: npt.ArrayLike) -> npt.NDArray[np.integer]:
    """Triangles of 16-bit indices stored in groups of four (three corners + padding); a last triangle stored without
    its padding word (a count of 4n + 3) is kept."""
    words = np.asarray(words)
    full = len(words) // 4 * 4
    tris = words[:full].reshape(-1, 4)[:, :3]
    if len(words) - full == 3:
        tris = np.concatenate([tris, words[full:].reshape(1, 3)])
    return tris


def triangles(path: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.float32] | None:
    """Collision triangles (local space) of a blueprint's Havok asset, or None: storage extended mesh subparts and
    convex shapes' boxes. Havok 5.5 (BFBC2, hkp* classes, described in the file) and Havok 4.6.1 (BF1943, hk* classes,
    layouts from havok461.py), in the file's own byte order."""
    try:
        pf = hkpack.Packfile(open(path, 'rb').read(), classes=havok461.CLASSES)
        return triangles_of(pf)
    except (ValueError, struct.error, IndexError):
        return None


def triangles_of(pf: hkpack.Packfile) -> npt.NDArray[np.float32] | None:
    """triangles() of a loaded packfile."""
    if pf.contents_version.startswith('Havok-4.'):
        tris: list[npt.NDArray[Any]] = []
        for off in pf.objects_of('hkStorageExtendedMeshShapeMeshSubpartStorage'):
            vertex_list, index_list = havok461.triangles(pf, off)
            if vertex_list and index_list:
                vertices, indices = np.asarray(vertex_list, np.float32), np.asarray(index_list, np.int64)
                if indices.max() < len(vertices):
                    tris.append(vertices[indices])
        for off in pf.objects_of('hkConvexVerticesShape'):
            box, _half, _centre = havok461.convex_box(pf, off)
            if box:
                tris.append(np.asarray(box, np.float32))
        return np.concatenate(tris).astype(np.float32) if tris else None
    endian = pf.e                   # the struct byte-order prefix, '<' or '>'
    tris = []
    for off in pf.objects_of('hkpStorageExtendedMeshShapeMeshSubpartStorage'):
        vertices_at = pf.deref(off + 8)
        vertex_count = struct.unpack_from(endian + 'i', pf.d, off + 12)[0]
        indices_at = pf.deref(off + 0x14)
        index_count = struct.unpack_from(endian + 'i', pf.d, off + 0x18)[0]
        if not (vertices_at and vertex_count > 0 and indices_at and index_count > 0):
            continue
        vertices = np.frombuffer(pf.d, dtype=endian + 'f4', count=vertex_count * 4,
                                 offset=vertices_at).reshape(-1, 4)[:, :3]
        indices = triangles16(np.frombuffer(pf.d, dtype=endian + 'u2', count=index_count, offset=indices_at))
        if len(indices) and indices.max() < vertex_count:
            tris.append(vertices[indices])
    # convex shapes (boxes, rails, doors): the 12 triangles of each shape's bounding box. Vertices are stored as
    # FourVectors (x0..3, y0..3, z0..3); the first array member of a plausible size holds them.
    for off in pf.objects_of('hkpConvexVerticesShape'):
        for k in range(0x10, 0x60, 4):
            vectors_at = pf.deref(off + k)
            if not vectors_at:
                continue
            count = struct.unpack_from(endian + 'i', pf.d, off + k + 4)[0]
            if 0 < count < 10000:
                four_vectors = np.frombuffer(pf.d, dtype=endian + 'f4', count=count * 12,
                                             offset=vectors_at).reshape(count, 3, 4)
                points = np.stack([four_vectors[:, 0, :].ravel(), four_vectors[:, 1, :].ravel(),
                                   four_vectors[:, 2, :].ravel()], 1)
                lo, hi = points.min(0), points.max(0)
                corners = np.array([[x, y, z] for x in (lo[0], hi[0]) for y in (lo[1], hi[1])
                                    for z in (lo[2], hi[2])])
                faces = [(0, 1, 3), (0, 3, 2), (4, 6, 7), (4, 7, 5), (0, 4, 5), (0, 5, 1), (2, 3, 7), (2, 7, 6),
                         (0, 2, 6), (0, 6, 4), (1, 5, 7), (1, 7, 3)]
                tris.append(corners[np.array(faces)])
                break
    return np.concatenate(tris).astype(np.float32) if tris else None


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 3:
        print(__doc__)
        return 1
    level_dir, level = argv[1], argv[2]
    bases = [os.path.join(level_dir, 'pkg'), os.path.join(level_dir, 'dist')] + argv[3:]
    flags = blueprint_flags(bases)
    level_xml = open(os.path.join(level_dir, 'dist', 'levels', level + '.xml'), encoding='utf-8',
                     errors='replace').read()
    # placed objects and group instances: {'bp': blueprint, 'flags': its flags, 'm': its 4 x 4 matrix, row by row}
    objs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for _typ, _guid, body in xmlinst.instances(level_xml, 'Entity.ReferenceObjectData'):
        transform = re.search(r'<complex name="Transform">([^<]*)</complex>', body)
        ref = xmlinst.field_ref(body, 'ReferencedObject')
        if transform and ref is not None:
            blueprint = ref.rsplit('/', 1)[0].lower()
            objs.append({'bp': blueprint, 'flags': flags.get(blueprint),
                         'm': [float(value) for value in transform.group(1).split('/')]})
    groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(level_dir, 'dist', 'levels', level, '*_HavokAsset.xml')):
        text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
        transforms = re.search(r'<array name="Transforms">([^<]*)<', text)
        if not transforms:
            continue
        transforms = transforms.group(1).split('/')
        assets = re.findall(r'<item ref="([^"]*)" />', text.split('<array name="Assets">')[1].split('</array>')[0])
        for i, asset in enumerate(assets):
            blueprint = re.sub(r'_havok$', '', asset.rsplit('/', 1)[0].lower())
            groups.append({'group': os.path.basename(path), 'bp': blueprint, 'flags': flags.get(blueprint),
                           'm': [float(value) for value in transforms[i * 16:(i + 1) * 16]]})
    # soldier spawn points (seed points of the path data)
    spawns: list[list[float]] = []
    for _typ, _guid, body in xmlinst.instances(level_xml, '.SoldierSpawnEntityData'):
        transform = re.search(r'<complex name="Transform">([^<]*)</complex>', body)
        if transform:
            matrix = [float(value) for value in transform.group(1).split('/')]
            if any(abs(coord) > 1e-3 for coord in matrix[12:15]):
                spawns.append(matrix[12:15])
    for name, value in (('soldier_spawns.json', spawns), ('order_points.json', order_points(level_xml)),
                        ('objects.json', objs), ('group_instances.json', groups)):
        with open(os.path.join(level_dir, name), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            json.dump(value, f)

    havok = havok_index(bases)
    # blueprints without their own collision asset use the one of the object their Mesh reference names
    for blueprint, target in mesh_aliases(bases).items():
        if blueprint not in havok and target in havok:
            havok[blueprint] = havok[target]
    cache, missing = {}, set()

    def tris_of(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> npt.NDArray[np.float32] | None:
        """An object's collision triangles in world space, or None (no collision asset)."""
        if obj['bp'] not in cache:
            cache[obj['bp']] = triangles(havok[obj['bp']]) if obj['bp'] in havok else None
        local = cache[obj['bp']]
        if local is None:
            missing.add(obj['bp'])
            return None
        matrix = np.array(obj['m']).reshape(4, 4)        # rows: right, up, forward, translation
        return (local @ matrix[:3, :3] + matrix[3, :3]).astype(np.float32)

    def barrier_arm(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> bool | np.bool:
        """Whole collision is one thin raised bar (boom barrier): >= 0.7 m above the object's origin, <= 0.5 m
        thick, >= 2 m long. Path data treats it as passable (DICE's routes cross closed checkpoint poles)."""
        if obj['bp'] not in havok:
            return False
        if obj['bp'] not in cache:
            cache[obj['bp']] = triangles(havok[obj['bp']])
        local = cache[obj['bp']]
        if local is None:
            return False
        points = local.reshape(-1, 3)
        lo, hi = points.min(0), points.max(0)
        return lo[1] >= 0.7 and hi[1] - lo[1] <= 0.5 and max(hi[0] - lo[0], hi[2] - lo[2]) >= 2.0

    def ignored(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> bool | np.bool:
        """Dynamic objects, objects with DisablePathfinding = PdtWhenAlive (doors ...) and barrier arms: path data
        ignores them."""
        flags_of = obj['flags']
        return ((len(flags_of) > 3 and flags_of[3]) or (len(flags_of) > 4 and flags_of[4] == 'PdtWhenAlive')
                or (flags_of[0] and barrier_arm(obj)))
    dynamic = [tris for tris in (tris_of(obj) for obj in objs + groups if obj['flags'] and ignored(obj))
               if tris is not None]
    # staircases and ramps (DICE blueprint names): their own collision is floor, not an obstacle to clearance
    stair_like = re.compile(r'stair|ramp|steps', re.I)
    stairs = [tris for tris in (tris_of(obj) for obj in objs + groups
                                if stair_like.search(obj['bp'].rsplit('/', 1)[-1]))
              if tris is not None]
    np.save(os.path.join(level_dir, 'stair_tris.npy'), np.concatenate(stairs) if stairs else np.zeros((0, 3, 3)))
    print(f'{sum(len(tris) for tris in stairs)} stair triangles from {len(stairs)} staircases / ramps')
    print('barrier arms:', sorted({obj['bp'].split('/')[-1] for obj in objs + groups
                                   if obj['flags'] and obj['flags'][0] and barrier_arm(obj)}))
    np.save(os.path.join(level_dir, 'dynamic_tris.npy'), np.concatenate(dynamic) if dynamic else np.zeros((0, 3, 3)))
    print(f'{sum(len(tris) for tris in dynamic)} dynamic-object triangles from {len(dynamic)} instances')
    # objects excluded from path finding (fences, sandbags, palm trees): their collision does not block clearance
    # (added to the dynamic set); only their footprint at ground level - parts reaching within 0.5 m of the
    # object's origin height - stays a barrier (exclude_footprint_tris.npy) instead of the whole object
    excluded = [obj for obj in objs + groups if obj['flags'] and obj['flags'][1]]
    excluded_tris, footprint_tris = [], []
    for obj in excluded:
        tris = tris_of(obj)
        if tris is None:
            continue
        excluded_tris.append(tris)
        base = obj['m'][13]
        footprint_tris.append(tris[tris[:, :, 1].min(1) <= base + 0.5])
    np.save(os.path.join(level_dir, 'exclude_tris.npy'),
            np.concatenate(excluded_tris) if excluded_tris else np.zeros((0, 3, 3)))
    np.save(os.path.join(level_dir, 'exclude_footprint_tris.npy'),
            np.concatenate(footprint_tris) if footprint_tris else np.zeros((0, 3, 3)))
    print(f'{len(excluded_tris)} excluded objects: {sum(len(tris) for tris in excluded_tris)} triangles, '
          f'footprint {sum(len(tris) for tris in footprint_tris)}')
    world = []
    for obj in objs + groups:
        if not (obj['flags'] and obj['flags'][0]) or obj['flags'][1]:
            continue
        tris = tris_of(obj)
        if tris is not None:
            world.append(tris)
    np.save(os.path.join(level_dir, 'forbid_tris.npy'), np.concatenate(world) if world else np.zeros((0, 3, 3)))
    print(f'{len(objs)} placed objects, {len(groups)} group instances, {len(flags)} blueprints with flags; '
          f'{sum(len(tris) for tris in world)} forbid triangles from {len(world)} instances; '
          f'no collision: {sorted(missing)}')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('levelobjects', gui=False)       # a log; an unexpected error explained in words (exit code 1)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/navbuild/__init__.py`:

```py
"""NavKit generator: collision samples -> Kynapse-format pathdata.hpd (infantry), for both NavKit variants (one copy
since 2026-10-31, in bf1943-auto-navkit-common). For BF1943 the samples are computed offline from the level's data
(navsample1943.py) and the big-endian navkit.py builds the normal sectors at 0.8 m and the detailed ones at 0.2 m
(build(..., detailed=...), merge_detailed) with soldier1943.SETTINGS; for BFBC2 (the little-endian navkit_le.py,
navregress.py) they came from OPFOR's in-game sampler, and the build takes NavKit's defaults (BFBC2).

Pipeline (research/KYNAPSE_SPEC.md sections 3 and 4):
  1. walkable surfaces: navwalk.walkable (slope, capsule, ForbidPathfinding objects, StepMax, perimeter seeds)
  2. sectors: 100 m grid from the level's SectorOffsets; each sector uses the samples -1 .. 126 of its
     window (two-sample overlap with each neighbour)
  3. tiles: 3 x 3 per sector, 50 samples each (edges half a sample outside the samples: -1.2, 38.8,
     78.8, 101.2 m); areas = connected regions of a tile (8-connected, AREA_LINK rule); the old bisection at
     the middle of their extent (over 25 samples) is off - DICE has no such cut (BISECT_AREAS)
  4. area boundary, traced on the half-sample lines and merged into straight runs:
       portal (B)   - to a connected surface in another area of the same sector
       border (C)   - to a connected surface outside the sector window (direction = outward axis)
       outline (E)  - everything else; where two cells of an area touch only diagonally, the two outline
                      corners between them are replaced by 45-degree segments (a bridge through the
                      half cells, as in DICE's outlines)
  5. neighbour links: per neighbouring sector, link objects {tile x, tile z, area index in tile} with the
     C records leading into that area
  6. graph: one node per area (sample nearest the area centre) and per portal run; border nodes on the
     overlap lines, shared by both sectors (same id and position); edges between nodes up to DistEdgeMax
     apart whose straight line stays on connected walkable samples; cost = 0x80000000 | floor(d * 16)
  7. write with kymesh.write_mesh / hpdtool.write, and beside the build <name>.cells.npz (write_cells): every area's
     own cells and ground heights and the build's SHA-256 - the RSNV exporter's cells and heights

Detail features D and F are not generated (counts 0, allowed by the format). Detailed zones are built at pitch 0.2 in a
second pass from their own sampling run and merged with the normal build. BF1943's settings (soldier1943.SETTINGS,
passed as build(settings=...)) turn on AREA_CLIFF, BORDER_SEAM_LINE, JOIN_MARGIN, SEAM_FINE_LINKS, MIXED_OVERLAP
(2026-10-26), SEAM_GAP_NODES (2026-10-24), SEAM_FAR_LINKS (2026-10-29) and NORMAL_LINKS_OWN_GRID (2026-11);
they took the float sector rule (COLUMN_SECTORS_CM off) until 2026-11 and NavKit's whole-centimetre one since.

Configuration (2026-10-31): the constants in config.py are documented defaults, never changed at run time. What a
build is made for comes in as a Settings (BFBC2 = NavKit's defaults); each stage's grid (pitch 0.8 or 0.2) is a Grid
(grid_at); both travel on the stage's Level, and what a build gathers as it goes (order nodes, ladder counts, the
areas' cells) is its BuildState. Before, soldier1943.configure() and set_pitch() rewrote this module's constants, and a
build was right only when they had run first.

The package (navbuild.py until 2026-10-31, split along its stages; every name it had is here as navbuild.<name>):
  config.py   the constants, Settings, Grid, BuildState, JoinScope
  inputs.py   input assembly: the sampling runs on the stage's grid, water and extent rules, the walkable surfaces
              (Level), stage_level (step 1)
  areas.py    a stage's sectors, tiles and areas, their traced boundaries and the links between sectors (steps 2-5)
  graph.py    a sector's route graph and its final tables (step 6)
  stages.py   stage: one grid's build, not yet written
  seams.py    links across mixed-pitch seams, after the two stages are merged
  merge.py    the detailed stage and the merge (merge_detailed), nodes at one position folded
  write.py    the .hpd file and its <name>.cells.npz (step 7)
  __init__.py build(): the normal stage, the detailed one and the merge, the file
  __main__.py the command line

Usage: python -B -m navbuild <samples.bin> <forbid_tris.npy> <XOffset> <ZOffset> <out.hpd> [--step 0.28 (BFBC2's
                   default; the big-endian navkit.py passes BF1943's soldier1943.STEP, 0.37)]
                   [--dynamic dynamic_tris.npy] [--high samples_high_capsule.bin] [--narrow samples_narrow.bin]
                   [--stairs stair_tris.npy] [--exclude exclude_tris.npy] [--exclude-foot exclude_footprint_tris.npy]
"""
import time
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any

# the package's modules, re-exported: navbuild.<name> is every name navbuild.py had (tests set
# navbuild.<module>.<CONSTANT> where they switch a rule, the module that reads it)
from .config import (  # noqa: F401
    AREA_CLIFF, AREA_CLIFF_REACH, AREA_LINK, AREA_Y_MAX, AREA_Y_MIN, BFBC2, BISECT_AREAS, BORDER_NODE_SPACING,
    BORDER_OWNER, BORDER_SEAM_LINE, BRIDGE_UNION, CARRY_RADIUS, CLIP_TO_REFERENCE, COLUMN_SECTORS_CM, DEDUP_GRAPH_NODES,
    DETAILED_LINK_STEP, DETAILED_PITCH, DETOUR_LINK_ALL, DETOUR_MAX, DETOUR_PASSES, DETOUR_REPAIR, DETOUR_TRIGGER,
    DIST_EDGE_MAX, EDGE_SECTOR_RULE, EDGE_SECTOR_TILES, GABRIEL_EDGES, HEADER, JOIN_MARGIN, LADDER_ALL_GROUND,
    LINK_RULE, LINK_STEP, MAX_AREA, MAX_WATER_DEPTH, MIXED_OVERLAP, NODE_COVER, NORMAL_LINKS_OWN_GRID, ONE_WAY_PORTALS,
    ORDER_MIN_ISLAND,
    ORDER_NODE_MIN, ORDER_NODES, PITCH, RADIUS, RESOLUTION, SEAM_FAR_LINKS, SEAM_FINE_LINKS, SEAM_GAP_NODES,
    SECTOR_SAMPLES, SLOPE_MAX, SORT_NODES_BY_ID, SYMMETRIC_PORTALS, TILE, TILE_20M_SECTORS, TILES, WINDOW, Y_OFFSET,
    BuildError, BuildState, Grid, JoinScope, Settings, grid_at)
from .inputs import (  # noqa: F401
    Level, column_sectors, deep_water, outside_bounds, same_grid, stage_level, to_pitch, water_tops)
from .areas import (  # noqa: F401
    _cliff, bisect, border_cell, bridge_union, build_areas, clip_bridges, components, cross_grid_resolver, drop_one_way,
    restore_one_way, same_grid_resolver, sector_links, sector_origin_index, sector_window, tiling, trace, trace_edges,
    trace_emit)
from .graph import (  # noqa: F401
    add_cover_nodes, add_order_nodes, build_graph, finalize_graph, gabriel_prune, join_groups, line_walkable,
    prune_order_nodes, repair_detours)
from .stages import stage  # noqa: F401
from .seams import (  # noqa: F401
    SEAM_FINE_BAND, SEAM_REACH, fine_columns, seam_far_links, seam_fine_links, seam_gap_nodes)
from .merge import (  # noqa: F401
    merge_coincident_border, merge_detailed)
from .write import (  # noqa: F401
    cells_path, read_cells, write_cells, write_file)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .config import Ladder, Log, Points, Water


def build(samples_path: str, tris_path: str | None, xoff: int, zoff: int, out_path: str, step: float = 0.28,
          log: 'Log' = print, dynamic_path: str | None = None, high_path: str | None = None,
          narrow_path: str | None = None, stairs_path: str | None = None, exclude_path: str | None = None,
          exclude_foot_path: str | None = None, seeds: 'Points | None' = None,
          edits: Sequence[dict[str, Any]] | None = None, water: 'Water | None' = None,
          max_water_depth: float | None = MAX_WATER_DEPTH, bounds: Sequence[float] | None = None,
          order_points: 'Points | None' = None, detailed: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
          ladders: 'list[Ladder] | None' = None, settings: Settings = BFBC2) -> BuildState:
    """settings: what the build is made for (Settings: BFBC2, NavKit's defaults, or soldier1943.SETTINGS).
    edits: the operations of a navigation side file (navedits.py applies the walkability ones).
    water: the level's water mesh (vertices, triangles; core/bfbc2core/water.py): ground more than max_water_depth
    under it is not walkable, as in DICE's data (hand edits forcing ground walkable still win).
    bounds: (minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ) of the reference path data (CLIP_TO_REFERENCE), or None.
    detailed: {'samples': a pitch-0.2 sampling run, 'high': its high-capsule run (or None), 'sectors': {(X, Y)}} -
    the second pass: those sectors are built at pitch 0.2 (DICE's detailed zones) and merged with the normal build
    (merge_detailed). Without it the build is the normal one, unchanged.
    Returns the build's BuildState (its order nodes, ladder counts and the areas' cells)."""
    t0 = time.time()
    state = BuildState(detailed_sectors=set((detailed or {}).get('sectors') or ()))
    common: dict[str, Any] = dict(tris_path=tris_path, step=step, log=log, dynamic_path=dynamic_path,
                                  narrow_path=narrow_path, stairs_path=stairs_path, exclude_path=exclude_path,
                                  exclude_foot_path=exclude_foot_path, edits=edits, water=water,
                                  max_water_depth=max_water_depth, bounds=bounds, order_points=order_points, t0=t0,
                                  ladders=ladders, settings=settings, state=state)
    normal = stage(samples_path, high_path, xoff, zoff, seeds=seeds, grid=grid_at(PITCH, settings), **common)
    graphs = merge_detailed(normal, detailed, xoff, zoff, seeds, common, log) if detailed else normal['graphs']
    if ladders:
        log(f'ladders: {len(ladders)}; links made {state.ladder_stats.get("linked", 0)} (counted per stage), ends in '
            f'two sectors {state.ladder_stats.get("split", 0)}')
    write_file(graphs, out_path, log, t0, state, settings)
    return state
```

`bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/navbuild/__main__.py`:

```py
"""navbuild's command line: python -B -m navbuild <samples.bin> <forbid_tris.npy> <XOffset> <ZOffset> <out.hpd> [...]
(from bf1943-auto-navkit-common\tools; or python -B <that folder>\navbuild ...). The options are in navbuild's
docstring (navbuild/__init__.py), which a run without its five arguments prints."""
import sys

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import navbuild  # noqa: E402


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    args = [arg for arg in argv[1:] if not arg.startswith('--')]
    opts = dict(zip(argv[1:], argv[2:]))
    if any(arg in ('-h', '--help') for arg in argv[1:]):
        print(navbuild.__doc__)
        return 0
    if len(args) < 5:
        print(navbuild.__doc__)
        return 1
    navbuild.build(args[0], args[1] if args[1] != '-' else None, int(args[2]), int(args[3]), args[4],
                   float(opts.get('--step', 0.28)), dynamic_path=opts.get('--dynamic'), high_path=opts.get('--high'),
                   narrow_path=opts.get('--narrow'), stairs_path=opts.get('--stairs'),
                   exclude_path=opts.get('--exclude'), exclude_foot_path=opts.get('--exclude-foot'))
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('navbuild', gui=False)       # a log; an unexpected error explained in words (exit code 1)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```
