`bf1943-console-readers/README.md`:

```md
# BF1943 console readers

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** - the STFS reader extracts your own BF1943 (XBLA)
content package; `bf1943-xenia-kit` uses it (`stfs.Package`). OPFOR's disc image reader (`xiso\xiso.py`) was
removed: BF1943 is download-only, so it has no disc. It remains in OPFOR's `bfbc2-tool-suite` and in this
repository's history.

A read-only Python reader for Xbox 360 content packages, from your own console downloads. It only reads the
standard file-system structure: there is no decryption, and no keys are involved.

| Folder | Reads | Commands |
|---|---|---|
| `stfs\stfs.py` | Xbox 360 content packages (STFS: LIVE / PIRS / CON), such as BF1943's XBLA package | `info <package>`, `list <package> [filter]`, `extract <package> <outdir> [filter]` |

`filter` is a case-insensitive part of the file name. It needs only Python 3. `extract` checks every name in the
package before it writes anything: a name that would leave `<outdir>` (a `..`, `.` or empty part, a drive, a
backslash or colon, leading or trailing spaces) is refused with nothing written, since package names are untrusted.
So are two files that would be one file on Windows (names equal but for case) and a file where a folder goes. An
unknown command or a missing argument prints the usage and exits 1.

```
python stfs\stfs.py info    <your BF1943 package>
python stfs\stfs.py list    <your BF1943 package> levels
python stfs\stfs.py extract <your BF1943 package> out
```

## Errors and logs

The reader keeps a log in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\bf1943-tool-suite\logs\` like the suite's other tools; on an error
it prints the cause, what to do and the log's path (exit code 1). A damaged package is refused with a
`ValueError`: a folder entry that is (through its parents) its own parent, or a file whose blocks hold fewer bytes
than its declared size (a package cut short), or a fragmented file whose block chain comes back to a block it
already read, or a name longer than its 40-byte field, or a parent index that is no folder entry - never a hang, a
short file, repeated content or a file moved to the root. A package whose volume descriptor says its hash tables'
second copies are current (block separation bit 1) is refused unread: the reader follows only the first copies.
So is a package with two copies of each hash table (bit 0 clear) and more than 0xAA allocated blocks: there each
level-1 entry chooses its level-0 table's current copy, which the reader does not follow (BF1943's own package is
read-only, bit 0 set, so it is read). A header or file table cut short is a damaged package. A file without a
LIVE, PIRS or CON signature, a 0x24-byte volume descriptor, a plausible header size and a file table of at least
one block is refused as no STFS package. `extract` reads and checks each file before writing
it, through a temporary file beside it, so a damaged file leaves a copy extracted earlier as it was. Tests: `tests\test_console_readers.py`
(the STFS reader on packages it builds, including names that try to leave the output folder, parent loops and
files cut short, block chains that loop and a damaged file over an earlier copy; quick tier); your own BF1943 package is read by the Xenia kit's full
build test (bf1943 tier).

Format notes are in the script's header (STFS follows the public Free60 documentation).

Developed for Project OPFOR. Xbox is a trademark of Microsoft; Battlefield 1943 is © Electronic Arts / DICE.

```

`bf1943-console-readers/stfs/stfs.py`:

```py
"""stfs.py - read-only lister/extractor for Xbox 360 content packages (STFS: LIVE / PIRS / CON).

Reads a package file: `info` and `list` print its header and file table, `extract` writes the chosen files under an
output folder. Package(path) is the library form: .entries (the file table, one dict per entry) and .read(entry).

Usage: python stfs.py info <package>
       python stfs.py list <package> [filter]
       python stfs.py extract <package> <outdir> [filter]      (filter = case-insensitive substring)
       extract refuses (nothing written) a package whose names would leave <outdir> ('..', a drive, ...).
       A damaged file (a block chain that loops, fewer bytes than its size) stops extract with an error and leaves
       an earlier extracted copy of that file as it was. Two files that would be one file here (names equal but
       for case) or a file where a folder goes also stop extract before anything is written.
       An unknown command or a missing argument prints this and exits 1. Refused as damaged: a name longer than
       its 40-byte field, a parent that is no folder entry, a header or file table cut short. Refused as no STFS
       package: no LIVE / PIRS / CON signature, a volume descriptor size other than 0x24, a header size outside
       0x39D-0x100000, a file table of no blocks. Refused unread: a
       package whose block separation has bit 1 set (its second hash-table copies are current; this reader reads
       the first copies only), and a package with two copies of each hash table and more than 0xAA allocated
       blocks (there each level-1 entry chooses its level-0 table's current copy, which this reader does not follow).

Format (public STFS documentation, Free60): header with display name (UTF-16BE at 0x411), header size
(u32 BE at 0x340) and the volume descriptor at 0x379 (block separation u8 at 0x37B, file-table block
count u16 LE at 0x37C, file-table first block u24 LE at 0x37E, allocated block count u32 BE at 0x395). Data blocks are 0x1000 bytes from the
first 4 KiB boundary after the header, with a hash table interleaved before every 0xAA data blocks (and
a level-1 table every 0x70E4); hash entries (0x18 bytes: SHA-1, status, next block u24 BE) chain the
blocks of fragmented files. File table entries are 0x40 bytes: name (0x28), flags (low 6 bits = name
length, 0x40 = blocks consecutive, 0x80 = directory), block count u24 LE at 0x29, first block u24 LE at
0x2F, parent index u16 BE at 0x32 (0xFFFF = root), size u32 BE at 0x34.
"""
import os
import struct
import sys
import tempfile
from typing import Any

BLOCK = 0x1000
HEADER_MIN = 0x39D          # through the volume descriptor's allocated and unallocated block counts

# a file table entry: name, dir, consecutive, count, start, parent and size as read, and path (from its parents)
type Entry = dict[str, Any]


class Package:
    """An open package (its file stays open in .f until closed): its header fields and file table (.entries)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        self.f = open(path, 'rb')
        header = self.f.read(0x1000)
        if len(header) < HEADER_MIN:                # 2026-10-30 review: an IndexError before
            self.f.close()
            raise ValueError(f'damaged package: {len(header)} bytes, shorter than an STFS header '
                             f'({HEADER_MIN:#x} bytes); nothing was read')
        self.magic = header[:4]
        self.name = header[0x411:0x411 + 0x80].decode('utf-16-be', 'ignore').split('\0')[0]
        self.header_size: int = struct.unpack_from('>I', header, 0x340)[0]
        self.separation = header[0x37B]
        self.ft_blocks: int = struct.unpack_from('<H', header, 0x37C)[0]
        self.ft_start = int.from_bytes(header[0x37E:0x381], 'little')
        self.allocated: int = struct.unpack_from('>I', header, 0x395)[0]
        self.base = (self.header_size + 0xFFF) & ~0xFFF
        # read-only packages (separation bit 0 set) keep one hash table per level; others keep two
        self.shift = 0 if (self.separation & 1) else 1
        # an STFS package: its signature, a volume descriptor of 0x24 bytes, a header that ends past the descriptor,
        # and a file table of at least one block (2026-10-30 second review: 4,096 zero bytes read as an empty package)
        why = ('no LIVE, PIRS or CON signature' if self.magic not in (b'LIVE', b'PIRS', b'CON ') else
               f'volume descriptor size {header[0x379]:#x}, not 0x24' if header[0x379] != 0x24 else
               f'header size {self.header_size:#x}' if not HEADER_MIN <= self.header_size <= 0x100000 else
               'a file table of no blocks' if not self.ft_blocks else None)
        if why:
            self.f.close()
            raise ValueError(f'not an STFS package ({why}); nothing was read')
        try:
            if self.shift == 1 and self.allocated > 0xAA:
                # two copies of each table and more than one level: each level-1 entry's status bit 0x40 says which
                # copy of its level-0 table is current (Velocity, GetHashAddressOfBlock). This reader reads the first
                # copies only, so it could follow stale block chains (2026-10-30 review: refused, not read wrong)
                raise ValueError(f'package not read: it keeps two copies of each hash table and has {self.allocated} '
                                 f'blocks (over 0xAA, so level-1 entries choose each level-0 copy), which this reader '
                                 f'does not follow')
            if self.separation & 2:
                # bit 1: the package was last written to the second copy of its hash tables. This reader follows
                # block chains through the first copy only, which may then be stale (2026-10-30: refused rather
                # than read wrong; the active-copy rules are not implemented)
                raise ValueError(f'package not read: its volume descriptor (block separation {self.separation:#x}, '
                                 f'bit 1 set) says its hash tables\' second copies are the current ones, and this '
                                 f'reader reads only the first copies')
            self.entries = self._file_table()
        except BaseException:
            self.f.close()
            raise

    def _fix(self, block: int) -> int:
        """Data block number -> raw block number: a level-0 hash table precedes every 0xAA data blocks
        (the first one included), a level-1 table every 0x70E4, a level-2 table after that."""
        with_level0 = (((block + 0xAA) // 0xAA) << self.shift) + block
        if block < 0xAA:
            return with_level0
        level1_tables = ((block + 0x70E4) // 0x70E4) << self.shift
        if block < 0x70E4:
            return with_level0 + level1_tables
        return (1 << self.shift) + with_level0 + level1_tables

    def _addr(self, block: int) -> int:
        return self.base + self._fix(block) * BLOCK

    def _hash_entry(self, block: int) -> bytes:
        """Level-0 hash entry of a data block (first copy of the table)."""
        if block < 0xAA:
            raw = 0
        else:
            raw = (block // 0xAA) * (0xAA + (1 << self.shift)) + (((block // 0x70E4) + 1) << self.shift)
            if block // 0x70E4:
                raw += 1 << self.shift
        self.f.seek(self.base + raw * BLOCK + (block % 0xAA) * 0x18)
        return self.f.read(0x18)

    def _next(self, block: int) -> int:
        entry = self._hash_entry(block)
        return int.from_bytes(entry[0x15:0x18], 'big')

    def _blocks(self, start: int, count: int, consecutive: bool) -> list[int]:
        """A file's data block numbers: a run from start, or the chain its hash entries name."""
        if consecutive:
            return list(range(start, start + count))
        out: list[int] = []
        block = start
        seen: set[int] = set()
        for _ in range(count):
            if block in seen:                       # a damaged chain: it loops back to a block already read
                raise ValueError(f'damaged package: the block chain from block {start} comes back to block {block} '
                                 f'after {len(out)} block(s); nothing was read')
            seen.add(block)
            out.append(block)
            block = self._next(block)
        return out

    def _file_table(self) -> list[Entry]:
        joined = bytearray()                        # joined in place (up to 65,535 blocks: bytes += copied them all)
        for block in self._blocks(self.ft_start, self.ft_blocks, False):
            self.f.seek(self._addr(block))
            chunk = self.f.read(BLOCK)
            if len(chunk) < BLOCK:                  # 2026-10-30 review: a cut table was read past its end
                raise ValueError(f'damaged package: the file table\'s block {block} holds {len(chunk)} of {BLOCK} '
                                 f'bytes (the package is cut short); nothing was read')
            joined += chunk
        raw = bytes(joined)
        entries: list[Entry] = []
        for i in range(0, len(raw), 0x40):
            e = raw[i:i + 0x40]
            flags = e[0x28]
            if not flags & 0x3F:
                break
            # the name field is 0x28 bytes: a longer name reads the entry's other fields
            if flags & 0x3F > 0x28:
                raise ValueError(f'damaged package: entry {i // 0x40} has a name of {flags & 0x3F} bytes in a 40-byte '
                                 f'field; nothing was read')
            entries.append({'name': e[:flags & 0x3F].decode('latin-1'), 'dir': bool(flags & 0x80),
                            'consecutive': bool(flags & 0x40), 'count': int.from_bytes(e[0x29:0x2C], 'little'),
                            'start': int.from_bytes(e[0x2F:0x32], 'little'),
                            'parent': struct.unpack_from('>H', e, 0x32)[0],
                            'size': struct.unpack_from('>I', e, 0x34)[0]})
        for i, e in enumerate(entries):
            parent = e['parent']
            if parent != 0xFFFF and (parent >= len(entries) or not entries[parent]['dir']):  # before: taken as the root
                raise ValueError(f'damaged package: entry {i} ({e["name"]!r}) names entry {parent} as its parent '
                                 f'folder, and '
                                 f'{"there is no such entry" if parent >= len(entries) else "that entry is a file"}; '
                                 f'nothing was read')
        for i, e in enumerate(entries):
            parts, parent, seen = [e['name']], e['parent'], {i}
            while parent != 0xFFFF and parent < len(entries):
                if parent in seen:                  # a damaged table: the parent chain loops
                    raise ValueError(f'damaged package: entry {i} ({e["name"]!r}) has itself among its parent '
                                     f'folders (entry {parent}); nothing was read')
                seen.add(parent)
                parts.append(entries[parent]['name'])
                parent = entries[parent]['parent']
            e['path'] = '/'.join(reversed(parts))
        return entries

    def read(self, e: Entry) -> bytes:
        """The file's bytes; ValueError when its blocks hold fewer than its declared size (a damaged or cut package)."""
        if e['size'] > e['count'] * BLOCK:
            raise ValueError(f'damaged package: {e["path"]} declares {e["size"]} bytes in {e["count"]} block(s) '
                             f'of {BLOCK} bytes')
        out = bytearray()
        # only the blocks that hold its size, and none past the end of the package (2026-10-31 review, while fuzzing:
        # a count of 2^24 blocks was read block by block, millions of reads past the end, before the size check
        # refused it)
        need = min(e['count'], -(-e['size'] // BLOCK))
        for block in self._blocks(e['start'], need, e['consecutive']):
            self.f.seek(self._addr(block))
            chunk = self.f.read(BLOCK)
            out += chunk
            if len(chunk) < BLOCK:
                break
        if len(out) < e['size']:
            raise ValueError(f'damaged package: {e["path"]} declares {e["size"]} bytes, the package holds {len(out)} '
                             f'(it ends early)')
        return bytes(out[:e['size']])


def safe_target(dest: str, path: str) -> str:
    """Where an archive path is extracted under dest; ValueError for a path that would leave it (a '..', '.' or
    empty part, a drive or root, a backslash or colon in a name - package names are untrusted input)."""
    parts = path.split('/')
    for part in parts:
        if part in ('', '.', '..') or '\\' in part or ':' in part or part != part.strip():
            raise ValueError(f'unsafe path in the package: {path!r} (part {part!r}); nothing was extracted')
    root = os.path.realpath(dest)
    target = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, *parts))
    if os.path.commonpath([root, target]) != root or target == root:
        raise ValueError(f'unsafe path in the package: {path!r} leaves {dest}; nothing was extracted')
    return target


def write_file(dst: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    """dst holding data, or as it was: written to a temporary file beside it, then put in its place."""
    folder = os.path.dirname(dst)
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=folder, prefix='.stfs-', suffix='.tmp')
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(data)
        os.replace(tmp, dst)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.remove(tmp)
        raise


COMMANDS = {'info': (3, 3), 'list': (3, 4), 'extract': (4, 5)}      # command -> (fewest, most) arguments with argv[0]


def extract_plan(pkg: Package, dest: str, flt: str) -> list[tuple[Entry, str]]:
    """[(entry, target)] of the files extract writes, every package path checked first (safe_target); ValueError when
    two files would be one file on this system (names equal but for case, here: the second would replace the first)
    or a file would stand where another file's folder goes. Nothing is written before this passes."""
    for e in pkg.entries:
        safe_target(dest, e['path'])
    root = os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(dest))
    plan: list[tuple[Entry, str]] = []
    owner: dict[str, str] = {}          # target (normcased) -> package path
    folders: dict[str, str] = {}        # folder (normcased) -> the first package path under it
    for e in pkg.entries:
        if e['dir'] or flt not in e['path'].lower():
            continue
        target = safe_target(dest, e['path'])
        key = os.path.normcase(target)
        if key in owner:
            raise ValueError(f'damaged package: {owner[key]!r} and {e["path"]!r} would be one file on this system; '
                             f'nothing was extracted')
        owner[key] = e['path']
        folder = os.path.dirname(key)
        while len(folder) > len(root):
            folders.setdefault(folder, e['path'])
            folder = os.path.dirname(folder)
        plan.append((e, target))
    for key, path in owner.items():
        if key in folders:
            raise ValueError(f'damaged package: the file {path!r} would stand where {folders[key]!r} needs a folder; '
                             f'nothing was extracted')
    return plan


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 2 or argv[1] not in COMMANDS or not COMMANDS[argv[1]][0] <= len(argv) <= COMMANDS[argv[1]][1]:
        print(__doc__)                              # an unknown command or a missing argument does nothing: exit 1
        return 1
    cmd = argv[1]
    pkg = Package(argv[2])
    try:
        if cmd == 'info':
            print(f'{pkg.magic!r} "{pkg.name}" header {pkg.header_size:#x} separation {pkg.separation} '
                  f'file table {pkg.ft_blocks} blocks at {pkg.ft_start}; {len(pkg.entries)} entries')
        elif cmd == 'list':
            flt = argv[3].lower() if len(argv) > 3 else ''
            for e in pkg.entries:
                if not e['dir'] and flt in e['path'].lower():
                    print(f'{e["size"]:>12}  {e["path"]}')
        else:
            flt = argv[4].lower() if len(argv) > 4 else ''
            for e, dst in extract_plan(pkg, argv[3], flt):      # every path checked before anything is written
                write_file(dst, pkg.read(e))            # read (and checked) first: a damaged entry leaves dst as it was
                print(f'{e["size"]:>12}  {dst}')
    finally:
        pkg.f.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('stfs', gui=False)       # a log; an unexpected error explained in words (exit code 1)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-console-readers/tests/test_console_readers.py`:

```py
r"""The STFS reader (stfs.py) on packages built here: both kinds (read-only: one hash table per level; others:
two), with a consecutive file, a fragmented file (hash-entry chain), a folder; info, list and extract, with a
filter; damaged packages (parent loops, short files, block chains that loop) refused, and a damaged file leaves
an earlier extracted copy intact. Your own BF1943 package is read by the Xenia kit's full build test (run_tests.py bf1943).

  python test_console_readers.py
"""
import contextlib
import io
import os
import shutil
import struct
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True                        # run_tests.py starts tests without -B
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import stfs  # noqa: E402


class Checks:
    def __init__(self):
        self.failed = 0

    def check(self, ok, what, detail=''):
        self.failed += not ok
        print(f'{"ok  " if ok else "FAIL"} {what}' + (f'  ({detail})' if detail and not ok else ''))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ STFS

def build_stfs(path, read_only, top_name='top.txt'):
    """Data blocks: 0 file table; 1-2 Content/a.bin (consecutive); 5 -> 3 -> 4 Content/b.bin (fragmented);
    6 top.txt (or top_name, for the path-safety cases)."""
    files = {'Content/a.bin': os.urandom(6000), 'Content/b.bin': os.urandom(9000), top_name: b'top level'}
    h = bytearray(0x1000)
    h[0:4] = b'LIVE'
    header_size = 0x971A
    struct.pack_into('>I', h, 0x340, header_size)
    h[0x379] = 0x24                                     # the volume descriptor's size
    h[0x37B] = 1 if read_only else 0
    struct.pack_into('<H', h, 0x37C, 1)
    h[0x37E:0x381] = (0).to_bytes(3, 'little')
    name = 'Test Package'.encode('utf-16-be')
    h[0x411:0x411 + len(name)] = name
    base = (header_size + 0xFFF) & ~0xFFF
    tables = 1 if read_only else 2

    def entry(name, flags, start, count, parent, size):
        e = bytearray(0x40)
        e[:len(name)] = name.encode('latin-1')
        e[0x28] = len(name) | flags
        e[0x29:0x2C] = count.to_bytes(3, 'little')
        e[0x2C:0x2F] = count.to_bytes(3, 'little')
        e[0x2F:0x32] = start.to_bytes(3, 'little')
        struct.pack_into('>H', e, 0x32, parent)
        struct.pack_into('>I', e, 0x34, size)
        return bytes(e)

    table = (entry('Content', 0x80, 0, 0, 0xFFFF, 0) + entry('a.bin', 0x40, 1, 2, 0, 6000) +
             entry('b.bin', 0x00, 5, 3, 0, 9000) + entry(top_name, 0x40, 6, 1, 0xFFFF, 9))
    blocks = {0: table, 1: files['Content/a.bin'][:0x1000], 2: files['Content/a.bin'][0x1000:],
              5: files['Content/b.bin'][:0x1000], 3: files['Content/b.bin'][0x1000:0x2000], 4: files['Content/b.bin'][0x2000:],
              6: files[top_name]}
    hashes = bytearray(0x1000)
    for b, nxt in ((0, 0xFFFFFF), (5, 3), (3, 4), (4, 0xFFFFFF)):
        hashes[b * 0x18 + 0x15:b * 0x18 + 0x18] = nxt.to_bytes(3, 'big')
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(h)
        for k in range(tables):                       # the level-0 hash table(s) before the first data block
            f.seek(base + k * 0x1000)
            f.write(hashes)
        for b, blob in blocks.items():
            f.seek(base + (tables + b) * 0x1000)
            f.write(blob.ljust(0x1000, b'\0'))
    return files


def stfs_cli(*args):
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        code = stfs.main(['stfs.py', *args])
    return code, buf.getvalue()


def main(argv):
    c = Checks()
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='console_test_')
    try:
        for read_only in (True, False):
            label = 'read-only package' if read_only else 'package with two hash tables'
            path = os.path.join(work, f'pkg_{int(read_only)}')
            files = build_stfs(path, read_only)
            p = stfs.Package(path)
            c.check(p.magic == b'LIVE' and p.name == 'Test Package' and p.shift == (0 if read_only else 1), f'stfs: header ({label})')
            paths = {e['path']: e for e in p.entries}
            c.check(set(paths) == {'Content', 'Content/a.bin', 'Content/b.bin', 'top.txt'} and paths['Content']['dir'],
                    f'stfs: file table with folder paths ({label})', str(sorted(paths)))
            c.check(all(p.read(paths[k]) == v for k, v in files.items()), f'stfs: consecutive and fragmented files read exactly ({label})')
            p.f.close()
            code, out = stfs_cli('list', path, 'content/')
            c.check(code == 0 and 'Content/a.bin' in out and 'top.txt' not in out and 'Content\n' not in out, f'stfs: list with a filter ({label})')
            dest = os.path.join(work, f's_{int(read_only)}')
            code, out = stfs_cli('extract', path, dest)
            c.check(all(open(os.path.join(dest, *k.split('/')), 'rb').read() == v for k, v in files.items()), f'stfs: extract ({label})')
            code, out = stfs_cli('info', path)
            c.check(code == 0 and '4 entries' in out, f'stfs: info ({label})')
        # crafted names must not leave the destination: refused before anything is written
        for bad in ('../outside.bin', '..', '.', 'a\\..\\..\\x.bin', 'C:x.bin', ' top.txt'):
            path = os.path.join(work, 'evil')
            build_stfs(path, True, top_name=bad)
            dest = os.path.join(work, 'evil_out')
            shutil.rmtree(dest, ignore_errors=True)
            try:
                stfs_cli('extract', path, dest)
                refused = False
            except ValueError as e:
                refused = 'unsafe path' in str(e)
            outside = os.path.exists(os.path.join(work, 'outside.bin')) or os.path.exists(os.path.join(work, 'x.bin'))
            c.check(refused and not outside and not os.path.exists(dest), f'stfs: a package name {bad!r} is refused, nothing written')
        # damaged packages: a folder that is its own parent (or two that are each other's), a file shorter than its size
        table = (0x971A + 0xFFF & ~0xFFF) + 0x1000                     # data block 0 of a read-only package
        for label, parents in (('a folder that is its own parent', {0: 0}), ('two entries that are each other\'s parent', {0: 1, 1: 0})):
            path = os.path.join(work, 'cycle')
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                for i, parent in parents.items():
                    f.seek(table + i * 0x40 + 0x32)
                    f.write(struct.pack('>H', parent))
            try:
                stfs.Package(path).f.close()
                why = 'read without an error'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            c.check('parent' in why, f'stfs: {label} is refused', why)
        for label, size, cut in (('a file cut short by the end of the package', 9, 3), ('a size larger than its blocks', 0x1001, None)):
            path = os.path.join(work, 'short')
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                f.seek(table + 3 * 0x40 + 0x34)                         # top.txt, data block 6
                f.write(struct.pack('>I', size))
                if cut is not None:
                    f.truncate(table + 6 * 0x1000 + cut)
            p = stfs.Package(path)
            try:
                got = p.read(next(e for e in p.entries if e['path'] == 'top.txt'))
                why = f'{len(got)} bytes returned'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            p.f.close()
            c.check('bytes' in why and 'returned' not in why, f'stfs: {label} is refused', why)
        # a fragmented file's block chain that loops (b.bin: 5 -> 3 -> 4): refused, not the same block read twice
        hashes = table - 0x1000                                         # the level-0 hash table of a read-only package
        for label, links in (('loops on its first block', {5: 5}), ('comes back to its first block', {3: 5})):
            path = os.path.join(work, 'loop')
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                for b, nxt in links.items():
                    f.seek(hashes + b * 0x18 + 0x15)
                    f.write(nxt.to_bytes(3, 'big'))
            p = stfs.Package(path)
            try:
                got = p.read(next(e for e in p.entries if e['path'] == 'Content/b.bin'))
                why = f'{len(got)} bytes returned'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            p.f.close()
            c.check('chain' in why and 'returned' not in why, f'stfs: a block chain that {label} is refused', why)
        # a damaged file met by extract leaves the copy extracted earlier as it was (read before anything is written)
        path = os.path.join(work, 'again')
        build_stfs(path, True)
        dest = os.path.join(work, 'again_out')
        stfs_cli('extract', path, dest, 'top.txt')
        with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
            f.seek(table + 3 * 0x40 + 0x34)                             # top.txt: a size larger than its one block
            f.write(struct.pack('>I', 0x1001))
        try:
            stfs_cli('extract', path, dest, 'top.txt')
            why = 'extracted without an error'
        except ValueError as e:
            why = str(e)
        kept = open(os.path.join(dest, 'top.txt'), 'rb').read()
        c.check('damaged' in why and kept == b'top level' and os.listdir(dest) == ['top.txt'],
                'stfs: a damaged file leaves its earlier extracted copy intact (no temporary file left)',
                f'{why}; top.txt holds {kept!r}; folder {os.listdir(dest)}')
        # 2026-10-30 review: the command line's exit codes; extract's collisions; damaged file tables; second copies
        path = os.path.join(work, 'cli')
        build_stfs(path, True)
        code, out = stfs_cli('lsit', path)
        c.check(code == 1 and 'Usage' in out, f'stfs: an unknown command prints the usage and exits 1 (exit {code})')
        code, out = stfs_cli('extract', path)
        c.check(code == 1 and 'Usage' in out, f'stfs: extract without a folder prints the usage and exits 1 (exit {code})')

        def renamed(name, index, parent=None):
            """The package with entry <index> renamed (and moved to <parent>)."""
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                f.seek(table + index * 0x40)
                e = bytearray(f.read(0x40))
                e[:0x28] = name.encode('latin-1').ljust(0x28, b'\0')
                e[0x28] = (e[0x28] & 0xC0) | len(name)
                if parent is not None:
                    struct.pack_into('>H', e, 0x32, parent)
                f.seek(table + index * 0x40)
                f.write(e)
        for label, args in (('two files whose names differ only in case', ('TOP.TXT', 1, 0xFFFF)),
                            ('a file named as other files\' folder', ('content', 3))):
            renamed(*args)
            dest = os.path.join(work, 'collide_out')
            shutil.rmtree(dest, ignore_errors=True)
            try:
                stfs_cli('extract', path, dest)
                why = 'extracted without an error'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            c.check('damaged' in why and not os.path.exists(dest), f'stfs: extract refuses {label}, nothing written', why)
        for label, edit in (('a parent past the file table', lambda e: struct.pack_into('>H', e, 0x32, 0x0123)),
                            ('a parent that is a file', lambda e: struct.pack_into('>H', e, 0x32, 1)),
                            ('a name longer than its 40-byte field', lambda e: e.__setitem__(0x28, 0x40 | 0x30))):
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                f.seek(table + 2 * 0x40)                                # Content/b.bin
                e = bytearray(f.read(0x40))
                edit(e)
                f.seek(table + 2 * 0x40)
                f.write(e)
            try:
                stfs.Package(path).f.close()
                why = 'read without an error'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            c.check('damaged' in why, f'stfs: {label} is refused', why)
        build_stfs(path, False)
        with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
            f.seek(0x37B)
            f.write(bytes([2]))                                         # its hash tables' second copies are current
        try:
            stfs.Package(path).f.close()
            why = 'read without an error'
        except ValueError as e:
            why = str(e)
        c.check('second copies' in why, 'stfs: a package whose second hash-table copies are current is refused', why)
        # 2026-10-30 second review: two table copies over more than one level (level-1 entries choose the current
        # level-0 copy, which the reader does not follow) refused; a read-only one of that size still reads; a header or
        # file table cut short is a damaged package, not an IndexError
        for read_only, wanted in ((False, 'level-1'), (True, None)):
            build_stfs(path, read_only)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                f.seek(0x395)
                f.write(struct.pack('>I', 0xAB))                        # 171 allocated blocks
            try:
                stfs.Package(path).f.close()
                why = 'read without an error'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            label = 'read-only package' if read_only else 'package with two copies of each table'
            c.check(wanted in why if wanted else why == 'read without an error',
                    f'stfs: a {label} of more than 0xAA blocks is {"refused" if wanted else "read"}', why)
        for label, cut in (('a header cut short', 0x200), ('a file table cut short', table + 0x100)):
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                f.truncate(cut)
            try:
                stfs.Package(path).f.close()
                why = 'read without an error'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            except Exception as e:
                why = f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
            c.check(why.startswith('damaged package'), f'stfs: {label} is a damaged package', why)
        # 2026-10-30 second review (user's): no signature, or a header that is no STFS header, is refused
        for label, edit in (('4,096 zero bytes', lambda f: (f.truncate(0), f.write(bytes(0x1000)))),
                            ('another signature', lambda f: (f.seek(0), f.write(b'XEX2'))),
                            ('a volume descriptor of another size', lambda f: (f.seek(0x379), f.write(bytes([0x10])))),
                            ('a file table of no blocks', lambda f: (f.seek(0x37C), f.write(bytes(2))))):
            build_stfs(path, True)
            with open(path, 'r+b') as f:
                edit(f)
            try:
                stfs.Package(path).f.close()
                why = 'read without an error'
            except ValueError as e:
                why = str(e)
            except Exception as e:
                why = f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
            c.check(why.startswith('not an STFS package'), f'stfs: {label} is not an STFS package', why)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
    print('all passed' if not c.failed else f'{c.failed} check(s) failed')
    return 1 if c.failed else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

`bf1943-console-readers/tests/test_fuzz_stfs.py`:

```py
r"""stfs.Package fuzzed: damaged packages refused with ValueError

Mutation fuzzing (core/fuzzcheck.py) of the STFS reader on the packages test_console_readers.py builds (no game data;
both kinds: one hash table per level, and two): the header and volume descriptor, the file table, the hash entries
that chain fragmented files, and the data. On any input the package opens and every file in it reads, or the reader
raises ValueError, within its time and memory limits; a package cut short is never read as whole. Fixed seeds;
BF1943_FUZZ=long for more (README "Tests").
"""
import io
import os

import fuzzcheck
import stfs

READERS = fuzzcheck.fixtures('bf1943-console-readers/tests/test_console_readers.py')


def seeds(folder):
    out = []
    for read_only in (True, False):
        p = os.path.join(folder, f'seed{int(read_only)}.stfs')
        READERS.build_stfs(p, read_only)
        data = open(p, 'rb').read()
        tables = 1 if read_only else 2
        base = 0xA000
        table = base + tables * 0x1000                  # data block 0: the file table
        fields = [(0x340, '>I'), (0x37B, 'B'), (0x37C, '<H'), (0x37E, '<H'), (0x395, '>I'), (0x379, 'B')]
        for k in range(4):
            e = table + 0x40 * k
            fields += [(e + 0x28, 'B'), (e + 0x29, '<H'), (e + 0x2F, '<H'), (e + 0x32, '>H'), (e + 0x34, '>I')]
        fields += [(base + b * 0x18 + 0x16, '>H') for b in (0, 3, 4, 5)]
        bounds = [0x340, 0x37C, 0x39D, 0x1000, base] + [base + 0x1000 * k for k in range(1, tables + 8)]
        out.append((data, bounds, fields))
    return out


def test_package(tmp_path):
    made = seeds(str(tmp_path))

    def read(data):
        stfs.open = lambda path, mode: io.BytesIO(data)     # the case in memory: Package opens no file
        try:
            pkg = stfs.Package('case.stfs')
        finally:
            del stfs.open
        return [(e['path'], pkg.read(e)) for e in pkg.entries if not e['dir']]
    # a package cut inside the padding of its last block is read the same: it lost no data (same=)
    report = fuzzcheck.run('stfs.Package', read, [d for d, _, _ in made], iterations=1500,
                           boundaries=[b for _, b, _ in made], fields=[f for _, _, f in made],
                           same=lambda a, b: a == b)
    assert report.ok, report.text()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ regressions

def test_regression_block_count(tmp_path):
    """A file entry of 2^24 - 1 blocks holding 6,000 bytes was read block by block (millions of reads past the end,
    and a list of every block number) before its size was checked; now only its size's blocks are read."""
    import time
    data, _, _ = seeds(str(tmp_path))[0]
    p = str(tmp_path / 'count.stfs')
    damaged = bytearray(data)
    e = 0xA000 + 0x1000 + 0x40                          # the read-only seed's file table, entry 1 (Content/a.bin)
    damaged[e + 0x29:e + 0x2C] = (0xFFFFFF).to_bytes(3, 'little')
    with open(p, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(bytes(damaged))
    pkg = stfs.Package(p)
    try:
        t = time.perf_counter()
        entry = next(x for x in pkg.entries if x['path'] == 'Content/a.bin')
        assert len(pkg.read(entry)) == 6000 and time.perf_counter() - t < 2.0
    finally:
        pkg.f.close()

```

`bf1943-dbx-tools/ARCHITECTURE.md`:

```md
# DbxEdit: how it is built

This page is for developers who will change DbxEdit's code. To use the tools, read the [README](README.md). For the
binary format and what every command does to a file, read [FORMAT.md](FORMAT.md). Section numbers below are
FORMAT.md's.

## Overview

DbxEdit reads and writes binary `.dbx` partitions, BF1943's and BFBC2's alike. A partition is a string table plus a
tokenised tree of elements. DbxEdit's code is 13 C# source files in namespace `Bfbc2Dbx`, listed in
[`DbxEdit.rsp`](DbxEdit.rsp). Three programs compile that same list:
- `DbxEdit.exe`, the command line;
- `DbxEditGUI.exe`, the window (adds `DbxEditGUI.cs`);
- `LevelDiff.exe`, in [`bf1943-diff-workbench/level-diff`](../bf1943-diff-workbench/level-diff/README.md) (adds
  `LevelDiff.cs`).

The three programs share one reader, one writer and one way to write files. The reader accepts exactly what core's
Python reader [`dbx.py`](../core/bfbc2core/dbx.py) accepts, and the XML export matches `dbx.to_xml` character for
character. A file that is read and written again without an edit comes out byte for byte the same. Every output goes
through `SafeWrite`, which refuses the game folder. Core's [`csbuild.py`](../core/bfbc2core/csbuild.py) rebuilds an
exe whenever it is not built from the current sources.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    FE["front ends<br/>DbxEdit.cs Program, DbxEditGUI.cs, LevelDiff.cs"]
    IN["binary .dbx"]
    RD["DbxFile: reader<br/>DbxEdit.Format.cs"]
    PY["core dbx.py<br/>(the same rules in Python)"]
    XE["XmlExport"]
    XMLF[".xml"]
    XI["XmlImport<br/>XmlImport.cs, Values.cs"]
    TB["TypeBook<br/>types learned from --like and --types files"]
    ED["Editor: the edit commands"]
    LC["LevelCheck, SlotFixer<br/>LevelRules1943, Bf1943Types"]
    CT["CullTrees1943<br/>(--bundle folders)"]
    SJ["bf1943-reflection-schema-full.json<br/>(research workspace)"]
    GEN["schema1943.py"]
    SCH["DbxEdit.Schema1943.cs<br/>Bf1943Schema"]
    WR["DbxFile.Serialize<br/>DbxEdit.Writer.cs"]
    SW["SafeWrite<br/>refuses the game folder; temporary file, then replace"]
    OUT["out.dbx, .xml, LevelDiff --json"]
    FIND["findings and exit code"]

    FE --> RD
    IN --> RD
    PY -.->|"same accept/refuse; to_xml equals XmlExport"| RD
    RD --> XE --> SW
    XMLF --> XI
    RD --> TB --> XI --> WR
    RD --> ED --> WR
    RD --> LC --> FIND
    CT --> FIND
    LC -->|"fixslots"| WR
    SJ --> GEN --> SCH --> LC
    WR --> SW --> OUT
    SW --> XMLF
```

## Module map

| File | Responsibility | Key entry points |
|---|---|---|
| `DbxEdit.cs` | the command line: one front end per command, exit codes | `Program.Main`, `Run`, `Xml`, `Roundtrip`, `Edit`, `Import`, `Check`, `FixSlots`, `Binary` |
| `DbxEdit.Format.cs` | reading: varints, `Element`, the string table, `DbxFile` | `new DbxFile(bytes)`, `DbxFile.Read(path)`, `Instances`, `Get`, `Intern`, `Walkable`, `MaxEditDepth` |
| `DbxEdit.Writer.cs` | writing a `DbxFile` back to bytes | `DbxFile.Serialize` |
| `DbxEdit.XmlExport.cs` | binary to XML (section 3) | `XmlExport.Convert`, `ValueText` |
| `DbxEdit.XmlImport.cs` | XML to binary (section 6): the XML reader, matched to the reference file | `XmlImport.Import(xml, reference, typeFiles, out report)`, `Guesses` |
| `DbxEdit.Values.cs` | value typing: `TypeBook`, and the typing half of `XmlImport` | `TypeBook.Learn`, `Find`; `XmlImport.EncodeValue`, `Notes` |
| `DbxEdit.Editor.cs` | the edit commands (section 5) | `Replace`, `ReplacePrefix`, `Drop`, `DropField`, `SetByte`, `SetField`, `SetPartitionGuid`, `AddItem`, `CopyField`, `Graft` |
| `DbxEdit.LevelCheck.cs` | the level check, BFBC2's rules, cull slots (section 7) | `LevelCheck.Detect`, `Run`; `SlotFixer.Fix`; `PlacedObject` |
| `DbxEdit.LevelRules1943.cs` | BF1943's rules and its reflected classes | `LevelRules1943.Check`, `Bf1943Types.IsA`, `Find`, `FieldClass`, `EnumValues` |
| `DbxEdit.CullTrees1943.cs` | BF1943's static cull trees, with `--bundle` (the other half of `LevelRules1943`) | `LevelRules1943.CheckCullTrees` |
| `DbxEdit.Schema1943.cs` | generated data: classes, structs, enums and members, as strings | `Bf1943Schema.Types` |
| `DbxEdit.SafeWrite.cs` | every file write | `SafeWrite.Bytes`, `Text`, `GameFolder`, `InGameFolder`, `WriteRefusedException` |
| `DbxEdit.ToolLog.cs` | the log and error reports, as core `errors.py` keeps them | `ToolLog.Start`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Fail`, `Explain` |
| `DbxEditGUI.cs` (not in the list) | the window; calls the classes above | `Bfbc2Dbx.Gui.GuiProgram`, `MainWindow.Edit`, `EditHistory` |
| `schema1943.py` | rewrites the generated block in `DbxEdit.Schema1943.cs` | `main` |

## How the parts fit

**Reader.**
- `DbxFile(byte[])` parses the 24-byte `{binary}` header, the string table and the element tree (sections 1 and 2).
- Every count, offset and varint is checked before use. A damaged file throws `InvalidDataException` with the offset,
  where `dbx.py` raises `ValueError` for the same file.
- Each `Element` keeps its raw payload bytes, so numbers keep their exact width.
- `DbxFile.Read(path)` adds the path to the message.
- `Walkable` refuses files nested more than `MaxEditDepth` (1,000) levels deep for edit, check, import and LevelDiff.
  `xml` and `roundtrip` take any depth, because they walk the tree iteratively.

**Writer.** `Serialize` keeps the original string area and offsets unless `TableChanged`. It writes the tree from its
elements. So an unedited file comes out unchanged, and an edit changes only what it touches (section 4). `roundtrip`
is the check: it reads and writes every file and reports any that differ.

**XML export and import.**
- `XmlExport.Convert` writes the format of section 3. Its `WholeNumberFields` list is the same as `dbx.py`'s
  `WHOLE_NUMBER_FIELDS`.
- `XmlImport.Import` parses the XML with its own small parser, `TextParser`, which refuses NUL characters.
- It matches each element to the reference file (`--like`, or the `.dbx` next to the XML). An unchanged value keeps its
  exact bytes. A changed value takes the reference's type.
- New elements are typed from a `TypeBook` learned from the reference and the `--types` files. Anything still unknown
  is guessed from the text and listed in `Guesses`, and the command exits 3.

**Value typing.** `TypeBook` records the element kind, number width, float or integer, and bool or byte first byte for
each `tag/first attribute value`. `XmlImport.EncodeValue` gives the bytes for a new text of an existing element, typed
as that element is stored. `setfield` and the window both use it. A decimal field stays decimal, an integer field
takes only integers, and a value that does not fit is refused (`InvalidDataException`). `Notes` collects what was
rounded or changed kind.

**Editor operations.** `Editor` wraps one `DbxFile` and changes its table and tree in place. Each method returns a
count or a success flag, and `Program.Edit` prints it. `Program.Edit` applies its commands in order, reads `@file`
command lists, and checks each command's argument count against its `Usage` table. It writes once, at the end.

**Level checks and cull trees.**
- `LevelCheck.Detect` picks the rule set. If the `LevelData` has BFBC2-only fields, it uses BFBC2's rules; otherwise
  BF1943's. `--rules` overrides it.
- `LevelCheck.Run` walks every instance for empty object-list entries, world objects without their parts, and
  references. With `--bundle`, it resolves references into other partitions through a folder index (`BundleIndex`).
- For BF1943 it then calls `LevelRules1943.Check`, the rules all five shipped levels satisfy, and with `--bundle`
  also `CheckCullTrees`.
- `Bf1943Types` loads `Bf1943Schema.Types` on first use. It answers "is class A a B?", "what class must this member
  point to?" and "which values does this enum have?".
- `SlotFixer.Fix` (`fixslots`) copies cull slots from another level. It matches objects by GUID, then by blueprint and
  position, then by nearest within 50 m.

**SafeWrite.** `SafeWrite.Bytes` and `Text` are the only way any of the three programs writes a file.
- `GameFolder` finds the game folder the way core `game1943.find_game` does: `BF1943_GAME`, else the Xenia kit's
  `dist\xenon` under the suite the exe was built in. A folder counts only when it holds `levels\`.
- `InGameFolder` resolves links and junctions and compares folder identities, so other casings, junctions and shares
  are caught too.
- A write goes to a `~xxxxxxx.tmp` file beside the target, is flushed, and then `MoveFileEx` replaces the target. A
  failed write deletes the temporary file and leaves the old one in place. A hard link at the target loses only its
  name.

**Command front end.**
- `Program.Main` starts `ToolLog`, then dispatches on the first argument: `xml`, `roundtrip`, `edit`, `import`,
  `check` or `fixslots`.
- Exit codes:

  | Code | Meaning |
  |---|---|
  | 0 | done |
  | 1 | failed, or `check` found errors |
  | 2 | bad usage, or the command could not run (a damaged or missing file, a refused write; `ToolLog.Fail`) |
  | 3 | `import` had to guess some types |

- `ToolLog` writes `%LOCALAPPDATA%\bf1943-tool-suite\logs\<tool>-<date>.log` and keeps the 20 newest.

**Window (`DbxEditGUI.cs`).** `MainWindow` holds the open `DbxFile` and an `EditHistory`: the undo stack (each edit's
document before it, as bytes), the edit script (each edit's DbxEdit command, or a `#` comment when it has none) and the
undo depth the file on disk holds (`savedAt`, so an undo past a save marks the document modified).
- Every edit goes through `MainWindow.Edit(apply)`, one transaction (`EditHistory.Run`): the document is serialized,
  `apply` changes it (in place through `Editor`, or by replacing it, as an XML import does) and returns the edit's
  script line, or null when it changed nothing. With a line, the snapshot and the line are recorded together. With
  null, nothing is recorded. When `apply` throws, the document becomes the snapshot again, the tree is rebuilt from it,
  nothing is recorded and the exception goes on (to "Value not accepted", "Import failed" or the window's error
  report). So the undo stack and the script always hold the same edits (2026-11-05: Drop or Graft throwing after the
  snapshot left an undo state without a script line).
- `Undo` pops a state and its script line together (`EditHistory.Undo`). Opening a file starts a new `EditHistory`;
  a file that cannot be opened leaves the old document and its history.

## Building: build.bat, LevelDiff and csbuild

- **`build.bat`** makes this folder the current folder (csc reads the response file's names relative to it). It runs
  the .NET Framework 4 compiler twice:
  - `@DbxEdit.rsp` gives `DbxEdit.exe`;
  - `DbxEditGUI.cs @DbxEdit.rsp` with `-main:Bfbc2Dbx.Gui.GuiProgram` gives `DbxEditGUI.exe`.
- **LevelDiff's `build.bat`** changes to this folder (or to `DBX_TOOLS`) and compiles its own `LevelDiff.cs` with
  `@DbxEdit.rsp` and `-main:LevelDiff`. LevelDiff uses `DbxFile.Read`, `Walkable`, `XmlExport.ValueText`,
  `SafeWrite.Text` (for `--json`) and `ToolLog`.
- **`core/bfbc2core/csbuild.py`** reads `DbxEdit.rsp` (`dbx_sources`) to know what each exe is built from.
  `tools()` maps `dbxedit`, `dbxgui` and `leveldiff` to their exe, `build.bat` and sources. `ensure(name)` rebuilds
  the exe when any of these is true:
  - it is missing;
  - it is older than a source, `DbxEdit.rsp` or its `build.bat`;
  - the SHA-256 of those files differs from the one recorded at its last build in `<exe>.sources` (git-ignored).

  The hub and the tests get their exes only through `csbuild`.
- **The reader's two copies.** `core/bfbc2core/dbx.py` is the reader in Python. Other tools read partitions with it,
  and `to_xml` is DbxEdit's XML. The C# reader's comments name the `dbx.py` rule each check follows. A change to either
  reader goes into both and into FORMAT.md. The tests below catch any difference.

## Key invariants

- **Byte-identical round trip.** Anything an edit does not change is written back as it was read. `DbxEdit roundtrip`
  and the BF1943 tier check it on every Wake Island partition.
- **The C# reader and `dbx.py` agree.** They accept and refuse the same files, and `XmlExport.Convert` equals
  `dbx.to_xml`.
- **The game folder is never written.** `SafeWrite` refuses it, whether reached directly, through a junction or under
  another casing.
- **Writes are atomic.** A failed write leaves the old file and no temporary file behind.
- **No stale exes.** `csbuild.ensure` refuses to hand out an exe built from other sources. Every `DbxEdit.*.cs` in this
  folder must be listed in `DbxEdit.rsp`, and the rsp must list nothing else.
- **The generated schema is not edited by hand.** `schema1943.py` replaces only the block between
  `BEGIN GENERATED BF1943 SCHEMA` and `END GENERATED BF1943 SCHEMA`. It records the schema file's SHA-256 and the
  executable's.

## Tests

| File | Tier | Guards |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_csharp_tools.py` | quick | `csbuild`'s rebuild reasons (on a fake tool); the rsp names every source and each `build.bat` compiles it; builds DbxEdit and LevelDiff; then runs `csharp_regressions.py` |
| `tests/csharp_regressions.py` | (run by the above) | the reader against `dbx.py` (refusals, exit codes, equal XML); nesting limits; SafeWrite (a made-up `BF1943_GAME`, casing, junctions, hard links, failed writes); edit commands and their usage errors; the level check and `fixslots`; LevelDiff; DbxEditGUI through reflection |
| `tests/test_levelcheck1943.py` | bf1943 | the five shipped levels pass BF1943's rules; `--bundle` references and cull trees; 25 broken copies of Wake Island and five of its cull tree fail with their rule's message; rule detection; `fixslots` |
| `../tests/test_bf1943_tools.py dbxedit` | bf1943 | every Wake Island partition round-trips byte for byte; the XML equals `dbx.py`'s; the level check passes; LevelDiff finds no change between a file and itself |
| `../core/tests/test_dbx_malformed.py`, `../core/tests/test_fuzz_core.py`, `../tests/test_fuzz_real.py` | quick, quick, bf1943 | `dbx.py` on damaged files, fuzzed on made-up files and on your partitions |

## Where to start

**Add an edit command.**
1. Write the operation as an `Editor` method.
2. Add its `case` and `Usage` entry in `Program.Edit` (`DbxEdit.cs`), and its line in the usage text.
3. Add it to the window's menus in `DbxEditGUI.cs` if the window should offer it.
4. Describe it in FORMAT.md section 5, and add a `check_*` group to `tests/csharp_regressions.py`.

**Add or change a BF1943 level rule.**
1. Put rules on a single partition in `LevelRules1943.Check`, and rules that need the cull trees in
   `CullTrees1943.cs`.
2. Keep the five shipped levels at 0 errors and 0 warnings.
3. Add a broken copy that the rule catches to `tests/test_levelcheck1943.py`, and describe the rule in FORMAT.md
   section 7.
4. If the rule needs more of the executable's schema, regenerate it with `schema1943.py` instead of editing
   `DbxEdit.Schema1943.cs`.

**Change how the format is read, or add a source file.**
1. Change `DbxEdit.Format.cs` and `core/bfbc2core/dbx.py` together, and update FORMAT.md sections 1 and 2.
2. Run `tests/test_csharp_tools.py`, `core/tests/test_dbx_malformed.py` and the bf1943 tier's `dbxedit` test.
3. A new file named `DbxEdit.<Part>.cs` goes into `DbxEdit.rsp`. `test_csharp_tools.py` fails until it is listed.
