```py
import fbrb1943  # noqa: E402

PY = sys.executable
HEADER = b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x0b'          # mtime 0, OS byte 0x0b, as the game's bundles
failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def made_up(entries=(('a/one.bin', b'first entry'), ('two.bin', b'second'))):
    """A stored (not gzip) bundle of the entries (default: a/one.bin and two.bin), in the layout fbrb1943.py reads."""
    strings, offs = b'', {}
    for s in [n for n, _ in entries] + ['RawFileAsset']:
        if s in offs:
            continue
        offs[s] = len(strings)
        strings += s.encode('ascii') + b'\0'
    d = struct.pack('>II', 2, len(strings)) + strings + struct.pack('>I', len(entries))
    pos = 0
    for name, data in entries:
        d += struct.pack('>6I', offs[name], 0, pos, len(data), len(data), offs['RawFileAsset'])
        pos += len(data)
    d += b'\0' + struct.pack('>I', pos)
    directory = fbrb1943.gzip_member(d, HEADER)
    return b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(directory)) + directory + b''.join(x for _, x in entries)


def run(env, *args):
    r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', TOOL, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace', env=env)
    return r.returncode, r.stdout + r.stderr


def flip(path):
    """The same path with every letter's case swapped (the same file on Windows)."""
    return path.swapcase()


def junction(target, link):
    """A directory junction link -> target (Windows; no privilege needed); False when one cannot be made."""
    if os.name != 'nt':
        return False
    try:
        import _winapi
        _winapi.CreateJunction(target, link)
    except (ImportError, AttributeError, OSError):
        return False
    return os.path.isdir(link) and fbrb1943.canonical(link) == fbrb1943.canonical(target)


def foreign(entries=(('a.bin', b'aa'), ('b.bin', b'bb'))):
    """A bundle whose directory lists its entries out of payload order, as the game's build_overlay-00.fbrb does (the
    reader refuses it; no bundle this tool writes is laid out so)."""
    strings, offs = b'', {}
    for s in [n for n, _ in entries] + ['RawFileAsset']:
        offs[s] = len(strings)
        strings += s.encode('ascii') + b'\0'
    d = struct.pack('>II', 2, len(strings)) + strings + struct.pack('>I', len(entries))
    sizes = [len(x) for _, x in entries]
    starts = [sum(sizes[k + 1:]) for k in range(len(entries))]          # the last entry's data first
    for (name, data), at in zip(entries, starts):
        d += struct.pack('>6I', offs[name], 0, at, len(data), len(data), offs['RawFileAsset'])
    d += b'\0' + struct.pack('>I', sum(sizes))
    directory = fbrb1943.gzip_member(d, HEADER)
    return b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(directory)) + directory + b''.join(x for _, x in reversed(entries))


def game_markers(root):
    """root made a game copy as own_game_root recognises one."""
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'levels'), exist_ok=True)
    open(os.path.join(root, 'config.zz'), 'wb').write(b'made-up config')
    open(os.path.join(root, 'levels', 'levels-common-00.fbrb'), 'wb').write(made_up())
    open(os.path.join(root, 'build_overlay-00.fbrb'), 'wb').write(foreign())


def second_review(tmp, env, game, raw, new):
    r"""2026-10-30 second review: a mod folder laid out as the game is not a game copy; another spelling of the game
    folder (\\localhost\C$\...) is the game folder; a gzip template with flags is refused; replace refuses a name two
    entries hold."""
    # a mod folder: replaced bundles in levels\<level>\, even a replaced levels-common-00.fbrb, a config.zz and a
    # build_overlay-00.fbrb that replace wrote (contiguous): outputs inside it are allowed
    mod = os.path.join(tmp, 'mods', 'my-mod')
    lvl = os.path.join(mod, 'levels', 'wake_island_s')
    os.makedirs(lvl)
    modded = os.path.join(lvl, 'wake_island_s-00.fbrb')
    for p in (modded, os.path.join(mod, 'levels', 'levels-common-00.fbrb'), os.path.join(mod, 'build_overlay-00.fbrb')):
        open(p, 'wb').write(raw)
    open(os.path.join(mod, 'config.zz'), 'wb').write(b'a ported config')
    code, out = run(env, 'extract', modded, os.path.join(mod, 'extracted'))
    check(code == 0 and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(mod, 'extracted', 'two.bin')),
          f'a bundle in a mod folder laid out as the game extracts into that folder (exit {code}: {out.strip()[-120:]})')
    code, out = run(env, 'replace', modded, os.path.join(lvl, 'v2.fbrb'), f'two.bin={new}')
    check(code == 0 and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(lvl, 'v2.fbrb')),
          f'a bundle in a mod folder is replaced into a second file beside it (exit {code}: {out.strip()[-120:]})')
    check(fbrb1943.own_game_root(modded) is None and fbrb1943.is_game_copy(os.path.join(tmp, 'OtherCopy')),
          'own_game_root: a mod folder is no game copy, a folder with the game\'s markers is one')

    # another spelling of the game folder: the administrative share and the \\?\ prefix
    drive, rest = os.path.splitdrive(os.path.abspath(game))
    if os.name == 'nt' and len(drive) == 2:
        spellings = [('\\\\localhost\\' + drive[0] + '$' + rest, 'the \\\\localhost\\C$ share'),
                     ('\\\\127.0.0.1\\' + drive[0] + '$' + rest, 'the \\\\127.0.0.1\\C$ share'),
                     ('\\\\?\\' + drive + rest, 'a \\\\?\\ path')]
        for alias, label in spellings:
            if not os.path.isdir(alias):
                print(f'skip extract into the game folder as {label}: that spelling cannot be opened here')
                continue
            code, out = run(env, 'extract', os.path.join(tmp, 'Input.fbrb'), os.path.join(alias, 'levels', 'via'))
            check(code != 0 and os.listdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels')) == [],
                  f'extract refuses the game folder spelled as {label} (exit {code})')
            code, out = run(env, 'replace', os.path.join(tmp, 'Input.fbrb'), os.path.join(alias, 'levels', 'x.fbrb'),
                            f'two.bin={new}')
            check(code != 0 and os.listdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels')) == [],
                  f'replace refuses the game folder spelled as {label} (exit {code})')

    # a gzip template with FNAME set: refused, not rebuilt into a bundle that does not read back
    import zlib
    payload = b'onetwo'
    c = zlib.compressobj(9, zlib.DEFLATED, -15, 9)
    body = b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x0bpayload\0' + c.compress(payload) + c.flush() + \
        struct.pack('<II', zlib.crc32(payload), len(payload))
    strings = b'a.bin\0b.bin\0RawFileAsset\0'
    d = struct.pack('>II', 2, len(strings)) + strings + struct.pack('>I', 2)
    d += struct.pack('>6I', 0, 0, 0, 3, 3, 12) + struct.pack('>6I', 6, 0, 3, 3, 3, 12) + b'\1' + struct.pack('>I', 6)
    directory = fbrb1943.gzip_member(d, HEADER)
    named = b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(directory)) + directory + body
    try:
        out_raw, _, _ = fbrb1943.Bundle(named).build({'a.bin': b'ONE'})
        try:
            got = fbrb1943.Bundle(out_raw).data('a.bin')
            why = f'rebuilt, reads {got!r}'
        except Exception as e:
            why = f'rebuilt into a bundle that does not read ({type(e).__name__})'
    except ValueError as e:
        why = str(e)
    check('flag byte' in why, f'a gzip template with its name flag set is refused ({why[:90]})')

    # replace of a name two entries hold (equal, or equal but for case): refused, nothing written
    for label, entries in (('two entries of one name', [('x.dbx', b'FIRST'), ('x.dbx', b'second')]),
                           ('two names equal but for case', [('x.dbx', b'FIRST'), ('X.DBX', b'second')])):
        path = os.path.join(tmp, 'dup.fbrb')
        open(path, 'wb').write(made_up(entries))
        dst = os.path.join(tmp, 'dup_out.fbrb')
        if os.path.exists(dst):
            os.remove(dst)
        code, out = run(env, 'replace', path, dst, f'x.dbx={new}')
        check(code != 0 and not os.path.exists(dst), f'replace refuses {label}, nothing written (exit {code})')


def main():
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='fbrb_guards_')
    try:
        game = os.path.join(tmp, 'Game')
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(game, 'levels'))
        env = {**os.environ, 'BF1943_GAME': game, 'LOCALAPPDATA': tmp}
        raw = made_up()
        check(fbrb1943.Bundle(raw).data('a/one.bin') == b'first entry', 'the made-up bundle reads back')
        src = os.path.join(tmp, 'Input.fbrb')
        open(src, 'wb').write(raw)
        new = os.path.join(tmp, 'new.bin')
        open(new, 'wb').write(b'replaced')

        code, out = run(env, 'replace', src, os.path.join(tmp, 'copy.fbrb'), f'two.bin={new}')
        check(code == 0 and fbrb1943.Bundle(open(os.path.join(tmp, 'copy.fbrb'), 'rb').read()).data('two.bin') == b'replaced',
              'replace writes a copy elsewhere')
        if os.name == 'nt':
            code, out = run(env, 'replace', src, flip(src), f'two.bin={new}')
            check(code != 0 and open(src, 'rb').read() == raw, f'replace refuses its input named in another case (exit {code})')
            for target in (os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'x.fbrb'), flip(os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'x.fbrb'))):
                code, out = run(env, 'replace', src, target, f'two.bin={new}')
                check(code != 0 and os.listdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels')) == [],
                      f'replace refuses the game folder as {target[len(tmp):]} (exit {code})')
        for target in (game, os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'out'), flip(os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'out'))):
            code, out = run(env, 'extract', src, target)
            check(code != 0 and os.listdir(game) == ['levels'] and os.listdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels')) == [],
                  f'extract refuses the game folder as {target[len(tmp):] or "itself"} (exit {code})')
        out_dir = os.path.join(tmp, 'out')
        code, out = run(env, 'extract', src, out_dir)
        check(code == 0 and open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'a', 'one.bin'), 'rb').read() == b'first entry', 'extract elsewhere writes the entries')
        manifest = open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'fbrb.manifest.json'), 'rb').read()
        check(b'\n' in manifest and b'\r' not in manifest and manifest.decode('utf-8').startswith('{'),
              'fbrb.manifest.json is UTF-8 with \\n newlines (no \\r)')

        # a hard link already in the output (out\a\one.bin, or the replace output) to a file in the game folder:
        # realpath cannot see a hard link, so only writing a new file and moving it into place keeps the game file
        game_file = os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'linked.bin')
        for label in ('extract', 'replace'):
            original = b'game data, never written'
            open(game_file, 'wb').write(original)
            hout = os.path.join(tmp, 'hout')
            shutil.rmtree(hout, ignore_errors=True)
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(hout, 'a'))
            dest = os.path.join(hout, 'a', 'one.bin') if label == 'extract' else os.path.join(hout, 'copy.fbrb')
            try:
                os.link(game_file, dest)
            except (OSError, AttributeError, NotImplementedError):
                print(f'skip {label} over a hard link: no hard link could be made here')
                continue
            if label == 'extract':
                code, out = run(env, 'extract', src, hout)
                wrote = open(dest, 'rb').read() == b'first entry'
            else:
                code, out = run(env, 'replace', src, dest, f'two.bin={new}')
                wrote = open(dest, 'rb').read()[:4] == b'FbRB' and fbrb1943.Bundle(open(dest, 'rb').read()).data('two.bin') == b'replaced'
            check(open(game_file, 'rb').read() == original and code == 0 and wrote
                  and os.listdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels')) == ['linked.bin'],
                  f'{label} over a hard link to a game file writes the output and leaves the game file unchanged '
                  f'(exit {code})')
            check(not [f for _, _, fs in os.walk(hout) for f in fs if f.endswith('.tmp')],
                  f'{label} leaves no temporary file')
        os.remove(game_file)

        # a write that fails part-way leaves the destination as it was and no temporary file behind
        fdir = os.path.join(tmp, 'fail')
        os.makedirs(fdir)
        fdst = os.path.join(fdir, 'x.bin')
        open(fdst, 'wb').write(b'before')
        saved_fdopen = os.fdopen

        def failing_fdopen(fd, *a, **k):
            f = saved_fdopen(fd, *a, **k)

            class Failing:
                def __enter__(self):
                    return self

                def __exit__(self, *exc):
                    f.close()

                def write(self, data):
                    f.write(data[:2])
                    raise OSError('made-up write failure')
            return Failing()
        os.fdopen = failing_fdopen
        try:
            fbrb1943.write_file(fdst, b'after')
            failed = False
        except OSError:
            failed = True
        finally:
            os.fdopen = saved_fdopen
        check(failed and open(fdst, 'rb').read() == b'before' and os.listdir(fdir) == ['x.bin'],
              f'a failed write leaves the destination as it was and no temporary file ({os.listdir(fdir)})')

        # a junction already inside the output folder (out\a -> the game folder, or -> another folder): the entry
        # a/one.bin stays inside the output folder by name, but would be written through the junction
        elsewhere = os.path.join(tmp, 'elsewhere')
        os.makedirs(elsewhere)
        for label, target in (('the game folder', os.path.join(game, 'levels')), ('a folder outside the output', elsewhere)):
            jout = os.path.join(tmp, 'jout')
            shutil.rmtree(jout, ignore_errors=True)
            os.makedirs(jout)
            link = os.path.join(jout, 'a')
            if not junction(target, link):
                print(f'skip extract through a junction to {label}: no junction could be made here')
                continue
            try:
                code, out = run(env, 'extract', src, jout)
                check(code != 0 and os.listdir(target) == [],
                      f'extract refuses an entry that a junction in the output sends to {label} (exit {code}, '
                      f'{os.listdir(target)} there)')
            finally:
                os.rmdir(link)                                          # the junction only, not its target

        # another drive than the game folder: not inside it (os.path.commonpath raises for paths on two drives)
        if os.name == 'nt':
            from bfbc2core import game1943
            saved = game1943.find_game
            try:
                drive = os.path.splitdrive(game)[0].upper()
                other = ('D:' if drive != 'D:' else 'E:') + '\\mods\\x.fbrb'
                game1943.find_game = lambda given=None: game
                try:
                    inside = fbrb1943.inside_game(other)
                except ValueError as e:
                    inside = f'ValueError: {e}'
                check(inside is False, f'an output on another drive is not in the game folder ({inside})')
                check(fbrb1943.inside_game(flip(os.path.join(game, 'levels'))) is True,
                      'the game folder named in another case is the game folder')
            finally:
                game1943.find_game = saved

        # 2026-10-30 review: entries that would be one file here (the second replaced the first, exit 0, and the
        # manifest listed both), a file where a folder goes, an entry named as the manifest: refused, nothing written
        for label, entries in (('two entries of one name', [('x.dbx', b'FIRST'), ('x.dbx', b'second')]),
                               ('two names equal but for case', [('levels/x.dbx', b'FIRST'), ('Levels/X.dbx', b'second')]),
                               ('a file where a folder goes', [('a', b'file'), ('a/b.bin', b'in a folder a')]),
                               ('an entry named as the manifest', [('fbrb.manifest.json', b'{}')])):
            path = os.path.join(tmp, 'collide.fbrb')
            open(path, 'wb').write(made_up(entries))
            cout = os.path.join(tmp, 'collide_out')
            shutil.rmtree(cout, ignore_errors=True)
            code, out = run(env, 'extract', path, cout)
            check(code != 0 and not os.path.exists(cout), f'extract refuses {label}, nothing written (exit {code})')

        # another game copy than BF1943_GAME's: the input bundle's own copy is only read too (a game copy holds
        # config.zz, levels\levels-common-00.fbrb and a build_overlay-00.fbrb in the game's own layout)
        other = os.path.join(tmp, 'OtherCopy')
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(other, 'levels', 'lv'))
        game_markers(other)
        own = os.path.join(other, 'levels', 'lv', 'level-00.fbrb')
        open(own, 'wb').write(raw)
        before = sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(other, 'levels', 'lv')))
        code, out = run(env, 'extract', own, os.path.join(other, 'levels'))
        check(code != 0 and sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(other, 'levels'))) == ['levels-common-00.fbrb', 'lv'],
              f'extract refuses the input bundle\'s own game copy (exit {code})')
        code, out = run(env, 'replace', own, os.path.join(other, 'levels', 'lv', 'level-01.fbrb'), f'two.bin={new}')
        check(code != 0 and sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(other, 'levels', 'lv'))) == before,
              f'replace refuses the input bundle\'s own game copy (exit {code})')
        code, out = run(env, 'extract', own, os.path.join(tmp, 'from_other'))
        check(code == 0 and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tmp, 'from_other', 'two.bin')),
              f'a bundle of another copy extracts elsewhere (exit {code})')
        second_review(tmp, env, game, raw, new)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

```

`bf1943-fbrb-tool/tests/test_fuzz_fbrb.py`:

```py
r"""fbrb1943.Bundle fuzzed: damaged bundles refused with ValueError

Mutation fuzzing (core/fuzzcheck.py) of the bundle reader on made-up bundles built by test_fbrb_guards.py's builder
(no game data): the whole file (stored and gzip payloads) and, under its gzip, the directory itself. On any input
Bundle returns or raises ValueError (never struct.error, gzip's BadGzipFile, EOFError or zlib.error), within its
time and memory limits, and a bundle it accepts rebuilds (Bundle.build) to one that reads back the same. Fixed seeds;
BF1943_FUZZ=long for more (README "Tests").
"""
import gzip
import struct

import fbrb1943
import fuzzcheck

GUARDS = fuzzcheck.fixtures('bf1943-fbrb-tool/tests/test_fbrb_guards.py')
ENTRIES = (('a/one.bin', b'first entry'), ('two.bin', b'second'), ('levels/x.dbx', bytes(range(40))))


def compressed(entries=ENTRIES):
    """made_up()'s bundle with its payload gzip, as most of the game's are (the directory's flag byte 1)."""
    raw = GUARDS.made_up(entries)
    cut = struct.unpack_from('>I', raw, 4)[0]
    d = bytearray(gzip.decompress(raw[8:8 + cut]))
    d[-5] = 1
    directory = fbrb1943.gzip_member(bytes(d), GUARDS.HEADER)
    payload = fbrb1943.gzip_member(b''.join(x for _, x in entries), GUARDS.HEADER)
    return b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(directory)) + directory + payload


def read(raw):
    b = fbrb1943.Bundle(raw)
    for e in b.entries:
        b.data(e['name'])
    return b


def same_after_build(b, _raw):
    """A bundle the reader accepts rebuilds to one that reads back with the same entries and bytes, or build() refuses
    it in words (a gzip header with a flag set, which it does not copy: README of the bundle tool)."""
    try:
        rebuilt = b.build()[0]
    except ValueError:
        return None
    again = fbrb1943.Bundle(rebuilt)
    if [(e['name'], e['type'], e['size']) for e in again.entries] != [(e['name'], e['type'], e['size'])
                                                                      for e in b.entries]:
        return 'the rebuilt bundle lists other entries'
    if again.payload != b.payload:
        return 'the rebuilt bundle holds other bytes'
    return None


def test_bundle_bytes():
    seeds = [GUARDS.made_up(ENTRIES), compressed()]
    bounds = []
    for s in seeds:
        cut = struct.unpack_from('>I', s, 4)[0]
        bounds.append([0, 4, 8, 18, 8 + cut - 8, 8 + cut, 8 + cut + 10, len(s) - 8, len(s) - 1])
    report = fuzzcheck.run('fbrb1943.Bundle', read, seeds, iterations=1500, boundaries=bounds,
                           fields=[[(4, '>I')], [(4, '>I')]], check=same_after_build)
    assert report.ok, report.text()


def test_bundle_directory():
    """The directory's own fields (counts, offsets, sizes, the string table), mutated under a fresh gzip member."""
    raw = GUARDS.made_up(ENTRIES)
    cut = struct.unpack_from('>I', raw, 4)[0]
    d = gzip.decompress(raw[8:8 + cut])
    payload = raw[8 + cut:]
    strlen = struct.unpack_from('>I', d, 4)[0]
    count = struct.unpack_from('>I', d, 8 + strlen)[0]
    at = 12 + strlen
    fields = [(0, '>I'), (4, '>I'), (8 + strlen, '>I'), (len(d) - 4, '>I')] + \
        [(at + 24 * k + 4 * w, '>I') for k in range(count) for w in range(6)]
    bounds = [4, 8, 8 + strlen, at, at + 24, len(d) - 5, len(d) - 4]

    def bundle_of(directory):
        z = fbrb1943.gzip_member(directory, GUARDS.HEADER)
        return read(b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(z)) + z + payload)
    report = fuzzcheck.run('fbrb1943 directory', bundle_of, [d], iterations=1500, boundaries=[bounds],
                           fields=[fields], check=lambda b, _d: same_after_build(b, None))
    assert report.ok, report.text()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ regressions

def test_regression_cut_and_damaged_gzip():
    """A header cut inside its 8 bytes or a directory cut short was a struct.error; a directory or payload that is not
    whole gzip data passed gzip's BadGzipFile and EOFError through."""
    raw = GUARDS.made_up(ENTRIES)
    for data in (b'FbRB', b'FbRB' + bytes(4), raw[:0x12], b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', 1) + b'\x1f\0', compressed()[:-8]):
        assert fuzzcheck.outcome(fbrb1943.Bundle, data).startswith('ValueError'), fuzzcheck.outcome(fbrb1943.Bundle, data)


def test_regression_directory_fields():
    """A directory of 4 or 8 bytes was a struct.error; a name offset past the string table read a name out of the
    entries after it."""
    raw = GUARDS.made_up(ENTRIES)
    cut = struct.unpack_from('>I', raw, 4)[0]
    d = gzip.decompress(raw[8:8 + cut])

    def bundle_of(directory):
        z = fbrb1943.gzip_member(directory, GUARDS.HEADER)
        return fbrb1943.Bundle(b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(z)) + z + raw[8 + cut:])
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(bundle_of, d[:4]) and fuzzcheck.refused(bundle_of, d[:8])
    strlen = struct.unpack_from('>I', d, 4)[0]
    past = bytearray(d)
    struct.pack_into('>I', past, 12 + strlen, strlen + 4)       # entry 0's name: just past the string table
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(bundle_of, bytes(past))

```

`bf1943-map-inspector/README.md`:

```md
# BF1943 Map Inspector (bf1943-map-inspector)

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** (2026-10-23) - it opens BF1943 levels from your own copy,
read straight from the bundles through `core/bfbc2core/level1943.py`.

Browse a Battlefield 1943 level in 3D and inspect every object: where it is, what it is, which file it comes from,
its full property tree, and how it links to other objects.

**Opening it:** in the suite window (`BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw`), Levels tab: choose a level, then **Open in Map
Inspector** (or double-click the level). Or double-click `inspector.py` here: a picker of your copy's levels opens.
Or from a command line:

```
python inspector.py <level>          e.g. python inspector.py wake_island_s   (or guadal_canal, iwo_jima_s, coral_sea)
```

The level is read from the game folder `bf1943-xenia-kit` extracts (`BF1943_GAME` selects another). The copy is
only read; nothing is unpacked or written. Needs Python 3.10+ with `numpy`, `moderngl`, `glfw` and `imgui-bundle`
(`pip install numpy moderngl glfw imgui-bundle`).

## What it shows

| Layer | From |
|---|---|
| terrain, water | the level's height field (`core/bfbc2core/terrain.py`, big-endian) and sea surface (`water.py`) |
| placed objects, destructibles, dynamic objects, ladders | collision of the placed objects; the group comes from the blueprint (ladder: `LadderEntityData`; destructible: two or more health states) |
| group members | static model groups |
| soldier and vehicle spawns, per team | team 1 (US) blue, team 2 (Japan) red; a short line shows the facing |
| end-of-round spawns | `EndOfRoundSoldierSpawnEntityData` (hidden at start) |
| bases, flags | the capture points, as `bf1943-spawn-map` reads them (a base cannot change team) |
| combat areas, DMZs | their outlines (`DmzEntityData` names its team) |
| map markers | `MapMarkerEntityData` (hidden at start) |
| area points, other | hidden at start |

BF1943's spawns are all `TeamNeutral` in the data, so a spawn takes the side of the base that owns it, or of the
carrier it stands on. BF1943's levels have no Rush objectives, AI orders or effects, so the inspector has no such
layers.

## Using it

- **Camera:** left drag rotates, right or middle drag pans, the wheel zooms, double-click flies to the
  point. F switches to fly mode: hold the right button and use W A S D, Q / E for down / up, Shift for speed.
- **Select:** click an object. The Selection panel shows its type, GUID, partition, blueprint, team,
  player type and position, the objects that reference it, and the full property tree; references in the
  tree are buttons that follow them (with *back*). Over the scene, yellow lines go to what it references and
  cyan lines come from what references it.
- **Search:** by GUID, type, id, name or blueprint, and filter by type; results fly the camera to the object.
- **Measure (M):** clicks add points; the panel gives the last segment (length, horizontal, height, slope),
  the path total, and the last point's height above the terrain. Esc clears.
- Hovering shows what is under the mouse and where.

Window layout is kept in `%APPDATA%\bf1943-tool-suite\`.

For tests: `inspector.py <level> --screenshot out.png [--frames N] [--select <guid>] [--measure "x,y,z;x,y,z"]`
draws, saves a screenshot and exits (exit code 1, nothing written, when the viewer took no picture).
`tests/test_inspector.py` checks that exit code without game data or a window.

```

`bf1943-map-inspector/inspector.py`:

```py
"""BF1943 Map Inspector: browse a BF1943 level in 3D and inspect every object's source and properties.

Reads a level from your copy's bundles (core level1943.py) and shows it in a window; --screenshot draws it, saves
the picture and exits.

  python inspector.py <level>                 e.g. inspector.py wake_island_s (read from your copy's bundles,
                                              core level1943.py; BF1943_GAME selects the game folder)
  python inspector.py <level> --screenshot out.png [--select <guid>] [--frames N]   draw, save, exit (tests)
                     [--measure "x,y,z;x,y,z;..."]   with measure points (tests)

Click an object to select it, double-click to fly the camera to it. Left drag rotates, right or middle drag
pans, the wheel zooms; F switches to fly mode (hold the right button, W A S D, Q / E, Shift faster).
M switches measuring on and off: clicks then add points (distance, height difference); Esc clears them.
The selection's links are drawn over the scene: yellow to what it references, cyan from what references it.
"""
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, cast

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
    # the log and error reports start before the heavy imports,
    from bfbc2core import errors                 # so a missing library is reported too
    errors.setup('map-inspector', gui='--screenshot' not in sys.argv)

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
from imgui_bundle import imgui  # noqa: E402

from bfbc2core import dbx, level1943 as levelmod, viewer  # noqa: E402

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import numpy.typing as npt

    from bfbc2core.level import Entity, Level

type Colour = tuple[float, float, float]
type Point = npt.NDArray[np.float64]
# an overlay line: from, to, colour
type Segment = tuple[Point, Point, Colour]

TERRAIN_ID = 0xFFFFFE
WATER_ID = 0xFFFF00          # + the index of the triangle's shader in Inspector.water_shaders
BLUE, RED, GREY = (0.20, 0.55, 1.00), (1.00, 0.30, 0.25), (0.70, 0.70, 0.75)
# layer: colour, marker size for entities without collision (None: not drawn without collision)
LAYERS: list[tuple[str, Colour, float | None]] = [
    ('terrain', (0.42, 0.47, 0.36), None),
    ('water', (0.18, 0.42, 0.78), None),
    ('placed object', (0.62, 0.60, 0.56), 1.0),
    ('destructible', (0.80, 0.64, 0.46), 1.0),
    ('dynamic object', (0.62, 0.48, 0.34), 0.6),
    ('ladder', (0.95, 0.90, 0.35), 1.0),
    ('group member', (0.55, 0.53, 0.50), None),
    ('soldier spawn, team 1', BLUE, 1.2),
    ('soldier spawn, team 2', RED, 1.2),
    ('soldier spawn, no team', GREY, 1.2),
    ('vehicle spawn, team 1', (0.35, 0.80, 1.00), 2.5),
    ('vehicle spawn, team 2', (1.00, 0.58, 0.35), 2.5),
    ('vehicle spawn, neutral', (0.75, 0.85, 0.80), 2.5),
    ('end-of-round spawn', (0.85, 0.85, 0.55), 0.8),
    ('base', (1.00, 0.60, 0.10), 3.0),
    ('flag', (1.00, 0.85, 0.20), 2.5),
    ('combat area', (0.85, 0.25, 0.85), 1.5),
    ('dmz', (0.30, 0.85, 0.65), 1.5),
    ('map marker', (0.80, 0.80, 0.95), 1.0),
    ('area point', (0.70, 0.70, 0.95), 0.6),
    ('other', (0.60, 0.60, 0.60), 0.6),
]
HIDDEN_AT_START = {'area point', 'other', 'end-of-round spawn', 'map marker'}
# BF1943: Team1 holds the Allies' (US) base, Team2 the Axis' (Japanese) one
TEAM_NAME = {1: 'team 1 (US)', 2: 'team 2 (Japan)', 0: 'neutral', None: 'no team'}
REF_TO, REF_FROM, MEASURE = (1.0, 0.9, 0.2), (0.3, 0.95, 1.0), (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
# a spawn's layer by its team (layer_name)
SOLDIER_SPAWN_LAYER: dict[int | None, str] = {1: 'soldier spawn, team 1', 2: 'soldier spawn, team 2'}
VEHICLE_SPAWN_LAYER: dict[int | None, str] = {1: 'vehicle spawn, team 1', 2: 'vehicle spawn, team 2'}


def layer_name(entity: 'Entity') -> str:
    """The layer an entity is drawn in: its category, spawns split by team."""
    if entity.category == 'soldier spawn':
        return SOLDIER_SPAWN_LAYER.get(entity.team, 'soldier spawn, no team')
    if entity.category == 'vehicle spawn':
        return VEHICLE_SPAWN_LAYER.get(entity.team, 'vehicle spawn, neutral')
    return entity.category


class Inspector:
    """The level's scene (a layer per LAYERS entry), the links between its objects, and the window's panels and
    state: selection, search, measuring. Each panel takes the viewer it is drawn in (`view`)."""

    scene_triangles: int                # set by main(), for the status bar

    def __init__(self, lvl: 'Level') -> None:
        self.lvl = lvl
        self.scene = viewer.Scene()
        self.layer_index: dict[str, int] = {}
        for name, colour, _ in LAYERS:
            self.layer_index[name] = self.scene.layer(name, colour)
        sizes = {name: size for name, _, size in LAYERS}
        self.entity_layer = [self.layer_index.get(layer_name(e), self.layer_index['other']) for e in lvl.entities]
        with_mesh: set[int] = set()
        for mesh in lvl.meshes:
            self.scene.add_triangles(mesh.triangles, mesh.entity, self.entity_layer[mesh.entity])
            with_mesh.add(mesh.entity)
        for e in lvl.entities:
            if e.index in with_mesh or e.position is None:
                continue
            size = sizes.get(layer_name(e), 0.6)
            if size:
                layer = self.entity_layer[e.index]
                centre = e.position + np.array([0, size / 2, 0])
                self.scene.add_box(centre, size, e.index, layer)
                if e.category in ('soldier spawn', 'vehicle spawn'):        # facing: the transform's forward row
                    forward = cast('npt.NDArray[np.float64]', e.matrix)[2, :3]    # positioned: it has a matrix
                    self.scene.add_lines([[centre, centre + forward * (size * 2.5)]], e.index, layer)
        for shape in lvl.shapes:                                           # outlines, in their owner's layer
            layer = self.entity_layer[shape.entity]
            self.scene.add_polyline(shape.points, shape.entity, layer, closed=shape.closed)
            if shape.height > 0:
                top = shape.points + np.array([0, shape.height, 0])
                self.scene.add_polyline(top, shape.entity, layer, closed=shape.closed)
                self.scene.add_lines(np.stack([shape.points, top], axis=1), shape.entity, layer)
        if lvl.terrain is not None:
            self.scene.add_indexed(lvl.terrain[0], lvl.terrain[1], TERRAIN_ID, self.layer_index['terrain'])
        self.water_shaders: list[str] = []
        water = lvl.water
        if water is not None and len(water):
            shader = np.array(water.shader if water.shader else [''] * len(water))
            for name in dict.fromkeys(shader):                             # one id per shader, for the tooltip
                shader_index = len(self.water_shaders)
                self.water_shaders.append(name)
                self.scene.add_indexed(water.vertices, water.triangles[shader == name], WATER_ID + shader_index,
                                       self.layer_index['water'])
        self.counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        for e in lvl.entities:
            self.counts[layer_name(e)] = self.counts.get(layer_name(e), 0) + 1
        self.guids = {e.guid.lower(): e for e in lvl.entities}
        self.referrers: 'dict[int, list[tuple[str, Entity]]]' = {}         # entity index -> [(field, entity)]
        for e in lvl.entities:
            if e.short_type == 'LevelData':                                # lists every object; not a link
                continue
            for path, ref in e.refs():
                target = self.guids.get(ref.lower())
                if target is not None and target is not e:
                    self.referrers.setdefault(target.index, []).append((path, e))
        types: dict[str, int] = {}
        for e in lvl.entities:
            types[e.short_type] = types.get(e.short_type, 0) + 1
        self.types = sorted(types.items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
        self.type_filter = ''
        self.selected: 'Entity | None' = None
        self.search = ''
        self.results: 'list[Entity]' = []
        self.history: 'list[Entity | None]' = []
        self.measuring = False
        self.measure: list[Point] = []                                     # world points

    # --- selection ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def select(self, view: viewer.Viewer, entity: 'Entity | None', focus: bool = False) -> None:
        self.selected = entity
        view.selected = entity.index if entity is not None else viewer.NO_ID
        if entity is not None and focus and entity.position is not None:
            view.camera.focus(entity.position, 40.0)
        self.update_overlay(view)

    def links(self, e: 'Entity | None') -> list[Segment]:
        """Segments to the positioned entities the selection references (yellow) and that reference it (cyan)."""
        out: list[Segment] = []
        if e is None or e.position is None:
            return out
        for _, ref in e.refs():
            target = self.guids.get(ref.lower())
            if target is not None and target is not e and target.position is not None:
                out.append((e.position, target.position, REF_TO))
        for _, referrer in self.referrers.get(e.index, ()):
            if referrer.position is not None:
                out.append((referrer.position, e.position, REF_FROM))
        return out

    def update_overlay(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        segments = self.links(self.selected)
        for start, end in zip(self.measure, self.measure[1:]):
            segments.append((start, end, MEASURE))
        for point in self.measure:                                         # small crosses at measure points
            for arm in ((0.4, 0, 0), (0, 0.4, 0), (0, 0, 0.4)):
                segments.append((point - np.array(arm), point + np.array(arm), MEASURE))
        view.set_overlay(segments)  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]  # numpy points; set_overlay only keeps them

    def on_pick(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> Callable[[int | None], None]:
        """The viewer's click handler: a measure point while measuring, else the clicked object selected."""
        def handler(object_id: int | None) -> None:
            if self.measuring:
                if view.pick_point is not None:
                    self.measure.append(np.asarray(view.pick_point, dtype=np.float64))
                self.update_overlay(view)
                return
            if object_id is None or object_id >= len(self.lvl.entities):   # sky, terrain, water
                self.select(view, None)
            else:
                self.select(view, self.lvl.entities[object_id])
        return handler

    def set_measuring(self, view: viewer.Viewer, on: bool) -> None:
        self.measuring = on
        view.select_on_click = not on

    def keys(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        if imgui.get_io().want_capture_keyboard:
            return
        if imgui.is_key_pressed(imgui.Key.m):
            self.set_measuring(view, not self.measuring)
        if imgui.is_key_pressed(imgui.Key.escape) and self.measure:
            self.measure = []
            self.update_overlay(view)

    def follow(self, view: viewer.Viewer, target: 'Entity') -> None:
        self.history.append(self.selected)
        self.select(view, target, focus=True)

    # --- panels -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def panel_layers(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        self.keys(view)
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((10, 10), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((320, 640), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Layers and search')
        imgui.text(f'{self.lvl.name}: {len(self.lvl.entities)} entities')
        imgui.separator()
        for name, colour, _ in LAYERS:
            n = self.counts.get(name, 1 if name == 'terrain' else 0)
            if name == 'water':
                n = len(self.lvl.water) if self.lvl.water is not None else 0
            if not n:
                continue
            layer = self.layer_index[name]
            imgui.color_button(f'##c{name}', imgui.ImVec4(*colour, 1.0), 0, (14, 14))
            imgui.same_line()
            changed, on = imgui.checkbox(f'{name} ({n})', view.layer_visible(layer))
            if changed:
                view.set_layer_visible(layer, on)
        imgui.separator()
        changed_search, self.search = imgui.input_text('search', self.search)
        changed_type = False
        if imgui.begin_combo('type', self.type_filter or 'any type'):
            if imgui.selectable('any type', not self.type_filter)[0]:
                self.type_filter, changed_type = '', True
            for type_name, n in self.types:
                if imgui.selectable(f'{type_name} ({n})', self.type_filter == type_name)[0]:
                    self.type_filter, changed_type = type_name, True
            imgui.end_combo()
        if changed_search or changed_type:
            self.results = self.matches(self.search.lower().strip())
        imgui.text_disabled(f'{len(self.results)} shown - GUID, type, id, name or blueprint')
        imgui.begin_child('results', (0, 0))
        for e in self.results:
            label = f'{e.short_type}  {e.name or e.id or e.blueprint or ""}##{e.index}'
            if imgui.selectable(label, self.selected is e)[0]:
                self.select(view, e, focus=True)
        imgui.end_child()
        imgui.end()

    def matches(self, query: str) -> list['Entity']:
        """The first 500 entities of the chosen type whose GUID, type, id, name or blueprint holds query (2 characters
        at least; a shorter one lists the type's entities, or none without a type)."""
        pool = [e for e in self.lvl.entities if not self.type_filter or e.short_type == self.type_filter]
        if len(query) >= 2:
            pool = [e for e in pool
                    if query in ' '.join((e.guid, e.type, e.id or '', e.name or '', e.blueprint or '')).lower()]
        elif not self.type_filter:
            pool = []
        return pool[:500]

    def tree(self, view: viewer.Viewer, element: dbx.Element, path: str) -> None:
        """Property tree of an element: containers expand, values show inline, local references are links."""
        for k, child in enumerate(element.children or ()):
            name = child.attr('name') or child.tag
            ref = child.attr('ref')
            if child.children is not None:
                label = f'{name}  [{len(child.children)}]##{path}/{k}'
                if imgui.tree_node(label):
                    self.tree(view, child, f'{path}/{k}')
                    imgui.tree_pop()
            elif ref is not None:
                target = self.guids.get(ref.lower())
                if target is not None:
                    if imgui.small_button(f'-> {name}##{path}/{k}'):
                        self.follow(view, target)
                    imgui.same_line()
                    imgui.text_disabled(f'{target.short_type} {target.name or target.id or ""}')
                else:
                    imgui.text(f'{name} -> {ref}')
            else:
                value = dbx.value(child)
                imgui.text(f'{name} = {value if len(value) < 140 else value[:140] + " ..."}')

    def panel_selection(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        width = imgui.get_io().display_size.x
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((width - 480, 10), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((470, 720), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Selection')
        e = self.selected
        if e is None:
            imgui.text_disabled('Click an object (double-click: fly to it).')
        else:
            if self.history and imgui.small_button('< back'):
                self.select(view, self.history.pop(), focus=True)
            imgui.text(e.short_type)
            imgui.text_disabled(e.type)
            facts = [('guid', e.guid), ('id', e.id), ('name', e.name), ('category', e.category),
                     ('blueprint', e.blueprint), ('blueprint object', e.blueprint_type),
                     ('source', e.partition + (f'  ({e.group})' if e.group else ''))]
            if e.team is not None:
                facts.append(('team', TEAM_NAME[e.team]))
            if e.ai is not None:
                facts.append(('player type', 'AI (PlayerType is not SSHumanPlayer)' if e.ai else 'human player'))
            if e.destructible:
                facts.append(('destructible', 'yes (health states / breakable parts)'))
            for label, value in facts:
                if value:
                    imgui.text(f'{label}: {value}')
            if e.position is not None:
                position = e.position
                imgui.text(f'position: {position[0]:.2f}, {position[1]:.2f}, {position[2]:.2f}')
            if imgui.button('fly to'):
                self.select(view, e, focus=True)
            imgui.same_line()
            if imgui.button('copy guid'):
                imgui.set_clipboard_text(e.guid)
            refs = self.referrers.get(e.index, [])
            if refs and imgui.tree_node(f'referenced by [{len(refs)}]##refby'):
                for k, (field, referrer) in enumerate(refs[:200]):
                    if imgui.small_button(f'<- {referrer.short_type} {referrer.name or referrer.id or ""}##rb{k}'):
                        self.follow(view, referrer)
                    imgui.same_line()
                    imgui.text_disabled(field)
                imgui.tree_pop()
            imgui.separator()
            imgui.begin_child('props', (0, 0))
            self.tree(view, e.element, str(e.index))
            imgui.end_child()
        imgui.end()

    def panel_measure(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        if not self.measuring and not self.measure:
            return
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((340, 10), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Measure', flags=imgui.WindowFlags_.always_auto_resize)
        changed, on = imgui.checkbox('measuring (M)', self.measuring)
        if changed:
            self.set_measuring(view, on)
        imgui.same_line()
        if imgui.small_button('clear (Esc)'):
            self.measure = []
            self.update_overlay(view)
        points = self.measure
        if not points:
            imgui.text_disabled('Click points on the terrain or objects.')
        else:
            last = points[-1]
            imgui.text(f'{len(points)} points; last at {last[0]:.2f}, {last[1]:.2f}, {last[2]:.2f}')
            if self.lvl.heightfield is not None:
                above = last[1] - float(self.lvl.heightfield.height(last[0], last[2]))
                imgui.text(f'last point above terrain: {above:+.2f} m')
            depth = self.water_above(last)
            if depth is not None:
                imgui.text(f'water surface above it: {depth:+.2f} m')
            if len(points) >= 2:
                step = points[-1] - points[-2]
                flat = float(np.hypot(step[0], step[2]))
                imgui.text(f'last segment: {np.linalg.norm(step):.2f} m')
                imgui.text(f'  horizontal {flat:.2f} m, height {step[1]:+.2f} m, '
                           f'slope {np.degrees(np.arctan2(step[1], max(flat, 1e-9))):+.1f} deg')
                total = sum(float(np.linalg.norm(end - start)) for start, end in zip(points, points[1:]))
                imgui.text(f'path total: {total:.2f} m')
        imgui.end()

    def water_above(self, p: Point) -> float | None:
        """Height of the water surface over point p minus p's height, or None where there is no water."""
        water = self.lvl.water
        if water is None or not len(water):
            return None
        # barycentric coordinates (l1, l2, l3) of p in each water triangle (a, b, c) seen from above; d is twice the
        # triangle's signed area in x-z
        t = water.vertices[water.triangles].astype(np.float64)             # (m, 3, 3)
        a, b, c = t[:, 0], t[:, 1], t[:, 2]
        d = (b[:, 2] - c[:, 2]) * (a[:, 0] - c[:, 0]) + (c[:, 0] - b[:, 0]) * (a[:, 2] - c[:, 2])
        with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
            l1 = ((b[:, 2] - c[:, 2]) * (p[0] - c[:, 0]) + (c[:, 0] - b[:, 0]) * (p[2] - c[:, 2])) / d
            l2 = ((c[:, 2] - a[:, 2]) * (p[0] - c[:, 0]) + (a[:, 0] - c[:, 0]) * (p[2] - c[:, 2])) / d
        l3 = 1 - l1 - l2
        inside = (l1 >= 0) & (l2 >= 0) & (l3 >= 0) & np.isfinite(l1)
        if not inside.any():
            return None
        k = np.nonzero(inside)[0][0]
        return float(l1[k] * a[k, 1] + l2[k] * b[k, 1] + l3[k] * c[k, 1] - p[1])

    def tooltip(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        io = imgui.get_io()
        if (io.want_capture_mouse or self.measuring or view.hovered == viewer.NO_ID
                or imgui.is_mouse_down(imgui.MouseButton_.left)):
            return
        if view.hovered == TERRAIN_ID:
            text = 'terrain'
        elif WATER_ID <= view.hovered < WATER_ID + len(self.water_shaders):
            text = 'water  ' + (self.water_shaders[view.hovered - WATER_ID] or '(shader unknown)')
        elif view.hovered < len(self.lvl.entities):
            hovered = self.lvl.entities[view.hovered]
            text = f'{hovered.short_type}  {hovered.name or hovered.id or hovered.blueprint or ""}'
            if hovered.team is not None:
                text += f'\n{TEAM_NAME[hovered.team]}'
        else:
            return
        if view.hover_point is not None:
            point = view.hover_point
            text += f'\n{point[0]:.1f}, {point[1]:.1f}, {point[2]:.1f}'
        imgui.set_tooltip(text)

    def panel_status(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        self.tooltip(view)
        io = imgui.get_io()
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((10, io.display_size.y - 40), imgui.Cond_.always)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((io.display_size.x - 20, 30), imgui.Cond_.always)
        flags = imgui.WindowFlags_.no_decoration | imgui.WindowFlags_.no_inputs | imgui.WindowFlags_.no_background
        imgui.begin('##status', flags=flags)
        imgui.text(f'{view.fps:5.1f} fps   {self.scene_triangles:,} triangles   {view.renderer}   '
                   f'camera: {"fly" if view.camera.fly else "orbit"} (F)   '
                   f'click: {"measure" if self.measuring else "select"} (M)   '
                   f'terrain: {"height field" if self.lvl.heightfield is not None else "samples"}')
        imgui.end()


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    opts: dict[str, str] = {}           # --option -> its value
    args: list[str] = []
    k = 1
    while k < len(argv):
        if argv[k].startswith('--'):
            if k + 1 >= len(argv):
                print(f'error: {argv[k]} needs a value')
                return 2
            opts[argv[k]] = argv[k + 1]
            k += 2
        else:
            args.append(argv[k])
            k += 1
    try:                                                    # bad options are said before the level loads
        measure = measure_points(opts['--measure']) if '--measure' in opts else None
        frames = frame_count(opts.get('--frames', '40'))
    except ValueError as e:
        print('error:', e)
        return 2
    if not args:                                            # started without a level: ask for one
        from bfbc2core import pick
        picked = pick.pick_level('BF1943 Map Inspector')
        if not picked:
            return 1
        args = [picked]
    lvl = levelmod.load(args[0])
    inspector = Inspector(lvl)
    inspector.scene_triangles = inspector.scene.triangle_count()
    panels = [inspector.panel_layers, inspector.panel_selection, inspector.panel_measure, inspector.panel_status]
    view = viewer.Viewer(inspector.scene, f'BF1943 Map Inspector - {lvl.name}', panels=panels)
    view.on_pick = inspector.on_pick(view)
    for name in HIDDEN_AT_START:
        view.set_layer_visible(inspector.layer_index[name], False)
    if '--select' in opts:
        entity = lvl.by_guid(opts['--select'])
        if entity is not None:
            inspector.select(view, entity, focus=True)
    if measure is not None:
        inspector.measure = [np.array(point) for point in measure]
        inspector.set_measuring(view, True)
        inspector.update_overlay(view)
    if '--screenshot' in opts:
        view.exit_after = frames
    view.run()
    if '--screenshot' in opts:
        return save_screenshot(opts['--screenshot'], view.screenshot)
    return 0


def measure_points(text: str) -> list[list[float]]:
    """--measure "x,y,z;x,y,z;...": one or more finite points; ValueError otherwise."""
    try:
        points = [[float(coordinate) for coordinate in point.split(',')] for point in text.split(';') if point.strip()]
    except ValueError:
        points = []
    if not points or any(len(point) != 3 or not all(np.isfinite(point)) for point in points):
        raise ValueError(f'--measure {text!r}: give points as "x,y,z;x,y,z;..."')
    return points


def frame_count(text: str) -> int:
    """--frames N: a whole number of frames, at least 1; ValueError otherwise."""
    try:
        n = int(text)
    except ValueError:
        n = 0
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError(f'--frames {text!r}: give a whole number of frames (1 or more)')
    return n


def save_screenshot(path: str, shot: 'npt.ArrayLike | None') -> int:
    """Writes the viewer's screenshot to path: exit code 0, or 1 when the viewer took none (nothing written)."""
    if shot is None:
        print(f'error: no screenshot was taken - {path} not written')
        return 1
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.imsave(path, np.asarray(shot))
    print('screenshot:', path)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    # a crash: logged, explained in a window, exit code 1 (errors: imported by the bootstrap above, under the same
    # condition)
    with errors.guard():  # pyright: ignore[reportPossiblyUnboundVariable]
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

```py
"""Tests for inspector.py without game data or a window: the --screenshot exit code when the viewer took no picture.

  python -B test_inspector.py
"""
import os
import sys
import tempfile

import numpy as np

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use('bf1943-map-inspector', suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
import inspector  # noqa: E402

failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def options():
    """--measure and --frames are checked before the level loads; an option without its value is exit code 2."""
    if not hasattr(inspector, 'measure_points'):         # an older inspector would load the level and open a window
        check(False, 'options are checked before the level loads (no measure_points)')
        return
    check(inspector.measure_points('1,2,3;4,5,6') == [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]] and inspector.frame_count('7') == 7,
          'good --measure and --frames are read')
    for f, bad in ((inspector.measure_points, '1,2'), (inspector.measure_points, 'a,b,c'), (inspector.measure_points, ''),
                   (inspector.measure_points, 'inf,0,0'), (inspector.frame_count, '0'), (inspector.frame_count, 'x')):
        try:
            f(bad)
            check(False, f'{f.__name__} {bad!r} is refused')
        except ValueError:
            check(True, f'{f.__name__} {bad!r} is refused')
    for args in (['--measure', '1,2'], ['--frames', 'x'], ['--screenshot']):
        check(inspector.main(['inspector.py', 'wake_island_s'] + args) == 2,
              f'{" ".join(args)}: exit code 2 before the level loads')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    options()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        out = os.path.join(tmp, 'shot.png')
        check(inspector.save_screenshot(out, None) == 1 and not os.path.exists(out),
              'no screenshot from the viewer: exit code 1, nothing written')
        check(inspector.save_screenshot(out, np.zeros((4, 4, 3), np.uint8)) == 0 and os.path.isfile(out),
              'a screenshot: written, exit code 0')
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

```
