```md
# BF1943 Navigation Studio (bf1943-navigation-studio)

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** (2026-10-23) for viewing and the path test; there is no
editing.

View a BF1943 level's navigation build in 3D, over the level's terrain, water and collision, with its bases, flags,
spawns and ladders. The build is NavKit's (`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian`): BF1943 ships no path data, so there is
no DICE file to compare with.

**Opening it:** in the suite window (`BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw`), Levels tab: choose a level, then **Open in
Navigation Studio**. Or double-click `studio.py` here: a picker of your copy's levels opens. Or from a command line:

```
python studio.py <level>                       e.g. python studio.py wake_island_s
python studio.py <level> [--hpd <file.hpd>] [--color island|sector|pitch|small-islands]
```

**Files.** The level is read from your copy's bundles (`core/bfbc2core/level1943.py`; `--game <folder>` or
`BF1943_GAME` selects the game folder); the copy is only read. The default build is `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.hpd`, written by
`bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian` (`python navkit.py all <level>`); `--hpd` opens another file. Without a build the
studio says so and exits. Route nodes stand 0.9 m above the ground (half the soldier's 1.8 m).

**Layers:** terrain, water, collision; the build's walkable ground (its 0.8 m cells, on the exact terrain height
where their area's outline lies on the terrain, else at the area's own height: floors above the terrain, such as
house floors, show at their height since 2026-10-24), outlines, portals, border portals, the route graph, ladder ground (violet: ground
reached only through a ladder link) and ladder links; soldier spawns of team 1 (US), of team 2 (Japan) and at
flags; bases, flags and ladders. Collision, outlines, portals, border portals and the route graph are hidden at
start.

**Colour the ground by**

| Mode | Shows |
|---|---|
| island | connected parts of the route graph: the main network green, every other island its own colour |
| sector | the 100 m sectors |
| pitch | detailed zones (0.2 m areas) in orange |
| small islands | islands under 25 nodes in magenta |

In the island modes, ground whose area has no route node in its sector (on no island) is drawn near-black, never in
the main network's green (2026-10-30).

**Path test (P).** Press P, click a start and an end on the ground: the cheapest route over the build's route
graph (its directed edges and stored costs) is drawn, with its cost, length and the detour against the straight
line. Without a route the panel says why: which island each point is on and where they come closest (drawn in
red, with a button that flies there), or that no route node is within 15 m of a point. It plans over the graph
only; a runtime also smooths the route through the areas. (`core/bfbc2core/navpath.py`; `--path "x,y,z;x,y,z"`
for tests.)

**Panels**

- *Navigation:* the build's areas (detailed ones), cells, route nodes and edges, islands, ladder links and
  ladder ground; colour mode; layers.
- *Islands, spawns and flags:* the spawns, bases and flags that are not on the main network (or have no route
  node within 15 m), each with a button that flies there; the carriers are their own networks (the sea divides
  them). Then the islands, largest first, with their size.
- *Selection:* click ground to see its area (sector, tile, layer, pitch, cells, boundary pieces, island);
  click a spawn, base or flag to see its island and its nearest route node. Hovering shows the area under the
  mouse.
- *Path test:* see above.

The camera works as in the Map Inspector (left drag rotates, right drag pans, wheel zooms, double-click flies
to a point, F for fly mode). For tests and pictures: `--screenshot out.png [--frames N] [--color ...] [--island N]
[--path "x,y,z;x,y,z"] [--focus x,y,z [--distance m]] [--yaw rad] [--pitch rad] [--hide <layer>,...]` (`--pitch 1.45`
looks almost straight down; the audit's pictures of the seam breaks and the Iwo Jima beach pocket were made this way,
`work\levels\<level>\audit\pictures\`). `--path` takes exactly two points (else exit code 2 before the level loads);
`--screenshot` ends with exit code 1, writing nothing, when the viewer took no picture. `tests/test_studio.py` checks
the colours, `--path` and that exit code without game data or a window.

The navigation data comes from `core/bfbc2core/navdata.py`, which reads the file with NavKit's byte-exact reader.

The BFBC2 studio's DICE comparison, `--compare` / overlay and edit workflow (`editing.py`, `overlay.py`, navtune
side files with `navkit apply` / `install`) were removed: BF1943 has no DICE reference and no Kynapse runtime to
install into.

```

`bf1943-navigation-studio/studio.py`:

```py
"""BF1943 Navigation Studio: a BF1943 level's navigation build in 3D, with its bases, flags, spawns and ladders.

Reads a level from your copy's bundles and NavKit's .hpd build of it; shows them in a window, or with --screenshot
draws them, saves the picture and exits.

  python studio.py <level> [--hpd <file.hpd>] [--color island|sector|pitch|small-islands] [--game <folder>]
  python studio.py <level> --screenshot out.png [--frames N] [--color ...] [--island N] [--path "x,y,z;x,y,z"]
                   [--focus x,y,z [--distance m]] [--yaw rad] [--pitch rad] [--hide <layer>,...]
                   (tests and pictures; the orbit camera's angles in radians, pitch held within +-1.55: 1.5 looks
                   almost straight down)

The level comes from your copy's bundles (core level1943.py); the build is NavKit's (bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian:
navkit.py build <level> writes work\\levels\\<level>\\navkit\\<level>.hpd, the default; nodes stand half the
soldier's 1.8 m above the ground). BF1943 ships no path data, so there is no reference file to compare with.

Layers: terrain, water, collision, the build's walkable ground (its 0.8 m cells), outlines, portals, border
portals, the route graph, ladder ground and ladder links; soldier spawns (by team), bases, flags and ladders.
Colour the ground by island (the main network is green), by sector, by pitch (detailed 0.2 m zones in orange), or
small islands (under 25 nodes in magenta). Panels: the build's figures and layers; islands (largest first, fly to
each) with the spawns and flags off the main network; the selected area or spawn; the path test (P: click the
start, then the end). The camera works as in the Map Inspector.
"""
import colorsys
import os
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
    # the log and error reports start before the heavy imports,
    from bfbc2core import errors                 # so a missing library is reported too
    errors.setup('navigation-studio', gui='--screenshot' not in sys.argv)

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
from imgui_bundle import imgui  # noqa: E402

from bfbc2core import game1943, level1943, navdata, navpath, viewer  # noqa: E402

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import numpy.typing as npt

    from bfbc2core.level import Entity, Level
    from bfbc2core.terrain import Heightfield

type Colour = tuple[float, float, float]
type Vector = npt.NDArray[np.float64]
# a spawn, base, flag or ladder: (kind, label, position, its entity)
type MapPoint = tuple[str, str, Vector, 'Entity']
# an overlay line: from, to, colour
type Segment = tuple[Vector, Vector, Colour]

NODE_HEIGHT = 0.9                                        # soldier1943: nodes half the soldier's 1.8 m up
ID_AREA = 0x200000                                       # + area index
ID_POINT = 0x100000                                      # + index into Studio.points (spawns, bases, flags)
TERRAIN_ID, WATER_ID, OBJECTS_ID, GRAPH_ID = 0xFFFFFE, 0xFFFFFD, 0xFFFFF0, 0xFFFFF1
COLOR_MODES = ['island', 'sector', 'pitch', 'small islands']
MAIN, NORMAL, DETAILED = (0.35, 0.75, 0.35), (0.30, 0.60, 0.80), (1.0, 0.60, 0.15)
DIMMED, WARNING, MISSING = (0.45, 0.48, 0.45), (0.95, 0.25, 0.85), (0.9, 0.15, 0.15)
LADDER = (0.62, 0.35, 1.0)                               # ground reached only by ladder links, and the links
PATH = (1.0, 0.85, 0.1)
NO_ISLAND = (0.15, 0.15, 0.15)                           # ground whose area has no route node: on no island
LIFT = 0.06                                              # ground cells drawn just above the surface
SMALL = 25                                               # nodes: an island this small is a pocket, not a network
POINT_LAYERS = [('soldier spawns, team 1 (US)', (0.2, 0.55, 1.0)), ('soldier spawns, team 2 (Japan)', (1.0, 0.3, 0.25)),
                ('soldier spawns, at flags', (0.85, 0.85, 0.85)), ('bases', (1.0, 0.6, 0.1)),
                ('flags', (1.0, 0.85, 0.2))]
# a soldier spawn's layer by its team (others: 'at flags')
SPAWN_LAYER: dict[int | None, str] = {1: POINT_LAYERS[0][0], 2: POINT_LAYERS[1][0]}
STATUS_FLAGS = imgui.WindowFlags_.no_decoration | imgui.WindowFlags_.no_inputs | imgui.WindowFlags_.no_background


def hue(k: int, s: float = 0.65, v: float = 0.92) -> Colour:
    """Colour k of a sequence of well-spread hues (golden-ratio steps); s and v: saturation and value."""
    return colorsys.hsv_to_rgb((k * 0.618034) % 1.0, s, v)


def default_hpd(level: str) -> str:
    """NavKit's build of the level, where navkit.py writes it."""
    return os.path.join(game1943.level_work(level), 'navkit', f'{level}.hpd')


def cell_quads(xz: 'npt.NDArray[np.float64]', y: 'npt.NDArray[np.float64]', heightfield: 'Heightfield | None' = None,
               lift: float = LIFT) -> 'npt.NDArray[np.float64]':
    """Two triangles per 0.8 m cell. Cells on terrain follow it (each corner at the terrain's height), so slopes
    show as a surface rather than as steps; other cells (floors, roofs, decks) are flat at their height."""
    half = navdata.GRID / 2
    x, z = xz[:, 0], xz[:, 1]
    corners = ((-half, -half), (half, -half), (half, half), (-half, half))
    on_terrain = np.zeros(len(y), dtype=bool)
    if heightfield is not None and len(y):
        on_terrain = np.abs(heightfield.height(x, z) - y) < 0.05
    corner_points = []
    for dx, dz in corners:
        corner_y = y.copy()
        if on_terrain.any():            # only with a height field
            terrain = cast('Heightfield', heightfield)
            corner_y[on_terrain] = terrain.height(x[on_terrain] + dx, z[on_terrain] + dz)
        corner_points.append(np.stack([x + dx, corner_y + lift, z + dz], axis=1))
    c0, c1, c2, c3 = corner_points
    return np.stack([np.stack([c0, c1, c2], 1), np.stack([c0, c2, c3], 1)], axis=1).reshape(-1, 3, 3)


def box_tris(lo: 'npt.ArrayLike', hi: 'npt.ArrayLike') -> 'npt.NDArray[np.float32]':
    """The 12 triangles of the axis-aligned box from corner lo to corner hi."""
    lo, hi = np.asarray(lo, np.float32), np.asarray(hi, np.float32)
    corners = np.array([[x, y, z] for x in (lo[0], hi[0]) for y in (lo[1], hi[1]) for z in (lo[2], hi[2])],
                       np.float32)
    faces = [(0, 1, 3, 2), (4, 6, 7, 5), (0, 4, 5, 1), (2, 3, 7, 6), (0, 2, 6, 4), (1, 5, 7, 3)]
    return np.array([triangle for a, b, c, d in faces
                     for triangle in (corners[[a, b, c]], corners[[a, c, d]])])


class Studio:
    """The level's scene with the build's layers and points (spawns, bases, flags, ladders), and the window's panels
    and state: selection, colour mode, path test. Each panel takes the viewer it is drawn in (`view`)."""

    triangles: int                      # set by main(), for the status bar

    def __init__(self, lvl: 'Level', nav: navdata.NavData, color: str = 'island') -> None:
        self.lvl, self.nav, self.color = lvl, nav, color
        self.scene = viewer.Scene()
        new_layer = self.scene.layer
        self.layers = {'terrain': new_layer('terrain', (0.40, 0.44, 0.36)),
                       'water': new_layer('water', (0.18, 0.42, 0.78)),
                       'collision': new_layer('collision', (0.58, 0.57, 0.55))}
        if lvl.terrain is not None:
            self.scene.add_indexed(lvl.terrain[0], lvl.terrain[1], TERRAIN_ID, self.layers['terrain'])
        if lvl.water is not None and len(lvl.water):
            self.scene.add_indexed(lvl.water.vertices, lvl.water.triangles, WATER_ID, self.layers['water'])
        for mesh in lvl.meshes:
            self.scene.add_triangles(mesh.triangles, OBJECTS_ID, self.layers['collision'])
        build_layers = (('ground', MAIN), ('outlines', (0.95, 0.95, 0.95)), ('portals', (0.3, 0.9, 1.0)),
                        ('border portals', (1.0, 0.9, 0.2)), ('route graph', (1.0, 0.4, 0.9)))
        layer = {name: new_layer(name, colour) for name, colour in build_layers}
        self.layers.update(layer)
        self.ground_batch = self.scene.add_triangles(cell_quads(nav.cell_xz, nav.cell_y, lvl.heightfield),
                                                     np.repeat(ID_AREA + nav.cell_area, 2), layer['ground'])
        drop = np.array([0, nav.y_offset - 0.12, 0])
        lines = [(k, line) for k, area in enumerate(nav.areas) for line in area.outline]
        if lines:                                    # all outline polylines at once: segments within each line
            line_points = np.concatenate([line for _, line in lines])
            owner = np.repeat(np.arange(len(lines)), [len(line) for _, line in lines])
            keep = owner[:-1] == owner[1:]
            area_of_line = np.array([k for k, _ in lines])
            self.scene.add_lines(np.stack([line_points[:-1][keep], line_points[1:][keep]], axis=1) - drop,
                                 ID_AREA + area_of_line[owner[:-1][keep]], layer['outlines'])
        for key, field in (('portals', 'portals'), ('border portals', 'borders')):
            segments = [(k, portal[0], portal[1])
                        for k, area in enumerate(nav.areas) for portal in getattr(area, field)]
            if segments:
                self.scene.add_lines(np.array([[p0, p1] for _, p0, p1 in segments]) - drop,
                                     np.array([ID_AREA + k for k, _, _ in segments]), layer[key])
        ladder_edge = nav.ladder_edge if nav.ladder_edge is not None else np.zeros(len(nav.edges), bool)
        if len(nav.edges):
            raised = nav.node_pos - np.array([0, nav.y_offset - 0.2, 0])
            edges = nav.edges[~ladder_edge]
            self.scene.add_lines(np.stack([raised[edges[:, 0]], raised[edges[:, 1]]], axis=1), GRAPH_ID,
                                 layer['route graph'])
        ladder_area = np.array([area.ladder for area in nav.areas], dtype=bool)
        if ladder_area.any() and len(nav.cell_area):
            on_ladder = ladder_area[nav.cell_area]
            self.layers['ladder ground'] = new_layer('ladder ground', LADDER)
            self.scene.add_triangles(cell_quads(nav.cell_xz[on_ladder], nav.cell_y[on_ladder], lvl.heightfield,
                                                LIFT + 0.05),
                                     np.repeat(ID_AREA + nav.cell_area[on_ladder], 2), self.layers['ladder ground'])
        if ladder_edge.any():
            self.layers['ladder links'] = new_layer('ladder links', LADDER)
            edges = nav.edges[ladder_edge]
            raised = nav.node_pos - np.array([0, nav.y_offset - 0.3, 0])
            self.scene.add_lines(np.stack([raised[edges[:, 0]], raised[edges[:, 1]]], axis=1), GRAPH_ID,
                                 self.layers['ladder links'])
        # points: soldier spawns (and their alternates), bases, flags; ladders as boxes
        for name, colour in POINT_LAYERS:
            self.layers[name] = new_layer(name, colour)
        self.points: list[MapPoint] = []             # (kind, label, position, entity)
        # level1943.load's bf1943-spawn-map objectives, by GUID
        objectives = lvl.objectives  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]  # BF1943 only, not a Level field
        roles: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {objective['guid']: objective for objective in objectives}
        for e in lvl.entities:
            if e.position is None:
                continue
            if e.category == 'soldier spawn':
                name = SPAWN_LAYER.get(e.team, POINT_LAYERS[2][0])
                self.add_point(name, 'spawn', e.name or e.short_type, e.position, 1.2, e)
            elif e.category in ('base', 'flag'):
                objective = roles.get(e.guid.lower(), {})
                self.add_point('bases' if e.category == 'base' else 'flags', e.category,
                               objective.get('name') or e.name or '', e.position, 2.5, e, tall=25.0)
        self.layers['ladders'] = new_layer('ladders', (0.95, 0.9, 0.35))
        for e in lvl.entities:
            if e.category == 'ladder':
                mesh = next((candidate for candidate in lvl.meshes if candidate.entity == e.index), None)
                if mesh is not None:
                    vertices = mesh.triangles.reshape(-1, 3)
                    k = len(self.points)
                    name = cast(str, e.blueprint).rsplit('/', 1)[-1]      # a ladder is a placed blueprint
                    self.points.append(('ladder', name, (vertices.min(0) + vertices.max(0)) / 2, e))
                    self.scene.add_triangles(box_tris(vertices.min(0) - 0.05, vertices.max(0) + 0.05), ID_POINT + k,
                                             self.layers['ladders'])
        self.main = 0 if nav.islands else -1         # navdata: islands largest first
        self.point_island = [self.island_at(point[2]) for point in self.points]
        self.selected: tuple[str, int] | None = None     # ('area', area index) or ('point', index into points)
        # the path test (P): on or off, its clicked points (start, end) and the route between them
        self.path_mode = False
        self.path_pts: list[Vector] = []
        self.route: navpath.Route | None = None
        self.apply_colors()

    def add_point(self, layer: str, kind: str, label: str, pos: 'npt.ArrayLike', size: float, ent: 'Entity',
                  tall: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """A spawn, base or flag: a box of size m (or a pillar tall m high) in layer, pickable as ID_POINT + index."""
        k = len(self.points)
        position = np.asarray(pos, dtype=np.float64)
        self.points.append((kind, label, position, ent))
        if tall:
            self.scene.add_triangles(box_tris((position[0] - 0.6, position[1], position[2] - 0.6),
                                              (position[0] + 0.6, position[1] + tall, position[2] + 0.6)),
                                     ID_POINT + k, self.layers[layer])
        else:
            self.scene.add_box(np.asarray(pos) + np.array([0, size / 2, 0]), size, ID_POINT + k, self.layers[layer])

    def island_at(self, point: Vector) -> tuple[int | None, float]:
        """(island index or None, route node distance): the nearest node within navpath's join limits."""
        node, distance = navpath.join(self.nav, point)
        return (None, distance) if node is None else (int(self.nav.node_island[node]), distance)

    # --- colours ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def cell_colors(self) -> 'npt.NDArray[np.float64]':
        """(cells, 3) RGB of each ground cell in the colour mode (self.color)."""
        nav = self.nav
        cell_area = nav.cell_area
        island = np.array([area.island for area in nav.areas])[cell_area] if len(cell_area) else np.zeros(0, int)
        if self.color == 'sector':
            sector = np.array([area.sector for area in nav.areas])[cell_area]
            unique, inverse = np.unique(sector, return_inverse=True)
            colours = np.array([hue(k * 7 + 3, 0.5, 0.85) for k in range(len(unique))]).reshape(-1, 3)
            return colours[inverse.ravel()]
        if self.color == 'pitch':
            detailed = np.array([area.detailed for area in nav.areas], dtype=bool)[cell_area]
            return np.where(detailed[:, None], np.array(DETAILED), np.array(NORMAL)).reshape(-1, 3)
        # an area with no route node in its sector has no island (navdata: island -1): NO_ISLAND, never the main
        # network's green - that is the ground no route reaches
        none = (island < 0) | (island >= max(len(nav.islands), 1))
        if self.color == 'small islands':
            size = np.array([i.nodes for i in nav.islands] or [0])
            nodes = size[np.clip(island, 0, len(size) - 1)]
            colours = np.where((nodes >= SMALL)[:, None], np.array(DIMMED), np.array(WARNING)).reshape(-1, 3)
            colours[island == 0] = MAIN
            colours[none] = NO_ISLAND
            return colours
        table = np.array([MAIN] + [hue(k) for k in range(1, max(len(nav.islands), 1))]).reshape(-1, 3)
        colours = table[np.clip(island, 0, len(table) - 1)].reshape(-1, 3)
        colours[none] = NO_ISLAND
        return colours

    def apply_colors(self, view: viewer.Viewer | None = None) -> None:
        """The ground's colours in the viewer, or in the scene before the viewer has it."""
        colours = np.repeat(self.cell_colors(), 2, axis=0)
        if view is not None:
            view.set_colors(self.ground_batch, colours)
        else:
            vertices, tags, _ = self.scene.batches[self.ground_batch]
            self.scene.batches[self.ground_batch] = (vertices, tags,
                                                     viewer.triangle_colors(colours, len(vertices) // 3))

    # --- path test (P) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def set_path_mode(self, view: viewer.Viewer, on: bool) -> None:
        self.path_mode = on
        view.select_on_click = not on

    def path_point(self, view: viewer.Viewer, clicked: 'npt.ArrayLike') -> None:
        """A click in path mode: the start, then the end (a third click starts again)."""
        points = self.path_pts
        if len(points) >= 2:
            points.clear()
        points.append(np.asarray(clicked, dtype=np.float64))
        self.route = navpath.route(self.nav, points[0], points[1]) if len(points) == 2 else None
        segments: list[Segment] = []
        for point in points:
            for arm in ((0.6, 0, 0), (0, 1.5, 0), (0, 0, 0.6)):
                segments.append((point - np.array(arm), point + np.array(arm), (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)))
        route = self.route
        if route is not None:
            ground = navpath.ground_nodes(self.nav) + np.array([0, 0.35, 0])
            if route.found:
                chain = ground[route.nodes]
                segments += [(chain[k], chain[k + 1], PATH) for k in range(len(chain) - 1)]
                segments += [(points[0], chain[0], PATH), (chain[-1], points[1], PATH)]
            elif route.gap:
                gap_start, gap_end = ground[route.gap[0]], ground[route.gap[1]]
                up = np.array([0, 3, 0])
                segments += [(gap_start, gap_end, MISSING), (gap_start, gap_start + up, MISSING),
                             (gap_end, gap_end + up, MISSING)]
        view.set_overlay(segments)  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]  # numpy points; set_overlay only keeps them

    def panel_path(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        if not self.path_mode and self.route is None:
            return
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((380, 10), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Path test', flags=imgui.WindowFlags_.always_auto_resize)
        changed, on = imgui.checkbox('path test (P): click the start, then the end', self.path_mode)
        if changed:
            self.set_path_mode(view, on)
        if imgui.small_button('clear##path'):
            self.path_pts, self.route = [], None
            view.set_overlay([])
        for label, point in zip(('start', 'end'), self.path_pts):
            imgui.text(f'{label}: {point[0]:.1f}, {point[1]:.1f}, {point[2]:.1f}')
        route = self.route
        if route is not None:
            if route.found:
                imgui.text(f'route: cost {route.cost:.1f} m over {len(route.nodes)} nodes '
                           f'(length {route.length:.1f} m, straight {route.straight:.1f} m, '
                           f'x{route.cost / max(route.straight, 1e-9):.2f})')
            else:
                imgui.text(f'no route: {route.reason}')
                if route.gap and imgui.small_button('fly to the gap'):
                    view.camera.focus((self.nav.node_pos[route.gap[0]] + self.nav.node_pos[route.gap[1]]) / 2, 40.0)
        imgui.text_disabled('Over the route graph only; a runtime also smooths the route through the areas.')
        imgui.end()

    def on_pick(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> Callable[[int | None], None]:
        """The viewer's click handler: a path test point in path mode, else the clicked area or point selected."""
        def handler(object_id: int | None) -> None:
            if self.path_mode:
                if view.pick_point is not None:
                    self.path_point(view, view.pick_point)
                return
            self.selected = None
            if object_id is not None and ID_AREA <= object_id < ID_AREA + len(self.nav.areas):
                self.selected = ('area', object_id - ID_AREA)
            elif object_id is not None and ID_POINT <= object_id < ID_POINT + len(self.points):
                self.selected = ('point', object_id - ID_POINT)
        return handler

    # --- panels -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def panel_main(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((10, 10), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((360, 640), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Navigation')
        imgui.text(f'{self.lvl.name}')
        summary = navdata.summary(self.nav)
        imgui.text_disabled(os.path.basename(self.nav.path))
        imgui.text(f'  {summary["areas"]:,} areas ({summary["detailed areas"]:,} detailed), {summary["cells"]:,} cells')
        imgui.text(f'  {summary["nodes"]:,} nodes, {summary["edges"]:,} edges, {summary["islands"]} islands '
                   f'({summary["large islands (25+ nodes)"]} large)')
        if summary['ladder links']:
            imgui.text(f'  {summary["ladder links"]} ladder links, {summary["ladder ground cells"]:,} cells of '
                       f'ladder ground')
        imgui.separator()
        imgui.text('colour the ground by')
        for mode in COLOR_MODES:
            imgui.same_line()
            if imgui.radio_button(mode, self.color == mode):
                self.color = mode
                self.apply_colors(view)
        imgui.separator()
        for name, layer in self.layers.items():
            changed, on = imgui.checkbox(name, view.layer_visible(layer))
            if changed:
                view.set_layer_visible(layer, on)
        imgui.end()

    def panel_islands(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        nav = self.nav
        width = imgui.get_io().display_size.x
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((width - 440, 10), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((430, 440), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Islands, spawns and flags')
        off = [(k, point, island) for k, (point, island) in enumerate(zip(self.points, self.point_island))
               if point[0] in ('spawn', 'flag', 'base') and island[0] != self.main]
        count = sum(1 for point in self.points if point[0] in ('spawn', 'flag', 'base'))
        imgui.text(f'{count} spawns, bases and flags; {len(off)} not on the main network')
        imgui.text_disabled('(the carriers are their own networks: the sea divides them)')
        if off and imgui.tree_node('off the main network'):
            for k, (kind, label, pos, _), (island, _distance) in off[:150]:
                if island is not None:
                    where = f'island {island} ({nav.islands[island].nodes} nodes)'
                else:
                    where = 'no route node within 15 m'
                if imgui.small_button(f'fly##pt{k}'):
                    view.camera.focus(pos, 30.0)
                imgui.same_line()
                imgui.text(f'{kind} {label}: {where}')
            imgui.tree_pop()
        imgui.separator()
        imgui.text(f'{len(nav.islands)} islands (largest first; island 0 is the main network)')
        imgui.begin_child('islands', (0, 0))
        for k, island in enumerate(nav.islands[:300]):
            if imgui.small_button(f'fly##is{k}'):
                view.camera.focus(island.centre - np.array([0, nav.y_offset, 0]), 40.0 if k else 300.0)
            imgui.same_line()
            imgui.text(f'{k}: {island.nodes:,} nodes, {island.cells:,} cells')
        imgui.end_child()
        imgui.end()

    def panel_selection(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        if self.selected is None:
            return
        io = imgui.get_io()
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((io.display_size.x - 440, 460), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((430, 220), imgui.Cond_.first_use_ever)
        imgui.begin('Selection')
        kind, k = self.selected
        if kind == 'point':
            point_kind, label, pos, ent = self.points[k]
            imgui.text(f'{point_kind} {label}')
            imgui.text_disabled(f'{ent.short_type} {ent.guid}')
            imgui.text(f'at {pos[0]:.1f}, {pos[1]:.1f}, {pos[2]:.1f}' + (f', team {ent.team}' if ent.team else ''))
            island, distance = self.point_island[k]
            imgui.text('no route node within 15 m' if island is None else
                       f'island {island}' + (' (main network)' if island == self.main else '')
                       + f', route node {distance:.1f} m away')
        else:
            area = self.nav.areas[k]
            island = self.nav.islands[area.island] if 0 <= area.island < len(self.nav.islands) else None
            imgui.text(f'area {k}: sector 0x{area.sector:04X}, area {area.index}, tile {area.tile[0]},{area.tile[1]}, '
                       f'layer {area.layer}')
            imgui.text(f'pitch {area.pitch:.2f} m{" (detailed zone)" if area.detailed else ""}, {area.cells:,} cells, '
                       f'height {area.min_y:.1f} - {area.max_y:.1f} m')
            if area.ladder:
                imgui.text_colored(imgui.ImVec4(*LADDER, 1.0), 'ladder ground: reached only through a ladder link')
            imgui.text(f'{len(area.outline)} outline lines, {len(area.portals)} portals, '
                       f'{len(area.borders)} border portals')
            if island is not None:
                imgui.text(f'island {area.island}{" (main network)" if area.island == 0 else ""}: '
                           f'{island.nodes:,} nodes, {island.cells:,} cells')
        imgui.end()

    def panel_status(self, view: viewer.Viewer) -> None:
        io = imgui.get_io()
        if not io.want_capture_keyboard and imgui.is_key_pressed(imgui.Key.p):
            self.set_path_mode(view, not self.path_mode)
        if not io.want_capture_mouse and view.hovered != viewer.NO_ID:
            if ID_AREA <= view.hovered < ID_AREA + len(self.nav.areas):
                area = self.nav.areas[view.hovered - ID_AREA]
                imgui.set_tooltip(f'area {view.hovered - ID_AREA} - sector 0x{area.sector:04X}, island {area.island}, '
                                  f'pitch {area.pitch:.1f}')
            elif ID_POINT <= view.hovered < ID_POINT + len(self.points):
                point_kind, label, _, _ = self.points[view.hovered - ID_POINT]
                imgui.set_tooltip(f'{point_kind} {label}')
        imgui.set_next_window_pos((10, io.display_size.y - 40), imgui.Cond_.always)
        imgui.set_next_window_size((io.display_size.x - 20, 30), imgui.Cond_.always)
        imgui.begin('##status', flags=STATUS_FLAGS)
        imgui.text(f'{view.fps:5.1f} fps   {self.triangles:,} triangles   {view.renderer}   colour: {self.color}   '
                   f'camera: {"fly" if view.camera.fly else "orbit"} (F)   P: path test')
        imgui.end()


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    opts: dict[str, str] = {}           # --option -> its value
    args: list[str] = []
    k = 1
    while k < len(argv):
        if argv[k].startswith('--'):
            if k + 1 >= len(argv):
                print(f'error: {argv[k]} needs a value')
                return 2
            opts[argv[k]] = argv[k + 1]
            k += 2
        else:
            args.append(argv[k])
            k += 1
    try:                                                    # bad options are said before the level loads
        checked = check_options(opts)
    except ValueError as e:
        print('error:', e)
        return 2
    if not args:                                            # started without a level: ask for one
        from bfbc2core import pick
        picked = pick.pick_level('BF1943 Navigation Studio')
        if not picked:
            return 1
        args = [picked]
    lvl = level1943.load(args[0], opts.get('--game'))
    hpd = opts.get('--hpd', default_hpd(lvl.lv))
    if not os.path.isfile(hpd):
        print(f'no navigation build for {lvl.lv} ({hpd}): build it with bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian '
              f'(python navkit.py all {lvl.lv}), or pass --hpd <file>')
        return 1
    print(f'navigation: {hpd}')
    nav = navdata.load(hpd, lvl.heightfield, y_offset=NODE_HEIGHT)
    studio = Studio(lvl, nav, checked['color'])
    studio.triangles = studio.scene.triangle_count()
    panels = [studio.panel_main, studio.panel_islands, studio.panel_selection, studio.panel_path, studio.panel_status]
    view = viewer.Viewer(studio.scene, f'BF1943 Navigation Studio - {lvl.name}', panels=panels)
    view.on_pick = studio.on_pick(view)
    hide = set(opts.get('--hide', 'collision,outlines,portals,border portals,route graph').split(','))
    for name, layer in studio.layers.items():
        if name in hide:
            view.set_layer_visible(layer, False)
    if checked['island'] is not None and checked['island'] < len(nav.islands):
        view.camera.focus(nav.islands[checked['island']].centre, 60.0)
    if checked['path'] is not None:                         # tests: a path test between two points
        studio.set_path_mode(view, True)
        for point in checked['path']:
            studio.path_point(view, point)
        route = cast(navpath.Route, studio.route)           # two points given: a route was searched
        print('path: ' + (f'cost {route.cost:.1f} m, {len(route.nodes)} nodes' if route.found
                          else f'none - {route.reason}'))
    if checked['focus'] is not None:                        # tests: the camera on a point
        view.camera.focus(np.array(checked['focus']), checked['distance'])
    if checked['yaw'] is not None:                          # the orbit camera's angles (radians; pitch 1.5 looks down)
        view.camera.yaw = checked['yaw']
    if checked['pitch'] is not None:
        view.camera.pitch = max(-1.55, min(1.55, checked['pitch']))
    if '--screenshot' in opts:
        view.exit_after = checked['frames']
    view.run()
    if '--screenshot' in opts:
        return save_screenshot(opts['--screenshot'], view.screenshot)
    return 0


def check_options(opts: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The options' values, checked before the level loads: {'color', 'island', 'frames', 'path', 'focus', 'distance',
    'yaw', 'pitch'} (None where not given); ValueError naming the option otherwise."""
    def number(key: str, default: float | None = None) -> float | None:
        if key not in opts:
            return default
        try:
            value = float(opts[key])
        except ValueError:
            value = float('nan')
        if not np.isfinite(value):
            raise ValueError(f'{key} {opts[key]!r}: give a number')
        return value

    def whole(key: str, default: int | None = None, low: int = 0) -> int | None:
        if key not in opts:
            return default
        try:
            n = int(opts[key])
        except ValueError:
            n = low - 1
        if n < low:
            raise ValueError(f'{key} {opts[key]!r}: give a whole number ({low} or more)')
        return n
    color = opts.get('--color', 'island').replace('-', ' ')   # small-islands: the 'small islands' mode
    if color not in COLOR_MODES:
        modes = ', '.join(mode.replace(' ', '-') for mode in COLOR_MODES)
        raise ValueError(f'--color {opts["--color"]!r}: give one of {modes}')
    focus = None
    if '--focus' in opts:
        focus = points(opts['--focus'], 1, '--focus', '"x,y,z"')[0]
    return {'color': color, 'island': whole('--island'), 'frames': whole('--frames', 40, 1),
            'path': path_points(opts['--path']) if '--path' in opts else None, 'focus': focus,
            'distance': number('--distance', 45.0), 'yaw': number('--yaw'), 'pitch': number('--pitch')}


def points(text: str, count: int, key: str, form: str) -> list[list[float]]:
    """count points "x,y,z" separated by ";", all finite; ValueError otherwise."""
    try:
        parsed = [[float(coordinate) for coordinate in point.split(',')] for point in text.split(';') if point.strip()]
    except ValueError:
        parsed = []
    if len(parsed) != count or any(len(point) != 3 or not all(np.isfinite(point)) for point in parsed):
        raise ValueError(f'{key} {text!r}: give {form}')
    return parsed


def path_points(text: str) -> list[list[float]]:
    """--path "x,y,z;x,y,z": exactly two points (the start and the end); ValueError otherwise."""
    return points(text, 2, '--path', 'two points, "x,y,z;x,y,z"')


def save_screenshot(path: str, shot: 'npt.ArrayLike | None') -> int:
    """Writes the viewer's screenshot to path: exit code 0, or 1 when the viewer took none (nothing written)."""
    if shot is None:
        print(f'error: no screenshot was taken - {path} not written')
        return 1
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.imsave(path, np.asarray(shot))
    print('screenshot:', path)
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    # a crash: logged, explained in a window, exit code 1 (errors: imported by the bootstrap above, under the same
    # condition)
    with errors.guard():  # pyright: ignore[reportPossiblyUnboundVariable]
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-navigation-studio/tests/test_studio.py`:

```py
"""Tests for studio.py without game data or a window: the ground colours of areas on no island, the --path option, and
the --screenshot exit code when the viewer took no picture.

  python -B test_studio.py
"""
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import types

import numpy as np

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use('bf1943-navigation-studio', suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
import studio  # noqa: E402

failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def colours():
    """An area with no route node in its sector (navdata leaves its island -1) is not painted as the main network."""
    areas = [types.SimpleNamespace(island=0, sector=1, detailed=False), types.SimpleNamespace(island=-1, sector=1, detailed=True),
             types.SimpleNamespace(island=1, sector=2, detailed=False)]
    nav = types.SimpleNamespace(cell_area=np.array([0, 1, 2]), areas=areas,
                                islands=[types.SimpleNamespace(nodes=100), types.SimpleNamespace(nodes=3)])
    for mode in ('island', 'small islands'):
        c = studio.Studio.cell_colors(types.SimpleNamespace(nav=nav, color=mode))
        check(c.shape == (3, 3) and np.allclose(c[0], studio.MAIN) and np.allclose(c[1], studio.NO_ISLAND)
              and not np.allclose(c[2], studio.MAIN), f'{mode}: main network green, an area on no island not green')
    for mode in ('sector', 'pitch', 'island'):
        empty = types.SimpleNamespace(cell_area=np.zeros(0, int), areas=[], islands=[])
        c = studio.Studio.cell_colors(types.SimpleNamespace(nav=empty, color=mode))
        check(c.shape == (0, 3), f'{mode}: a build without cells gives no colours, shaped (0, 3)')


def options():
    check(studio.path_points('1,2,3;4,5,6') == [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]], '--path: two points')
    for bad in ('1,2,3', '1,2,3;4,5,6;7,8,9', '1,2;3,4', 'a,b,c;1,2,3'):
        try:
            studio.path_points(bad)
            check(False, f'--path {bad!r} is refused')
        except ValueError:
            check(True, f'--path {bad!r} is refused')
    check(studio.main(['studio.py', 'wake_island_s', '--path', '1,2,3']) == 2, 'a bad --path ends with exit code 2 at once')
    if not hasattr(studio, 'check_options'):              # an older studio would load the level and open a window
        check(False, 'the other options are checked before the level loads (no check_options)')
        return
    good = studio.check_options({'--island': '2', '--frames': '5', '--focus': '1,2,3', '--color': 'small-islands',
                                 '--yaw': '0.5', '--pitch': '1.2', '--distance': '30'})
    check(good['island'] == 2 and good['frames'] == 5 and good['focus'] == [1, 2, 3] and good['color'] == 'small islands'
          and good['yaw'] == 0.5 and good['pitch'] == 1.2 and good['distance'] == 30, f'good options are read ({good})')
    for key, bad in (('--island', 'x'), ('--island', '-1'), ('--frames', '0'), ('--frames', 'many'), ('--focus', '1,2'),
                     ('--yaw', 'left'), ('--pitch', 'nan'), ('--distance', 'far'), ('--color', 'rainbow'),
                     ('--path', 'nan,0,0;1,2,3')):
        try:
            studio.check_options({key: bad})
            check(False, f'{key} {bad!r} is refused')
        except ValueError:
            check(True, f'{key} {bad!r} is refused')
    for args in (['--island', 'x'], ['--frames', '0'], ['--screenshot']):
        check(studio.main(['studio.py', 'wake_island_s'] + args) == 2, f'{" ".join(args)}: exit code 2 before the level loads')


def screenshot():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        out = os.path.join(tmp, 'shot.png')
        check(studio.save_screenshot(out, None) == 1 and not os.path.exists(out),
              'no screenshot from the viewer: exit code 1, nothing written')
        check(studio.save_screenshot(out, np.zeros((4, 4, 3), np.uint8)) == 0 and os.path.isfile(out),
              'a screenshot: written, exit code 0')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    colours()
    options()
    screenshot()
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```

`bf1943-spawn-map/README.md`:

```md
# BF1943 spawn map (bf1943-spawn-map)

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** - a new BF1943 tool; it reads BF1943's Xbox 360 level bundles (from the Xenia kit's extracted copy) through `fbrb1943.py` and `core/bfbc2core/dbx.py`.

Lists each BF1943 level's objectives (the two bases and the flags) with the soldier and vehicle spawns each one owns, read from the level's own data. Bots use it to choose where to spawn and what to attack or defend.

```
python -B spawnmap.py                       every multiplayer level, from bf1943-xenia-kit\output\title\dist\xenon
python -B spawnmap.py wake_island_s         one level
python -B spawnmap.py <dist\xenon folder> [level ...] [--json spawns.json] [--navflags]
```

The default game folder is the one `bf1943-xenia-kit` builds from your own package. The tool only reads it; with `--json` it also writes the map as JSON.

With `--navflags` (2026-10-30) it also writes `work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.flags.txt` for each level (`BF1943_WORK` sets another work folder): plain lines a C program reads, `flag <index> <base|flag> <initial owner 0|1|2> <x> <y> <z> <radius> <name>`, and `spawn <team> <objective> <x> <y> <z>` for each base's soldier spawn and its alternates. navhost and rsbot's offline tests (project-opfor-bf1943 `TnT/Code/Engine/AI/Bots`) read it. Only real objectives become flags (2026-10-30): one with no index or no position, or a point at the map origin that owns no spawn (Coral Sea's three "Spawn" points, all index 0), is named in a `# left out` comment instead; each index appears once (a duplicate is an error).

## What it reads

Everything comes from `levels/<level>.dbx`, found in whichever of the level's bundles holds it.

| Type | Fields used |
|---|---|
| `CapturePointEntityData` (an objective) | `Name`, `LocationName` (text ID), `Index`, `InitialOwnerTeam`, `CaptureRadius`, `OnlyTakeableByTeam`, `UnableToChangeTeam` (set on the two bases), `Spawners` (the spawns it owns; their team follows the point's owner) |
| `SoldierSpawnEntityData` | `Team`, `PlayerType` (`SSHumanPlayer` / `SSAiPlayer`), `Enabled`, `LocationNameSid`, `AlternativeSpawnPoints` (more positions for the same spawn) |
| `VehicleSpawnEntityData` | the vehicle blueprint and its team |

Positions are the `Transform` translation (x, y, z, with y up), in metres.

## Findings (2026-10-23)

- **Wake Island, Guadalcanal, Iwo Jima:** each has two bases with a fixed team and five neutral flags. Each base or flag has one soldier spawn, with 4–6 alternate positions, and its own vehicles.
- **Coral Sea:**
  - the two carrier bases;
  - three placeholder points named "Spawn", at the map origin;
  - the Air Superiority zone;
  - two `SSAiPlayer` spawners that no objective owns.

## Tests

`tests/test_spawnmap.py` checks `--navflags`' lines on a made-up map (and that placeholder objectives and duplicate indices are handled; `--made-up` stops there, the quick tier), then runs the tool on the default game folder when it exists, checks every level's two bases, that every soldier spawn has a team, and that each level's flags have unique indices and none at the map origin.

```

`bf1943-spawn-map/spawnmap.py`:

```py
r"""BF1943 spawn map: each level's objectives (bases and flags) with the soldier and vehicle spawns they own.

Reads each level's main DBX partition from the game folder's bundles; prints the map, and writes it as JSON (--json)
and as the flags files navhost and rsbot read (--navflags). spawn_map(game, level) is the library form.

  python -B spawnmap.py [<dist\xenon folder>] [level ...] [--json <file>] [--navflags]

<dist\xenon folder> is an extracted BF1943 game folder (default: bf1943-xenia-kit\output\title\dist\xenon,
which `xeniakit.py build` makes from your own package). Levels default to every multiplayer level found
(wake_island_s, guadal_canal, iwo_jima_s, coral_sea). Only reads; nothing is written except --json and --navflags.

From each level's main partition (levels/<level>.dbx):
  CapturePointEntityData   an objective: Name, LocationName (text id), Index, InitialOwnerTeam, CaptureRadius,
                           OnlyTakeableByTeam, UnableToChangeTeam (a base cannot change hands), Spawners (the
                           spawns the point owns: their team follows the point's owner)
  SoldierSpawnEntityData   Team, PlayerType (SSHumanPlayer / SSAiPlayer), Enabled, LocationNameSid,
                           AlternativeSpawnPoints (AlternateSpawnEntityData: more positions for the same spawn)
  VehicleSpawnEntityData   the vehicle blueprint and its team
Positions are the Transform's translation (x, y, z; y is up), in metres.

--navflags also writes <suite>\work\levels\<level>\navkit\<level>.flags.txt (BF1943_WORK sets another work folder)
for each level: the objectives and the bases' soldier spawns as plain lines a C program reads (navhost and rsbot's
tests, project-opfor-bf1943 TnT/Code/Engine/AI/Bots), in FLAGS_FORMAT below.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SUITE = os.path.dirname(HERE)
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
from bfbc2core import dbx  # noqa: E402
from fbrb1943 import Bundle  # noqa: E402

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from bfbc2core.dbx import Element

# spawn_map's result (level, bundle, objectives, unowned soldier and vehicle spawns), an objective and a spawn:
# JSON-like dicts
type LevelMap = dict[str, Any]
type Objective = dict[str, Any]
type Spawn = dict[str, Any]
DEFAULT_GAME = os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-xenia-kit', 'output', 'title', 'dist', 'xenon')
LEVELS = ['wake_island_s', 'guadal_canal', 'iwo_jima_s', 'coral_sea']
WORK = os.environ.get('BF1943_WORK') or os.path.join(SUITE, 'work')
FLAGS_FORMAT = '''# rsflags 1 <level>: written by bf1943-spawn-map/spawnmap.py --navflags (from levels/<level>.dbx)
# flag <index> <base|flag> <initial owner: 0 neutral, 1, 2> <x> <y> <z> <capture radius, 0: an area> <name>
# spawn <team 1 or 2> <objective index> <x> <y> <z>   (a base's soldier spawn and its alternates)'''
TEAM_NUMBER = {'TeamNeutral': 0, 'Team1': 1, 'Team2': 2}


def placeholder(objective: Objective) -> str | None:
    """Why an objective is not a real flag, or None: no Index or no position, or a point at the map origin that owns no
    spawn (Coral Sea's three "Spawn" capture points, all Index 0)."""
    if objective['index'] in (None, '') or objective['position'] is None:
        return 'no index' if objective['index'] in (None, '') else 'no position'
    if all(coordinate == 0 for coordinate in objective['position']) and not objective['spawns']:
        return 'at the map origin, owning no spawn'
    return None


def flags_text(level_map: LevelMap) -> str:
    """The level's objectives and base spawns as FLAGS_FORMAT lines: real objectives only (placeholder() ones are
    named in a comment), each index once (a duplicate is an error: the C readers key flags by index)."""
    lines = FLAGS_FORMAT.replace('<level>', level_map['level'], 1).splitlines()
    real: list[Objective] = []
    left_out: list[str] = []
    for objective in level_map['objectives']:
        why = placeholder(objective)
        if why:
            left_out.append(f'{objective["name"] or objective["location"] or "-"} (index {objective["index"]}: {why})')
        else:
            real.append(objective)
    if left_out:
        lines.append('# left out, not flags: ' + '; '.join(left_out))
    seen: dict[int, str] = {}           # index -> the objective's name
    for objective in real:
        index = int(objective['index'])
        label = objective['name'] or objective['location']
        if index in seen:
            raise ValueError(f'{level_map["level"]}: objectives {seen[index]!r} and {label!r} share index {index}')
        seen[index] = label
        x, y, z = objective['position']
        name = (objective['name'] or objective['location'] or '-').replace(' ', '_')
        owner = TEAM_NUMBER.get(objective['initial_owner'], 0)
        radius = float(objective['capture_radius'] or 0)
        lines.append(f'flag {index} {objective["role"]} {owner} {x:.2f} {y:.2f} {z:.2f} {radius:.2f} {name}')
    for objective in real:
        if objective['role'] != 'base':
            continue
        for spawn in objective['spawns']:
            if spawn['kind'] != 'soldier' or TEAM_NUMBER.get(spawn['team'], 0) == 0:
                continue
            # the spawn's own position and its resolved alternates (an unresolved one is its GUID, a string)
            points = [spawn['position']] + [alt for alt in spawn['alternates'] if isinstance(alt, list)]
            for point in points:
                if point is not None:
                    lines.append(f'spawn {TEAM_NUMBER[spawn["team"]]} {int(objective["index"])} '
                                 f'{point[0]:.2f} {point[1]:.2f} {point[2]:.2f}')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def level_partition(game: str, level: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
    """The bytes of levels/<level>.dbx, from whichever of the level's bundles holds it."""
    folder = os.path.join(game, 'levels', level)
    want = f'levels/{level}.dbx'
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
        if name.endswith('.fbrb'):
            bundle = Bundle(open(os.path.join(folder, name), 'rb').read())
            for e in bundle.entries:
                if e['name'].lower() == want:
                    return bundle.data(e['name']), name
    raise FileNotFoundError(f'{want} is in none of {folder}\\*.fbrb')


def kind(instance: 'Element') -> str:
    """The instance's type name without its namespace."""
    return (instance.attr('type') or '').rsplit('.', 1)[-1]


def guid(instance: 'Element') -> str:
    """The instance's GUID, lower case (every instance of a partition has one)."""
    return cast(str, instance.attr('guid')).lower()


def scalar(instance: 'Element', name: str) -> str | None:
    field = instance.child(name)
    return None if field is None else dbx.value(field)


def number(instance: 'Element', name: str) -> float | None:
    field = instance.child(name)
    return None if field is None or field.kind != dbx.NUMBERS else dbx.floats(field)[0]


def refs(instance: 'Element', name: str) -> list[str]:
    """The references an array field holds: local GUIDs (lower case) or 'partition/guid' paths."""
    field = instance.child(name)
    if field is None:
        return []
    return [cast(str, member.attr('ref')).lower() for member in (field.children or ()) if member.attr('ref')]


def ref(instance: 'Element', name: str) -> str | None:
    field = instance.child(name)
    return cast(str, field.attr('ref')).lower() if field is not None and field.attr('ref') else None


def position(instance: 'Element') -> list[float] | None:
    """The Transform's translation (x, y, z), rounded to cm; None without a 4x4 Transform."""
    transform = instance.child('Transform')
    if transform is None or transform.kind != dbx.NUMBERS:
        return None
    matrix = dbx.floats(transform)
    return [round(matrix[12], 2), round(matrix[13], 2), round(matrix[14], 2)] if len(matrix) == 16 else None


def soldier_spawn(instance: 'Element', by_guid: dict[str, 'Element']) -> Spawn:
    alternates: list[list[float] | None | str] = []     # a position, or the GUID of an alternate not found
    for alternate_guid in refs(instance, 'AlternativeSpawnPoints'):
        alternate = by_guid.get(alternate_guid)
        alternates.append(position(alternate) if alternate is not None else alternate_guid)
    return dict(guid=guid(instance), kind='soldier', name=scalar(instance, 'Name') or '',
                team=scalar(instance, 'Team'), player_type=scalar(instance, 'PlayerType'),
                enabled=scalar(instance, 'Enabled'), location=scalar(instance, 'LocationNameSid') or '',
                position=position(instance), alternates=alternates)


def vehicle_spawn(instance: 'Element') -> Spawn:
    blueprint = ref(instance, 'Vehicle') or ref(instance, 'Template') or ''
    return dict(guid=guid(instance), kind='vehicle', name=scalar(instance, 'Name') or '',
                team=scalar(instance, 'Team'),
                vehicle=blueprint.rsplit('/', 2)[-2] if blueprint.count('/') >= 2 else blueprint,
                position=position(instance))


def spawn_map(game: str, level: str) -> LevelMap:
    """The level's objectives with the spawns each owns, and the soldier and vehicle spawns no objective owns."""
    data, bundle = level_partition(game, level)
    partition = dbx.parse(data)
    by_guid = {(e.attr('guid') or '').lower(): e for e in partition.instances}
    owned: set[str] = set()
    objectives: list[Objective] = []
    for e in partition.instances:
        if kind(e) != 'CapturePointEntityData':
            continue
        spawns: list[Spawn] = []
        for spawner_guid in refs(e, 'Spawners'):
            spawner = by_guid.get(spawner_guid)
            if spawner is None:
                spawns.append(dict(guid=spawner_guid, kind='external'))
            elif kind(spawner) == 'SoldierSpawnEntityData':
                spawns.append(soldier_spawn(spawner, by_guid))
            elif kind(spawner) == 'VehicleSpawnEntityData':
                spawns.append(vehicle_spawn(spawner))
            else:
                spawns.append(dict(guid=spawner_guid, kind=kind(spawner)))
            owned.add(spawner_guid)
        base = scalar(e, 'UnableToChangeTeam') == 'true'
        objectives.append(dict(guid=guid(e), name=scalar(e, 'Name') or '', role='base' if base else 'flag',
                               location=scalar(e, 'LocationName') or '', index=scalar(e, 'Index'),
                               initial_owner=scalar(e, 'InitialOwnerTeam'),
                               only_takeable_by=scalar(e, 'OnlyTakeableByTeam'),
                               capture_radius=number(e, 'CaptureRadius'), position=position(e), spawns=spawns))
    objectives.sort(key=lambda objective: (objective['role'] != 'base', int(objective['index'] or 0)))
    unowned = [soldier_spawn(e, by_guid) for e in partition.instances
               if kind(e) == 'SoldierSpawnEntityData' and (e.attr('guid') or '').lower() not in owned]
    # vehicles no objective owns (e.g. the carriers' own boats and planes): their team is their spawn's
    vehicles = [vehicle_spawn(e) for e in partition.instances
                if kind(e) == 'VehicleSpawnEntityData' and (e.attr('guid') or '').lower() not in owned]
    return dict(level=level, bundle=bundle, objectives=objectives, unowned_soldier_spawns=unowned,
                unowned_vehicle_spawns=vehicles)


def show(level_map: LevelMap) -> None:
    """Prints the level's map: objectives with their spawns and vehicles, then the spawns no objective owns."""
    print(f'== {level_map["level"]} ({level_map["bundle"]})')
    for objective in level_map['objectives']:
        soldiers = [spawn for spawn in objective['spawns'] if spawn['kind'] == 'soldier']
        vehicles = [spawn for spawn in objective['spawns'] if spawn['kind'] == 'vehicle']
        print(f'  {objective["role"]:4} #{objective["index"]} {objective["name"] or "-":28} '
              f'{objective["location"]:34} owner {objective["initial_owner"]:12}'
              f' at {objective["position"]}  radius {objective["capture_radius"]}')
        for spawn in soldiers:
            print(f'       soldier spawn {spawn["name"] or "-":30} {spawn["team"]:8} {spawn["player_type"]:14} '
                  f'at {spawn["position"]} + {len(spawn["alternates"])} alternates')
        if vehicles:
            counts: dict[str, int] = {}
            for vehicle in vehicles:
                counts[vehicle['vehicle']] = counts.get(vehicle['vehicle'], 0) + 1
            print('       vehicles: ' + ', '.join(f'{name} x{count}' for name, count in sorted(counts.items())))
    for vehicle in level_map['unowned_vehicle_spawns']:
        print(f'  (no objective) vehicle {vehicle["vehicle"]:24} {vehicle["team"] or "-":12} at {vehicle["position"]}')
    for spawn in level_map['unowned_soldier_spawns']:
        print(f'  (no objective) soldier spawn {spawn["name"] or "-"} {spawn["team"]} {spawn["player_type"]} '
              f'enabled {spawn["enabled"]} at {spawn["position"]}')


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='spawnmap.py', description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument('game', nargs='?', default=DEFAULT_GAME)
    parser.add_argument('levels', nargs='*')
    parser.add_argument('--json')
    parser.add_argument('--navflags', action='store_true',
                        help='also write work/levels/<level>/navkit/<level>.flags.txt')
    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
    if args.game in LEVELS:                   # spawnmap.py wake_island_s: the default game folder
        args.levels, args.game = [args.game] + args.levels, DEFAULT_GAME
    game: str = args.game
    levels: list[str] = args.levels or [level for level in LEVELS
                                        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels', level))]
    if not levels:
        raise SystemExit(f'no BF1943 levels in {game}: give the dist\\xenon folder of an extracted game')
    maps = [spawn_map(game, level) for level in levels]
    for level_map in maps:
        show(level_map)
    if args.json:
        write_whole(args.json, json.dumps(maps, indent=1))
    if args.navflags:
        # every level's text first (a level that cannot be written - a duplicate index - writes none), then each
        # file put in place whole: an existing flags file is never left empty or half written
        texts: list[tuple[str, str]] = [(level_map['level'], flags_text(level_map)) for level_map in maps]
        for level, text in texts:
            folder = os.path.join(WORK, 'levels', level, 'navkit')
            os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
            path = os.path.join(folder, f'{level}.flags.txt')
            write_whole(path, text)
            print(f'wrote {path}')
    return 0


def write_whole(path: str, text: str) -> None:
    """text (UTF-8, LF) at path, replacing the file only once the new one is written whole."""
    tmp = path + '.tmp'
    try:
        with open(tmp, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            f.write(text)
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.remove(tmp)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('spawnmap', gui=False)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`bf1943-spawn-map/tests/test_spawnmap.py`:

```py
"""Tests for spawnmap.py, on the game folder bf1943-xenia-kit builds (BF1943_GAME overrides; skipped when absent)."""
import os
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import spawnmap  # noqa: E402

failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def navflags():
    """--navflags' lines on a made-up map: a base with a spawn and an alternate, a neutral flag."""
    m = dict(level='made_up', objectives=[
        dict(name='Base One', location='', index='0', role='base', initial_owner='Team1', capture_radius=20.0,
             position=[1.0, 2.0, 3.0], spawns=[dict(kind='soldier', team='Team1', position=[4.0, 5.0, 6.0],
                                                    alternates=[[7.0, 8.0, 9.0], 'unresolved-guid'])]),
        dict(name='', location='CQ_FLAG', index='1', role='flag', initial_owner='TeamNeutral', capture_radius=None,
             position=[-1.5, 0.25, 10.0], spawns=[])])
    lines = [l for l in spawnmap.flags_text(m).splitlines() if not l.startswith('#')]
    check(lines == ['flag 0 base 1 1.00 2.00 3.00 20.00 Base_One', 'flag 1 flag 0 -1.50 0.25 10.00 0.00 CQ_FLAG',
                    'spawn 1 0 4.00 5.00 6.00', 'spawn 1 0 7.00 8.00 9.00'], f'--navflags lines: {lines}')


def placeholders():
    """Coral Sea's placeholder capture points (Index 0 at the map origin, no spawns), objectives without an index or a
    position, and a spawn without a position are not written; a duplicate index among real objectives is an error."""
    def obj(name, index, position, role='flag', spawns=()):
        return dict(name=name, location='', index=index, role=role, initial_owner='TeamNeutral', capture_radius=None,
                    position=position, spawns=list(spawns))
    base = obj('Carrier', '10', [5.0, 1.0, 5.0], 'base', [dict(kind='soldier', team='Team1', position=None,
                                                                alternates=[[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]])])
    m = dict(level='made_up', objectives=[base, obj('Spawn', '0', [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]), obj('Spawn', '0', [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
                                          obj('NoIndex', None, [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), obj('NoPos', '7', None),
                                          obj('Real', '5', [4.0, 5.0, 6.0])])
    try:
        text = spawnmap.flags_text(m)
    except Exception as e:                            # noqa: BLE001 - the old code: TypeError on a missing position
        check(False, f'placeholders: flags_text raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}')
        return
    lines = [l for l in text.splitlines() if not l.startswith('#')]
    check(lines == ['flag 10 base 0 5.00 1.00 5.00 0.00 Carrier', 'flag 5 flag 0 4.00 5.00 6.00 0.00 Real',
                    'spawn 1 10 1.00 1.00 1.00'], f'placeholders and objectives without index or position left out: {lines}')
    check('# left out, not flags: Spawn' in text, 'the left-out objectives are named in a comment')
    dup = dict(level='made_up', objectives=[obj('A', '3', [1.0, 0.0, 1.0]), obj('B', '3', [2.0, 0.0, 2.0])])
    try:
        spawnmap.flags_text(dup)
        check(False, 'a duplicate index is an error')
    except ValueError:
        check(True, 'a duplicate index is an error')


def files_whole():
    """--navflags with a level that cannot be written (a duplicate index): no level's existing flags file is changed -
    the old tool had already truncated it to 0 bytes - and a good run replaces them whole."""
    import tempfile

    def obj(name, index, x):
        return dict(name=name, location='', index=index, role='flag', initial_owner='TeamNeutral', capture_radius=None,
                    position=[x, 0.0, x], spawns=[])
    maps = {'lv_a': [obj('A', '1', 1.0)], 'lv_b': [obj('B', '3', 1.0), obj('C', '3', 2.0)]}
    saved = spawnmap.spawn_map, spawnmap.WORK
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        spawnmap.WORK = tmp
        spawnmap.spawn_map = lambda game, lv: dict(level=lv, bundle='x.fbrb', objectives=maps[lv],
                                                   unowned_soldier_spawns=[], unowned_vehicle_spawns=[])
        paths = {lv: os.path.join(tmp, 'levels', lv, 'navkit', f'{lv}.flags.txt') for lv in maps}
        for lv, p in paths.items():
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p))
            with open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
                f.write(f'# rsflags 1 {lv}\nflag 0 base 1 0.00 0.00 0.00 20.00 good\n')
        before = {lv: open(p, 'rb').read() for lv, p in paths.items()}
        import contextlib
        import io
        try:
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
                spawnmap.main(['spawnmap.py', tmp, 'lv_a', 'lv_b', '--navflags'])
            check(False, 'a duplicate index stops --navflags')
        except ValueError:
            pass
        finally:
            spawnmap.spawn_map, spawnmap.WORK = saved[0], tmp
        after = {lv: open(p, 'rb').read() for lv, p in paths.items()}
        check(after == before, f'--navflags with a level that cannot be written: no flags file changed '
                               f'({ {lv: len(v) for lv, v in after.items()} } bytes)')
        maps['lv_b'] = [obj('B', '3', 1.0)]
        spawnmap.spawn_map = lambda game, lv: dict(level=lv, bundle='x.fbrb', objectives=maps[lv],
                                                   unowned_soldier_spawns=[], unowned_vehicle_spawns=[])
        try:
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
                spawnmap.main(['spawnmap.py', tmp, 'lv_a', 'lv_b', '--navflags'])
        finally:
            spawnmap.spawn_map, spawnmap.WORK = saved
        texts = {lv: open(p, encoding='utf-8').read() for lv, p in paths.items()}
        left = [n for lv, p in paths.items() for n in os.listdir(os.path.dirname(p)) if n.endswith('.tmp')]
        check('flag 3 flag 0 1.00 0.00 1.00 0.00 B' in texts['lv_b'] and 'flag 1 flag' in texts['lv_a'] and not left,
              '... a good run writes every level\'s file whole, no temporary file left')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    navflags()
    placeholders()
    files_whole()
    if '--made-up' in sys.argv:                       # the quick tier: no game data
        print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
        sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
    game = os.environ.get('BF1943_GAME', spawnmap.DEFAULT_GAME)
    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(game, 'levels')):
        print(f'skip: no extracted game at {game} (run bf1943-xenia-kit build first)')
        sys.exit(0)
    for level in spawnmap.LEVELS:
        m = spawnmap.spawn_map(game, level)
        bases = [o for o in m['objectives'] if o['role'] == 'base']
        check(sorted(o['initial_owner'] for o in bases) == ['Team1', 'Team2']
              and all(any(s['kind'] == 'soldier' and s['team'] == o['initial_owner'] for s in o['spawns']) for o in bases),
              f'{level}: two bases, Team1 and Team2, each with a soldier spawn of its team')
        soldiers = [s for o in m['objectives'] for s in o['spawns'] if s['kind'] == 'soldier'] + m['unowned_soldier_spawns']
        check(soldiers and all(s['team'] in ('Team1', 'Team2', 'TeamNeutral') for s in soldiers),
              f'{level}: every soldier spawn has a team ({len(soldiers)})')
        flags = [l.split() for l in spawnmap.flags_text(m).splitlines() if l.startswith('flag ')]
        idx = [f[1] for f in flags]
        check(len(idx) == len(set(idx)) and not any(f[4:7] == ['0.00', '0.00', '0.00'] for f in flags),
              f'{level}: --navflags has {len(flags)} flags, each index once, none at the map origin')
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```
