`bf1943-xenia-kit/ARCHITECTURE.md`:

```md
# BF1943 Xenia kit: how it is built

This page is for developers who will change the kit's code. To use the kit, and for what each change does in the
game, read the [README](README.md).

## Overview

`xeniakit.py` turns your own BF1943 content package into a Xenia setup that plays offline. Nothing is downloaded and
no game data is shipped. A build makes these changes:
- It extracts the package and checks each 4 KB block's SHA-1 and each file's SHA-256 against `known.json`.
- It edits three of the extracted files: the main menu movie, the in-game menu movie and `config.zz`.
- It copies a Xenia patch file into Xenia's `patches` folder.
- It writes a copy of `xenia_canary.exe` with its UDP byte-order bug fixed.
- It writes manifests of everything it made. `verify` re-checks the build against them, and `launch` verifies and then
  starts Xenia.

Each edit is checked against the hash of a result that was tested in game, so the kit refuses to guess. It refuses
another package, another Xenia build, or a result that differs.

`--experiment-bots` adds a second patch file. `bots.py` writes it: PowerPC code, assembled by `ppcasm.py` into an
unused code cave and called from a hook in the server's player update. That code adds 23 server-side bots and talks to
a program outside Xenia through a mailbox in guest memory. Two programs use the mailbox: `guestmem.py` in the test
harness, and navhost in project-opfor-bf1943.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PKG["your content package<br/>(read only)"]
    XEN["xenia_canary.exe e6cd2e4bc<br/>(read only)"]
    KNOWN["known.json<br/>package, file, result and Xenia hashes"]
    STFS["stfs.Package<br/>bf1943-console-readers"]
    TITLE["output/title/<br/>90 files, verified"]
    MENU["menu_edits.py<br/>apt.Rewriter, fbrb1943.Bundle"]
    IGM["igm_edits.py"]
    CFG["config_edits.py<br/>zipfile"]
    PATCH["patches/5841097E - Battlefield 1943.patch.toml"]
    NET["netfix.py"]
    BOTS["bots.py CODE_SOURCE<br/>assembled by ppcasm.py"]
    XPATCH["Xenia patches folder<br/>patch file, optional bots patch"]
    FIXED["xenia_canary_netfix.exe"]
    MAN["output/kit-manifest.json<br/>output/title/title-manifest.json<br/>output/launch.cmd"]
    VER["verify, launch"]
    RUN["Xenia running the game"]
    MBOX[("mailbox block<br/>in guest memory")]
    HOST["guestmem.py (harness)<br/>navhost (project-opfor-bf1943)"]

    PKG --> STFS --> TITLE
    KNOWN -.-> TITLE
    TITLE -->|"mainmenu-00.fbrb"| MENU --> TITLE
    TITLE -->|"hud_multiplayer_cq-00.fbrb"| IGM --> TITLE
    TITLE -->|"config.zz"| CFG --> TITLE
    KNOWN -.-> MENU
    KNOWN -.-> IGM
    KNOWN -.-> CFG
    PATCH --> XPATCH
    BOTS -->|"only with --experiment-bots"| XPATCH
    XEN --> NET --> FIXED
    TITLE --> MAN
    FIXED --> MAN
    XPATCH --> MAN
    MAN --> VER --> RUN
    RUN -->|"bot code writes state, flags"| MBOX
    HOST -->|"writes commands"| MBOX
    MBOX -->|"reads state"| HOST
```

`build` runs in five numbered stages (`xeniakit.build`). The paths it refuses come first: an output that is not
empty, a missing `xenia_canary.exe`, a path `launch.cmd` cannot name, a package or Xenia with an unknown hash, and a
foreign file under the bots patch's name.

## Module map

| File | Responsibility | Key entry points |
|---|---|---|
| `xeniakit.py` | the command line; extract, edit, install, manifests, verify, launch | `build`, `extract`, `verify`, `launch`, `install_bots_patch`, `kit_bots_patches`, `launcher_text`, `safe_join` |
| `known.json` | the release's package and per-file hashes, the expected edit results, the Xenia build and netfix hashes, the patch file's hash | read as `KNOWN` |
| `menu_edits.py` | main menu movie (`Menu/main_nav.res`, `Menu/main_root.res` in `mainmenu-00.fbrb`) | `build`, `main_menu`, `host_list_is_local`, `no_autosave_notice`; helpers `constant_namer`, `retarget`, `check_targets` |
| `igm_edits.py` | in-game menu movie (`Menu/igm_mp_cq.res` in `hud_multiplayer_cq-00.fbrb`) | `build`, `team_selector`, `frontline_without_leaderboards`, `no_gamer_card`, `force_team` (experiment) |
| `config_edits.py` | `GameSettings.cfg` inside `config.zz`: the two network ports | `build`, `PORTS` |
| `patches/5841097E - Battlefield 1943.patch.toml` | Xenia's patch file: signed-in state, no network, no automatic team (`be32` words by address) | copied, after its hash is checked |
| `netfix.py` | NOPs over five byte swaps in Xenia's `sendto`, `WSASendTo` and `recvfrom` | `build`, `SITES`, `file_offset` |
| `bots.py` | the bots experiment: guest code, data and mailbox layout, its patch file, and Python models of the locked reads and writes | `build`, `patch_toml`, `CODE_SOURCE`, `assembler_symbols`, `guest_command`, `guest_record`, `host_record`, `MAILBOX_NAMES` |
| `ppcasm.py` | a small two-pass PowerPC assembler for the instructions `bots.py` uses; anything else is an `AsmError` | `assemble` |
| `../bf1943-automated-map-and-bot-test-harness/xenia-run/guestmem.py` | attaches to Xenia and reads and writes the mailbox | `Guest`, `block_of`, `bot_record`, `flag_records`, `write_command`, `drive` |

The APT movie reader and rewriter (`apt.py`) come from `bf1943-apt-tools`. The bundle reader and writer
(`fbrb1943.py`) come from `bf1943-fbrb-tool`. Both are shared folders (`core/suitepath.py`).

## The parts

**Menu and in-game menu edits.** The two `build` functions work the same way:
1. Read the movie from its bundle (`fbrb1943.Bundle.data`) and refuse an original that does not validate.
2. Rewrite action blocks with `apt.Rewriter`. Each edit finds its block by address or by owner and checks the
   instruction shapes it expects. It rewrites the instruction list, points branches at the new instructions
   (`retarget`), refuses a branch into a removed instruction (`check_targets`), and moves the item to the new code
   (`rw.repoint`).
3. Validate the new movie, rebuild the bundle, and read every entry back.

`igm_edits` also adds sprites, characters and placements for the CHOOSE YOUR SIDE window. It builds that window's
ActionScript from small code builders (`var`, `call`, `set_member`, `if_else`).

**Config edits.** `config_edits.build` rewrites the ZIP entry by entry and keeps each entry's header fields. It
changes exactly one line for each port and refuses any other count. It then re-reads the archive, checks the CRCs,
and compares every other entry.

**Patch file and netfix.** The patch file is a fixed file in this folder, made in operation-rising-sun from words
verified against the decoded image. The build checks its SHA-256 before copying it. If Xenia already has a file with
other contents under that name, the build refuses unless `--replace-patch` is given. `netfix.build` maps each virtual
address to a file offset through the PE section table and checks the original bytes before it writes the NOPs, so
another Xenia build is refused. The build keeps an identical `xenia_canary_netfix.exe` that is already there, because
Xenia may be running it.

**The bots experiment.**
- **Where the code goes.** The code, the bot table and the names go in a code cave at `CODE` (0x82AAA1C0, 0xE40
  bytes). The hook replaces the `bl` at `HOOK` (0x82391988) with a `bl` to the cave. The cave first makes the original
  call, then handles the bots.
- **How it is assembled.** `bots.build` assembles `CODE_SOURCE` twice. The first pass gives the code's size. The
  second places the table right after the code. The bot names and kit names are laid out as the game's
  `{begin, end, capacity}` strings.
- **The data area.** `DATA` (0x82D26E10, 0x1F0 bytes) holds:

  | Offset | Holds |
  |---|---|
  | `STATE`, `MANAGER`, `TICK` | the bots' lifecycle (with `HOLD`), the match's player manager, the tick |
  | `SLOTS` | one player slot per bot |
  | `HANDLE` | the kit lookup's handle |
  | `MBOX_MAGIC`, `MBOX` | the mailbox's magic and address |
  | `HOST_PLAYER`, `HOLD` | which match the bots belong to; the lifecycle's hold word; not part of the mailbox |

  The data area uses 0x90 bytes in all.
- **The bots' lifecycle.** One named state per game session, `bots.lifecycle(STATE, HOLD)`, kept in two data-area
  words that the code reads and writes separately (`make` writes `STATE`; `forget_hold` writes `HOLD`, then `STATE`).
  Each path that sets one word clears the other, so both set never occurs. The names, the word pairs and the
  transitions are `LIFE_*`, `LIFECYCLE_WORDS` and `LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS`; `test_bots.py` runs every transition on
  the code. (2026-11-05: named on the host side only. Folding them into one guest word would change the code's bytes;
  the code, the patch and the mailbox are unchanged.)

  | State | `STATE` `HOLD` | Meaning |
  |---|---|---|
  | `none` | 0 0 | no bots this match; made once the first player (the host) has a soldier |
  | `made` | 1 0 | bots made for this match (`MANAGER` and `HOST_PLAYER` recorded); stepped every tick |
  | `held` | 0 1 | the host left a match its bots are still in; nothing is made until the player list empties or the manager changes |

  | From | To | Path (`CODE_SOURCE` label) | When (each tick, after the server's own player update) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | any | `none` | `forget` | no player manager; an empty player list; another manager |
  | `made` | `made` | `respawn` | the recorded host is the first player and a bot is still in the list (or none was made) |
  | `made` | `none` | `forget` | none of the bots is in the list (a new match at the old addresses) |
  | `made` | `held` | `forget_held` | another first player while bots are still in the list (the host left) |
  | `none` | `made` | `make`, then `create` | the host has a soldier and the block is allocated |
  | `none` | `none` | `make`, then `out` | the host has no soldier yet, or no block was allocated |
  | `held` | `held` | `make`, then `out` | still held |
- **The mailbox.** It is allocated once per match with the game's allocator, `ALLOC_SIZE` 0xD40 bytes, laid out as
  big-endian words:

| Part | Offset | Contents | Lock |
|---|---|---|---|
| header | 0x00 | `H_MAGIC` `RSM2`, `H_VERSION` 2, counts and sizes, `H_MANAGER`, `H_TICK` (0x1C), `H_FLAGS` (0x20) | none: `H_FLAGS` then `H_TICK`, with `lwsync` between |
| bot state record | `BOT0` 0x40 + 0x40 × slot, `R_*` 0x00 to 0x1C | tick, player, soldier, team, x, y, z, tick | two ticks: the guest writes `R_SEQ`, `lwsync`, the fields, `lwsync`, `R_SEQ_END` |
| bot command record | same slot, `C_*` 0x20 to 0x3C | stamp, throttle, strafe, yaw, pitch, buttons high and low, `C_SEQ` | sequence: the host makes it odd, writes, then makes it even and new |
| capture point record | `FLAG0` 0x600 + 0x30 × k, up to 8 | tick, entity, owner, control, enabled, radius, x, y, z, tick (`F_SEQ_END` 0x2C) | two ticks, as the state record |
| guest-only copies | `BLOCK_SIZE` 0x780 + 0x40 × slot | each bot's last whole command | the guest's own; hosts never see it |

  - **Reading the state and flag records.** A host reads the closing tick, then the fields, then the opening tick. It
    takes the record only when the two ticks are equal (`bots.host_record`, up to `TRIES` reads).
  - **Reading the command record.** The guest reads `C_SEQ`, the record and `C_SEQ` again. It takes the record only
    when both reads give the same even value (`bots.guest_command`, `TRIES` 4 times). If no read is whole, it uses the
    bot's last whole command. Any command whose stamp is 0, or older than `STALE` (10) ticks, gives a neutral frame,
    so the bots stand still when the host stops.
  - **Matching the match.** Each tick the code compares the match with the one it recorded: the player manager, the
    first player (`HOST_PLAYER`), and each bot still in the player list. When the match has changed, it forgets the
    bots, `MBOX` and its magic (lifecycle `none`). When the host has left, the lifecycle is `held`, which stops it
    from making new bots until the player list empties or the manager changes.

**The host programs.** `guestmem.py` finds Xenia's guest memory. It accepts a base address only where guest
`0x82000000` starts with `MZ`. It then checks that the bot code is in place and that the hook branches to it. It
reads the mailbox through `MBOX`. `write_command` writes three times: the odd sequence, then the stamp and fields in
one write, then the even sequence. While a command is held, `drive` keeps rewriting the stamp. navhost (in
project-opfor-bf1943 `TnT/Code/Engine/AI/Bots/navhost`) is the real host. Its `src/rsmbox.h` is a copy of
`MAILBOX_NAMES`, and its own tests check it against `bots.py`.

**verify and launch.** `verify` compares these with their recorded SHA-256:
- every title file, against `title-manifest.json`;
- the fixed Xenia, the patch file and the bots patch (if one was built), against `kit-manifest.json`;
- `launch.cmd`, against the text `launcher_text` gives for `kit-manifest.json`'s paths and GPU backend
  (`launcher_problem`).

It then checks the build's bot mode. A normal build allows no kit-made bots patch in Xenia's folder (found by its
`bots.HEADER` first line, under any name). A bots build allows only its own. `launch` runs `verify`, then starts
`launch_args` from the fixed Xenia's folder. `launch.cmd` is UTF-8 and switches the console to code page 65001 for the
lines that name paths (`launcher_text`).

## Key invariants

- **Inputs are only read.** The package and `xenia_canary.exe` are opened for reading. `extract` writes with
  `open(..., 'xb')` into a title folder that must be empty, and `safe_join` refuses any package path that would leave
  that folder.
- **Byte-identical results.** The build refuses unless these SHA-256s match `known.json`:
  - the package;
  - each extracted file;
  - each edited resource: `main_nav.res`, `main_root.res`, `igm_mp_cq.res` (not with `--experiment-team`) and
    `GameSettings.cfg`;
  - the kit's patch file and the fixed Xenia.

  The rebuilt bundles and `config.zz` are recorded in `title-manifest.json` but not pinned in `known.json`.
- **Bot mode is all or nothing.** `install_bots_patch` leaves exactly zero kit bots patches (a normal build) or
  exactly one, its own (a bots build). It refuses a foreign file under the kit's name before writing anything, and
  `verify` enforces the same rule.
- **launch.cmd is what the build wrote.** `build` records its `--gpu` in `kit-manifest.json` (`gpu`), and `verify`
  regenerates `launch.cmd` with `launcher_text` from the manifest and compares bytes: a missing or different file fails
  it (and so `launch`). A manifest from before 2026-11-05 has no `gpu`, so either backend's text is accepted for it.
  Before 2026-11-05 `verify` did not look at `launch.cmd` (a review found it), and a `launch.cmd` from a kit older than
  the code-page switch (2026-10-31) now fails until you rebuild.
- **Mailbox locks.** The state and flag records use two ticks, written in a fixed order with `lwsync`, and readers
  compare the closing tick with the opening one. Commands use an even/odd sequence with a stale-stamp limit. The
  layout and version 2 stay fixed: the guest-only copies and `HOLD` sit outside the host-visible block.
- **The bot code fits.** `bots.build` raises when the blob passes `CODE_END` or the data passes `DATA_END`, and when
  the two assembler passes disagree on the code's size. `ppcasm` refuses unknown mnemonics, wrong operand counts and
  r0-based `addi`/`addis`/loads and stores.

| `tests/test_xeniakit.py --game` | bf1943 | a full build from your package against a scratch Xenia folder; verify accepts it and notices a changed file; your Xenia folder is unchanged |

## Where to start

**Change a menu.** Start in `menu_edits.py` or `igm_edits.py`, and use `bf1943-apt-tools` to disassemble the movie.
1. Add an edit function that finds its block and checks the shapes it expects, then call it from `build`.
2. Add a made-up movie case to `tests/test_menu_igm_edits.py`.
3. Test the change in game.
4. Record the new result's hash in `known.json` (`expected`). Until you do, `build` refuses it.

**Change the bots' guest code.** Edit `CODE_SOURCE` in `bots.py`. If you need an instruction `ppcasm.py` lacks, add it
there with a capstone check in `test_ppcasm.py`.
1. Keep the room it reports. `test_bots.py` tells you whether the code still fits.
2. If the mailbox changes, change the `MAILBOX_NAMES` constants and `VERSION`, then `guestmem.py` and navhost's
   `rsmbox.h` in the same change.
3. Extend the interpreter cases in `test_bots.py` for any new locked read or write.

**Support another Xenia or game build.** Every address here is tied to one build. That covers `netfix.SITES`, the patch
file's words, and the `bots.py` hook and cave (module hash `872BBE31C0FBA21B`). Find the new sites, then update
`known.json` (`xenia`, `game`) together with them.

```

`bf1943-xenia-kit/README.md`:

```md
# BF1943 Xenia kit

Part of the BF1943 Tool Suite. **BF1943 status: ready** - a new BF1943 tool; it reads your own BF1943 (XBLA) package and Xenia Canary.
How the kit is built (the edits, the patch file and netfix, the bots code and its mailbox, verify and launch): [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md).

Turns your own copy of Battlefield 1943 (XBLA) into a Xenia setup that plays offline:
- **Local Match** opens a browser of locally hosted maps.
- Picking a map starts a local match: the game's own server and client on your PC, with no EA servers.
- Before your first deploy, **CHOOSE YOUR SIDE** lets you pick USMC or Imperial Japan.

The kit ships no game data. Everything it makes comes from your copy and goes into `output/`, which is never committed. A build from the known package matches the setup tested on 2026-10-22 in every file `known.json` pins (the package, each extracted file, the edited resources, the patch file and the fixed Xenia); the rebuilt bundles and `config.zz` are recorded in `title-manifest.json` but not pinned, and `--experiment-team` and the bots patch have no reference hashes ([ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), "Key invariants"). `tests\test_xeniakit.py --game` checks this.

## What you need

- Your Battlefield 1943 content package: the file `945CD965D6B2B2584A9C06CE16F38A075A6D390558` from `5841097E\000D0000\`. Only the full release with SHA-256 `36f96e27…6550` is accepted.
- **Xenia Canary build `e6cd2e4bc` (Windows)**, with `xenia_canary.exe` SHA-256 `732cb7d5…`. Another build is refused, because the network fix is tied to this build's exact code.
- **A profile in Xenia.** Start Xenia once, create a profile and sign it in. The game needs a signed-in profile; the patch file then reports it as signed in to Xbox LIVE.
- Python 3.10 or newer. No extra libraries are needed.

## Use

```
python -B xeniakit.py build "<path to the package>" "<Xenia folder>"
output\launch.cmd
```

`build` takes about half a minute; `--out <folder>` builds somewhere other than `output\`. `verify` re-checks everything the build made, `launch.cmd` too (it must be byte for byte what the build writes for `kit-manifest.json`, with the `--gpu` the build recorded there: a missing or edited `launch.cmd` fails), and `launch` verifies and then starts the game. All three take `--out`. `--gpu d3d12` switches from Vulkan to DirectX 12: on `build` it goes into `launch.cmd`, on `launch` it applies to that start.

`launch.cmd` is UTF-8, with `%` in a path doubled. cmd.exe reads a batch file line by line in the console's code page (the OEM one, such as 437 or 850, unless the console is set to UTF-8, 65001), so its first lines, plain ASCII, note the console's code page and switch it to 65001 before the lines that name paths, and its last line switches it back: it works in either kind of console, with any folder name (accents, Cyrillic, CJK letters). Only a path with a double quote is refused. Before 2026-10-30 the file was UTF-8 without the switch, so a folder such as `Xenia José` made `launch.cmd` fail in an OEM console ("The system cannot find the path specified"), and a `%` was expanded; until 2026-10-31 it was written in the OEM code page, which failed the same way in a UTF-8 console and refused folders that page cannot hold. Until 2026-11-05 `verify` did not check `launch.cmd`; since then a build made by an older kit, whose `launch.cmd` has no code-page switch, fails `verify` (and `launch`) until you rebuild into an empty `--out`. A `kit-manifest.json` from before then does not record the `--gpu`, so `verify` accepts either backend's `launch.cmd` for it.

The kit refuses rather than guesses: another game version, another Xenia build, a damaged package, an edited result or an existing patch file with other contents (unless you pass `--replace-patch`) all stop it with a message. Your package and `xenia_canary.exe` are only read.

### What `build` makes

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `output\title\` | Your game, extracted (every data block's SHA-1 and every file's SHA-256 checked against `known.json`), with three files edited (below) |
| `output\title\title-manifest.json`, `output\kit-manifest.json` | Every file's hash, every change made and the `--gpu` used; `verify` uses them |
| `output\launch.cmd` | Starts `xenia_canary_netfix.exe --gpu=vulkan --license_mask=1 output\title\default.xex` |
| `<Xenia>\patches\5841097E - Battlefield 1943.patch.toml` | Xenia's patch file for the game (applied in memory, by module hash `872BBE31C0FBA21B`) |
| `<Xenia>\xenia_canary_netfix.exe` | A copy of Xenia with its UDP address bug fixed; `xenia_canary.exe` stays as it was |

Xenia's settings are not changed. The two command-line options in `launch.cmd` are the only Xenia settings the kit needs.

## Every change, and why

### Xenia and the game's code

| Change | Where | Without it |
|---|---|---|
| Signed in to Xbox LIVE: sign-in state 2, all privileges | patch file, 9 code words | Online menus ask you to sign in to Xbox LIVE |
| No network (`XNET_GET_XNADDR_NONE`) | patch file, 1 code word | The menu loops on "Connecting": Xenia reports a network with no gateway |
| No automatic team on joining | patch file, 1 code word | "Start" puts you on the smaller team (USMC) before CHOOSE YOUR SIDE; now you have no team until you choose |
| Full licence | `--license_mask=1` in `launch.cmd` | The game runs as the Trial version (Xenia cannot check XBLA licences) |
| UDP addresses in network order | `xenia_canary_netfix.exe`, 5 instructions (`netfix.py`) | Xenia byte-swaps the destination of every UDP packet: the client's join requests go to `1.0.0.127` on the internet instead of its own server, and the match never starts |

### The game's files (`output\title`)

| File | Change | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `menu\main\mainmenu-00.fbrb` (`main_nav`) | **Quick Match** becomes **LOCAL MATCH**. It opens a browser of the four maps (Wake Island, Guadalcanal and Iwo Jima Conquest; Coral Sea Air Superiority), and picking one hosts a local match (`hostMultiplayerLocal`). The browser is the game's own developer host list, tidied and given a heading | `menu_edits.py` |
| same | **Leaderboards** and **Return to Game Library** removed from the main menu | `menu_edits.py` |
| same | **No EA Online check** when the main menu opens. Join With Friends and Private Match still report that they cannot connect, by design until LAN play | `menu_edits.py` |
| same (`main_root`) | **No "the game is saving" icon notice** at startup | `menu_edits.py` |
| `menu\hud\hud_multiplayer_cq-00.fbrb` (`igm_mp_cq`) | **CHOOSE YOUR SIDE** before the first deploy of each match. Two cards, USMC and JAPAN, show the game's own soldier portraits and flags. Left/right (stick or D-pad) chooses and A confirms. The class menu and the deploy labels stay hidden until the server has switched you, then the deploy screen redraws itself for your side: each class card with its own soldier and icon. The HUD's spawn banner and the scoreboard headers name your new side. You cannot enter battle before choosing | `igm_edits.py` |
| same | **FRONTLINE REPORT** (the in-game menu) without Leaderboards: My Squad, Scoreboard, Help & Options, Achievements, Exit Game, Respawn/Suicide | `igm_edits.py` |
| same | **No See Gamer Card** button on My Squad, the scoreboard or the friends list (an Xbox LIVE overlay, empty offline) | `igm_edits.py` |
| `config.zz` (`GameSettings.cfg`) | Network ports 1001/1003 become 25001/25003 | `config_edits.py` |

Port numbers below 1024 are the problem: Xenia moves the server's ports by +10000 but not the client's destination, so the client never finds its server.

The evidence behind each change is in `operation-rising-sun/research/AGENT_PROGRESS.md` (2026-10-22).

## Known limits

- **Xenia crashes when a second match loads in one session** (seen twice, at `xenia_canary_netfix.exe+0x25338A` in a job thread). It is Xenia's bug, not the game's or the kit's. Restart Xenia between matches.
- **Experiment, for development only:** `--experiment-team 1|2` replaces the side choice with a fixed team request each time the deploy screen opens.

## Experiment: offline bots (`--experiment-bots`)

`build --experiment-bots` also writes a second patch file, `5841097E - Battlefield 1943 - bots experiment.patch.toml`, generated by `bots.py` from its PowerPC source (assembled by `ppcasm.py`). A normal build removes every bots patch the kit made from Xenia's patches folder (under any name: before 2026-10-30 only the kit's own file name, so a renamed copy passed the build and failed its `verify`), and a bots build leaves exactly its own; a file under the kit's name that the kit did not make is refused before anything is written. `verify` (and so `launch`) fails while a bots patch is in Xenia's patches folder that the build did not make, as another build against the same Xenia leaves it.

Once you have a soldier in a match, the bot code adds 23 bots for a full 24-player match: 11 on your side and 12 against, Rifleman, Infantry and Scout in turn (`MAX_BOTS` and `DEFAULT_BOTS` in `bots.py`). They are server-side players with no network connection, created the way the game's own leftover AI spawner creates players.

| Working (2026-10-23) | Not yet |
|---|---|
| The bots join (the game announces "Bot 1 USMC Rifleman connected."), take their team's kit and appear on the scoreboard | No decisions in the guest: each bot's input is its command record in the host mailbox (below), so they stand until a host program writes it (navhost, or `guestmem.py input` in the test harness) |
| Each server tick they get an input frame and their soldier is stepped with it, as a human's is when that player's input arrives | No aiming, navigation or objectives yet: nothing in the build decides what to send |
| A host mailbox written from outside Xenia (2026-10-30; v1 in game: walk, strafe, facing, sprint (button 22), jump and crouch work). Mailbox v2 (N4, 2026-10-30): a command record per bot, each bot's state, the capture points' owners | v2 is tested offline only, not yet in game |
| Each spawns at its own team's base and respawns after dying | A fixed 23 bots; a chosen count comes later |
| They are friendly or hostile to you according to their side, and stand on the deck | |

The bot code reports to Xenia's log (`DbgPrint`, lines starting `rs-bots:`): the mailbox's address, each bot created, each spawn (with the spawn point's ID) and, every 64 ticks (about 2 s), each soldier's position. The research behind each step is in `operation-rising-sun/research/AGENT_PROGRESS.md` (2026-10-23, 2026-10-30).

### Host mailbox v2 (milestone N4)

v1 (probe N0) was one command for every bot, in the bot code's small data area. v2 gives every bot its own:

- **The block.** Once per match, when the bots are made, the bot code allocates one block of `ALLOC_SIZE` (0xd40) bytes with the game's allocator (`82627d10`, as for the bots' input states): the host-visible mailbox (`BLOCK_SIZE`, 0x780) and after it, guest-only, each bot's copy of its last whole command (below). It clears it and writes its header (magic `RSM2`, version 2, the record counts and sizes, the match's player manager). Then it stores the block's address (`MBOX`) and the magic (`MBOX_MAGIC`) in its data area. A new match clears both. Without a block no bots are made; the next tick tries again.
- **Which match the bots belong to** (2026-10-30). When it makes the bots the code also records the match's first player, the host's (`HOST_PLAYER`, in its data area after `MBOX`; not part of the mailbox). The bots, the block's address and magic are forgotten when the player manager is gone (between matches), its player list is empty, the manager differs from the recorded one, or its first player is not the recorded host. Before, only the manager was compared and a missing manager left everything in place: a new match whose manager reused the old address would have taken the old match's freed bot players as its own.
  - Each tick (2026-10-31) every bot slot's player must also still be in the manager's player list. A slot whose player is not there (a bot the game removed) is cleared and never touched again. When none of the bots is left although some were made, it is a new match at the old manager's and host's addresses (a deterministic allocator makes that likely, not rare), and the bots are forgotten: before, its freed players were stepped.
  - When the first player is not the recorded host but the bots are still in the list, the host left: the bots are forgotten and a hold (`HOLD`, data area `+0x8c`) is set, and no bots are made again until the player list empties or the manager changes, which clears it. Before 2026-10-31 the next tick made a new set with a bot as its host, beside the 23 orphaned ones.
  - The tests run the code's entry on the interpreter for each case.
  - **The lifecycle** (named 2026-11-05). `STATE` (1 while bots exist for this match) and `HOLD` are one state, `bots.lifecycle(STATE, HOLD)`: `none` (0, 0: no bots; made once the host has a soldier), `made` (1, 0) or `held` (0, 1: the host left). Both set never occurs. The transitions (`bots.LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS`, also tabled in `ARCHITECTURE.md`): any state goes to `none` with no manager, an empty list or another manager; `made` stays `made` while the recorded host is first and a bot is still listed, goes to `none` when no bot is listed, and to `held` when another player is first while bots are still listed; `none` goes to `made` when the host has a soldier and the block is allocated; `held` stays `held`. `test_bots.py` runs every transition on the code. Only the host side changed: the two words, their offsets and the code's bytes are as before (a single guest word would change the code); `guestmem.py bots` prints the state's name.
- **Per bot slot** (`BOT0 + 0x40 * slot`):
  - the guest writes a state record every tick: the tick, then player, soldier (0 while dead), team and position, then the tick again, with `lwsync` after the opening tick and before the closing one. The two ticks are a lock: while the record is written the opening tick is new and the closing one old. A reader reads the closing tick, then the fields, then the opening tick, each read finished before the next, and takes the fields only when the two ticks are the same (no later write had begun: the ticks only grow); otherwise it tries again (`bots.host_record` is that read in Python; guestmem and navhost make it, up to 4 tries). Comparing the two ticks of one copy is not enough: a copy can take the old opening tick, new fields and the old closing tick (a review found it, 2026-10-30; the tests reproduce it on the old readers). The guest already wrote in this order, so the layout, the tick semantics and the version (2) are unchanged: the fix is the readers, and the two `lwsync`s keep the order on hardware that would reorder the stores;
  - the host writes a command record: the stamp (the tick it answered), throttle, strafe, absolute yaw and pitch, the two button words, and a sequence word (`C_SEQ`, the record's last word). The sequence is a lock: the host makes it odd (`(seq + 1) | 1`), writes the stamp and fields, then makes it even and new (`+ 1`). The bot code reads the sequence, the whole record into registers (with `lwsync` between), then the sequence again, and takes the record only when both reads are the same even value, keeping it as the bot's last whole command (a guest-only copy after the host-visible block: readers see no change, so the version stays 2); otherwise it tries again, `TRIES` (4) times in all, and then uses the last whole command. Before 2026-10-31 that tick's frame was neutral: held buttons were released for one tick, a spurious edge (ChangePose, a toggle, flipped crouch; Jump pressed again), whenever the guest read during a host's write. guestmem and navhost write the stamp and fields in one call, between the odd and the even sequence, so a record is open as briefly as they can make it. It then uses the command only while its stamp is not 0 and `tick - stamp` (unsigned) is at most `STALE` (10) ticks (a stamp of 0, a new or zeroed record, was taken while the tick was still at most 10 before 2026-10-30, as the tick counts from 1 in a session's first match); otherwise the frame stays neutral, so the bots stand when the host stops. A host stopped mid-write leaves the sequence odd, and the bots stand until a host writes again.
  - Before 2026-10-30 the stamp was written last and nothing else guarded the fields, so a read during a write could take the new throttle with the old facing or buttons (a review found it; the tests reproduce it on the old code). The word was spare and is zero in a new block, an even sequence, so a host that does not lock is read as before, without the protection: the version stays 2, since nothing a reader already used changed meaning. `bots.guest_command` is the read in Python, for the hosts' tests.
- **Per capture point** (`FLAG0 + 0x30 * k`, up to 8, in the game's own iteration order: `825c5470` / `825c1290` over type `82d57850`): the tick, the entity, owner (`+0x80`), control (`+0xa0`), enabled (`+0xad`), radius (data `+0x114`), position, the tick again, under the same two-tick lock as the state records. A capture point without data gets radius 0 (before 2026-10-30 its record kept an earlier tick's radius). The header's flag count and then its tick are written after all of them (`lwsync` before each). The count and the tick are not a locked pair: a reader takes each flag record by its own two ticks, and a record whose tick is older than the newest one read is left from a tick that found more capture points (guestmem marks it stale).

The code, table and names take 0xd38 of the cave's 0xe40 bytes (0x108 free); the data area uses 0x90 of its 0x1f0 bytes. The mailbox layout and its version (2) are unchanged by the 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31 fixes (the command copies lie after the host-visible block; `HOLD` is in the data area, not the mailbox). The readers are navhost (project-opfor-bf1943 `TnT/Code/Engine/AI/Bots/navhost`; its `rsmbox.h` is a copy of this layout that its tests check against `bots.py`) and `guestmem.py`.

## Tests

- `python -B tests\test_xeniakit.py` checks the patch file, the port edit and the Xenia fix without game data, and that `verify` enforces the build's bot mode on a made-up build: a normal build fails while Xenia's patches folder holds a bots experiment patch (enabled or not, under its own name or another: another build against the same Xenia may have left it), and a bots build fails with a second one (each made-up build has its `launch.cmd`, which `verify` now checks). It also checks the build's bots patch step (`install_bots_patch`): a normal build removes every kit-made bots patch, a renamed copy too, and keeps other patch files; a bots build leaves exactly its own; a foreign file under the kit's name is refused with nothing changed. On Windows it writes `launch.cmd` for a Xenia folder named with an accented letter, a `%` and Cyrillic and CJK letters, and runs it under cmd.exe in a new hidden console set to code page 437 and then 65001, with the start line turned into an echo (nothing is launched): the `cd` reaches the folder, the start line names the paths whole, and the console has its code page back; the same file without its `chcp` line fails in 437 (so the switch is what makes it work), and a path with a double quote is refused.
- With `--game` it also runs a full build from your package into a temporary folder, against a scratch Xenia folder holding only a copy of `xenia_canary.exe` (so your Xenia folder is never written): every edited file must match `known.json`, the patch file must reach the scratch folder, `verify` must accept the build and must notice a changed file. Afterwards it checks that your Xenia folder's patch files and `xenia_canary_netfix.exe` are unchanged. Without your package or Xenia it skips.
- `tests	est_xeniakit_build.py` (pytest-style; `python -B -m pytest` or the suite's `run_tests.py quick`) runs `build`, `verify` and `launch` on a made-up package and Xenia, with every refusal. It also checks that `verify` checks `launch.cmd` in a normal, a `--gpu d3d12` and an `--experiment-bots` build: the file as the build wrote it passes, an edited one (another option, or the other GPU backend) and a missing one fail, and for a manifest without the recorded `--gpu` either backend's file passes.

- `python -B tests\test_ppcasm.py` checks the PowerPC assembler against capstone (an independent decoder; skipped with a note when capstone is not installed). `la` into r0 is `lis` + `ori` (an `addi` with base r0 adds to 0, so `lis` + `addi` lost the high half before 2026-10-30), and the test runs each `la`/`li32` pair as capstone decodes it for the value it leaves; `addi`/`addis` with base r0 and loads or stores with base r0 are refused, since the instruction reads 0 there. Operand counts are checked: an extra operand (which was dropped, so a typo assembled as something else) and a missing one (an `IndexError` without a line number) are an `AsmError` naming the line since 2026-10-30.
- `python -B tests\test_bots.py` checks that the bots code assembles, fits its code cave, and that the hook branches to it, and the mailbox: the layout fits, and capstone decodes the code's mailbox reads and writes as the layout names them (state and command records, header, flag records, the stale check, the allocation, the capture-point iteration). It also runs the code's command read on a small interpreter of capstone's decoding while the host's writes land between its loads at every offset and pace: it takes the old command, the new one or none, never a mix; an odd sequence, a stale or future stamp and a sequence that never settles give the neutral frame (with no earlier command); `bots.guest_command` agrees in every case. With an earlier whole command, a read that finds the host writing uses it while it is fresh: Jump held across that tick gives one press, no release, and the copy goes stale after `STALE` ticks. It runs the code's state and flag record writes on the same kind of interpreter (the stores in `bots.guest_record`'s order, `lwsync` after the opening tick and before the closing one) while `bots.host_record` reads between its steps at many offsets and paces: the read takes the old record, the new one or none, never a mix, and a read of one copy comparing its two ticks takes a mix there. It runs the code's entry on the interpreter for each match case (the same match; no player manager; the manager's address reused by a new match with another first player; an empty list; another manager; no bots yet; the manager and host both at reused addresses with none of the bots in the list; the host gone with the bots still there; no bot made) and checks which path it takes, that a bot gone from the list has its slot cleared, what forgetting clears (the hold too), and that making the bots records the host's player; after the host leaves, nothing is made on the following ticks, the hold ends when the list empties or the manager changes, and then bots are made again; a stamp of 0 at tick 5 gives the neutral frame; a capture point without data gets radius 0; the header's count comes before its tick with `lwsync` between. `--image` also checks it against the decoded BF1943 image, first its SHA-256 (and that the game's own code uses `lwsync`).

All of them are in the suite's `run_tests.py`: the three without game data in the quick tier, `test_xeniakit.py --game` and `test_bots.py --image` in the bf1943 tier. `--image` first checks the image's SHA-256 against operation-rising-sun's `research/evidence/xex-image-integrity.json` (or the hash recorded in the test without it) and skips the other image checks on a mismatch.

```

`bf1943-xenia-kit/bots.py`:

```py
"""Experiment: server-side bots for BF1943 in Xenia, as a second Xenia patch file.

Input: a list of bots, (side, class) each (DEFAULT_BOTS: a full 12 v 12 match). Output: build() assembles the guest
code below (ppcasm) with its bot table and names, and gives the patch words; patch_toml() gives the patch file's text
(`python -B bots.py` prints it). The mailbox layout names (MBOX_MAGIC ... BLOCK_SIZE) are shared with the host
programs that drive the bots.

BF1943's AI was stripped (no AI controller, orders or navigation), but its server still creates players with no
network connection: the leftover AI spawner (SoldierSpawnEntity, 8236bc98) does so. The bots here are created the
same way, then given what a human player gets from the network, and spawned through the human spawn path:

  per server frame, after the server's own player update (8238eb68, called at 0x82391988):
    1. once a human player has a soldier: for each bot,
         createPlayer 82387ef0(manager, 0)          a ServerPlayer with no connection
         addPlayer    8238efd8(manager, p, name)    name as a {begin, end} string
         8240dfe0(server context + 0x44, p)          as the network join does next: the score and stats
                                                    managers (the first run's bots were not on the scoreboard)
         an input state (82627d10(0x168), constructor 822c1478), attached with 8236f230(p, state): the soldier
                                                    reads its controls from it (no frames are pushed yet:
                                                    it stands still)
         ready        82375130(p)                   (also keeps 8238eb68 from giving it its default soldier)
         setTeam      82374f90(p, team)             1 USMC, 2 Japan
         the team's kit by asset name: 82378988(handle, "Objects/Soldiers/US/Assault") finds the loaded
         SoldierEntityData; 82373a28(p + 0x1f4, it) makes it the player's kit (a counted reference)
    2. every frame, each bot:
       gets one neutral input frame, as the server makes for a connection with no input queued (823af4a0):
       822bd4a8(frame) clears it; its sequence number (+0x98) is the current frame's (input state +0x160) plus
       one; +0x80 is the server's time step (the hook's f1; 822f1d70 writes it there for entities without a
       player) and +0x84 is carried over (823a1f80 does the same); 822c15d0(state, frame) pushes it. Its controls
       come from the host mailbox (below): throttle, strafe, absolute facing and buttons, when the host answered a
       recent tick; otherwise the frame stays neutral and the bot stands;
       the bot's state (its player, soldier, team and position) goes to the mailbox;
       and without a soldier (+0x120), asks to spawn at its base: 82382720(p, spawn). The spawn is found by
       identity, not by list position: in the per-team lists 82343f68(owner, 1 and 2), the first spawn entity
       whose data's Team (entity + 0x14 -> data + 0x88) is the bot's team, turned into a spawn id (822a83a8).
       (With spawn 0, or the first entry of either list, each side's bots spawned on the other side's carrier:
       runs of 2026-10-23.) The server refuses while a respawn delay runs, so this also respawns them.
    3. every frame, after the bots: each capture point's owner, control, radius and position go to the mailbox.

Host mailbox v2 (milestone N4, 2026-10-30; v1 was probe N0's single command for every bot): one block per match,
from the game's allocator, its address in the data area; a state and a command record per bot, a record per capture
point. Layout: the MBOX_MAGIC ... BLOCK_SIZE names below. Readers: navhost (project-opfor-bf1943
TnT/Code/Engine/AI/Bots/navhost, its rsmbox.h a checked copy of the layout) and the harness's guestmem.py.

Stepping: a soldier is advanced only by its virtual +0x104 (822f05c8), which the network path calls once per
input frame it drains from a connection (823b2c80, at 823b2ed4). The physics world skips characters while the
setting Physics.SingleStepCharacter is on (8253e4c8 tests the character's +0xd2, which the soldier constructor sets
from it), and the per-tick update 822f1d70 runs only the last part of the step (+0x114), and only for players with
the AI flag (+0x214). In BFBC2 the setting is probably turned off in levels with AI (LevelData.HasAI; a BFBC2 lead,
unverified), so its physics world steps AI soldiers (research/evidence/ai-soldier-control.json). The bots therefore call +0x104 after each frame they push, and keep
the AI flag at 0 so that 822f1d70 does not apply the input a second time. (Runs of 2026-10-23: without stepping,
with the flag 0 the bots stood at their spawn transform 0.8 m above the deck; with it 1 they stood on the deck
but ignored all input.) Evidence and addresses: operation-rising-sun/research/AGENT_PROGRESS.md (2026-10-22,
"Bots: the server player pipeline", and the 2026-10-23 bot entries). The addresses are this build's (module hash 872BBE31C0FBA21B) only.
"""
import struct
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Sequence

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
import ppcasm  # noqa: E402

PATCH_FILE = '5841097E - Battlefield 1943 - bots experiment.patch.toml'
HEADER = '# Generated by bf1943-xenia-kit/bots.py.'
HOOK = 0x82391988            # bl 0x8238eb68 in the server player update 82391930
HOOK_ORIGINAL = 0x4BFFD1E1   # that bl
CODE = 0x82AAA1C0            # unused, zero: the end of the BINK code section's last page (to 0x82AAB000)
CODE_END = 0x82AAB000
DATA = 0x82D26E10            # unused, zero: after .data, before fieldinf (to 0x82D27000)
DATA_END = 0x82D27000
MAX_BOTS = 23               # a full 24-player match (12 v 12) with the host
# data layout: state words, then a player slot per bot, then the kit lookup's handle, then the host mailbox's address
STATE, MANAGER, TICK, SLOTS = 0x0, 0x4, 0x8, 0x10
HANDLE = SLOTS + 4 * MAX_BOTS + 4
# Host mailbox v2 (milestone N4: navhost; guestmem.py in the test harness). The data area has no room for a command
# block per bot, so once per match, when the bots are created, the bot code allocates one block with the game's
# allocator (82627d10, as for the input states), clears it, writes its header, and then stores its address (MBOX) and
# MBOX_MAGIC in the data area; a new match (forget) clears both. The block, big-endian words:
#   header (H_*): magic, version, bot count, bot record size, flag record count and size, the match's player manager,
#     the tick (written last each tick, after the bots and flags) and how many flags the tick found
#   per bot slot k at BOT0 + BOT_SIZE * k: a state record the guest writes every tick (R_*: the tick, then player,
#     soldier (0: dead or not spawned), team, position x y z as float bits, then the tick again), and a command
#     record the host writes (C_*: the stamp,
#     the tick it answered; throttle, strafe (actions 0 and 1), absolute yaw and pitch (frame + 0x88 / + 0x8c, used
#     with button bit 40), the button u64 at frame + 0x78 as high and low words; then a sequence word, C_SEQ). The
#     sequence is a lock: the host makes it odd, writes the stamp and fields, then makes it even and new
#     ((seq + 1) | 1, then that + 1). The guest reads the sequence, the record, the sequence again, and takes the
#     record only when both are the same even value (else it tries again, TRIES times in all), keeping it as the bot's
#     last whole command (a guest-only copy, G_*, after the block); with no whole read this tick the last whole command
#     is used. When that one's stamp is more than STALE ticks old (or ahead, or none: 0), the frame is neutral, so the
#     bots stand if the host stops. (Before 2026-10-30 the stamp was written last and nothing else guarded the fields: a read
#     during a write could mix the new throttle with the old facing. The word was spare, so zero is an even
#     sequence: a host that does not lock is read as before.)
#   per capture point f (FLAG0 + FLAG_SIZE * f, up to MAX_FLAGS, in the game's own iteration order): the tick, the
#     entity, owner team (+0x80), control 0-100 (+0xa0, float bits), enabled (+0xad), radius (data + 0x114, float
#     bits), position x y z, then the tick again.
#   State and flag records are under a two-word sequence lock: the guest writes the opening tick (R_SEQ, F_SEQ), lwsync,
#     the fields, lwsync, the closing tick (R_SEQ_END, F_SEQ_END). While it writes, the opening tick is the new one and
#     the closing the old: they differ. A host reads the closing tick, then the fields, then the opening tick, each
#     read after the one before, and takes the fields only when the two ticks are the same (then no write had begun
#     after the one it closed: the ticks only grow), else tries again a few times (host_record is the read in Python).
#     Comparing the two ticks of one copy is not enough: a copy can take the old opening tick, then some new fields,
#     then the old closing tick (a review found it, 2026-10-30; the tests reproduce it). The write order was already
#     this one, so the version stays 2: only the readers and the lwsyncs changed. A tick of 0: never written.
#   The header's flag count and tick (H_FLAGS, H_TICK) are written after the flag records, the count first (lwsync
#     between), but they are not a locked pair: a reader takes each flag record by its own two ticks, and a record
#     whose tick is older than the newest one it read is left from a tick that found more capture points (guestmem
#     marks it stale).
MBOX_MAGIC = HANDLE + 16
MBOX = MBOX_MAGIC + 4
MAILBOX_END = MBOX + 4
# The match the bots were made in: its player manager (MANAGER) and its first player (HOST_PLAYER, the host's), stored
# when the bots are made. The bots are forgotten when either differs, when the manager is gone or the player list is
# empty: before 2026-10-30 only the manager was compared, and a new match whose manager reused the old one's address
# would have taken the old match's freed bot players as its own. Not part of the mailbox (navhost does not read it).
# Each tick, while bots exist, every slot's player must also still be in the manager's list (2026-10-30): a slot whose
# player is not is cleared (a bot the game removed); when none is left and some were made, it is a new match at the old
# addresses, and the bots are forgotten. When the host is gone but the bots are still in the list (the host left), the
# bots are forgotten and HOLD is set: no bots are made again until the list empties or the manager changes (before
# 2026-10-30 the next tick made a new set, with a bot as its host). Not part of the mailbox either.
HOST_PLAYER = MAILBOX_END
HOLD = HOST_PLAYER + 4
DATA_USED = HOLD + 4
# The bots' lifecycle: one named state (lifecycle(), its table) kept in the two data-area words above, STATE and HOLD,
# which the code reads and writes separately (2026-11-05: named host-side; the code and its bytes are unchanged).
LIFE_NONE, LIFE_MADE, LIFE_HELD = 'none', 'made', 'held'
LIFECYCLE_WORDS = {LIFE_NONE: (0, 0), LIFE_MADE: (1, 0), LIFE_HELD: (0, 1)}     # state: (STATE word, HOLD word)
LIFE_ANY = 'any'
# (key, from, to, path: the code's decision label then where the tick ends, when); every tick, after the server's own
# player update. tests/test_bots.py runs each row on the code.
LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS = (
    ('no-manager', LIFE_ANY, LIFE_NONE, ('forget', 'out'), 'no player manager (between matches)'),
    ('empty-list', LIFE_ANY, LIFE_NONE, ('forget', 'out'), 'nobody in the match (it ended)'),
    ('other-manager', LIFE_ANY, LIFE_NONE, ('forget', 'out'), 'another player manager than the one recorded'),
    ('same-match', LIFE_MADE, LIFE_MADE, ('respawn', 'respawn'),
     'the recorded host is the first player and a bot is still in the list (or none was made): the bots are stepped'),
    ('new-match', LIFE_MADE, LIFE_NONE, ('forget', 'out'),
     'the host is the first player but none of the bots is in the list: a new match at the old addresses'),
    ('host-reused', LIFE_MADE, LIFE_NONE, ('forget', 'out'),
     'another first player and none of the bots in the list: another match at the old manager\'s address'),
    ('host-left', LIFE_MADE, LIFE_HELD, ('forget_held', 'out'),
     'another first player while bots are still in the list: the host left; the bots are forgotten'),
    ('make', LIFE_NONE, LIFE_MADE, ('make', 'create'),
     'the first player (the host) has a soldier and the mailbox block is allocated: the bots are made'),
    ('host-no-soldier', LIFE_NONE, LIFE_NONE, ('make', 'out'), 'the first player has no soldier yet'),
    ('no-block', LIFE_NONE, LIFE_NONE, ('make', 'out'), 'the allocator gave no block (tried again next tick)'),
    ('held', LIFE_HELD, LIFE_HELD, ('make', 'out'), 'held: nothing is made while the list keeps players and the manager'),
)
MAGIC = 0x52534D32           # 'RSM2', in the data area and the block's header
VERSION = 2
STALE = 10                   # ticks: an older command gives a neutral frame; a stamp of 0 (never answered) gives one too
MAX_FLAGS = 8
H_MAGIC, H_VERSION, H_BOTS, H_BOT_SIZE, H_FLAGS_MAX, H_FLAG_SIZE, H_MANAGER, H_TICK, H_FLAGS = (4 * k for k in range(9))
BOT0, BOT_SIZE = 0x40, 0x40
R_SEQ, R_PLAYER, R_SOLDIER, R_TEAM, R_X, R_Y, R_Z, R_SEQ_END = (4 * k for k in range(8))
C_STAMP, C_THROTTLE, C_STRAFE, C_YAW, C_PITCH, C_BUTTONS_HI, C_BUTTONS_LO, C_SEQ = (0x20 + 4 * k for k in range(8))
TRIES = 4                    # reads of a command record before a neutral frame (the guest's own; not in rsmbox.h),
                             # and of a state or flag record by host_record
LWSYNC = 0x7C2004AC          # lwsync (ppcasm has no mnemonic for it; the game's own code uses it)
FLAG0 = BOT0 + BOT_SIZE * MAX_BOTS
FLAG_SIZE = 0x30
F_SEQ, F_ENTITY, F_OWNER, F_CONTROL, F_ENABLED, F_RADIUS, F_X, F_Y, F_Z = (4 * k for k in range(9))
F_SEQ_END = 0x2C
BLOCK_SIZE = FLAG0 + FLAG_SIZE * MAX_FLAGS
# Guest-only, after the host-visible block (2026-10-30; readers see no change, so the version stays 2): per bot slot k
# at BLOCK_SIZE + BOT_SIZE * k, the bot's last whole command, laid out as its command record (G_x = G0 + C_x from the
# slot's record). When a read finds the host writing (TRIES times), this copy is used while its stamp is fresh, instead
# of a neutral frame, which released held buttons for that tick (a spurious edge for toggles such as ChangePose).
G0 = BLOCK_SIZE - BOT0
G_STAMP, G_THROTTLE, G_STRAFE, G_YAW, G_PITCH, G_BUTTONS_HI, G_BUTTONS_LO = (
    G0 + field for field in (C_STAMP, C_THROTTLE, C_STRAFE, C_YAW, C_PITCH, C_BUTTONS_HI, C_BUTTONS_LO))
ALLOC_SIZE = BLOCK_SIZE + BOT_SIZE * MAX_BOTS
CP_TYPE = 0x82D57850         # ServerCapturePointEntity's type (research/evidence/bot-interfaces.json)
# the mailbox's names, for the assembler and for readers that check their own copy of the layout (navhost's rsmbox.h)
MAILBOX_NAMES = ('MBOX_MAGIC', 'MBOX', 'MAGIC', 'VERSION', 'STALE', 'MAX_FLAGS', 'H_MAGIC', 'H_VERSION', 'H_BOTS',
                 'H_BOT_SIZE', 'H_FLAGS_MAX', 'H_FLAG_SIZE', 'H_MANAGER', 'H_TICK', 'H_FLAGS', 'BOT0', 'BOT_SIZE',
                 'R_SEQ', 'R_PLAYER', 'R_SOLDIER', 'R_TEAM', 'R_X', 'R_Y', 'R_Z', 'R_SEQ_END', 'C_STAMP', 'C_THROTTLE',
                 'C_STRAFE', 'C_YAW', 'C_PITCH', 'C_BUTTONS_HI', 'C_BUTTONS_LO', 'C_SEQ', 'FLAG0', 'FLAG_SIZE', 'F_SEQ',
                 'F_ENTITY', 'F_OWNER', 'F_CONTROL', 'F_ENABLED', 'F_RADIUS', 'F_X', 'F_Y', 'F_Z', 'F_SEQ_END',
                 'BLOCK_SIZE', 'CP_TYPE')
FRAME = 0x1E0                # stack frame: an input frame buffer at +0x80 (0x100 bytes, 16-aligned); saves (to -0x58) above it
BUF = 0x80
DT = BUF + 0x104             # the saved time step (float), between the buffer and the saved registers

TEAMS = {1: 'US', 2: 'RU'}   # asset folder per team (Japan's soldiers keep BFBC2's RU name)
KITS = {'Rifleman': 'Assault', 'Infantry': 'Support', 'Scout': 'Specialist'}
FRIENDLY, ENEMY = 1, 2       # a bot's side, relative to the host's team (read when the bots are created)
CLASSES = ['Rifleman', 'Infantry', 'Scout']
# a full match: 11 on the host's side and 12 against, the classes in turn
DEFAULT_BOTS = ([(FRIENDLY, CLASSES[k % 3]) for k in range(11)] + [(ENEMY, CLASSES[k % 3]) for k in range(12)])

CODE_SOURCE = '''
hook:
    mflr r12
    stw r12, -8(r1)
    std r22, -0x58(r1)
    std r23, -0x50(r1)
    std r24, -0x48(r1)
    std r25, -0x40(r1)
    std r26, -0x38(r1)
    std r27, -0x30(r1)
    std r28, -0x28(r1)
    std r29, -0x20(r1)
    std r30, -0x18(r1)
    std r31, -0x10(r1)
    stwu r1, -FRAME(r1)
    stfs f1, DT(r1)          # the server's time step (82391930 passes it to 8238eb68 in f1), for the frames
    bl 0x8238eb68            # the server's own player update (r3, f1 as the caller set them)
    la r31, DATA
    bl 0x82349d78            # server context
    lwz r30, 0x28(r3)        # player manager
    cmpwi r30, 0
    beq forget               # none (between matches): the bots are gone
    lwz r4, 0x54(r30)        # players: begin, end
    lwz r5, 0x58(r30)
    cmplw r4, r5
    beq forget               # nobody in the match (it ended): the bots are gone
    lwz r3, MANAGER(r31)
    cmplw r3, r30
    bne forget               # another match's player manager
    lwz r3, STATE(r31)
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq make
    li r9, 0                 # bots made: each slot's player must still be in the manager's list (r9: found there),
    li r10, 0                # else its slot is cleared (r10: gone) and it is never touched again (a freed player)
    la r28, SLOTS_ADDR
    li r29, MAX_BOTS
check_slot:
    lwz r6, 0(r28)
    cmpwi r6, 0
    beq check_next
    mr r7, r4
check_find:
    cmplw r7, r5
    beq check_gone
    lwz r8, 0(r7)
    addi r7, r7, 4
    cmplw r8, r6
    bne check_find
    addi r9, r9, 1
    b check_next
check_gone:
    li r8, 0
    stw r8, 0(r28)
    addi r10, r10, 1
check_next:
    addi r28, r28, 4
    addi r29, r29, -1
    cmpwi r29, 0
    bne check_slot
    lwz r6, 0(r4)            # the match's first player must still be the host the bots were made with
    lwz r7, HOST_PLAYER(r31)
    cmplw r6, r7
    bne host_changed
    cmpwi r9, 0
    bne respawn              # the same match (bots the game removed are dropped above)
    cmpwi r10, 0
    beq respawn              # no bot was made (the server was full): nothing to check
    b forget                 # none of the bots is in the list: a new match at the old manager's and host's addresses
host_changed:
    cmpwi r9, 0
    beq forget               # another match (the manager's address reused by it)
    b forget_held            # the host left and the bots are still in the match: no new bots until it ends
make:                        # lifecycle none or held
    lwz r3, HOLD(r31)        # held (the host left this match): no bots until the list empties or the manager changes
    cmpwi r3, 0
    bne out
    lwz r4, 0(r4)            # the first player (the host's own) has a soldier: the match is running
    lwz r5, 0x120(r4)
    cmpwi r5, 0
    beq out
    li r3, ALLOC_SIZE        # the host mailbox, one block per match (82627d10 as for the input states), and after it
    bl 0x82627d10            # the bots' guest-only command copies; no bots without it: the next tick tries again
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq out
    mr r29, r3
    li r4, 0
    li r5, ALLOC_SIZE
clear_mailbox:               # the allocator need not clear it
    addi r5, r5, -4
    add r6, r29, r5
    stw r4, 0(r6)
    cmpwi r5, 0
    bne clear_mailbox
    li32 r4, MAGIC           # its header
    stw r4, H_MAGIC(r29)
    li r4, VERSION
    stw r4, H_VERSION(r29)
    li r4, MAX_BOTS
    stw r4, H_BOTS(r29)
    li r4, BOT_SIZE
    stw r4, H_BOT_SIZE(r29)
    li r4, MAX_FLAGS
    stw r4, H_FLAGS_MAX(r29)
    li r4, FLAG_SIZE
    stw r4, H_FLAG_SIZE(r29)
    stw r30, H_MANAGER(r29)
    stw r29, MBOX(r31)       # then its address, then the magic word: a host reading both sees a complete block
    li32 r4, MAGIC
    stw r4, MBOX_MAGIC(r31)
    la r3, FMT_MAILBOX       # report: the mailbox's address
    mr r4, r29
    bl 0x829fa7ec
    lwz r4, 0x54(r30)        # the host's player again (the calls above used the volatile registers)
    lwz r4, 0(r4)
    stw r4, HOST_PLAYER(r31) # the match's key, with the manager
    lwz r25, 0x30(r4)        # the host's team: bots are friendly (the same) or enemy (3 - it)
    mr r5, r4                # report: the host's player and team (Xenia logs DbgPrint)
    lwz r6, 0x30(r4)
    la r3, FMT_HOST
    mr r4, r5
    mr r5, r6
    bl 0x829fa7ec
    li r3, 1
    stw r3, STATE(r31)       # lifecycle none -> made: create once per match (the data area is per game session: see
                             # AGENT_PROGRESS)
    la r29, BOTS
    la r28, SLOTS_ADDR
create:
    lwz r3, 0(r29)           # side (FRIENDLY or ENEMY), 0 ends the table
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq respawn
    mr r24, r25              # the bot's team
    cmpwi r3, FRIENDLY
    beq side_known
    li r24, 3
    subf r24, r25, r24
side_known:
    mr r3, r30
    li r4, 0
    bl 0x82387ef0            # createPlayer
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq respawn              # server full
    stw r3, 0(r28)
    mr r4, r3
    mr r3, r30
    lwz r5, 12(r29)
    bl 0x8238efd8            # addPlayer(manager, player, name)
    bl 0x82349d78            # as the network join does next (823af188): register the player with the
    lwz r3, 0x44(r3)         # server's score and stats managers, 8240dfe0(context + 0x44, player)
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq input
    lwz r4, 0(r28)
    bl 0x8240dfe0
input:
    li r3, 0x168
    bl 0x82627d10            # memory for an input state
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq team
    bl 0x822c1478            # construct it
    mr r4, r3
    lwz r3, 0(r28)
    bl 0x8236f230            # player + 0x118 = it
team:
    lwz r3, 0(r28)
    bl 0x82375130            # ready to spawn
    lwz r3, 0(r28)
    mr r4, r24
    bl 0x82374f90            # setTeam
    li r4, 0
    stw r4, HANDLE(r31)
    stw r4, HANDLE_4(r31)
    stw r4, HANDLE_8(r31)
    stw r4, HANDLE_C(r31)
    addi r3, r31, HANDLE
    lwz r4, 4(r29)           # the kit's name for team 1 (USMC) or team 2 (Japan)
    cmpwi r24, 1
    beq kit_named
    lwz r4, 8(r29)
kit_named:
    bl 0x82378988            # the kit's SoldierEntityData, by asset name
    lwz r4, HANDLE(r31)
    cmpwi r4, 0
    beq next
    lwz r3, 0(r28)
    addi r3, r3, 0x1f4
    bl 0x82373a28            # player kit = it
next:
    la r3, FMT_CREATED       # report: the bot, its team and kit
    lwz r4, 0(r28)
    lwz r5, 0x30(r4)
    lwz r6, 0x1f4(r4)
    bl 0x829fa7ec
    addi r29, r29, 16
    addi r28, r28, 4
    b create
respawn:
    lwz r3, TICK(r31)        # a server tick count, for the position reports
    addi r3, r3, 1
    stw r3, TICK(r31)
    andi. r3, r3, 63         # every 64 ticks also report the host's soldier (the first player), to check the
    bne bots_loop            # position reading against a soldier that is known to move
    lwz r4, 0x54(r30)
    lwz r4, 0(r4)
    lwz r3, 0x120(r4)
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq bots_loop
    bl 0x822a7bb0
    lwz r5, 0x30(r3)
    lwz r6, 0x34(r3)
    lwz r7, 0x38(r3)
    lwz r4, 0x54(r30)
    lwz r4, 0(r4)
    la r3, FMT_HOST_POSITION
    bl 0x829fa7ec
bots_loop:
    lwz r22, MBOX(r31)       # each bot's records in the host mailbox (made with the bots, so never 0 here)
    addi r22, r22, BOT0
    la r28, SLOTS_ADDR
    li r29, MAX_BOTS
spawn:
    lwz r27, 0(r28)
    cmpwi r27, 0
    beq skip
    lwz r5, TICK(r31)        # its state record: the tick first, the fields, then the tick again (record_end),
    stw r5, R_SEQ(r22)       # lwsync between (a two-word sequence lock: R_SEQ new and R_SEQ_END old while it is
    .long LWSYNC             # written; a host reads R_SEQ_END, the fields, R_SEQ, and takes them when the two agree)
    lwz r3, 0x118(r27)       # its input state: one neutral frame per tick, as the server makes for a
    cmpwi r3, 0              # connection with no input queued (823af4a0 -> 822bd4a8, 823a1f80, 822c15d0)
    beq record
    addi r3, r1, BUF
    bl 0x822bd4a8            # a cleared frame
    lwz r3, 0x118(r27)
    lwz r4, 0x160(r3)        # the current frame:
    lwz r5, 0x98(r4)
    addi r5, r5, 1
    stw r5, BUF_98(r1)       # its sequence number + 1
    lwz r5, DT(r1)
    stw r5, BUF_80(r1)       # the frame's time step (+0x80: 822f1d70 stores its f1 there, 822ba678); copied
                             # from the cleared first frame it stayed 0, and the soldiers never moved
                             # (with the AI flag they settled onto the deck but ignored forward input)
    lwz r5, 0x84(r4)
    stw r5, BUF_84(r1)
    li r7, TRIES             # the host's command, read whole (a sequence lock): the sequence, the record into
command:                     # registers, the sequence again; taken only when both reads are the same even value,
    lwz r8, C_SEQ(r22)       # else tried again, TRIES times in all, then a neutral frame
    .long LWSYNC             # (lwsync: the record's loads after the first sequence load, and before the second)
    lwz r6, C_STAMP(r22)
    lwz r9, C_THROTTLE(r22)
    lwz r10, C_STRAFE(r22)
    lwz r11, C_YAW(r22)
    lwz r12, C_PITCH(r22)
    lwz r0, C_BUTTONS_HI(r22)
    lwz r3, C_BUTTONS_LO(r22)
    .long LWSYNC
    lwz r4, C_SEQ(r22)
    cmplw r8, r4
    bne command_again        # the host wrote meanwhile
    andi. r4, r4, 1
    beq command_whole        # even: no write was under way
command_again:
    addi r7, r7, -1
    cmpwi r7, 0
    bne command
    b command_last           # no whole read this tick (the host was writing): the last whole command, while fresh
command_whole:               # kept as the bot's last whole command (a guest-only copy after the block's host layout)
    stw r6, G_STAMP(r22)
    stw r9, G_THROTTLE(r22)
    stw r10, G_STRAFE(r22)
    stw r11, G_YAW(r22)
    stw r12, G_PITCH(r22)
    stw r0, G_BUTTONS_HI(r22)
    stw r3, G_BUTTONS_LO(r22)
command_last:                # (before 2026-10-30 a read that found the host writing gave a neutral frame: held
    lwz r6, G_STAMP(r22)     # buttons were released for that tick, a spurious edge for toggles such as ChangePose)
    cmpwi r6, 0              # a stamp of 0 answered nothing (a new or zeroed record): neutral, even while the tick,
    beq push                 # which counts from 1 and is never reset, is still at most STALE
    lwz r5, TICK(r31)        # used if it answered a tick at most STALE ticks ago (tick - stamp, unsigned: a stamp
    subf r5, r6, r5          # ahead is as old)
    cmplwi r5, STALE
    bgt push                 # else a neutral frame: the bot stands
    lwz r9, G_THROTTLE(r22)
    lwz r10, G_STRAFE(r22)
    lwz r11, G_YAW(r22)
    lwz r12, G_PITCH(r22)
    lwz r0, G_BUTTONS_HI(r22)
    lwz r3, G_BUTTONS_LO(r22)
    stw r9, BUF_THROTTLE(r1)     # EIAThrottle (action 0, an analog float at frame + 8)
    stw r10, BUF_STRAFE(r1)      # EIAStrafe (action 1, frame + 0x0c)
    stw r0, BUF_BUTTONS_HI(r1)   # the button bits (actions 8-39; bit 40: the absolute facing is valid), a u64
    stw r3, BUF_BUTTONS_LO(r1)
    stw r11, BUF_YAW(r1)     # the absolute facing read with bit 40 (82308268): frame + 0x88 and + 0x8c
    stw r12, BUF_PITCH(r1)
push:
    lwz r3, 0x118(r27)
    addi r4, r1, BUF
    bl 0x822c15d0            # push it
    lwz r3, 0x120(r27)       # and step the soldier with it, as the network path does after each frame it
    cmpwi r3, 0              # drains (823b2ed4): soldier virtual +0x104 (822f05c8: facing, jump and velocity
    beq record               # (+0x110), the character physics with frame dt, then placement (+0x114)),
    lwz r11, 0(r3)           # entry index 0. Nothing else steps a soldier: the physics world skips characters
    lwz r11, 0x104(r11)      # while Physics.SingleStepCharacter is on (8253e4c8), and the per-tick update
    mtctr r11                # 822f1d70 runs only +0x114, and only for AI-flagged players.
    li r4, 0
    bctrl
record:
    lwz r3, 0x120(r27)       # the state record: player, soldier, team, and where the server has the soldier
    stw r27, R_PLAYER(r22)   # (its transform, 822a7bb0, translation row at +0x30, as raw float bits)
    stw r3, R_SOLDIER(r22)
    lwz r5, 0x30(r27)
    stw r5, R_TEAM(r22)
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq record_end
    bl 0x822a7bb0
    lwz r5, 0x30(r3)
    lwz r6, 0x34(r3)
    lwz r7, 0x38(r3)
    stw r5, R_X(r22)
    stw r6, R_Y(r22)
    stw r7, R_Z(r22)
    lwz r4, TICK(r31)        # report: every 64 ticks, the same position in the log
    andi. r4, r4, 63
    bne record_end
    lwz r3, 0x120(r27)
    lwz r8, 0x328(r3)        # the soldier's throttle limit (822edb28 clamps action 0 to it)
    li r9, 0
    li r10, 0
    lwz r3, 0x118(r27)
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq report
    lwz r3, 0x160(r3)        # the bot's current input frame: throttle (+0x08) and time step (+0x80)
    lwz r9, 8(r3)
    lwz r10, 0x80(r3)
report:
    mr r4, r27
    la r3, FMT_POSITION
    bl 0x829fa7ec
record_end:
    lwz r5, TICK(r31)
    .long LWSYNC             # the fields before the closing tick
    stw r5, R_SEQ_END(r22)
spawn_it:
    lwz r4, 0x120(r27)       # no soldier yet (or dead): ask to spawn at its team's base
    cmpwi r4, 0
    bne skip
    bl 0x82349d78            # the spawn lists' owner, as 82382720 finds it (0x8238278c):
    lwz r11, 0x2c(r3)        # *(*(context + 0x2c) + 0x74) + 8
    lwz r3, 0x74(r11)
    lwz r26, 8(r3)
    li r25, 1                # search the lists of teams 1 and 2 for a spawn of the bot's own team
lists:
    mr r3, r26
    mr r4, r25
    bl 0x82343f68            # that team's list: begin, end
    lwz r24, 0(r3)
    lwz r23, 4(r3)
entries:
    cmplw r24, r23
    beq next_list
    lwz r3, 0(r24)           # a spawn entity
    addi r24, r24, 4
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq entries
    lwz r4, 0x14(r3)         # its data (SoldierSpawnEntityData; 8236b688 reads it so) and the data's Team
    cmpwi r4, 0              # (+0x88, read so by the constructor 82362a40)
    beq entries
    lwz r4, 0x88(r4)
    lwz r5, 0x30(r27)
    cmpw r4, r5
    bne entries
    bl 0x822a83a8            # the bot's own base: its spawn id, as 82382720 makes it
    mr r26, r3
    b request
next_list:
    addi r25, r25, 1
    cmpwi r25, 3
    bne lists
    li r26, 0                # none found: the server's own default
request:
    mr r3, r27
    mr r4, r26
    bl 0x82382720
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq skip
    la r3, FMT_SPAWNED       # report a spawn: the bot, its team, the spawn asked for, the soldier
    mr r4, r27
    lwz r5, 0x30(r27)
    mr r6, r26
    lwz r7, 0x120(r27)
    bl 0x829fa7ec
skip:
    addi r22, r22, BOT_SIZE
    addi r28, r28, 4
    addi r29, r29, -1
    cmpwi r29, 0
    bne spawn
    lwz r29, MBOX(r31)       # the capture points, for the host: iterated as the game's own code does (82326d30):
    addi r29, r29, FLAG0     # 825c5470(iterator, *(*context) + 4, type), then 825c1290(iterator) until it gives 0
    li r28, 0                # (the frame buffer is free now: the iterator's 16 bytes go there)
    bl 0x82349d78
    lwz r4, 0(r3)
    lwz r4, 4(r4)
    la r5, CP_TYPE
    addi r3, r1, BUF
    bl 0x825c5470
flag_next:
    addi r3, r1, BUF
    bl 0x825c1290
    cmpwi r3, 0
    beq flags_done
    mr r27, r3
    lwz r5, TICK(r31)        # its record: the tick, the fields, the tick again (lwsync between: as the state record)
    stw r5, F_SEQ(r29)
    .long LWSYNC
    stw r27, F_ENTITY(r29)
    lwz r5, 0x80(r27)        # owner team
    stw r5, F_OWNER(r29)
    lwz r5, 0xa0(r27)        # control 0-100 (float)
    stw r5, F_CONTROL(r29)
    lbz r5, 0xad(r27)        # enabled
    stw r5, F_ENABLED(r29)
    lwz r5, 0x14(r27)        # its data's capture radius (+0x114, float); without data r5 is 0 and so is the radius
    cmpwi r5, 0              # (before 2026-10-30 the record kept an earlier tick's radius)
    beq flag_radius
    lwz r5, 0x114(r5)
flag_radius:
    stw r5, F_RADIUS(r29)
    mr r3, r27              # its position, as the game's capture scan reads it (82361f14)
    bl 0x822a7bb0
    lwz r5, 0x30(r3)
    stw r5, F_X(r29)
    lwz r5, 0x34(r3)
    stw r5, F_Y(r29)
    lwz r5, 0x38(r3)
    stw r5, F_Z(r29)
    lwz r5, TICK(r31)
    .long LWSYNC
    stw r5, F_SEQ_END(r29)
    addi r29, r29, FLAG_SIZE
    addi r28, r28, 1
    cmpwi r28, MAX_FLAGS
    blt flag_next
flags_done:
    lwz r3, MBOX(r31)        # the flag count, then the tick: this tick's records are all written
    .long LWSYNC
    stw r28, H_FLAGS(r3)
    .long LWSYNC             # the count before the tick (not a locked pair: readers go by each record's own ticks)
    lwz r5, TICK(r31)
    stw r5, H_TICK(r3)
    b out
forget_held:                 # lifecycle made -> held: the host left, its bots still in the match: forget them and
    li r3, 1                 # hold (make nothing more) until the list empties or the manager changes (before
    b forget_hold            # 2026-10-30 the next tick made a new set with a bot as the host, beside the old one)
forget:                      # lifecycle -> none: clear the state, mailbox, key, hold and slots, remember this
    li r3, 0                 # manager (0 when there is none)
forget_hold:
    stw r3, HOLD(r31)        # the lifecycle's HOLD word, then its STATE word below
    li r3, 0
    stw r3, MBOX_MAGIC(r31)
    stw r3, MBOX(r31)
    stw r3, STATE(r31)
    stw r3, HOST_PLAYER(r31)
    stw r30, MANAGER(r31)
    la r28, SLOTS_ADDR
    li r29, MAX_BOTS
clear:
    stw r3, 0(r28)
    addi r28, r28, 4
    addi r29, r29, -1
    cmpwi r29, 0
    bne clear
out:
    addi r1, r1, FRAME
    lwz r12, -8(r1)
    mtlr r12
    ld r22, -0x58(r1)
    ld r23, -0x50(r1)
    ld r24, -0x48(r1)
    ld r25, -0x40(r1)
    ld r26, -0x38(r1)
    ld r27, -0x30(r1)
    ld r28, -0x28(r1)
    ld r29, -0x20(r1)
    ld r30, -0x18(r1)
    ld r31, -0x10(r1)
    blr
FMT_HOST:
    .string "rs-bots: host player %08x team %d"
FMT_CREATED:
    .string "rs-bots: bot %08x team %d kit %08x"
FMT_HOST_POSITION:
    .string "rs-bots: host %08x soldier position %08x %08x %08x"
FMT_POSITION:
    .string "rs-bots: bot %08x soldier position %08x %08x %08x limit %08x throttle %08x dt %08x"
FMT_SPAWNED:
    .string "rs-bots: spawned %08x team %d at spawn id %08x soldier %08x"
FMT_MAILBOX:
    .string "rs-bots: host mailbox v2 at %08x"
'''


type Side = int                         # FRIENDLY or ENEMY
type Bot = tuple[Side, str]             # (side, class: a KITS key)
type PatchWord = tuple[int, int, str]   # (guest address, big-endian word, comment)
type WordReader = Callable[[int], int]  # a record's word at an offset


def lifecycle(state: int, hold: int) -> str:
    """The bots' lifecycle from the data area's STATE and HOLD words: one named state per game session. The code keeps
    it in the two words and reads and writes them separately (forget_hold writes HOLD and then STATE; make reads HOLD,
    then writes STATE 1); each path that sets one clears the other, so (1, 1) never occurs: 'invalid (state, hold)'.

        state   STATE HOLD  meaning
        none      0    0    no bots this match: they are made once the first player (the host) has a soldier
        made      1    0    bots made for this match (its MANAGER and HOST_PLAYER recorded); stepped every tick
        held      0    1    the host left a match its bots are still in: nothing is made until the player list
                            empties or the manager changes

        from   to     path (label in CODE_SOURCE)  when (LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS, in the order the code tests)
        any    none   forget                       no player manager; an empty player list; another manager
        made   made   respawn                      the recorded host first and a bot still in the list (or none made)
        made   none   forget                       none of the bots in the list (a new match at the old addresses,
                                                   the host's player the same or another)
        made   held   forget_held                  another first player while bots are still in the list (the host
                                                   left)
        none   made   make -> create               the host has a soldier and the block is allocated
        none   none   make -> out                  the host has no soldier yet, or no block was allocated
        held   held   make -> out                  still held

    Forgetting also clears the mailbox address and magic, the match key and every bot slot, and records the manager
    (0 when there is none). Before 2026-11-05 the two words had no shared name; navhost does not read them (they are
    outside the mailbox block), guestmem.py shows the name."""
    for name, words in LIFECYCLE_WORDS.items():
        if words == (state, hold):
            return name
    return f'invalid ({state}, {hold})'


def string_record(text: str, at: int) -> bytes:
    """A {begin, end, capacity end} string (end past the NUL, as the game's own strings) followed by its text."""
    raw = text.encode('ascii') + b'\0'
    raw += b'\0' * (-len(raw) % 4)
    chars = at + 12
    return struct.pack('>III', chars, chars + len(text) + 1, chars + len(text) + 1) + raw


def assembler_symbols(table: int = 0) -> dict[str, int]:
    """The names CODE_SOURCE uses: the data area's, the stack frame's and the mailbox's; BOTS is the table's address."""
    symbols = {
        # the data area
        'DATA': DATA, 'STATE': STATE, 'MANAGER': MANAGER, 'TICK': TICK, 'SLOTS_ADDR': DATA + SLOTS,
        'HANDLE': HANDLE, 'HANDLE_4': HANDLE + 4, 'HANDLE_8': HANDLE + 8, 'HANDLE_C': HANDLE + 12,
        # the stack frame and its input frame buffer
        'FRAME': FRAME, 'BUF': BUF, 'BUF_98': BUF + 0x98, 'BUF_80': BUF + 0x80, 'DT': DT,
        'BUF_THROTTLE': BUF + 8, 'BUF_BUTTONS_LO': BUF + 0x7C, 'BUF_STRAFE': BUF + 0x0C, 'BUF_BUTTONS_HI': BUF + 0x78,
        'BUF_YAW': BUF + 0x88, 'BUF_PITCH': BUF + 0x8C, 'BUF_84': BUF + 0x84,
        'MAX_BOTS': MAX_BOTS, 'FRIENDLY': FRIENDLY, 'BOTS': table,
        'TRIES': TRIES, 'LWSYNC': LWSYNC, 'HOST_PLAYER': HOST_PLAYER, 'HOLD': HOLD, 'ALLOC_SIZE': ALLOC_SIZE,
        # the guest-only copy of each bot's last whole command
        'G_STAMP': G_STAMP, 'G_THROTTLE': G_THROTTLE, 'G_STRAFE': G_STRAFE, 'G_YAW': G_YAW, 'G_PITCH': G_PITCH,
        'G_BUTTONS_HI': G_BUTTONS_HI, 'G_BUTTONS_LO': G_BUTTONS_LO,
    }
    symbols.update({name: globals()[name] for name in MAILBOX_NAMES})
    return symbols


def guest_command(word: WordReader, tick: int, last: list[int] | None = None) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
    """The bot code's command read, in Python, for the hosts' tests (tests/test_bots.py checks it against the code):
    word(offset) gives a word of the bot's record (C_SEQ, C_STAMP, ...). last is the bot's guest-only copy of its last
    whole command (a list of 7 words, updated in place; None: none yet, all zero, as in a new block): a whole read
    replaces it, and the copy is what is used. (stamp, throttle, strafe, yaw, pitch, buttons hi, buttons lo) as words,
    or None: a neutral frame (no fresh command)."""
    fields = (C_STAMP, C_THROTTLE, C_STRAFE, C_YAW, C_PITCH, C_BUTTONS_HI, C_BUTTONS_LO)
    copy = last if last is not None else [0] * len(fields)
    for _ in range(TRIES):
        seq = word(C_SEQ)
