`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_callgraph_export.py`:

```py
r"""XEX tools: call graph and string export on a made-up image

export_callgraph_strings.py's main() on a made-up research workspace (no game data; nothing read from or written to
operation-rising-sun): a 16 KB stand-in image with .rdata (strings in each encoding, a function pointer table, a
vtable), .text (functions written instruction by instruction to reach each kind of call edge, each tracked and
untracked instruction class, a merge, an unreached block, two code gaps found through a call and a data word), .data
(pointer cells) and an import table, plus a made-up Ghidra call reference table. The module's pinned image hash is
replaced by the made-up one for the test and restored afterwards. Checked: the edge kinds, the inferred functions, the
strings and their references, the vtable candidate, the cross-check, the tables and the evidence it writes.
"""
import contextlib
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import struct
import sys

import export_callgraph_strings as E

BASE = 0x82000000
SIZE = 0x4000
F_A, F_B, F_C, THUNK, HELPER = 0x82001000, 0x82001800, 0x82001840, 0x82001880, 0x82001900
GAP1, GAP2, F_D, F_E = 0x82001A00, 0x82001B00, 0x82001C00, 0x82001D00
CTR, LR, XER = 9, 8, 1


class Asm:
    def __init__(self, start):
        self.start, self.words = start, []

    @property
    def pc(self):
        return self.start + 4 * len(self.words)

    def w(self, *words):
        self.words += words

    def d(self, op, rt, ra, imm):
        self.w(op << 26 | rt << 21 | ra << 16 | (imm & 0xFFFF))

    def x(self, xo, rs, ra, rb):
        self.w(31 << 26 | rs << 21 | ra << 16 | rb << 11 | xo << 1)

    def mtspr(self, spr, rs):
        self.x(467, rs, spr & 31, spr >> 5)

    def mfspr(self, rt, spr):
        self.x(339, rt, spr & 31, spr >> 5)

    def li32(self, r, value):
        self.d(15, r, 0, value >> 16)
        self.d(14, r, r, value & 0xFFFF)

    def b(self, target, link=0):
        self.w(18 << 26 | ((target - self.pc) & 0x3FFFFFC) | link)

    def bc(self, bo, target, link=0):
        self.w(16 << 26 | bo << 21 | ((target - self.pc) & 0xFFFC) | link)

    def bclr(self, bo, link):
        self.w(19 << 26 | bo << 21 | 16 << 1 | link)

    def bcctr(self, bo, link):
        self.w(19 << 26 | bo << 21 | 528 << 1 | link)


def function_a():
    a = Asm(F_A)
    a.d(15, 3, 0, 0x8200)                  # lis r3
    a.d(14, 3, 3, 0x100)                   # addi: 'hello world'
    a.d(14, 4, 3, 2)                       # its interior
    a.d(24, 3, 5, 0x80)                    # ori: the short string 'ab'
    a.d(25, 3, 6, 0)                       # oris
    a.d(24, 30, 7, 0)                      # ori of a symbol, 0: a copy
    a.d(24, 30, 7, 1)                      # ori of a symbol: unknown
    a.d(15, 20, 0, 0x8200)                 # lis r20 (kept over calls)
    a.d(32, 8, 20, 0x300)                   # read-only word: F_B
    a.mtspr(CTR, 8)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # indirect_resolved
    a.d(32, 8, 20, 0x304)                   # THUNK
    a.mtspr(CTR, 8)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # import_call
    a.d(32, 8, 20, 0x308)                   # inside F_A, not a start
    a.mtspr(CTR, 8)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # indirect_resolved_nonentry
    a.d(14, 10, 20, 0x310)                  # the vtable
    a.d(36, 10, 31, 0)                     # stw r10, 0(r31): a vtable store
    a.d(32, 11, 31, 0)                     # remembered
    a.d(32, 12, 11, 4)                     # its second slot: F_C
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)
    a.w(*[32 << 26 | 11 << 21 | 30 << 16, 32 << 26 | 12 << 21 | 11 << 16 | 8])        # [[r30] + 8]
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # virtual
    a.d(32, 12, 29, 0x10)
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # [x + 0x10]
    a.d(32, 11, 28, 4)
    a.d(32, 12, 11, 8)
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # [[x + 4] + 8]
    a.mtspr(CTR, 27)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)                         # an incoming register: unknown
    a.li32(12, F_B)
    a.mtspr(LR, 12)
    a.bclr(20, 1)                          # blrl to F_B
    a.mfspr(0, LR)
    a.mfspr(3, CTR)
    a.mfspr(4, XER)
    a.bclr(12, 1)                          # conditional blrl (LR = the return address: inside F_A)
    a.bcctr(12, 1)                         # conditional bcctrl
    for target in (F_B, THUNK, HELPER + 4, F_A + 8, GAP1, 0x82003900):
        a.b(target, 1)
    a.bc(20, F_C, 1)                       # bcl always: a call
    a.bc(12, F_C, 1)                       # conditional call
    a.bc(12, F_C)                          # conditional tail call
    a.bc(12, THUNK)                        # conditional import tail call
    a.bc(12, HELPER + 4)                   # conditional helper tail call
    a.d(34, 3, 20, 0x100)                   # lbz
    a.d(33, 3, 31, 4)                      # lwzu
    a.d(35, 3, 31, 1)                      # lbzu
    a.d(37, 3, 1, -16)                     # stwu
    a.d(38, 3, 20, 0x3010)                  # stb to .data
    a.d(36, 20, 20, 0x3014)                  # stw a constant to .data
    a.d(32, 9, 20, 0x3014)                  # ... and read it back
    a.d(32, 9, 20, 0x3018)                  # writable: unknown
    a.d(32, 9, 20, 0x400)                   # an import slot: not folded
    a.d(32, 9, 20, 0x3800)                  # BINKBSS: not folded
    a.d(32, 9, 20, 0x7000)                  # past the image
    a.d(46, 29, 1, 0)                      # lmw
    a.d(47, 29, 1, 0)                      # stmw
    a.d(48, 1, 20, 0x100)                   # lfs
    a.d(49, 1, 31, 8)                      # lfsu
    a.d(52, 1, 31, 8)                      # stfs
    a.d(55, 1, 31, 8)                      # stfdu
    a.w(58 << 26 | 3 << 21 | 20 << 16 | 0x100)          # ld
    a.w(58 << 26 | 3 << 21 | 31 << 16 | 8 | 1)         # ldu
    a.w(62 << 26 | 3 << 21 | 31 << 16 | 8)             # std
    a.w(62 << 26 | 3 << 21 | 1 << 16 | (-32 & 0xFFFC) | 1)     # stdu
    for xo, rs, ra, rb in ((444, 3, 4, 3), (28, 3, 4, 5), (826, 3, 4, 5), (151, 3, 31, 4), (183, 3, 31, 4),
                           (0, 0, 3, 4), (55, 3, 31, 4), (23, 3, 31, 4), (266, 3, 4, 5), (19, 3, 0, 0), (1000, 3, 4, 5)):
        a.x(xo, rs, ra, rb)
    a.d(12, 3, 4, 1)                       # addic
    a.d(21, 4, 3, 0)                       # rlwinm
    a.d(30, 4, 3, 0)                       # rldicl
    a.w(0x100001C3 | 1 << 21 | 31 << 16 | 4 << 11)    # stvx128
    a.d(10, 0, 3, 0)                       # cmpli
    a.d(32, 3, 26, 0)
    for _ in range(5):
        a.d(32, 3, 3, 0)                   # nested loads past the cap
    a.mtspr(CTR, 3)
    a.bcctr(20, 1)
    a.bc(12, a.pc + 8)                     # inside, forward
    a.b(a.pc + 8)                          # inside, over one word
    a.w(0x60000000)                        # unreached (nop)
    a.d(14, 3, 0, 1)
    a.bc(20, F_E)                          # always, outside: tail call
    return a.words


def function_b():
    a = Asm(F_B)
    a.li32(12, F_C)
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 0)                         # resolved tail call
    return a.words


def function_c():
    a = Asm(F_C)
    a.li32(12, THUNK)
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 0)                         # import tail call
    return a.words


def function_d():
    a = Asm(F_D)
    a.li32(12, F_D + 0x10)
    a.mtspr(CTR, 12)
    a.bcctr(20, 0)                         # a branch inside: no edge
    a.mtspr(CTR, 27)                       # F_D + 0x10, reached through CTR only: seeded unreached
    a.bcctr(20, 0)                         # unresolved branch
    a.b(F_A)                               # never reached either
    return a.words


def function_e():
    a = Asm(F_E)
    top = a.pc
    a.bc(12, a.pc + 12)                    # to the merge
    a.d(14, 3, 0, 1)
    a.d(36, 3, 31, 0)                      # a remembered slot on one path only
    a.d(14, 4, 0, 0)                       # merge
    a.bc(12, top)                          # a loop back
    a.bclr(20, 0)                          # blr
    return a.words


def made_up_image():
    d = bytearray(SIZE)
    d[0x100:0x10C] = b'hello world\0'
    d[0x120:0x12F] = 'café au lait\0'.encode('utf-8')
    d[0x140:0x14A] = b'\xff\xfeABCDEFG\0'
    d[0x160:0x16C] = 'Words'.encode('utf-16-be') + b'\0\0'
    d[0x180:0x183] = b'ab\0'
    struct.pack_into('>4I', d, 0x300, F_B, THUNK, F_A + 4, 0)
    struct.pack_into('>3I', d, 0x310, F_B, F_C, 0)     # a vtable of two functions
    struct.pack_into('>I', d, 0x400, 0x12345678)       # an import slot
    struct.pack_into('>4I', d, 0x3000, 0x82000100, F_B, GAP2, 0)
    for start, words in ((F_A, function_a()), (F_B, function_b()), (F_C, function_c()), (F_D, function_d()),
                         (F_E, function_e()), (THUNK, [0x3D600000, 0x816B0000, 0x7D6903A6, 0x4E800420]),
                         (HELPER, [0xF9C1FF68, 0xF9E1FF70, 0x4E800020]),
                         (GAP1, [0x38600001, 18 << 26 | ((F_B - (GAP1 + 4)) & 0x3FFFFFC) | 1, 0x4E800020]),
                         (GAP2, [0x38600002, 0x4E800020])):
        struct.pack_into(f'>{len(words)}I', d, start - BASE, *words)
    return bytes(d), len(function_a())


def tsv(path, header, rows):
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        f.write('\t'.join(header) + '\n' + ''.join('\t'.join(r) + '\n' for r in rows))


@contextlib.contextmanager
def workspace(tmp):
    data, words_a = made_up_image()
    work = tmp / 'work/xex-analysis'
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp / 'research/evidence').mkdir(parents=True)
    (work / 'default.checked.memory.bin').write_bytes(data)
    tsv(work / 'sections.tsv', ['name', 'start', 'size', 'read', 'write', 'execute'],
        [['.rdata', '82000000', str(0x1000), '1', '0', '0'], ['.text', '82001000', str(0x2000), '1', '0', '1'],
         ['.data', '82003000', str(0x800), '1', '1', '0'], ['BINKBSS', '82003800', str(0x100), '1', '0', '0']])
    tsv(work / 'imports.tsv', ['slot', 'thunk', 'library', 'name'],
        [['82000400', f'{THUNK:08x}', 'xboxkrnl.exe', 'NtClose'], ['82000404', '', 'xam.xex', 'XamData']])
    ends = {F_A: F_A + 4 * words_a, F_B: F_B + 16, F_C: F_C + 16, F_D: F_D + 28, F_E: F_E + 24, HELPER: HELPER + 12}
    tsv(work / 'functions.tsv', ['start', 'end', 'prolog_bytes', 'exception_flag'],
        [[f'{s:08x}', f'{e:08x}', '0', '0'] for s, e in ends.items()])
    tsv(work / 'helper-entries.tsv', ['address', 'name'], [[f'{HELPER:08x}', '__savegprlr_14'],
                                                          [f'{HELPER + 4:08x}', '__savegprlr_15']])
    tsv(work / 'decompiled-index.tsv', ['address', 'name', 'file'],
        [[f'{F_A:08x}', 'big_function', 'big_function.c'], [f'{HELPER:08x}', '__savegprlr_14', '']])
    saved = (os.environ.get('BF1943_RESEARCH'), E.IMAGE_SHA256, sys.argv)
    os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = str(tmp)
    E.IMAGE_SHA256 = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            yield work
    finally:
        if saved[0] is None:
            os.environ.pop('BF1943_RESEARCH', None)
        else:
            os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = saved[0]
        E.IMAGE_SHA256, sys.argv = saved[1:]


def read(path):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f, delimiter='\t'))


def test_export(tmp_path):

def test_helpers():

    assert E.spr_field(31 << 26 | 3 << 21 | 9 << 16 | 467 << 1) == 9 and E.spr_field(0x7C0802A6) == 8

    assert not E.outside_every_function('direct_call', 'outside every function')
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_callgraph_memory.py`:

```py
"""export_callgraph_strings.py's remembered stores: a slot overwritten by a float store, dcbz or a VMX128 store is not
folded into a later load (no game data: a made-up function on a stand-in image).

  python -B test_callgraph_memory.py

Each case: r4 = a function's address, stw r4 to 0x10(r3), then the overwriting store, lwz r5 from 0x10(r3), mtctr r5,
bctrl. With the store remembered past the overwrite the call is "resolved" to that function; it must stay unresolved.
A control case (an unrelated slot overwritten) keeps the call resolved.
"""
import os
import sys
import tempfile

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
failures = []
F1, F2 = 0x82100000, 0x82200000


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def function(overwrite):
    return [15 << 26 | 4 << 21 | F2 >> 16,                     # lis  r4, F2 >> 16
            14 << 26 | 4 << 21 | 4 << 16,                      # addi r4, r4, 0
            36 << 26 | 4 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 0x10,               # stw  r4, 0x10(r3)
            overwrite,
            32 << 26 | 5 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 0x10,               # lwz  r5, 0x10(r3)
            31 << 26 | 5 << 21 | 9 << 16 | 467 << 1,           # mtctr r5
            0x4E800421, 0x4E800020]                            # bctrl, blr


def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:          # the module asks for a workspace; nothing is read from it
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'work'))
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'research'))
        os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = root
        import export_callgraph_strings as E
    cases = [('stfs f1, 0x10(r3)', 52 << 26 | 1 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 0x10, False),
             ('stfd f1, 0x0c(r3) (8 bytes over the slot)', 54 << 26 | 1 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 0x0C, False),
             ('dcbz r3, r6', 31 << 26 | 3 << 16 | 6 << 11 | 1014 << 1, False),
             ('stvx128 v1, r3, r6', 0x100001C3 | 1 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 6 << 11, False),
             ('stvlx128 v1, r3, r6', 0x10000503 | 1 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 6 << 11, False),
             ('stfs f1, 0x20(r3) (another slot)', 52 << 26 | 1 << 21 | 3 << 16 | 0x20, True)]
    for what, word, resolved in cases:
        code = function(word)

        class Image:
            end = 0x83000000
            import_thunks, import_slots = {}, {}

            def word(self, a):
                return code[(a - F1) // 4] if F1 <= a < F1 + 4 * len(code) else 0x4E800020

            def section(self, a):
                return dict(name='.text', write=False)

            def readonly(self, a):
                return False
        an = E.Analysis(Image(),  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]  # a made-up image with the methods it uses
                        [E.Function(F1, F1 + 4 * len(code), 'f1'), E.Function(F2, F2 + 4, 'f2')], {})
        an.run_function(an.starts[F1])
        kinds = [(kind, callee) for _, _, callee, kind, _ in an.edges]
        got = ('indirect_resolved', F2) in kinds
        check(got == resolved, f'{what}: the call through the reloaded slot is {"resolved" if got else "unresolved"}'
                               f' (expected {"resolved" if resolved else "unresolved"})')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_fuzz_xex.py`:

```py
r"""executable tools: XEX and image header readers fuzzed; map_imports runs on a made-up workspace

Mutation fuzzing (core/fuzzcheck.py) of the executable tools' readers of binary input, on made-up files (no game
data): verify_xex_image.security_info (the XEX2 security info and page descriptors), pe_layout (the decoded image's
PE headers), walk_relocations, and map_imports.parse (the XEX's optional headers and import directory, and the import
records in the image). On any input each returns or raises ValueError, within its time and memory limits. Then
map_imports.py, run as a script on a made-up research workspace, writes imports.tsv and its evidence (2026-10-31: it
always exited 1, naming its own path relative to the workspace). Fixed seeds; BF1943_FUZZ=long for more.
"""
import json
import os
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

import fuzzcheck
import map_imports
import verify_xex_image

TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE = 0x82000000
# (address, kind, library, ordinal): kind 0 an import slot, 1 the thunk of the slot before it
RECORDS = [[(BASE + 0x100, 0, 0, 5), (BASE + 0x200, 1, 0, 5), (BASE + 0x104, 0, 0, 9)],
           [(BASE + 0x110, 0, 1, 7), (BASE + 0x220, 1, 1, 7)]]
JAVA = ('public static ArrayList<Replacer> xam_replacer = new ArrayList<Replacer>() {{\n'
        '    new Replacer(0x5, "XamFive"), new Replacer(0x9, "XamNine")\n    };\n'
        'public static ArrayList<Replacer> xboxkrnl_replacer = new ArrayList<Replacer>() {{\n'
        '    new Replacer(0x7, "KeSeven")\n    };\n')


def xex_and_image():
    """(xex, image): an XEX2 with two optional headers (image base, import directory) and an import directory of two
    libraries; the image holds the records' words and 16-byte thunks."""
    image = bytearray(0x400)
    for lib in RECORDS:
        for address, kind, index, ordinal in lib:
            struct.pack_into('>I', image, address - BASE, kind << 24 | index << 16 | ordinal)
    strings = b'xam.xex\0xboxkrnl.exe\0\0\0'
    libs = b''
    for k, lib in enumerate(RECORDS):
        libs += struct.pack('>I', 40 + 4 * len(lib)) + bytes(32) + struct.pack('>HH', k, len(lib))
        libs += b''.join(struct.pack('>I', a) for a, _, _, _ in lib)
    start = 24 + 16
    directory = struct.pack('>III', 12 + len(strings) + len(libs), len(strings), len(RECORDS)) + strings + libs
    pe_offset = start + len(directory)
    head = b'XEX2' + struct.pack('>5I', 0, pe_offset, 0, 0, 2) + struct.pack('>4I', 0x10201, BASE, 0x103FF, start)
    return head + directory, bytes(image)


def security_xex(descriptors=3):
    """An XEX2 whose security info (at 0x100) has the two sizes, a 256-byte signature, the image info and digest, and
    `descriptors` page descriptors."""
    sec = 0x100
    out = bytearray(sec + 0x184 + 24 * descriptors)
    out[0:4] = b'XEX2'
    struct.pack_into('>5I', out, 4, 0, 0x2000, 0, sec, 0)
    struct.pack_into('>II', out, sec, 0x1000, descriptors * 0x10000)
    struct.pack_into('>III', out, sec + 8 + 256, 0x174, 0, BASE)
    struct.pack_into('>I', out, sec + 0x180, descriptors)
    for k in range(descriptors):
        struct.pack_into('>I', out, sec + 0x184 + 24 * k, 1 << 4 | 1)
    return bytes(out)


def pe_image(sections=('.text', '.data', '.reloc')):
    """A PE header block: e_lfanew 0x80, the file and optional headers, 16 data directories, the section headers, then
    one relocation block of two entries and an empty one."""
    out = bytearray(0x400)
    pe, optional_size = 0x80, 0xE0
    struct.pack_into('<I', out, 60, pe)
    out[pe:pe + 4] = b'PE\0\0'
    struct.pack_into('<HH', out, pe + 4, 0x1F2, len(sections))
    struct.pack_into('<H', out, pe + 20, optional_size)
    opt = pe + 24
    struct.pack_into('<I', out, opt + 28, BASE)
    struct.pack_into('<II', out, opt + 56, 0x30000, 0x1000)
    struct.pack_into('<I', out, opt + 92, 16)
    for k, name in enumerate(sections):
        struct.pack_into('<8sIIII', out, opt + optional_size + 40 * k, name.encode('ascii'), 0x1000, 0x1000 * (k + 1),
                         0x1000, 0x1000 * (k + 1))
    struct.pack_into('<II4H', out, 0x300, 0x1000, 16, 1, 2, 3, 4)
    return bytes(out)


def test_security_info():
    seed = security_xex()
    fields = [(8, '>I'), (16, '>I'), (0x100, '>I'), (0x104, '>I'), (0x100 + 0x180, '>I')]
    report = fuzzcheck.run('verify_xex_image.security_info', verify_xex_image.security_info, [seed], iterations=1500,
                           fields=[fields], boundaries=[[4, 24, 0x100, 0x108, 0x208, 0x220, 0x280, 0x284, len(seed) - 24]])
    assert report.ok, report.text()


def test_pe_layout():
    seed = pe_image()
    fields = [(60, '<I'), (0x86, '<H'), (0x94, '<H'), (0x98 + 92, '<I')]
    # the PE headers are read from the start of the image: what follows them (sections' bytes) is not read
    report = fuzzcheck.run('verify_xex_image.pe_layout', verify_xex_image.pe_layout, [seed], iterations=1500,
                           fields=[fields], prefix_ok=True)
    assert report.ok, report.text()
    report = fuzzcheck.run('verify_xex_image.walk_relocations', verify_xex_image.walk_relocations, [seed[0x300:]],
                           iterations=800, fields=[[(4, '<I'), (20, '<I')]], prefix_ok=True)
    assert report.ok, report.text()


def test_map_imports_parse():
    xex, image = xex_and_image()
    tables = map_imports.names_from_java(JAVA)
    out = map_imports.parse(xex, image, tables)
    assert [i['name'] for i in out['imports']] == ['XamFive', 'XamNine', 'KeSeven'], out['imports']
    fields = [(8, '>I'), (20, '>I'), (24, '>I'), (28, '>I'), (32, '>I'), (36, '>I'), (40, '>I'), (44, '>I'), (48, '>I')]
    report = fuzzcheck.run('map_imports.parse (xex)', lambda d: map_imports.parse(d, image, tables), [xex],
                           iterations=1500, fields=[fields], prefix_ok=True)
    assert report.ok, report.text()
    report = fuzzcheck.run('map_imports.parse (image)', lambda d: map_imports.parse(xex, d, tables), [image],
                           iterations=800, fields=[[(0x100, '>I'), (0x104, '>I'), (0x110, '>I'), (0x200, '>I')]],
                           prefix_ok=True)
    assert report.ok, report.text()


def test_map_imports_script(tmp_path):
    """The script on a made-up workspace: exit 0, imports.tsv with one row per import, its own path in the suite."""
    root = tmp_path / 'workspace'
    xex, image = xex_and_image()
    loader = root / map_imports.LOADER
    for folder in (root / 'work' / 'extracted', root / 'work' / 'xex-analysis', root / 'research' / 'evidence', loader):
        folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / 'work' / 'extracted' / 'default.xex').write_bytes(xex)
    (root / 'work' / 'xex-analysis' / 'default.checked.memory.bin').write_bytes(image)
    (loader / 'ImportRenamer.java').write_bytes(JAVA.encode('ascii'))
    (loader / 'XEXHeader.java').write_bytes(b'// made up\n')
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', os.path.join(TOOLS, 'map_imports.py')], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       cwd=str(root), env=dict(os.environ, BF1943_RESEARCH=str(root)))
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr
    tsv = (root / 'work' / 'xex-analysis' / 'imports.tsv').read_bytes()
    assert tsv == (b'library\tordinal\tname\tslot\tthunk\n'
                   b'xam.xex\t5\tXamFive\t0x82000100\t0x82000200\n'
                   b'xam.xex\t9\tXamNine\t0x82000104\t\n'
                   b'xboxkrnl.exe\t7\tKeSeven\t0x82000110\t0x82000220\n'), tsv
    evidence = json.loads((root / 'research' / 'evidence' / 'xex-imports.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    assert evidence['provenance']['parser']['path'] == 'bf1943-xex-tools/map_imports.py', evidence['provenance']
    assert [i['path'] for i in evidence['provenance']['inputs']] == ['work/extracted/default.xex',
                                                                    'work/xex-analysis/default.checked.memory.bin']


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ regressions

def test_regression_headers():
    """security_info and pe_layout on cut or damaged headers raised struct.error (and a file that is no XEX2 a
    SystemExit); map_imports.parse on an XEX without the image base or import directory header raised KeyError."""
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(verify_xex_image.security_info, b'XEX2')
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(verify_xex_image.security_info, b'XEX1' + bytes(20))
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(verify_xex_image.security_info, security_xex()[:-24])
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(verify_xex_image.pe_layout, bytes(10))
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(verify_xex_image.pe_layout, pe_image()[:0x1A0])        # inside the section headers
    xex, image = xex_and_image()
    no_base = bytearray(xex)
    struct.pack_into('>I', no_base, 24, 0x10202)
    assert fuzzcheck.refused(lambda d: map_imports.parse(d, image, map_imports.names_from_java(JAVA)), bytes(no_base))
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_map_imports_real.py`:

```py
r"""executable tools: map_imports.py rewrites the research workspace's imports.tsv byte for byte

map_imports.py on a scratch copy of the research workspace's inputs (BF1943_RESEARCH, else operation-rising-sun next
to the suite; nothing is written there): the extracted XEX, the checked image and XEXLoaderWV's two reference files.
It exits 0, its imports.tsv is byte-identical to the workspace's recorded work/xex-analysis/imports.tsv, and its
evidence differs from the recorded research/evidence/xex-imports.json only in the parser it names (its path in the
suite, not the research workspace's src/xexresearch/map_imports.py of 2026-10-16) and in its line endings (the
recorded file has CRLF). Skips without a workspace.
"""
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

TIER = 'bf1943'
TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SUITE = os.path.dirname(TOOLS)
SOURCE = os.environ.get('BF1943_RESEARCH') or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(SUITE), 'operation-rising-sun')
LOADER = 'work/tools/XEXLoaderWV/XEXLoaderWV/src/main/java/xexloaderwv'
INPUTS = ['work/extracted/default.xex', 'work/xex-analysis/default.checked.memory.bin',
          f'{LOADER}/ImportRenamer.java', f'{LOADER}/XEXHeader.java']
RECORDED = ['work/xex-analysis/imports.tsv', 'research/evidence/xex-imports.json']


def test_imports_tsv_as_recorded(tmp_path):
    if not all(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SOURCE, f)) for f in INPUTS + RECORDED):
        raise unittest.SkipTest(f'no research workspace with the XEX inputs at {SOURCE}')
    root = tmp_path / 'workspace'
    (root / 'research' / 'evidence').mkdir(parents=True)
    for f in INPUTS:
        (root / f).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(SOURCE, f), root / f)
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', os.path.join(TOOLS, 'map_imports.py')], capture_output=True, text=True,
                       cwd=str(root), env=dict(os.environ, BF1943_RESEARCH=str(root)))
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr
    with open(os.path.join(SOURCE, RECORDED[0]), 'rb') as f:
        assert (root / RECORDED[0]).read_bytes() == f.read(), 'imports.tsv differs from the recorded one'
    with open(os.path.join(SOURCE, RECORDED[1]), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        recorded = json.load(f)
    written = json.loads((root / RECORDED[1]).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    assert written['provenance'].pop('parser')['path'] == 'bf1943-xex-tools/map_imports.py'
    recorded['provenance'].pop('parser')
    assert written == recorded, 'the evidence differs from the recorded one beyond the parser it names'
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_map_project.py`:

```py
"""map_project.ps1 judges Ghidra's post-script by its result, not only by java's exit code (no Ghidra: a stand-in java).

  python -B test_map_project.py

Ghidra's headless analyzer exits 0 when a post-script throws, and ValidateXex.java writes saved-validation.txt only on
a pass. Run against a scratch workspace with BF1943_JAVA naming a stand-in that exits 0 and does what each case says:
- writes nothing (the script threw): the step fails, and an old PASS left from an earlier run is gone;
- writes PASS (and a warning on stderr): the step passes;
- exits 1: the step fails;
- -Script ApplyHelpers.java: a helper-application.txt cut short (no closing "function count=" line) fails, a whole one
  passes;
- -Script DumpCode.java (a script whose result cannot be confirmed): refused before java runs (before 2026-10-31 any
  such script's failure passed as success).
Windows only (PowerShell); skips elsewhere.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
failures = []
FAKE = r'''import os, sys
args = sys.argv[1:]
mode = os.environ['FAKE_JAVA_MODE']
root = args[args.index('-postScript') + 2]
open(os.path.join(root, 'java-ran'), 'w').write(args[args.index('-postScript') + 1])
sys.stderr.write('WARNING: a JVM warning on stderr\n')

if mode == 'apply_whole':
    open(os.path.join(root, 'helper-application.txt'), 'w').write('__savegprlr_14 x\nsuffix entries=1\nfunction count=2\n')
sys.exit(1 if mode == 'exit1' else 0)

def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def main():
    if os.name != 'nt':
        print('skip map_project.ps1: Windows PowerShell only')
        return
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'xex-analysis'))
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'research'))
        fake = os.path.join(root, 'fake_java.py')
        open(fake, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(FAKE)
        cmd = os.path.join(root, 'java.cmd')

        saved = os.path.join(root, 'work', 'xex-analysis', 'saved-validation.txt')

            return subprocess.run(['powershell', '-NoProfile', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-File',
                                   os.path.join(TOOLS, 'map_project.ps1'), *(args or ['-ValidateOnly'])], env=env, cwd=root,

        ran = os.path.join(root, 'work', 'xex-analysis', 'java-ran')
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_output_bytes.py`:

```py
"""The xex-tools' outputs that evidence (or vmx_inputs.INPUTS) pins by hash are written byte for byte as recorded.

  python -B test_output_bytes.py

Runs map_functions.py, classify_vmx.py, inventory_vmx.py and resolve_helpers.py on a scratch copy of the research
workspace's inputs (BF1943_RESEARCH, else operation-rising-sun next to the suite; nothing is written there) and compares
each pinned output with the workspace's recorded file: a rerun must not change the bytes the evidence names (a
line-ending change alone would stale the VMX fingerprint and five evidence files). Skips without a workspace.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SUITE = os.path.dirname(TOOLS)
SOURCE = os.environ.get('BF1943_RESEARCH') or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(SUITE), 'operation-rising-sun')
failures = []
# (tool, [pinned outputs]): each output is compared with the workspace's copy
STEPS = [('map_functions.py', ['work/xex-analysis/functions.tsv', 'work/xex-analysis/sections.tsv']),
         ('classify_vmx.py', ['work/vmx128/classified.tsv']),
         ('inventory_vmx.py', ['work/vmx128/inventory.tsv']),
         ('resolve_helpers.py', ['work/xex-analysis/helpers.tsv', 'work/xex-analysis/helper-entries.tsv',
                                 'work/xex-analysis/helper-branches.tsv'])]   # not pinned by hash, but a rerun keeps it
# pinned evidence whose bytes also hold the tool's own hash: only its line endings are compared
LINE_ENDINGS = ['research/evidence/xex-functions.json', 'research/evidence/xex-helper-resolution.json']
INPUTS = ['work/xex-analysis/default.checked.memory.bin']
XENONRECOMP = ['XenonRecomp-main/thirdparty/disasm/ppc-dis.c', 'XenonRecomp-main/XenonRecomp/recompiler.cpp',
               'XenonRecomp-main/XenonUtils/ppc_context.h', 'XenonRecomp-main/XenonUtils/xbox.h', 'XenonRecomp-main/README.md']


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def sha(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        return hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()


def endings(path):
    data = open(path, 'rb').read()
    crlf = data.count(b'\r\n')
    return 'crlf' if crlf and crlf == data.count(b'\n') else 'lf' if not crlf else 'mixed'


def main():
    needed = INPUTS + [o for _, outs in STEPS for o in outs] + LINE_ENDINGS
    if not all(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SOURCE, p)) for p in needed):
        print(f'skip pinned output bytes: no research workspace with the recorded outputs at {SOURCE}')
        return
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
        for d in ('work/xex-analysis', 'work/vmx128', 'research/evidence'):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, d))
        for p in INPUTS:
            shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(SOURCE, p), os.path.join(root, p))
        for m in XENONRECOMP:
            src = os.path.join(SOURCE, 'Tools', 'XenonRecomp', m)
            if os.path.isfile(src):
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(root, 'Tools', 'XenonRecomp', m)), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(src, os.path.join(root, 'Tools', 'XenonRecomp', m))
        env = dict(os.environ, BF1943_RESEARCH=root)
        for tool, outs in STEPS:
            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', os.path.join(TOOLS, tool)], cwd=root, env=env, capture_output=True,
                               text=True)
            check(r.returncode == 0, f'{tool} runs on the scratch workspace' + ('' if r.returncode == 0 else ': ' + r.stderr[-300:]))
            if r.returncode:
                return
            for o in outs:
                check(sha(os.path.join(root, o)) == sha(os.path.join(SOURCE, o)),
                      f'{tool}: {o} is byte-identical to the recorded file (its hash is pinned)')
        for o in LINE_ENDINGS:
            check(endings(os.path.join(root, o)) == endings(os.path.join(SOURCE, o)),
                  f'{o}: written with the recorded line endings ({endings(os.path.join(SOURCE, o))})')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_record_vmx.py`:

```py
"""record_vmx_validation.py on a scratch workspace: what the INPUTS fingerprint does not cover is checked and recorded.

  python -B test_record_vmx.py

Needs the checked image (the recorder checks its hash): BF1943_RESEARCH, else operation-rising-sun next to the suite;
only the image is copied from there, into a temporary folder, and nothing is written to the workspace. Every other
input is made up: the results are stamped with the scratch inputs' fingerprint as run_vmx.ps1 stamps them. Checked:
a whole run is recorded with its `environment` (every language-module file's hash, Ghidra, Java, the tested program);
Ghidra and Java are run_vmx.ps1's pinned installs even with BF1943_GHIDRA / BF1943_JAVA set (run_vmx.ps1 ignores them);
a module file that differs from the last record is refused even when its mtime is older than the run (a copy keeping
its mtime), and accepted with --module-changed; a module file changed after the run is refused; caller probes whose
program memory is not the image are refused.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SOURCE = os.environ.get('BF1943_RESEARCH') or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(TOOLS)), 'operation-rising-sun')
IMAGE = 'work/xex-analysis/default.checked.memory.bin'
IMAGE_SHA256 = 'cbb152d10bee2e9c0ed28732a1328791b5510672a83786a5daf67f7b5abff27a'
failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def write(root, rel, text):
    path = os.path.join(root, rel)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        f.write(text)


def main():
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SOURCE, IMAGE)):
        print(f'skip VMX recorder: no checked image at {os.path.join(SOURCE, IMAGE)}')
        sys.exit(0)                                 # the skip line last: the runner shows SKIP
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'research', 'evidence'))
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'xex-analysis'))
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(SOURCE, IMAGE), os.path.join(root, IMAGE))
        os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = root
        import vmx_inputs
        module = 'work/vmx128/XenonVMX128/data/languages/'
        for rel in vmx_inputs.INPUTS + [module + 'ppc_64.pspec', module + 'ppc_64_32.cspec', module + 'xenon.ldefs',
                                        'work/vmx128/decode-coverage.tsv', 'work/vmx128/unclassified-decode.tsv',
                                        'work/tools/xenia-95a5c3ee/ppc_emit_altivec.cc', 'work/tools/xenia-95a5c3ee/ppc_instr.h']:
            if not rel.startswith('bf1943-xex-tools/') and rel != IMAGE:
                write(root, rel, f'made up: {rel}\n')
        write(root, 'research/evidence/vmx128-language-inputs.json', json.dumps(dict(
            validated=[], opaque=[], modelled_vmx128=[], modelled_altivec=[], scalar_fp_overrides=[], semantics_version='x',
            still_opaque_reasons={}, removed_inherited=[], reference_archive_sha256='a', reference_member='m',
            reference_member_sha256='b')))
        time.sleep(0.05)
        stamp = vmx_inputs.fingerprint(root)

        def results(program_image=IMAGE_SHA256):
            for name in vmx_inputs.SUITES:
                write(root, f'work/vmx128/{name}', f'PASS COMPLETE made up\nINPUTS {stamp}\n')
            for name in vmx_inputs.PROBES:
                write(root, f'work/vmx128/{name}', f'decoded=1 unknown_words=0 vor128=0 decompile_completed=true diagnostic=\n'
                                                   f'image_sha256={program_image}\nINPUTS {stamp}\n')

        def record(*args):
            # BF1943_GHIDRA / BF1943_JAVA name other installs (map_project.ps1's stand-ins): run_vmx.ps1 ignores them,
            # and so must the record
            return subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', os.path.join(TOOLS, 'record_vmx_validation.py'), *args], cwd=root,
                                  env=dict(os.environ, BF1943_RESEARCH=root, BF1943_GHIDRA=os.path.join(root, 'other ghidra'),
                                           BF1943_JAVA=os.path.join(root, 'other java.exe')),
                                  capture_output=True, text=True)
        evidence = os.path.join(root, 'research', 'evidence', 'vmx128-decode-validation.json')
        results()
        r = record()
        env = json.load(open(evidence, encoding='utf-8')).get('environment') if r.returncode == 0 else None
        check(r.returncode == 0 and env is not None, 'a whole run is recorded with its environment'
              + ('' if r.returncode == 0 else ': ' + (r.stderr or r.stdout)[-300:]))
        if env:
            pspec = open(os.path.join(root, module, 'ppc_64.pspec'), 'rb').read()
            check(env['module_files'].get('data/languages/ppc_64.pspec') == hashlib.sha256(pspec).hexdigest()
                  and 'data/languages/ppc_64_32.cspec' in env['module_files'] and 'ghidra' in env and 'java' in env
                  and IMAGE_SHA256 in env['program'],
                  'the environment names every module file (the pspec and cspec too), Ghidra, Java and the tested program')
            check(env['ghidra']['path'] == 'C:/Tools/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC'
                  and env['java']['path'] == 'C:/Program Files/Java/jdk-26.0.2/bin/java.exe',
                  f'Ghidra and Java are run_vmx.ps1\'s pinned installs, not BF1943_GHIDRA / BF1943_JAVA '
                  f'({env["ghidra"]["path"]}, {env["java"]["path"]})')
            # a module file swapped after the run by a copy that keeps an older mtime: the mtime check passes it, the
            # last record's hashes do not
            pspec_path = os.path.join(root, module, 'ppc_64.pspec')
            before = os.stat(pspec_path).st_mtime
            write(root, module + 'ppc_64.pspec', 'swapped, old mtime\n')
            os.utime(pspec_path, (before - 3600, before - 3600))
            r = record()
            check(r.returncode != 0 and 'differs from the last record' in r.stderr
                  and json.load(open(evidence, encoding='utf-8'))['environment'] == env,
                  'a module file that differs from the last record is refused, though older than the run (mtime kept)'
                  + ('' if r.returncode else ': it was recorded'))
            r = record('--module-changed')
            env2 = json.load(open(evidence, encoding='utf-8'))['environment'] if r.returncode == 0 else {}
            check(r.returncode == 0 and 'accepted with --module-changed' in env2.get('module_compared', ''),
                  '--module-changed records a module change made on purpose, and says so')
        os.remove(evidence)
        time.sleep(0.05)
        write(root, module + 'ppc_64.pspec', 'changed after the run\n')
        r = record()
        check(r.returncode != 0 and 'module changed after the run' in r.stderr and not os.path.exists(evidence),
              'a pspec changed after the run (not in the fingerprint) is refused')
        time.sleep(0.05)
        results(program_image='0' * 64)
        r = record()
        check(r.returncode != 0 and 'not the checked image' in r.stderr and not os.path.exists(evidence),
              'caller probes that hashed another program (a stale project) are refused')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_vector_semantics.py`:

```py
"""The Xenon language's vector p-code generator (no game data, no Ghidra): every AltiVec and VMX128 mnemonic it
models produces a body; locals are unique, sized and clear of register names; the documented opaque set stays opaque;
the scalar-FP conversion bodies cover all eight forms; and the splicer keeps decoding headers.
(The emulated tests of the semantics themselves are TestVectorSemantics.java / TestScalarFp.java, run by run_vmx.ps1.)

  python -B test_vector_semantics.py
"""
import re
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import xenon_splice  # noqa: E402
import xenon_vector_semantics as vsem  # noqa: E402

failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


ALTIVEC = ('vaddfp vsubfp vmaddfp vnmsubfp vmaxfp vminfp vrefp vrsqrtefp vrfin vrfiz vrfim vrfip vcfsx vcfux vctsxs vctuxs '
           'vcmpbfp vcmpbfp. vcmpeqfp vcmpeqfp. vcmpgefp vcmpgefp. vcmpgtfp vcmpgtfp. vcmpequb vcmpequb. vcmpequh vcmpequw vcmpgtub vcmpgtuh '
           'vcmpgtuw vcmpgtsb vcmpgtsh vcmpgtsw vaddubm vadduhm vadduwm vsububm vsubuhm vsubuwm vaddsbs vaddshs vaddsws vaddubs vadduhs vadduws '
           'vsubsbs vsubshs vsubsws vsububs vsubuhs vsubuws vaddcuw vsubcuw vavgsb vavgsh vavgsw vavgub vavguh vavguw vmaxsb vmaxsh vmaxsw vmaxub '
           'vmaxuh vmaxuw vminsb vminsh vminsw vminub vminuh vminuw vmulesb vmulesh vmuleub vmuleuh vmulosb vmulosh vmuloub vmulouh vmsumubm vmsummbm '
           'vmsumuhm vmsumuhs vmsumshm vmsumshs vmhaddshs vmhraddshs vmladduhm vsum4ubs vsum4sbs vsum4shs vsum2sws vsumsws vand vandc vor vxor vnor '
           'vsel vperm vsldoi vmrghb vmrghh vmrghw vmrglb vmrglh vmrglw vspltb vsplth vspltw vspltisb vspltish vspltisw vslb vslh vslw vsrb vsrh vsrw '
           'vsrab vsrah vsraw vrlb vrlh vrlw vsl vsr vslo vsro vpkuhum vpkuwum vpkuhus vpkuwus vpkshus vpkswus vpkshss vpkswss vpkpx vupkhsb vupkhsh '
           'vupklsb vupklsh vupkhpx vupklpx lvebx lvehx lvewx lvsl lvsr lvx lvxl stvebx stvehx stvewx stvx stvxl mfvscr mtvscr').split()
VMX128 = ('vsldoi128 lvsl128 lvsr128 lvewx128 stvewx128 lvxl128 stvxl128 vperm128 vaddfp128 vsubfp128 vmulfp128 vmaddfp128 vmaddcfp128 vnmsubfp128 '
          'vmsum3fp128 vmsum4fp128 vpkshss128 vpkshus128 vpkswss128 vnor128 vpkswus128 vpkuhum128 vpkuhus128 vsel128 vpkuwum128 vslo128 vpkuwus128 '
          'vsro128 vcfpsxws128 vcfpuxws128 vcsxwfp128 vcuxwfp128 vrfim128 vrfin128 vrfip128 vrfiz128 vrefp128 vrsqrtefp128 vspltw128 vspltisw128 '
          'vcmpeqfp128 vcmpeqfp128. vrlw128 vcmpgefp128 vcmpgefp128. vslw128 vcmpgtfp128 vcmpgtfp128. vsraw128 vcmpbfp128 vcmpbfp128. vsrw128 '
          'vcmpequw128 vcmpequw128. vmaxfp128 vminfp128 vmrghw128 vmrglw128 vupkhsb128 vupklsb128').split()
REGISTER_LIKE = re.compile(r'^(r\d+|f\d+|v\d+|vs\d+|cr\d|ctr|lr|xer|pc)$')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    altivec_ops = dict(D='vrD', A='vrA', B='vrB', C='vrC', IMM='A_BITS', RA='RA_OR_ZERO', RB='B')
    vmx_ops = dict(D='XV', A='XA', B='XB', C='XC', IMM='A_BITS', RA='RA_OR_ZERO', RB='B')
    bad = []
    for names, ops in ((ALTIVEC, altivec_ops), (VMX128, vmx_ops)):
        for n in names:
            body = vsem.body(n, ops)
            if not body:
                bad.append(f'{n}: no body')
                continue
            text = '\n'.join(body)
            declared = re.findall(r'local (\w+):(\d+)', text)
            names_ = [d for d, _ in declared]
            if len(names_) != len(set(names_)):
                bad.append(f'{n}: duplicate local')
            if any(REGISTER_LIKE.match(d) for d in names_):
                bad.append(f'{n}: local named like a register')
            if 'None' in text or 'CALLOTHER' in text:
                bad.append(f'{n}: unresolved operand')
            dest = 'cr6' if False else ops['D']
            if not n.startswith('stv') and not n == 'mtvscr' and not any(l.startswith(dest + ' =') for l in body):
                bad.append(f'{n}: never writes {dest}')
            if n.endswith('.') and not any(l.startswith('cr6 =') for l in body):
                bad.append(f'{n}: record form does not write cr6')
    check(not bad, f'{len(ALTIVEC)} AltiVec and {len(VMX128)} VMX128 bodies: unique sized locals, destination written, CR6 for record forms ({"; ".join(bad[:5])})')
    check(all(vsem.body(n, vmx_ops) is None for n in ('vpkd3d128', 'vupkd3d128')), 'D3D pack/unpack have no single body (vpkd3d128 opaque)')
    est = {n: '\n'.join(vsem.body(n, vmx_ops if n.endswith('128') else altivec_ops)) for n in ('vexptefp', 'vlogefp', 'vexptefp128', 'vlogefp128')}
    check(all(t.count('exp2_estimate(' if 'expte' in n else 'log2_estimate(') == 4 for n, t in est.items()), 'vexptefp/vlogefp (+128): one named estimate op per lane')
    split = vsem.variants('vupkd3d128', vmx_ops)
    check([e for e, _ in split] == [' & xmuimm=20', ' & xmuimm=4', ''] and split[2][1] is None and 'vupkd3d128_xy_unknown' in '\n'.join(split[1][1])
          and 'CALLOTHER' not in '\n'.join(split[0][1]), 'vupkd3d128: UIMM 20 half-to-float modelled, UIMM 4 z/w modelled (x/y unknown op), others opaque')
    fp = {n: xenon_splice.fp_convert_body(n) for n in xenon_splice.FP_CONVERT}
    check(len(fp) == 8 and all(any(l.startswith('fD = ') for l in b) for b in fp.values()) and all(('cr1flags();' in b) == n.endswith('.') for n, b in fp.items()),
          'fctiw/fctiwz/fctid/fctidz bodies: all eight forms write fD; record forms update CR1')
    check(any('c52' in l for l in fp['fctiw']) and not any('c52' in l for l in fp['fctiwz']), 'fctiw rounds to nearest even, fctiwz truncates')
    sample = (':vadduwm vrD,vrA,vrB\tis OP=4 & vrD & vrA & vrB & XOP_0_10=128\n    & vrA_32_0 & vrA_32_1\n{\n    vrD_32_0 = vrA_32_0;\n}\n'
              ':dss STRM\tis $(NOTVLE) & OP=31 & STRM & XOP_1_10=822 & Rc=0\n{\n\tdataStreamStop(STRM:1);\n}\n'
              ':lvewx vrD,A,B\tis OP=31 & vrD & A & B & XOP_1_10=71 & Rc=0\n{\n\tvrD = loadVectorElementWordIndexed(A,B);\n}\n')
    out, done = xenon_splice.rewrite_altivec(sample)
    check(done == ['vadduwm', 'lvewx'] and 'dataStreamStop(STRM:1);' in out and 'vrA_32_0' not in out and ':lvewx vrD,RA_OR_ZERO,B' in out
          and '& RA_OR_ZERO &' in out and out.startswith('define register offset=0x101000 size=4 [ vscr ];'),
          'splicer: stream hints kept; sub-piece operands dropped; vector loads take RA_OR_ZERO; VSCR defined')
    print('PASS' if not failures else f'FAIL {len(failures)}')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_workspace.py`:

```py
"""The executable tools' research workspace lookup (no game data): workspace.py and workspace.ps1 accept a folder with
work\\ and research\\ (from BF1943_RESEARCH, or the current folder) and refuse one without, saying what to do.

  python -B test_workspace.py
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
import workspace  # noqa: E402

failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def ps(cwd, env):
    return subprocess.run(['powershell', '-NoProfile', '-Command', f"& '{os.path.join(HERE, 'workspace.ps1')}'"], cwd=cwd, env=env,
                          capture_output=True, text=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as good, tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as bad:
        for d in ('work', 'research'):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(good, d))
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != 'BF1943_RESEARCH'}
        old = dict(os.environ)
        os.environ.pop('BF1943_RESEARCH', None)
        cwd = os.getcwd()
        try:
            os.chdir(good)
            check(os.path.samefile(workspace.research_root(), good), 'workspace.py: the current folder when it has work\\ and research\\')
            os.chdir(bad)
            try:
                workspace.research_root()
                check(False, 'workspace.py refuses a folder without work\\ and research\\')
            except SystemExit as e:
                check('BF1943_RESEARCH' in str(e), 'workspace.py refuses a folder without them, naming BF1943_RESEARCH')
            os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = good
            check(os.path.samefile(workspace.research_root(), good), 'workspace.py: BF1943_RESEARCH wins over the current folder')
        finally:
            os.chdir(cwd)
            os.environ.clear()
            os.environ.update(old)
        if os.name == 'nt':
            r = ps(good, env)
            check(r.returncode == 0 and os.path.samefile(r.stdout.strip(), good), 'workspace.ps1: the current folder')
            r = ps(bad, env)
            check(r.returncode != 0 and 'BF1943_RESEARCH' in (r.stdout + r.stderr), 'workspace.ps1 refuses a folder without them')
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```

`bf1943-xex-tools/tests/test_xex_tables.py`:

```py
r"""XEX tools: section map, helper resolution, VX128 classes on a made-up image

map_functions.py, resolve_helpers.py, classify_vmx.py and xenonrecomp_reference.py on a made-up research workspace (no
game data, nothing read from or written to operation-rising-sun): an 8 MB stand-in image with a PE header, four
sections, .pdata records of each kind (a plain function, one exactly covering a register helper block, and records
with each error) and the six register helper blocks as resolve_helpers lays them out, and a stand-in XenonRecomp
reference (folder and ZIP). The modules' pinned hashes (image, reference archive and members) are replaced by the
made-up ones for the test and restored afterwards. Checked: the helper words against known PowerPC encodings, branch
targets, the tables and evidence each main() writes, and every refusal (another image, a helper that differs, a
reference that differs or is missing).
"""
import contextlib
import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import struct
import zipfile

import classify_vmx
import map_functions
import resolve_helpers
import xenonrecomp_reference as xr

BASE = 0x82000000
SIZE = 0x7C0000
FUNC = 0x82010000


def sha(b):
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


def pdata_word(length, prolog, bit30=True, exception=False):
    return (length // 4) << 8 | (prolog // 4) | (0x40000000 if bit30 else 0) | (0x80000000 if exception else 0)


def image():
    """The stand-in image: PE header (base 0x82000000; .rdata, .pdata, .text, and .bss past the image's end), a
    function at FUNC calling three helper entries and holding VX128 words, and the register helper blocks."""
    d = bytearray(SIZE)
    d[:2] = b'MZ'
    pe = 0x80
    struct.pack_into('<I', d, 60, pe)
    opt_size = 0xE0
    struct.pack_into('<4sHH', d, pe, b'PE\0\0', 0x1F2, 4)
    struct.pack_into('<H', d, pe + 20, opt_size)
    opt = pe + 24
    struct.pack_into('<I', d, opt + 28, BASE)
    sections = [(b'.rdata', 0x1000, 0x1000, 0x40000000), (b'.pdata', 0x2000, 8 * 7, 0x40000000),
                (b'.text', 0x10000, SIZE - 0x10000, 0x60000000), (b'.bss', SIZE, 0x1000, 0xC0000000)]
    for k, (name, rva, size, flags) in enumerate(sections):
        at = opt + opt_size + 40 * k
        struct.pack_into('<8sIIII', d, at, name, size, rva, size, rva)
        struct.pack_into('<I', d, at + 36, flags)
    struct.pack_into('<II', d, opt + 96 + 3 * 8, 0x2000, 8 * 7)
    for start, kind, restore in resolve_helpers.HELPER_BLOCKS:
        for first, last in ([(14, 31), (64, 127)] if kind == 'vmx' else [(14, 31)]):
            words = resolve_helpers.helper_words(kind, restore, first, last)
            struct.pack_into(f'>{len(words)}I', d, start - BASE, *words)
            start += 4 * len(words)
    save = resolve_helpers.HELPER_BLOCKS[0][0]
    gprlr = 4 * len(resolve_helpers.helper_words('gprlr', False, 14, 31))
    code = [bl(FUNC, save + 4 * 4), bl(FUNC + 4, save + 4 * 17), 0x48000000 | ((save - FUNC - 8) & 0x3FFFFFC),  # b
            0x100001C3 | 1 << 21 | 3 << 16,              # stvx128 (one table entry)
            0x10000003,                                  # matches both made-up masks (ambiguous)
            0x13FFFFFF,                                  # opcode 4, no entry
            0x38600000, 0x4E800020]                      # li r3, 0; blr
    struct.pack_into(f'>{len(code)}I', d, FUNC - BASE, *code)
    records = [(FUNC, pdata_word(4 * len(code), 8, exception=True)),
               (save, pdata_word(gprlr, gprlr, bit30=False)),    # exactly the gprlr save helper: resolved
               (FUNC + 0x40, pdata_word(16, 0, bit30=False)),    # bit 30 clear, no helper: unresolved
               (FUNC + 0x82, pdata_word(16, 0)),                 # misaligned
               (FUNC + 0x100, pdata_word(8, 16)),                # prologue past the end
               (BASE + SIZE, pdata_word(8, 0)),                  # outside the image's executable bytes
               (FUNC + 0x200, 0x40000000)]                       # zero length
    for k, (start, word) in enumerate(records):
        struct.pack_into('>II', d, 0x2000 + 8 * k, start, word)
    return bytes(d)


def bl(at, target):
    return 0x48000001 | ((target - at) & 0x3FFFFFC)


PPC_DIS = (b'/* made-up ppc-dis.c table rows */\n'
           b'{ "stvx128", VX128_1(4, 451), VX128_1_MASK, PPCVEC128, { VS128, RA, RB } },\n'
           b'{ "made_a", VX128(4, 0), VX128_MASK, PPCVEC128, { 0 } },\n'
           b'{ "made_b", VX128_3(4, 0), VX128_3_MASK, PPCVEC128, { 0 } },\n'
           b'{ "notvx", X(31, 0), X_MASK, PPC, { 0 } },\n')
MEMBERS = {'XenonRecomp-main/thirdparty/disasm/ppc-dis.c': PPC_DIS,
           'XenonRecomp-main/XenonRecomp/recompiler.cpp': b'// recompiler\n',
           'XenonRecomp-main/XenonUtils/ppc_context.h': b'// context\n',
           'XenonRecomp-main/XenonUtils/xbox.h': b'// xbox\n',
           'XenonRecomp-main/README.md': b'# XenonRecomp\n'}


@contextlib.contextmanager
def workspace(tmp, data=None, archive=False):
    """A made-up research workspace with the image and the reference; the modules' pins point at them."""
    data = image() if data is None else data
    for p in ('work/xex-analysis', 'work/vmx128', 'research/evidence'):
        (tmp / p).mkdir(parents=True)
    (tmp / 'work/xex-analysis/default.checked.memory.bin').write_bytes(data)
    if archive:
        (tmp / 'Tools').mkdir()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp / 'Tools/XenonRecomp.zip', 'w') as z:
            for name, content in MEMBERS.items():
                z.writestr(name, content)
    else:
        for name, content in MEMBERS.items():
            path = tmp / 'Tools/XenonRecomp' / name
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_bytes(content)
    saved = (os.environ.get('BF1943_RESEARCH'), resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH, map_functions.IMAGE_SHA256,
             classify_vmx.IMAGE_SHA256, xr.ARCHIVE_SHA256, xr.MEMBERS)
    os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = str(tmp)
    resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH = map_functions.IMAGE_SHA256 = classify_vmx.IMAGE_SHA256 = sha(data)
    xr.ARCHIVE_SHA256 = sha((tmp / 'Tools/XenonRecomp.zip').read_bytes()) if archive else '0' * 64
    xr.MEMBERS = {name: sha(content) for name, content in MEMBERS.items()}
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
            yield data
    finally:
        if saved[0] is None:
            os.environ.pop('BF1943_RESEARCH', None)
        else:
            os.environ['BF1943_RESEARCH'] = saved[0]
        (resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH, map_functions.IMAGE_SHA256, classify_vmx.IMAGE_SHA256, xr.ARCHIVE_SHA256,
         xr.MEMBERS) = saved[1:]


def test_helper_words_encodings():
    """The first words of each block against the PowerPC encodings (std/ld r14,-152(r1); stfd/lfd f14,-144(r12);
    li r11,-288 and stvx/lvx v14,r11,r12; li r11,-1024 and stvx128 v64,r11,r12), and each block ends in blr."""
    w = resolve_helpers.helper_words
    assert w('gprlr', False, 14, 31)[:1] == [0xF9C1FF68] and w('gprlr', False, 14, 31)[-2:] == [0x9181FFF8, 0x4E800020]
    assert w('gprlr', True, 14, 31)[:1] == [0xE9C1FF68] and w('gprlr', True, 14, 31)[-3:] == [0x8181FFF8, 0x7D8803A6,
                                                                                               0x4E800020]
    assert w('fpr', False, 14, 31)[0] == 0xD9CCFF70 and w('fpr', True, 14, 31)[0] == 0xC9CCFF70
    assert w('vmx', False, 14, 31)[:2] == [0x3960FEE0, 0x7DCB61CE] and w('vmx', True, 14, 31)[1] == 0x7DCB60CE
    assert w('vmx', False, 64, 127)[:2] == [0x3960FC00, 0x100B61CB] and len(w('vmx', True, 64, 127)) == 129
    assert resolve_helpers.branch_target(bl(0x82000100, 0x82000000), 0x82000100) == 0x82000000
    assert resolve_helpers.branch_target(0x48000102, 0x82000100) == 0x100, 'ba: absolute'
    assert resolve_helpers.branch_target(0x4BFFFFFD, 0x82000100) == 0x820000FC, 'bl -4'


def test_verified_blocks_refusals():
    data = image()
    saved = resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH
    try:
        resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH = sha(data)
        blocks = resolve_helpers.verified_blocks(data)
        assert [b['name'] for b in blocks] == ['__savegprlr_14', '__restgprlr_14', '__savefpr_14', '__restfpr_14',
                                               '__savevmx_14', '__savevmx_64', '__restvmx_14', '__restvmx_64']
        vmx64 = blocks[5]
        assert vmx64['start'] == blocks[4]['end'] and vmx64['entries'][1]['address'] - vmx64['entries'][0]['address'] == 8
        damaged = bytearray(data)
        damaged[resolve_helpers.HELPER_BLOCKS[2][0] - BASE] ^= 1
        resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH = sha(bytes(damaged))
        try:
            resolve_helpers.verified_blocks(bytes(damaged))
            why = None
        except ValueError as e:
            why = str(e)
        assert why == f'Full helper mismatch {resolve_helpers.HELPER_BLOCKS[2][0]:x}', why
        try:
            resolve_helpers.verified_blocks(data)
            why = None
        except ValueError as e:
            why = str(e)
        assert why == 'Unexpected image'
    finally:
        resolve_helpers.IMAGE_HASH = saved

        map_functions.main()
```
