`core/bfbc2core/level.py`:

```py
"""A BC2 level as the suite's tools see it: entities with transforms and sources, collision meshes, terrain.

    lvl = load('sp_01')                       # by level name, from Project OPFOR's game copy
    lvl.entities                              # every instance of the level partition (Entity)
    lvl.meshes                                # world-space collision triangles per placed object / group member
    lvl.terrain                               # (vertices, triangles): the level's height field (terrain.py),
                                              # or NavKit's in-game samples when it cannot be read, or None
    lvl.heightfield                           # terrain.Heightfield, for exact heights (height(x, z))
    lvl.shapes                                # outlines: areas (capture, combat, order areas) and routes (Shape)
    lvl.water                                 # water.Water: surface triangles and each one's shader (water.py)

Data comes from the level as NavKit prepares it (OPFOR's work\\levels\\<level>\\dist and pkg, and the shared
data in work\\navkit\\common\\); a level that is not prepared yet is prepared on first use (offline, no game).
"""
import glob
import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, cast

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

from . import dbx, terrain, water

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    # the Level fields named terrain and water hide these modules inside its class body
    from .terrain import Heightfield
    from .water import Water


# entity categories by type (DESIGN.md open question 6)
CATEGORIES = [
    ('soldier spawn', r'\.(SoldierSpawnEntityData|AlternateSpawnEntityData)$'),
    ('vehicle spawn', r'\.VehicleSpawnEntityData$'),
    ('objective', r'\.(MissionObjectiveEntityData|ArmDisarmAwardEntityData)$'),
    ('capture point', r'\.CapturePointEntityData$'),
    ('combat area', r'\.(CombatAreaTriggerEntityData|DamageAreaTriggerEntityData)$'),
    ('ai order', r'\.(AreaOrderEntityData|PatrolOrderEntityData|InterludeOrderEntityData|FireAtAreaOrderEntityData)$'),
    ('area point', r'\.AreaGeometryEntityData$'),
    ('placed object', r'\.ReferenceObjectData$'),
]
# placed objects (ReferenceObjectData), by what their blueprint's object is
OBJECT_CATEGORIES = {
    'LadderEntityData': 'ladder',
    'DynamicModelEntityData': 'dynamic object',      # movable or breakable props: crates, barrels
    'RigidModelEntityData': 'dynamic object',        # breakable fences
    'BangerEntityData': 'dynamic object',            # explosive props (gas cylinders)
    'EffectEntityData': 'effect',
}
TEAMS = {'Team1': 1, 'Team2': 2, 'TeamNeutral': 0}
SHAPE_FIELDS = (('Geometry', 'area'), ('SurroundingGeometry', 'outer area'), ('RouteWaypoints', 'route'))


@dataclass
class Entity:
    index: int
    guid: str
    type: str
    short_type: str
    category: str
    id: str | None
    name: str | None
    partition: str
    matrix: npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None  # 4 x 4, rows: right, up, forward, translation
    blueprint: str | None
    element: dbx.Element
    group: str | None = None              # static-group partition, for group members
    # placed objects: the type of the blueprint's object (StaticModelEntityData ...)
    blueprint_type: str | None = None
    destructible: bool = False            # placed objects: the blueprint has health states / breakable parts
    team: int | None = None               # 1, 2, 0 (neutral): spawns, capture points (initial owner), triggers
    ai: bool | None = None                # soldier spawns: True for AI soldiers, False for human players

    @property
    def position(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None:
        return None if self.matrix is None else self.matrix[3, :3]

    def refs(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Every reference in the property tree: (field path, ref), local GUIDs and partition/GUID paths."""
        out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        # in document order, with a stack rather than recursion: dbx.parse reads any nesting (2026-10-30: a deep
        # one raised RecursionError here)
        todo: list[tuple[Iterator[dbx.Element], str]] = [(iter(self.element.children or ()), '')]
        while todo:
            c = next(todo[-1][0], None)
            if c is None:
                todo.pop()
                continue
            path = todo[-1][1]
            name = c.attr('name') or c.tag
            r = c.attr('ref')
            if r is not None and r != 'null':
                out.append((path + name, r))
            if c.children is not None:
                todo.append((iter(c.children), path + name + '/'))
        return out


@dataclass
class Mesh:
    entity: int                           # index into Level.entities
    triangles: npt.NDArray[np.float32]    # (n, 3, 3) world space


@dataclass
class Shape:
    entity: int                           # the entity whose field it is (CapturePoint, CombatArea, an order ...)
    kind: str                             # 'area', 'outer area' or 'route'
    points: npt.NDArray[np.float64]       # (n, 3) world positions, in chain order
    closed: bool                          # areas are rings; routes are open
    height: float                         # areas: prism height above the points (0: flat)
    field: str


@dataclass
class Level:
    name: str
    lv: str
    opfor: str
    entities: list[Entity] = field(default_factory=list)
    meshes: list[Mesh] = field(default_factory=list)
    terrain: tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float32], npt.NDArray[np.uint32]] | None = None
    heightfield: 'Heightfield | None' = None  # terrain.Heightfield, when the level's terrain bundle was read
    water: 'Water | None' = None          # water.Water (may have no triangles), from the same bundle
    shapes: list[Shape] = field(default_factory=list)
    missing_collision: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def by_guid(self, guid: str) -> Entity | None:
        g = guid.lower()
        return next((e for e in self.entities if e.guid.lower() == g), None)


def category_of(t: str | None) -> str:
    for name, rx in CATEGORIES:
        if re.search(rx, t or ''):
            return name
    return 'other'


def transform_of(e: dbx.Element) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None:
    t = e.child('Transform')
    if t is None or t.kind != dbx.NUMBERS:
        return None
    v = dbx.floats(t)
    return np.array(v, dtype=np.float64).reshape(4, 4) if len(v) == 16 else None


def blueprint_of(e: dbx.Element) -> str | None:
    r = e.child('ReferencedObject')
    ref = r.attr('ref') if r is not None else None
    return ref.rsplit('/', 1)[0].lower() if ref and '/' in ref else None


def load(level: str, opfor: str | None = None, terrain_stride: int = 2,
         log: Callable[[str], object] = print) -> Level:
    import navkit_le as navkit
    import levelobjects
    root = navkit.find_opfor(opfor)
    lv = level.replace('\\', '/').split('/')[-1].lower()
    base = os.path.join(root, 'work', 'levels', lv)
    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(base, 'dist')):           # first use: NavKit's offline prepare step
        log(f'{lv}: not prepared yet - unpacking it (navkit_le.py prepare {lv}, once)')
        pr = navkit.Project(root)
        navkit.prepare(pr, pr.level(lv), log=log)
    bases = [os.path.join(base, 'pkg'), os.path.join(base, 'dist')]
    bases += [d for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'navkit', 'common', '*')) if os.path.isdir(d)]
    # the level partition (a Package overlay wins over Dist)
    part = None
    for b in bases[:2]:
        for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(b, 'levels', '*.dbx')):
            if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0].lower() == lv:
                part = part or f
    if part is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{lv}: level partition not found under {base}')
    LV = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(part))[0]
    lvl = Level(LV, lv, root)
    log(f'{LV}: reading {os.path.relpath(part, root)}')
    f = dbx.read(part)
    pname = 'levels/' + LV
    for el in f.instances:
        t = el.attr('type') or ''
        lvl.entities.append(Entity(len(lvl.entities), el.attr('guid') or '', t, t.rsplit('.', 1)[-1], category_of(t), el.attr('id'),
                                   (cast(dbx.Element, el.child('Name')).text if el.child('Name') is not None
                                    and cast(dbx.Element, el.child('Name')).kind == dbx.TEXT else None),
                                   pname, transform_of(el), blueprint_of(el), el))
    # static model groups: one entity per member placement. Each group file once: the Package copy wins over
    # Dist, as in the game (and levels\ / Levels\ are the same folder on Windows)
    group_files: dict[str, str] = {}
    for b in bases[:2]:
        for gf in glob.glob(os.path.join(b, 'levels', lv, '*_HavokAsset.dbx')):
            group_files.setdefault(os.path.basename(gf).lower(), gf)
    for gf in group_files.values():
            g = dbx.read(gf)
            for el in g.instances:
                tr, assets = el.child('Transforms'), el.child('Assets')
                if tr is None or assets is None or tr.kind != dbx.NUMBERS or not assets.children:
                    continue
                vals = np.array(dbx.floats(tr), dtype=np.float64)
                for k, item in enumerate(assets.children):
                    if 16 * (k + 1) > len(vals):
                        break
                    bp = re.sub(r'_havok$', '', (item.attr('ref') or '').rsplit('/', 1)[0].lower())
                    lvl.entities.append(Entity(len(lvl.entities), f'{el.attr("guid")}#{k}', 'StaticGroupMember', 'StaticGroupMember',
                                               'group member', None, bp.rsplit('/', 1)[-1], os.path.basename(gf)[:-4],
                                               vals[16 * k:16 * (k + 1)].reshape(4, 4), bp, item, group=os.path.basename(gf)))
    resolve_blueprints(lvl, bases)
    assign_teams(lvl)
    lvl.shapes = shapes_of(lvl)
    # collision
    havok = levelobjects.havok_index(bases)
    try:
        for bp, target in levelobjects.mesh_aliases(bases).items():
            if bp not in havok and target in havok:
                havok[bp] = havok[target]
    except Exception as e:                    # needs the converted XML NavKit's prepare writes
        lvl.notes.append(f'blueprint mesh aliases not read: {e}')
    cache, missing = {}, set()
    for e in lvl.entities:
        if e.blueprint is None or e.matrix is None:
            continue
        if e.blueprint not in cache:
            cache[e.blueprint] = levelobjects.triangles(havok[e.blueprint]) if e.blueprint in havok else None
        t = cache[e.blueprint]
        if t is None:
            missing.add(e.blueprint)
            continue
        m = e.matrix
        lvl.meshes.append(Mesh(e.index, (t @ m[:3, :3] + m[3, :3]).astype(np.float32)))
    lvl.missing_collision = sorted(missing)
    source = 'none'
    try:
        lvl.heightfield = heightfield_of(root, lv, log, terrain_name(f.instances))
    except Exception as e:                    # no terrain bundle, FbrbTool missing, unexpected layout
        lvl.notes.append(f'terrain height field not read: {e}')
    try:
        lvl.water = water.read(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'levels', lv, 'terrain'), terrain_name(f.instances) or lv)
    except Exception as e:
        lvl.notes.append(f'water not read: {e}')
    if lvl.heightfield is not None:
        lvl.terrain, source = lvl.heightfield.mesh(terrain_stride), 'height field'
    else:
        lvl.terrain = terrain_from_samples(root, lv, terrain_stride)
        source = 'samples' if lvl.terrain else 'none'
    n_tris = sum(len(m.triangles) for m in lvl.meshes)
    log(f'{LV}: {len(lvl.entities)} entities, {len(lvl.meshes)} with collision ({n_tris} triangles), '
        f'{len(missing)} blueprints without collision, terrain from {source}')
    return lvl


def resolve_blueprints(lvl: Level, bases: list[str]) -> None:
    """Placed objects: the blueprint's object type and whether it is destructible; categories from them."""
    files: dict[str, dict[str, dbx.Element]] = {}

    def instances(path: str) -> dict[str, dbx.Element]:
        if path not in files:
            files[path] = {}
            for b in bases:
                p = os.path.join(b, path + '.dbx')
                if os.path.isfile(p):
                    try:
                        files[path] = {(i.attr('guid') or '').lower(): i for i in dbx.read(p).instances}
                    except Exception:
                        pass
                    break
        return files[path]

    def broken_up(insts: dict[str, dbx.Element]) -> bool:
        """Health states or breakable part links anywhere in the blueprint (destructible buildings)."""
        for i in insts.values():
            for name in ('HealthStates', 'PartLinks'):
                c = i.child(name)
                if c is not None and c.children:
                    return True
        return False

    destructible: dict[str, bool] = {}
    for e in lvl.entities:
        if e.short_type != 'ReferenceObjectData':
            continue
        r = e.element.child('ReferencedObject')
        ref = r.attr('ref') if r is not None else None
        if not ref or '/' not in ref:
            continue
        path, guid = ref.rsplit('/', 1)
        insts = instances(path)
        obj = bp = insts.get(guid.lower())
        o = bp.child('Object') if bp is not None else None
        oref = o.attr('ref') if o is not None else None
        if oref and oref != 'null':
            if '/' in oref:
                p2, g2 = oref.rsplit('/', 1)
                obj = instances(p2).get(g2.lower())
            else:
                obj = insts.get(oref.lower())
        if obj is None:
            continue
        e.blueprint_type = (obj.attr('type') or '').rsplit('.', 1)[-1]
        if path not in destructible:
            destructible[path] = broken_up(insts)
        e.destructible = e.blueprint_type == 'StaticModelEntityData' and destructible[path]
        if (e.blueprint or '').startswith('objects/objects/mpobjective'):
            e.category = 'objective'                     # Rush M-COM stations
        elif e.destructible:
            e.category = 'destructible'
        else:
            e.category = OBJECT_CATEGORIES.get(e.blueprint_type, e.category)


def assign_teams(lvl: Level) -> None:
    """Team and AI / human from the entity's own fields; alternate spawn points take their spawner's team."""
    guids = {e.guid.lower(): e for e in lvl.entities}
    for e in lvl.entities:
        for name in ('Team', 'InitialOwnerTeam'):
            c = e.element.child(name)
            if c is not None and c.kind == dbx.TEXT and c.text in TEAMS:
                e.team = TEAMS[c.text]
                break
        c = e.element.child('PlayerType')
        if c is not None and c.kind == dbx.TEXT and c.text:
            e.ai = c.text != 'SSHumanPlayer'
    for e in lvl.entities:
        alt = e.element.child('AlternativeSpawnPoints')
        for item in (alt.children if alt is not None and alt.children else ()):
            t = guids.get((item.attr('ref') or '').lower())
            if t is not None and t.team is None:
                t.team, t.ai = e.team, e.ai


def shapes_of(lvl: Level) -> list[Shape]:
    """Outlines: chains of AreaGeometryEntityData points (Next links) referenced by Geometry, SurroundingGeometry
    and RouteWaypoints fields. A chain that comes back to its start is an area."""
    guids = {e.guid.lower(): e for e in lvl.entities}
    out: list[Shape] = []
    for e in lvl.entities:
        for name, kind in SHAPE_FIELDS:
            c = e.element.child(name)
            for item in (c.children if c is not None and c.children else ()):
                p = guids.get((item.attr('ref') or '').lower())
                pts, seen, closed, height = [], set(), False, 0.0
                while p is not None and p.position is not None:
                    if p.guid in seen:
                        closed = True
                        break
                    seen.add(p.guid)
                    pts.append(p.position)
                    h = p.element.child('Height')
                    if h is not None and h.kind == dbx.NUMBERS and not height:
                        height = float(dbx.floats(h)[0])
                    n = p.element.child('Next')
                    p = guids.get((n.attr('ref') or '').lower()) if n is not None else None
                if len(pts) >= 2:
                    out.append(Shape(e.index, kind, np.array(pts), closed and kind != 'route', height, name))
    return out


def terrain_name(entities: Iterable[dbx.Element]) -> str | None:
    """The terrain's name from the level's TerrainEntityData.TerrainAsset (terrains/mp_009/mp_009 for MP_009GR:
    a mode variant shares its base map's terrain), or None.

    The entity's transform is NOT applied to the heights: on 11 of the 13 campaign levels it moves the
    terrain by 1-59 m, yet the stored heights unmoved match the game's terrain to within centimetres."""
    for el in entities:
        if (el.attr('type') or '').endswith('.TerrainEntityData'):
            a = el.child('TerrainAsset')
            parts = ((a.attr('ref') or '') if a is not None else '').split('/')
            return parts[1].lower() if len(parts) >= 3 else None
    return None


def water_of(root: str, lv: str, log: Callable[[str], object] = print) -> 'water.Water | None':
    """The level's water (water.Water, or None), its terrain bundle unpacked once (as heightfield_of does)."""
    part = None
    for b in ('pkg', 'dist'):
        for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'levels', lv, b, 'levels', '*.dbx')):
            if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0].lower() == lv:
                part = part or f
    name = (terrain_name(dbx.read(part).instances) if part else None) or lv
    heightfield_of(root, lv, log, name)                  # unpacks the terrain bundle when it is not there yet
    return water.read(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'levels', lv, 'terrain'), name)


def heightfield_of(root: str, lv: str, log: Callable[[str], object] = print,
                   name: str | None = None) -> terrain.Heightfield | None:
    """The level's terrain height field, unpacking its terrain-00.fbrb into work\\levels\\<lv>\\terrain once.
    name: from terrain_name(); read from the level partition if not given."""
    import subprocess
    import navkit_le as navkit
    if name is None:
        part = None
        for b in ('pkg', 'dist'):
            for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'work', 'levels', lv, b, 'levels', '*.dbx')):
                if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0].lower() == lv:
                    part = part or f
        name = terrain_name(dbx.read(part).instances) if part else None
    name = name or lv
    dest = os.path.join(root, 'work', 'levels', lv, 'terrain')
    path = terrain.find(dest, name) if os.path.isdir(dest) else None
    if path is None:
        bundle = None
        for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, 'game', 'Dist', 'win32', 'levels', '*')):
            if os.path.basename(d).lower() == lv and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, 'terrain-00.fbrb')):
                bundle = os.path.join(d, 'terrain-00.fbrb')
        if bundle is None:
            return None
        log(f'{lv}: unpacking {os.path.relpath(bundle, root)}')
        tool = navkit.find_tool(root, 'FbrbTool.exe', 'bf1943-fbrb-tool')
        subprocess.run([tool, 'unpack', bundle, dest], check=True, capture_output=True)
        path = terrain.find(dest, name)
        if path is None:
            return None
    return terrain.read(path)


def terrain_from_samples(root: str, lv: str,
                         stride: int = 2) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float32], npt.NDArray[np.uint32]] | None:
    """A height-field mesh from NavKit's in-game samples: per column the highest surface that hit terrain,
    every <stride>-th sample. Returns (vertices (n, 3), triangles (m, 3) indices) or None."""
    import navsample
    import navwalk
    path = None
    for name in (f'{lv}_navkit.bin', f'{lv}_full.bin'):
        p = os.path.join(root, 'work', 'navsample', name)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            path = p
            break
    if path is None:
        return None
    s, _ = navsample.load(path)
    terrain = (s.hit[:, 0] == navwalk.TERRAIN_SHAPE_VTABLE) if s.hit is not None and len(s.hit) else np.ones(len(s.y), bool)
    cols = s.nx * s.nz
    column = np.repeat(np.arange(cols), np.diff(s.start[:cols + 1]))        # column of every surface
    top = np.full(cols, -np.inf, dtype=np.float32)
    np.maximum.at(top, column[terrain], s.y[terrain])                         # highest terrain surface per column
    full = np.where(np.isfinite(top), top, np.nan).reshape(s.nz, s.nx)
    ii = np.arange(0, s.nx, stride)
    jj = np.arange(0, s.nz, stride)
    h = full[np.ix_(jj, ii)]
    xs = s.min_x + ii * s.pitch
    zs = s.min_z + jj * s.pitch
    X, Z = np.meshgrid(xs, zs)
    verts = np.stack([X.ravel(), h.ravel(), Z.ravel()], axis=1).astype(np.float32)
    nz, nx = h.shape
    idx = np.arange(nz * nx).reshape(nz, nx)
    a, b, c, d = idx[:-1, :-1].ravel(), idx[:-1, 1:].ravel(), idx[1:, :-1].ravel(), idx[1:, 1:].ravel()
    ok = ~(np.isnan(h[:-1, :-1]) | np.isnan(h[:-1, 1:]) | np.isnan(h[1:, :-1]) | np.isnan(h[1:, 1:])).ravel()
    # no triangles across cliffs or between stacked surfaces (a step of more than 4 m between neighbours)
    hv = h.ravel()
    steep = (np.abs(hv[a] - hv[b]) > 4) | (np.abs(hv[a] - hv[c]) > 4) | (np.abs(hv[d] - hv[b]) > 4) | (np.abs(hv[d] - hv[c]) > 4)
    ok &= ~steep
    tris = np.concatenate([np.stack([a, c, b], 1)[ok], np.stack([b, c, d], 1)[ok]]).astype(np.uint32)
    verts[np.isnan(verts[:, 1]), 1] = 0
    return verts, tris

```

`core/bfbc2core/level1943.py`:

```py
"""A BF1943 level as the suite's tools see it, read straight from your copy's bundles (game1943.py): entities with
transforms and sources, collision meshes, terrain, water, outlines - the same Level / Entity / Mesh / Shape as
level.py gives for a BFBC2 level, so the 3D tools take either.

    lvl = load('wake_island_s')               # from find_game() (bf1943-xenia-kit's output, BF1943_GAME overrides)
    lvl.entities                              # the level partition's instances and the static-group members
    lvl.meshes                                # world-space collision per placed object and group member
    lvl.heightfield, lvl.terrain              # terrain.Heightfield (big-endian), and its mesh
    lvl.water                                 # water.Water: the sea surface
    lvl.shapes                                # outlines: capture areas, combat areas, DMZs (AreaGeometry chains)
    lvl.objectives                            # bf1943-spawn-map's bases and flags, with the spawns they own

BF1943's categories: 'base' and 'flag' (capture points: a base cannot change team), soldier / vehicle spawns,
'end-of-round spawn', 'combat area', 'dmz', 'map marker', 'area point'; placed objects by their blueprint:
'ladder' (LadderEntityData), 'destructible' (two or more health states), 'dynamic object', 'placed object'.
Level.opfor holds the game folder (the field's name is the BFBC2 loader's). Nothing is unpacked or written.
"""
import os
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from typing import Any, cast

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

from . import dbx, game1943, terrain, water
from .level import CATEGORIES, Entity, Level, Mesh, assign_teams, blueprint_of, category_of, shapes_of, transform_of

CATEGORIES_1943 = [
    ('end-of-round spawn', r'\.EndOfRoundSoldierSpawnEntityData$'),
    ('dmz', r'\.DmzEntityData$'),
    ('map marker', r'\.MapMarkerEntityData$'),
] + CATEGORIES
FLAG_INDEX = {'forbid': 0, 'exclude': 1, 'dynamic': 3, 'detailed': 5, 'destructible': 6, 'ladder': 7}


def category_1943(t: str | None) -> str:
    import re
    for name, rx in CATEGORIES_1943:
        if re.search(rx, t or ''):
            return name
    return category_of(t)


def load(level: str, game: str | None = None, terrain_stride: int = 2,
         log: Callable[[str], object] = print) -> Level:
    import levelobjects1943 as lo           # the big-endian NavKit's: on sys.path from the script (suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
    game = game1943.find_game(game)
    lv = level.replace('\\', '/').split('/')[-1].lower()
    g = game1943.Game(game, lv)
    f = g.partition(f'levels/{lv}')
    if f is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'levels/{lv}.dbx is in none of {lv}\'s bundles')
    name = next((dbx.value(c) for e in f.instances if lo.kind(e) == 'LevelData' for c in (e.children or ())
                 if c.attr('name') == 'Name' and c.kind == dbx.TEXT), lv)
    lvl = Level(name.rsplit('/', 1)[-1], lv, game)
    log(f'{lvl.name}: reading levels/{lv}.dbx')
    pname = 'levels/' + lv
    for el in f.instances:
        t = el.attr('type') or ''
        nm = el.child('Name')
        lvl.entities.append(Entity(len(lvl.entities), el.attr('guid') or '', t, t.rsplit('.', 1)[-1], category_1943(t),
                                   el.attr('id'), nm.text if nm is not None and nm.kind == dbx.TEXT else None, pname,
                                   transform_of(el), blueprint_of(el), el))
    # static-model groups: one entity per member placement (Physics.CompositeHavokAsset: Assets[i] + Transforms[i])
    for gname in g.names(f'levels/{lv}/'):
        if not gname.endswith('_havokasset.dbx'):
            continue
        for el in dbx.parse(cast(bytes, g.data(gname))).instances:     # a name from g.names(): its data is there
            if lo.kind(el) != 'CompositeHavokAsset':
                continue
            tr, assets = el.child('Transforms'), el.child('Assets')
            if tr is None or assets is None or tr.kind != dbx.NUMBERS or not assets.children:
                continue
            vals = np.array(dbx.floats(tr), dtype=np.float64)
            for k, item in enumerate(assets.children):
                if 16 * (k + 1) > len(vals):
                    break
                bp = (item.attr('ref') or '').rsplit('/', 1)[0].lower()
                bp = bp[:-len('_havok')] if bp.endswith('_havok') else bp
                lvl.entities.append(Entity(len(lvl.entities), f'{el.attr("guid")}#{k}', 'StaticGroupMember', 'StaticGroupMember',
                                           'group member', None, bp.rsplit('/', 1)[-1], os.path.basename(gname)[:-4],
                                           vals[16 * k:16 * (k + 1)].reshape(4, 4), bp, item, group=os.path.basename(gname)))
    # placed objects: category and flags from the blueprint (levelobjects1943.blueprint_info)
    info: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for e in lvl.entities:
        if e.short_type != 'ReferenceObjectData' or not e.blueprint:
            continue
        if e.blueprint not in info:
            info[e.blueprint] = lo.blueprint_info(g, e.blueprint)
        flags = info[e.blueprint][0]
        if not flags:
            continue
        fl = lambda k: len(flags) > FLAG_INDEX[k] and bool(flags[FLAG_INDEX[k]])
        e.destructible = fl('destructible')
        e.category = 'ladder' if fl('ladder') else 'destructible' if e.destructible else 'dynamic object' if fl('dynamic') else e.category
    assign_teams(lvl)
    for e in lvl.entities:                                  # DMZs name their team in TeamId
        c = e.element.child('TeamId') if e.short_type == 'DmzEntityData' else None
        if c is not None and c.kind == dbx.TEXT:
            e.team = {'Team1': 1, 'Team2': 2}.get(c.text, 0)
    lvl.shapes = shapes_of(lvl)
    # bases and flags (bf1943-spawn-map)
    import spawnmap
    m = cast(dict[str, Any], spawnmap.spawn_map(game, lv))
    lvl.objectives = m['objectives']  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]  # BF1943 only, not a Level field
    roles = {o['guid']: o['role'] for o in m['objectives']}
    for e in lvl.entities:
        if e.short_type == 'CapturePointEntityData':
            e.category = roles.get(e.guid.lower(), 'flag')
    # BF1943's spawns are all TeamNeutral in the data: a spawn's side is its owner's. A base never changes team, so
    # its spawns (and their alternates) take its initial owner; a flag's stay neutral (they follow the flag)
    by_guid = {e.guid.lower(): e for e in lvl.entities}
    teams = {'Team1': 1, 'Team2': 2}
    for o in m['objectives']:
        if o['role'] != 'base' or o['initial_owner'] not in teams:
            continue
        for s in o['spawns']:
            e = by_guid.get(s['guid'])
            if e is None:
                continue
            e.team = teams[o['initial_owner']]
            alt = e.element.child('AlternativeSpawnPoints')
            for item in (alt.children if alt is not None and alt.children else ()):
                a = by_guid.get((item.attr('ref') or '').lower())
                if a is not None:
                    a.team = e.team
    # collision
    cache: dict[str, Any]
    missing: dict[str, Any]
    cache, missing = {}, {}
    for e in lvl.entities:
        if e.blueprint is None or e.matrix is None:
            continue
        t = lo.collision(g, e.blueprint, cache, missing)
        alias = (info.get(e.blueprint) or (None, None))[1]
        if t is None and alias and alias != e.blueprint:
            t = lo.collision(g, alias, cache, missing)
        if t is not None:
            lvl.meshes.append(Mesh(e.index, lo.world(t, e.matrix)))
    lvl.missing_collision = sorted({bp for bps in missing.values() for bp in bps})
    # terrain and water: Terrains/<lv>/<lv>.* in the level's terrain bundle
    tname = terrain_name_1943(f.instances) or lv
    hf_data = g.data(f'terrains/{tname}/{tname}.heightfield-000.res')
    if hf_data:
        lvl.heightfield = terrain.read(hf_data)
        lvl.terrain = lvl.heightfield.mesh(terrain_stride)
    else:
        lvl.notes.append(f'no height field terrains/{tname}/{tname}.heightfield-000.res')
    mesh = g.data(f'terrains/{tname}/{tname}.water.mesh.res')
    if mesh:
        lvl.water = water_from_bytes(mesh)
    else:
        lvl.notes.append('no water mesh')
    # spawns no base owns (the carriers' boats, planes and guns): the side of the carrier they stand on
    carriers: list[tuple[int, npt.NDArray[np.float32], npt.NDArray[np.float32]]] = []
    for x in lvl.meshes:
        bp = lvl.entities[x.entity].blueprint or ''
        side = 1 if bp.endswith('/us_carrier') else 2 if bp.endswith('/jap_carrier') else None
        if side:
            v = x.triangles.reshape(-1, 3)
            carriers.append((side, v.min(0), v.max(0)))
    for e in lvl.entities:
        if e.category in ('vehicle spawn', 'soldier spawn') and not e.team and e.position is not None:
            p = e.position
            for side, lo_, hi_ in carriers:
                if lo_[0] <= p[0] <= hi_[0] and lo_[2] <= p[2] <= hi_[2] and lo_[1] - 1 <= p[1] <= hi_[1] + 1:
                    e.team = side
    n_tris = sum(len(x.triangles) for x in lvl.meshes)
    log(f'{lvl.name}: {len(lvl.entities)} entities, {len(lvl.meshes)} with collision ({n_tris} triangles), '
        f'{len(lvl.missing_collision)} blueprints without collision, '
        f'{len(lvl.objectives)} bases and flags')  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
    return lvl


def terrain_name_1943(instances: Iterable[dbx.Element]) -> str | None:
    """The terrain's name from TerrainEntityData.TerrainAsset (terrains/<name>/<name>/<guid>), or None."""
    for el in instances:
        if (el.attr('type') or '').endswith('.TerrainEntityData'):
            a = el.child('TerrainAsset')
            parts = ((a.attr('ref') or '') if a is not None else '').split('/')
            return parts[1].lower() if len(parts) >= 3 else None
    return None


def water_from_bytes(data: bytes) -> water.Water:
    """water.Water from a .Water.Mesh.res's bytes (water.read_mesh reads a file: a temporary one)."""
    import tempfile
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.water.mesh.res')
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as fh:
            fh.write(data)
        v, t = water.read_mesh(path)
    finally:
        os.remove(path)
    return water.Water(v, t)

```

`core/bfbc2core/materialmap1943.py`:

```py
"""A BF1943 level's terrain material map (TerrainMaterialMap .res, big-endian): the ground material under every
point of the terrain, 4096 x 4096 pixels over the height field's extent (0.5 m per pixel on the MP levels).

    mm = for_level(game, 'wake_island_s', heightfield)   # from the level's own bundles (game1943.Game)
    mm.names                                            # material names, by map index (the file's name table)
    mm.at(x, z)                                         # map indices at world points (arrays); -1 off the map
    mm.name_at(x, z)                                    # names

Format (operation-rising-sun research/GROUND_MATERIALS.md; decoded exactly on all four MP levels): u32 side, u16
tile count; then per tile (512 x 256 pixels, 8 across, row-major) u32 body size, the body, 256 u16 row lengths. A
row packs bytes as literals, or a pair of equal bytes followed by a count byte for count + 1 copies; each byte holds
two 4-bit indices, the low nibble the left pixel. Last, u32 size and NUL-separated names. Pixel (z, x) centres lie at
the height field's minimum + (index + 0.5) x pixel size, the height field's orientation.
"""
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass
from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, cast

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .game1943 import Game
    from .terrain import Heightfield


@dataclass
class MaterialMap:
    names: list[str]
    grid: npt.NDArray[np.uint8]  # (side, side) uint8 map index, [z, x]
    min_x: float = 0.0
    min_z: float = 0.0
    pixel: float = 1.0

    def at(self, x: npt.ArrayLike, z: npt.ArrayLike) -> npt.NDArray[np.int_]:
        side = self.grid.shape[0]
        i = np.floor((np.asarray(x, float) - self.min_x) / self.pixel).astype(int)
        j = np.floor((np.asarray(z, float) - self.min_z) / self.pixel).astype(int)
        ok = (i >= 0) & (i < side) & (j >= 0) & (j < side)
        out = np.full(np.shape(i), -1, int)
        out[ok] = self.grid[j[ok], i[ok]]
        return out

    def name_at(self, x: npt.ArrayLike, z: npt.ArrayLike) -> list[str | None]:
        k = np.atleast_1d(self.at(x, z))
        return [self.names[v] if 0 <= v < len(self.names) else None for v in k]


def read(data: bytes) -> MaterialMap:
    """MaterialMap(names, grid) from the .res bytes (no placement: see place). ValueError for a file that is not a
    whole material map."""
    if len(data) < 6:                   # 2026-10-31 fuzzing: a struct.error before
        raise ValueError(f'not a TerrainMaterialMap: {len(data)} bytes, shorter than its 6-byte header')
    side = struct.unpack_from('>I', data, 0)[0]
    tiles = struct.unpack_from('>H', data, 4)[0]
    tile_w_bytes, tile_rows = 256, 256
    tile_w = 2 * tile_w_bytes
    across = side // tile_w
    # at least one tile (a side of 0 read as an empty map, and place() then divided by zero), and every tile's size
    # word and row lengths inside the file before the map is made (2026-10-31 review: the count is a u16, so a few
    # damaged bytes could ask for a map of up to 65,535 tiles of 512 x 256 pixels, 8 GiB)
    if not side or across * tile_w != side or tiles != across * (side // tile_rows):
        raise ValueError(f'not a TerrainMaterialMap: side {side}, {tiles} tiles')
    if 6 + tiles * (4 + 512) + 4 > len(data):
        raise ValueError(f'not a TerrainMaterialMap: {tiles} tiles cannot fit in {len(data)} bytes')
    grid = np.zeros((side, side), np.uint8)
    p = 6
    for t in range(tiles):
        if p + 4 > len(data):
            raise ValueError(f'tile {t}: the file ends at {len(data)} bytes, before the tile')
        n = struct.unpack_from('>I', data, p)[0]
        if p + 4 + n + 512 > len(data):
            raise ValueError(f'tile {t}: {n} bytes of body and its row lengths run past the end of the file')
        body = data[p + 4:p + 4 + n]
        p += 4 + n
        lens = struct.unpack_from('>256H', data, p)
        p += 512
        if sum(lens) != n:
            raise ValueError(f'tile {t}: row lengths sum to {sum(lens)}, the body is {n} bytes')
        rows: list[bytes]
        rows, q = [], 0
        for ln in lens:
            row = body[q:q + ln]
            q += ln
            dec = bytearray()
            i = 0
            while i < len(row):
                b = row[i]
                if i + 1 < len(row) and row[i + 1] == b:
                    if i + 2 >= len(row):           # 2026-10-30 second review: an IndexError before
                        raise ValueError(f'tile {t}: a row ends inside a run (a pair with no count byte)')
                    dec += bytes([b]) * (row[i + 2] + 1)
                    i += 3
                else:
                    dec.append(b)
                    i += 1
            if len(dec) != tile_w_bytes:
                raise ValueError(f'tile {t}: a row decodes to {len(dec)} bytes, not {tile_w_bytes}')
            rows.append(bytes(dec))
        raw = np.frombuffer(b''.join(rows), np.uint8).reshape(tile_rows, tile_w_bytes)
        ty, tx = divmod(t, across)
        px = grid[ty * tile_rows:(ty + 1) * tile_rows, tx * tile_w:(tx + 1) * tile_w]
        px[:, 0::2] = raw & 0x0F
        px[:, 1::2] = raw >> 4
    if p + 4 > len(data):
        raise ValueError('the file ends before the name table')
    nbytes = struct.unpack_from('>I', data, p)[0]
    if p + 4 + nbytes != len(data):
        raise ValueError(f'{len(data) - p - 4 - nbytes} bytes after the name table')
    table = data[p + 4:p + 4 + nbytes]
    # every name ends with a zero byte, and every material the map uses has one (2026-10-30 second review: a last name
    # without its zero byte was dropped, and lookups of it gave None)
    if table and not table.endswith(b'\0'):
        last = table.rsplit(b'\0', 1)[-1][:40]
        raise ValueError(f'the name table\'s last name ({last!r}) does not end with a zero byte')
    try:
        names = [n.decode('ascii') for n in table.split(b'\0')[:-1]]
    except UnicodeDecodeError as e:     # a ValueError already; said in words
        raise ValueError(f'the name table holds a byte that is not ASCII ({e.object[e.start]:#x})') from None
    used = int(grid.max()) if grid.size else -1
    if used >= len(names):
        raise ValueError(f'the map uses material {used}, and the name table names {len(names)}')
    return MaterialMap(names, grid)


def place(mm: MaterialMap, heightfield: 'Heightfield') -> MaterialMap:
    """The map laid over the height field's extent."""
    mm.min_x, mm.min_z = float(heightfield.min[0]), float(heightfield.min[2])
    mm.pixel = float(heightfield.max[0] - heightfield.min[0]) / mm.grid.shape[0]
    return mm


def resource_name(game_index: Iterable[str], level: str) -> str | None:
    """The level's material map in the bundle index: terrains/<level>/<level>-materialmap.res, or on Coral Sea
    terrains/coral_sea/terrain.terrainmaterialmapasset.res. None when the level has none."""
    pre = f'terrains/{level}/'
    names = [n for n in game_index if n.startswith(pre) and n.endswith('.res') and 'materialmap' in n.lower()
             and '/textures/' not in n]
    return sorted(names)[0] if names else None


def for_level(game: 'Game', level: str, heightfield: 'Heightfield') -> MaterialMap | None:
    """The level's material map placed over its height field, from a game1943.Game (None when it has none)."""
    name = resource_name(game.names(), level)
    if name is None:
        return None
    return place(read(cast(bytes, game.data(name))), heightfield)     # a name from game.names(): its data is there

```

`core/bfbc2core/navdata.py`:

```py
"""A Kynapse path-data file (pathdata.hpd) as the suite's 3D tools draw it: walkable cells, area boundaries, the
route graph and its islands. Read with NavKit's byte-exact reader (bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools: hpdtool, kymesh,
navdiff); the format is in bf1943-auto-navkit-common/research/KYNAPSE_SPEC.md.

    nav = load(path, heightfield=None, cache_dir=None, y_offset=Y_OFFSET)
    nav.areas[k]                 NavArea: sector, tile, layer, pitch, boundary pieces, island
    nav.cell_xz, nav.cell_y      every walkable cell on the 0.8 m grid (navdiff's cells), its ground height
    nav.cell_area                the area each cell belongs to
    nav.node_pos, nav.edges      route graph: node positions (ground + nav.y_offset, as stored), edges as index pairs
    nav.edge_cost                each edge's cost in metres, as stored
    nav.node_island, nav.islands islands (connected parts of the graph), largest first
    nav.ladder_edge              the edges that are ladder links (LADDER_DY / LADDER_SLOPE)
    nav.y_offset                 how far above the ground the file stores nodes and outlines (load's y_offset)

Cells come from navdiff.area_cells (samples inside an area's boundary, height from the nearest boundary point, less
y_offset); where a cell and that boundary point lie on terrain (_ground), the terrain height field's height is used
instead. That step is slow for a whole level (10-40 s), so it is cached per file (size and date), y_offset and the
height field's contents when cache_dir is given.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pickle
import sys
import tempfile
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import IO, TYPE_CHECKING, Any

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .terrain import Heightfield

if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
# NavKit's shared tools (bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools, one of suitepath.SHARED: on sys.path from the script)
import hpdtool  # noqa: E402
import kymesh  # noqa: E402
import navdiff  # noqa: E402

GRID = navdiff.GRID
Y_OFFSET = navdiff.Y_OFFSET                 # boundaries and nodes are stored this far above the ground: DICE's 0.95,
                                            # load's default; BF1943 builds 0.9 (callers pass y_offset=
                                            # soldier1943.HEIGHT / 2). Cell heights use it too (navdiff.area_cells)
DETAILED = 0.5                              # areas with a smaller pitch are detailed zones (DICE: 0.2 m)
CACHE_VERSION = 6                           # 3: ladder links and ladder ground; 4: cell heights use Y_OFFSET;
                                            # 5: terrain heights only where the boundary lies on the terrain;
                                            # 6: NavData.y_offset (a version-5 entry has none)
LADDER_DY = 2.5                             # a ladder link: a route edge climbing more than this (m) ...
LADDER_SLOPE = 1.5                          # ... and more than this many metres per metre across - no walkable link is
                                            # that steep (DICE's files have none; NavKit's ladder links, ladders.py)


@dataclass
class NavArea:
    sector: int
    index: int                              # within its sector
    tile: tuple[int, int]
    layer: int
    pitch: float
    min_y: float
    max_y: float
    outline: list[npt.NDArray[np.float32]] = field(default_factory=list)  # polylines (ground + 0.95 m)
    portals: list[tuple[Any, ...]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (p0, p1, target area index in the sector)
    borders: list[tuple[Any, ...]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (p0, p1)
    island: int = -1                                             # index into NavData.islands
    cells: int = 0
    ladder: bool = False                                         # ground reached only through a ladder link

    @property
    def detailed(self) -> bool:
        return self.pitch < DETAILED


@dataclass
class Island:
    group: int                              # graph group id (a node id of the group)
    nodes: int
    cells: int
    centre: npt.NDArray[np.float64]


@dataclass
class NavData:
    path: str
    areas: list[NavArea]
    cell_xz: npt.NDArray[np.float64]        # (n, 2) cell centres
    cell_y: npt.NDArray[np.float64]         # (n,) ground height
    cell_area: npt.NDArray[np.int32]        # (n,) index into areas
    node_pos: npt.NDArray[np.float64]       # (m, 3)
    node_sector: npt.NDArray[np.int_]       # (m,)
    edges: npt.NDArray[np.int64]            # (k, 2) node indices, source -> destination
    edge_cost: npt.NDArray[np.float64]      # (k,) metres, as stored (the tag's floor(distance * 16) / 16)
    node_island: npt.NDArray[np.int32]      # (m,) index into islands
    islands: list[Island]
    ladder_edge: npt.NDArray[np.bool_] | None = None  # (k,) bool: the edge is a ladder link (LADDER_DY / LADDER_SLOPE)
    y_offset: float = Y_OFFSET              # node_pos and outlines stand this far above the ground (load's y_offset)

    @property
    def sectors(self) -> list[int]:
        return sorted({a.sector for a in self.areas})


def terrain_digest(heightfield: object) -> str | None:
    """A hash of the height field's contents (bounds, size, samples), or None for a height source without them
    (whose results are then not cached). 2026-10-30: the key held only whether there was a height field, so a
    changed terrain under an unchanged .hpd got the old terrain's cell heights back from the cache."""
    raw = getattr(heightfield, 'raw', None)
    if raw is None:
        raw = getattr(heightfield, 'heights', None)
    if raw is None:
        return None
    h = hashlib.sha1(np.ascontiguousarray(raw).tobytes())
    for v in (getattr(heightfield, 'min', None), getattr(heightfield, 'max', None), getattr(heightfield, 'size', None)):
        h.update(np.asarray(v, np.float64).tobytes() if v is not None else b'-')
    return h.hexdigest()[:20]


def _key(path: str, heightfield: object = None, y_offset: float = Y_OFFSET) -> str:
    st = os.stat(path)
    hf = f'hf:{terrain_digest(heightfield)}' if heightfield is not None else 'est'
    return hashlib.sha1(f'{CACHE_VERSION}|{os.path.abspath(path).lower()}|{st.st_size}|{st.st_mtime_ns}|{hf}|{y_offset}'.encode()).hexdigest()[:20]


ON_TERRAIN = 0.1                            # m: a boundary point lies on the terrain when its ground height is within
                                            # the terrain's height range half a cell around it, plus this


def _ground(xz: npt.NDArray[np.float64], est: npt.NDArray[np.float64], heightfield: 'Heightfield | None',
            near: npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None = None) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Cell heights: the terrain height field's where the cell lies on terrain, else navdiff's estimate (the nearest
    boundary point's ground height). On terrain: the estimate is within 1.5 m of the terrain at the cell, and the
    boundary point the estimate came from (near, (n, 2) x, z) lies on the terrain itself - without that test a floor
    up to 1.5 m above the terrain (a house's, Wake Island's beach houses: 1.0 m) took the terrain's height."""
    if heightfield is None or not len(xz):
        return est
    t = heightfield.height(xz[:, 0], xz[:, 1])
    on = np.abs(t - est) < 1.5
    if near is not None:
        h = GRID / 2
        ring = np.stack([heightfield.height(near[:, 0] + dx, near[:, 1] + dz)
                         for dx, dz in ((0, 0), (h, 0), (-h, 0), (0, h), (0, -h))])
        on &= (est >= ring.min(0) - ON_TERRAIN) & (est <= ring.max(0) + ON_TERRAIN)
    return np.where(on, t, est)


def _write_cache(path: str, write: Callable[[IO[bytes]], object]) -> None:
    """A cache file written beside itself and moved into place, so a tool closed while writing never leaves one cut
    short (2026-10-30: a cut .npz failed every later load of that level until deleted by hand)."""
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=os.path.dirname(path), prefix='.navdata-', suffix='.tmp')
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'wb') as fh:
            write(fh)
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.remove(tmp)
        raise


def _cells(f: hpdtool.HpdFile, heightfield: 'Heightfield | None', cache_dir: str | None, path: str,
           y_offset: float) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float64], npt.NDArray[np.float64], npt.NDArray[np.int32],
                                     npt.NDArray[np.float64]]:
    if cache_dir:
        cp = os.path.join(cache_dir, _key(path, y_offset=y_offset) + '.npz')
        if os.path.isfile(cp):
            try:
                with np.load(cp) as z:
                    xz, est, near, area = z['xz'], z['est'], z['near'], z['area']
                return xz, _ground(xz, est, heightfield, near), area, est
            except Exception:
                pass                                         # an unreadable cache entry is rebuilt
    xz, ys, nears, area_of = [], [], [], []
    k = 0
    for s in f.sectors:
        for a in kymesh.parse_mesh(s.mesh).areas:
            c = navdiff.area_cells(a, y_offset, points=True)
            if c:
                ij = np.array(list(c.keys()), dtype=np.float64)
                v = np.array(list(c.values()), dtype=np.float64)
                xz.append(ij * GRID)
                ys.append(v[:, 0])
                nears.append(v[:, 1:])
                area_of.append(np.full(len(c), k, dtype=np.int32))
            k += 1
    xz = np.concatenate(xz) if xz else np.zeros((0, 2))
    est = np.concatenate(ys) if ys else np.zeros(0)
    near = np.concatenate(nears) if nears else np.zeros((0, 2))
    area = np.concatenate(area_of) if area_of else np.zeros(0, np.int32)
    y = _ground(xz, est, heightfield, near)
    if cache_dir:
        _write_cache(os.path.join(cache_dir, _key(path, y_offset=y_offset) + '.npz'),
                     lambda fh: np.savez(fh, xz=xz, y=y, area=area, est=est, near=near))
    return xz, y, area, est


def load(path: str, heightfield: 'Heightfield | None' = None, cache_dir: str | None = None,
         y_offset: float = Y_OFFSET) -> NavData:
    """The file as NavData. y_offset: how far above the ground the file stores its nodes and outlines (DICE's 0.95;
    a BF1943 build's soldier1943.HEIGHT / 2). With cache_dir, the whole result is kept there per file (and per height
    source and y_offset), so opening a level again takes about a second. The key holds the height field's contents
    (terrain_digest)."""
    if cache_dir and (heightfield is None or terrain_digest(heightfield) is not None):
        pk = os.path.join(cache_dir, _key(path, heightfield, y_offset) + '.navdata.pkl')
        if os.path.isfile(pk):
            try:
                with open(pk, 'rb') as fh:
                    return pickle.load(fh)
            except Exception:
                pass                                         # an unreadable cache entry is rebuilt
        nav = _load(path, heightfield, cache_dir, y_offset)
        _write_cache(pk, lambda fh: pickle.dump(nav, fh, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL))
        return nav
    return _load(path, heightfield, None, y_offset)


AREA_EXTENT = 128.0                         # m: an area lies in one tile of its 100 m sector (KYNAPSE_SPEC.md); the
                                            # largest in the four BF1943 builds spans 41.6 m


def _check_area(path: str, sector: int, n: int, a: kymesh.Area) -> None:
    """ValueError unless the area's boundary points (navdiff.segments: outlines, portals, border portals) are finite
    and span at most AREA_EXTENT on x and z. 2026-10-31 fuzzing: an infinite point raised OverflowError in
    navdiff.area_cells; review: one 1e30 m away made it sample every 0.8 m of the box between, without end."""
    pts = ([q for line in a.outline for q in line] + [q for p in a.portals for q in (p.p0, p.p1)]
           + [q for b in a.border_portals for q in (b.p0, b.p1)])
    if not pts:
        return
    v = np.asarray(pts, dtype=np.float64)
    if not np.isfinite(v).all():
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: sector {sector:#06x} area {n} has a boundary point that is not a finite number')
    span = max(float(np.ptp(v[:, 0])), float(np.ptp(v[:, 2])))
    if span > AREA_EXTENT:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: sector {sector:#06x} area {n} spans {span:.1f} m, more than a sector '
                         f'({AREA_EXTENT:g} m at most)')


def _load(path: str, heightfield: 'Heightfield | None', cache_dir: str | None, y_offset: float = Y_OFFSET) -> NavData:
    f = hpdtool.parse(open(path, 'rb').read())
    areas: list[NavArea] = []
    for s in f.sectors:
        for n, a in enumerate(kymesh.parse_mesh(s.mesh).areas):
            _check_area(path, s.id, n, a)
            areas.append(NavArea(s.id, n, (a.tile_x, a.tile_z), a.layer, a.pitch, a.min_y, a.max_y,
                                 [np.asarray(l, dtype=np.float32) for l in a.outline if len(l) >= 2],
                                 [(np.asarray(p.p0), np.asarray(p.p1), p.target) for p in a.portals],
                                 [(np.asarray(b.p0), np.asarray(b.p1)) for b in a.border_portals]))
    xz, y, cell_area, _ = _cells(f, heightfield, cache_dir, path, y_offset)
    counts = np.bincount(cell_area, minlength=len(areas)) if len(cell_area) else np.zeros(len(areas), int)
    for a, n in zip(areas, counts):
        a.cells = int(n)

    # route graph: border nodes repeat in both sectors with the same id - one node per id
    index, pos, sec, edges, costs = {}, [], [], [], []
    for s in f.sectors:
        local = []
        n = len(s.nodes)
        for e in s.edges:                   # 2026-10-31 fuzzing: an IndexError before
            if e.src >= n or e.dst >= n:
                raise ValueError(f'{path}: sector {s.id:#06x} has an edge {e.src} -> {e.dst} past its {n} nodes')
        for nd in s.nodes:
            if nd.id not in index:
                index[nd.id] = len(pos)
                pos.append(nd.pos)
                sec.append(s.id)
            local.append(index[nd.id])
        for e in s.edges:
            edges.append((local[e.src], local[e.dst]))
            costs.append((e.tag & 0x7FFFFFFF) / 16.0)
    pos = np.array(pos, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 3)
    edges = np.array(edges, dtype=np.int64).reshape(-1, 2)
    parent = np.arange(len(pos))

    def find(a: int) -> int:
        while parent[a] != a:
            parent[a] = parent[parent[a]]
            a = parent[a]
        return a
    for a, b in edges:
        ra, rb = find(a), find(b)
        if ra != rb:
            parent[ra] = rb
    roots = np.array([find(k) for k in range(len(pos))], dtype=np.int64)
    # ladder links, and the walking parts of each island (its components without them): ground on any walking
    # part but the island's largest is reached through a ladder - ladder ground
    if len(edges):
        d = pos[edges[:, 1]] - pos[edges[:, 0]]
        dy, h = np.abs(d[:, 1]), np.hypot(d[:, 0], d[:, 2])
        ladder_edge = (dy > LADDER_DY) & (dy > LADDER_SLOPE * h)
    else:
        ladder_edge = np.zeros(0, bool)
    walk = np.arange(len(pos))

    def wfind(a: int) -> int:
        while walk[a] != a:
            walk[a] = walk[walk[a]]
            a = walk[a]
        return a
    for (a, b), lad in zip(edges, ladder_edge):
        if not lad:
            ra, rb = wfind(a), wfind(b)
            if ra != rb:
                walk[ra] = rb
    walk_root = np.array([wfind(k) for k in range(len(pos))], dtype=np.int64)
    base = {}
    if ladder_edge.any():
        wsize = Counter(walk_root.tolist())
        for k in range(len(pos)):
            r, w = roots[k], walk_root[k]
            if r not in base or wsize[w] > wsize[base[r]]:
                base[r] = w
    sizes = Counter(roots.tolist())
    order = [r for r, _ in sizes.most_common()]
    rank = {r: k for k, r in enumerate(order)}
    node_island = np.array([rank[r] for r in roots], dtype=np.int32)

    # each area's island: the graph node of its sector nearest to the area's cells (an area has its own node,
    # near its centre; tiny areas without one take their neighbour's)
    sec_nodes = {}
    for k, s in enumerate(sec):
        sec_nodes.setdefault(s, []).append(k)
    sec_nodes = {s: np.array(v) for s, v in sec_nodes.items()}
    centre = np.zeros((len(areas), 3))
    if len(cell_area):
        for d in range(2):
            centre[:, [0, 2][d]] = np.bincount(cell_area, weights=xz[:, d], minlength=len(areas)) / np.maximum(counts, 1)
        centre[:, 1] = np.bincount(cell_area, weights=y, minlength=len(areas)) / np.maximum(counts, 1)
    for k, a in enumerate(areas):
        cand = sec_nodes.get(a.sector)
        if cand is None or not len(cand):
            continue
        p = pos[cand]
        d = np.hypot(p[:, 0] - centre[k, 0], p[:, 2] - centre[k, 2]) + 3.0 * np.abs(p[:, 1] - y_offset - centre[k, 1])
        kn = cand[int(np.argmin(d))]
        a.island = int(node_island[kn])
        a.ladder = bool(base) and walk_root[kn] != base[roots[kn]]
    island_cells = Counter()
    for a in areas:
        island_cells[a.island] += a.cells
    islands: list[Island] = []
    for k, r in enumerate(order):
        sel = node_island == k
        islands.append(Island(int(r), int(sel.sum()), int(island_cells.get(k, 0)), pos[sel].mean(axis=0)))
    return NavData(path, areas, xz, y, cell_area, pos, np.array(sec), edges, np.array(costs, dtype=np.float64),
                   node_island, islands, ladder_edge, y_offset)


def compare_cells(cand: NavData, ref: NavData) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.bool_], npt.NDArray[np.bool_]]:
    """Per cell of each file: True where the other file has the same ground (navdiff's rule: the same 0.8 m
    cell; one floor on each side is the same ground, stacked floors pair by height within 4 m)."""
    def keyed(nav: NavData) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
        ij = np.round(nav.cell_xz / GRID).astype(np.int64)
        return (ij[:, 0] + 50_000) * 100_000 + (ij[:, 1] + 50_000)

    kc, kr = keyed(cand), keyed(ref)
    yc, yr = np.asarray(cand.cell_y, np.float64), np.asarray(ref.cell_y, np.float64)

    def same(keys: npt.NDArray[np.int64], y: npt.NDArray[np.float64], okeys: npt.NDArray[np.int64],
             oy: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> npt.NDArray[np.bool_]:
        """For each (key, y): does the other file have the key, and (one floor each) or a floor within STACK_TOL?"""
        uk, counts = np.unique(keys, return_counts=True)
        mine_n = counts[np.searchsorted(uk, keys)]
        order = np.lexsort((oy, okeys))
        sk, sy = okeys[order], oy[order]
        lo, hi = np.searchsorted(sk, keys, 'left'), np.searchsorted(sk, keys, 'right')
        other_n = hi - lo
        # the other file's nearest floor at the same key: composite (key, height) values, sorted - the
        # neighbours of (key, y) in that order are the nearest floors below and above
        comp_o = sk.astype(np.float64) * 1e5 + (sy + 2e4)
        comp_m = keys.astype(np.float64) * 1e5 + (y + 2e4)
        p = np.searchsorted(comp_o, comp_m)
        best = np.full(len(keys), np.inf)
        for q in (p - 1, p):
            ok = (q >= 0) & (q < len(sk))
            qq = np.clip(q, 0, max(len(sk) - 1, 0))
            hit = ok & (sk[qq] == keys) if len(sk) else np.zeros(len(keys), bool)
            best = np.where(hit, np.minimum(best, np.abs(sy[qq] - y) if len(sk) else best), best)
        return (other_n > 0) & (((other_n == 1) & (mine_n == 1)) | (best <= navdiff.STACK_TOL))
    return same(kc, yc, kr, yr), same(kr, yr, kc, yc)


def summary(nav: NavData) -> dict[str, int]:
    return {'areas': len(nav.areas), 'detailed areas': sum(a.detailed for a in nav.areas), 'cells': int(len(nav.cell_xz)),
            'nodes': int(len(nav.node_pos)), 'edges': int(len(nav.edges)), 'islands': len(nav.islands),
            'large islands (25+ nodes)': sum(i.nodes >= 25 for i in nav.islands), 'sectors': len(nav.sectors),
            'ladder links': int(nav.ladder_edge.sum() // 2) if nav.ladder_edge is not None else 0,
            'ladder ground cells': sum(a.cells for a in nav.areas if a.ladder)}


if __name__ == '__main__':
    nav = load(sys.argv[1])
    print(json.dumps(summary(nav), indent=1))
```

`core/bfbc2core/navpath.py`:

```py
"""The path test: a route between two points over a path-data file's route graph, or why there is none.

    r = route(nav, start, end)          # nav: navdata.NavData; start, end: world (x, y, z) on the ground
    r.found, r.nodes, r.cost, r.reason, r.start_island, r.end_island, r.gap

The points are joined to the graph at the nearest route node within 15 m horizontally and 4 m in height (as
the studio's spawn check does); the route is the cheapest over the file's own directed edges and their
stored costs (A*, straight-line distance times the graph's least cost per metre as the estimate, so the cheapest
route is found although the stored costs are rounded down). Without a route, the result says which island
each point is on and where the two islands come closest. This plans over the graph only: the game also
smooths the route through the areas, which this does not do (DESIGN.md section 7, question 4).
"""
import heapq
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

import numpy as np
import numpy.typing as npt

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .navdata import NavData

JOIN_XZ, JOIN_Y = 15.0, 4.0


@dataclass
class Route:
    found: bool
    nodes: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)        # node indices, start to end
    cost: float = 0.0                                     # sum of the stored edge costs (m)
    length: float = 0.0                                   # 3-D length of the node chain (m)
    straight: float = 0.0                                 # start to end, straight (m)
    start_node: int | None = None
    end_node: int | None = None
    start_join: float = 0.0                               # metres from the point to its node
    end_join: float = 0.0
    start_island: int | None = None
    end_island: int | None = None
    gap: tuple[int | None, int | None, float] | None = None  # (node in start island, node in end island, metres)
    reason: str = ''
    expanded: int = 0


def ground_nodes(nav: 'NavData') -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    return nav.node_pos - np.array([0, nav.y_offset, 0])


def join(nav: 'NavData', p: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> tuple[int | None, float]:
    """(node index, horizontal distance) nearest to p within the join limits, or (None, distance)."""
    if not len(nav.node_pos):
        return None, np.inf
    ground = ground_nodes(nav)
    dist = np.hypot(ground[:, 0] - p[0], ground[:, 2] - p[2])
    dist = np.where(np.abs(ground[:, 1] - p[1]) <= JOIN_Y, dist, np.inf)
    nearest = int(np.argmin(dist))
    if dist[nearest] <= JOIN_XZ:
        return nearest, float(dist[nearest])
    return None, float(dist[nearest])


def _adjacency(nav: 'NavData') -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.intp], npt.NDArray[np.int64], npt.NDArray[np.float64]]:
    """(first edge per node, edge targets, edge costs), the edges grouped by their source node; kept on nav."""
    cache = getattr(nav, '_adj', None)
    if cache is None:
        if len(nav.edges):
            order = np.argsort(nav.edges[:, 0], kind='stable')
            sources, targets, costs = nav.edges[order, 0], nav.edges[order, 1], nav.edge_cost[order]
        else:
            sources, targets, costs = np.zeros(0, int), np.zeros(0, int), np.zeros(0)
        first_edge = np.searchsorted(sources, np.arange(len(nav.node_pos) + 1))
        cache = (first_edge, targets, costs)
        # a cache kept on the object, not a NavData field
        nav._adj = cache  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
    return cache


def cost_scale(nav: 'NavData') -> float:
    """The least stored cost per metre of length over the graph's edges, at most 1 (0 when an edge of some length
    costs nothing): the straight-line estimate times this never exceeds a route's cost. 2026-10-30 second review: the
    stored costs are rounded down to 1/16 m, so the plain distance overestimated and a dearer route came back (5.1875
    where one of 5.125 existed)."""
    cache = getattr(nav, '_cost_scale', None)
    if cache is not None:
        return cache
    scale = 1.0
    if len(nav.edges):
        delta = nav.node_pos[nav.edges[:, 1]] - nav.node_pos[nav.edges[:, 0]]
        length = np.linalg.norm(delta, axis=1)
        has_length = length > 0
        if has_length.any():
            least = float((np.asarray(nav.edge_cost, float)[has_length] / length[has_length]).min())
            scale = max(0.0, min(1.0, least * (1.0 - 1e-9)))
    nav._cost_scale = scale  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]  # as _adj
    return scale


def closest_between(nav: 'NavData', ia: int, ib: int) -> tuple[int | None, int | None, float] | None:
    """The closest pair of nodes of two islands (horizontal metres)."""
    nodes_a = np.nonzero(nav.node_island == ia)[0]
    nodes_b = np.nonzero(nav.node_island == ib)[0]
    if not len(nodes_a) or not len(nodes_b):
        return None
    xz_a, xz_b = nav.node_pos[nodes_a][:, [0, 2]], nav.node_pos[nodes_b][:, [0, 2]]
    best = (None, None, np.inf)
    for chunk in range(0, len(xz_a), 512):                 # 512 nodes of island a at a time against all of b
        part = xz_a[chunk:chunk + 512]
        dist = np.hypot(part[:, None, 0] - xz_b[None, :, 0], part[:, None, 1] - xz_b[None, :, 1])
        i, j = np.unravel_index(int(np.argmin(dist)), dist.shape)
        if dist[i, j] < best[2]:
            best = (int(nodes_a[chunk + i]), int(nodes_b[j]), float(dist[i, j]))
    return best


def route(nav: 'NavData', start: npt.ArrayLike, end: npt.ArrayLike) -> Route:
    start, end = np.asarray(start, float), np.asarray(end, float)
    result = Route(False, straight=float(np.linalg.norm(end - start)))
    result.start_node, result.start_join = join(nav, start)
    result.end_node, result.end_join = join(nav, end)
    if result.start_node is None or result.end_node is None:
        which = 'start' if result.start_node is None else 'end'
        nearest = result.start_join if which == 'start' else result.end_join
        result.reason = (f'no route node within {JOIN_XZ:.0f} m of the {which} point '
                         f'(nearest {min(nearest, 9999):.0f} m)')
        return result
    result.start_island = int(nav.node_island[result.start_node])
    result.end_island = int(nav.node_island[result.end_node])
    first_edge, edge_target, edge_cost = _adjacency(nav)
    pos = nav.node_pos
    goal = result.end_node
    scale = cost_scale(nav)                                     # an estimate that never exceeds the stored costs
    best_cost = {result.start_node: 0.0}
    came_from: dict[int, int] = {}
    heap = [(scale * float(np.linalg.norm(pos[result.start_node] - pos[goal])), 0.0, result.start_node)]
    closed: set[int] = set()
    while heap:
        _, cost, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if node in closed:
            continue
        closed.add(node)
        if node == goal:
            break
        for k in range(first_edge[node], first_edge[node + 1]):
            neighbour = int(edge_target[k])
            new_cost = cost + float(edge_cost[k])
            if new_cost < best_cost.get(neighbour, np.inf):
                best_cost[neighbour] = new_cost
                came_from[neighbour] = node
                estimate = scale * float(np.linalg.norm(pos[neighbour] - pos[goal]))
                heapq.heappush(heap, (new_cost + estimate, new_cost, neighbour))
    result.expanded = len(closed)
    if goal not in closed:
        if result.start_island != result.end_island:
            result.gap = closest_between(nav, result.start_island, result.end_island)
            if result.gap:
                result.reason = (f'the points are on different islands ({result.start_island} and '
                                 f'{result.end_island}); they come closest {result.gap[2]:.1f} m apart')
            else:
                result.reason = f'the points are on different islands ({result.start_island}, {result.end_island})'
        else:
            result.reason = 'same island, but no route along the edges\' directions (one-way edges)'
        return result
    chain = [goal]
    while chain[-1] != result.start_node:
        chain.append(came_from[chain[-1]])
    result.nodes = chain[::-1]
    result.cost = best_cost[goal]
    if len(result.nodes) > 1:
        result.length = float(np.sum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(pos[result.nodes], axis=0), axis=1)))
    else:
        result.length = 0.0
    result.found = True
    return result

```

`core/bfbc2core/navtune.py`:

```py
"""Navigation side files: `<level>.navtune.json` (DESIGN.md section 5.1) - the edits made to a level's AI
navigation data, recorded by position so they still apply after the level is regenerated.

    t = NavTune.new('Levels/SP_01', base_path, kind='navkit')     # or load(path)
    t.add(op('unwalkable', region=box(...)))                       # by / when filled in
    t.undo(); t.redo()
    t.save(path)

Bases: 'navkit' (NavKit's output; every operation allowed) or 'dice' (the level's own path data; only additive
operations: links, route edges, traversal annotations, notes - DESIGN.md section 5.1, decided 2026-10-16).
Each operation records who made it (`by`: the PC's name unless set) and when (`when`, local time).
"""
import copy
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import socket
from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
from typing import Any

FORMAT, VERSION = 'bfbc2-navtune', 1
KINDS = ('navkit', 'dice')
TRAVERSALS = ('ladder', 'jump', 'vault', 'drop')
# operation -> required fields (besides op, by, when)
OPS = {
    'walkable': ('region',),
    'unwalkable': ('region',),
    'seed': ('at',),
    'unseed': ('at',),
    'link-areas': ('a', 'b'),
    'route-edge': ('a', 'b', 'action'),
    'traversal': ('kind', 'bottom', 'top'),
    'note': ('at', 'text'),
}
REGION_OPS = ('walkable', 'unwalkable', 'seed', 'unseed')          # need a rebuild: NavKit bases only


def author() -> str:
    """The name recorded with edits: the PC's name (Windows' computer name)."""
    return os.environ.get('COMPUTERNAME') or socket.gethostname() or 'unknown'


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.datetime.now().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()


def sha1_of(path: str) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b''):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def polygon(points: Iterable[Sequence[float]], y_low: float, y_high: float) -> dict[str, list[Any]]:
    return {'polygon': [[round(float(x), 3), round(float(z), 3)] for x, z in points], 'y': [round(float(y_low), 3), round(float(y_high), 3)]}


def box(x0: float, y0: float, z0: float, x1: float, y1: float, z1: float) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
    lo = [min(x0, x1), min(y0, y1), min(z0, z1)]
    hi = [max(x0, x1), max(y0, y1), max(z0, z1)]
    return {'box': [round(float(v), 3) for v in lo + hi]}


def point(p: Iterable[float]) -> list[float]:
    return [round(float(v), 3) for v in p]


def op(name: str, by: str | None = None, when: str | None = None, **fields: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """An operation with its fields; positions may be numpy arrays (stored rounded to millimetres)."""
    o: dict[str, Any] = {'op': name}
    for k, v in fields.items():
        if k in ('at', 'a', 'b', 'bottom', 'top'):
            v = point(v)
        o[k] = v
    o['by'] = by or author()
    o['when'] = when or now()
    return o


def validate(o: dict[str, Any], kind: str = 'navkit') -> list[str]:
    """Problems with one operation (empty list: fine)."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    name = o.get('op')
    if name not in OPS:
        return [f'unknown operation {name!r}']
    for k in OPS[name]:
        if k not in o:
            problems.append(f'{name}: {k} missing')
    if kind == 'dice' and name in REGION_OPS:
        problems.append(f'{name}: not allowed on a DICE base (region edits need a NavKit base)')
    for k in ('at', 'a', 'b', 'bottom', 'top'):
        if k in o and not (isinstance(o[k], list) and len(o[k]) == 3 and all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) for v in o[k])):
            problems.append(f'{name}: {k} must be [x, y, z]')
    if 'region' in o:
        r = o['region']
        if 'polygon' in r:
            if len(r['polygon']) < 3 or any(len(p) != 2 for p in r['polygon']):
                problems.append(f'{name}: a polygon needs 3 or more [x, z] points')
            if len(r.get('y', [])) != 2 or r['y'][0] > r['y'][1]:
                problems.append(f'{name}: y must be [low, high]')
        elif 'box' in r:
            b = r['box']
            if len(b) != 6 or any(b[k] > b[k + 3] for k in range(3)):
                problems.append(f'{name}: box must be [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1] with each low <= high')
        else:
            problems.append(f'{name}: region must be a polygon or a box')
    if 'two-way' in o and not isinstance(o['two-way'], bool):
        problems.append(f'{name}: two-way must be true or false')
    if name == 'route-edge' and o.get('action') not in ('add', 'remove'):
        problems.append('route-edge: action must be add or remove')
    if name == 'traversal':
        if o.get('kind') not in TRAVERSALS:
            problems.append(f'traversal: kind must be one of {", ".join(TRAVERSALS)}')
    if name == 'note' and not str(o.get('text', '')).strip():
        problems.append('note: text is empty')
    return problems


class NavTune:
    def __init__(self, level: str, base: dict[str, Any], operations: Iterable[dict[str, Any]] | None = None) -> None:
        self.level = level
        self.base = base                       # {'kind', 'sha1', 'file'}
        self.operations = list(operations or [])
        self.redo_stack: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.dirty = False

    @classmethod
    def new(cls, level: str, base_path: str, kind: str = 'navkit') -> 'NavTune':
        if kind not in KINDS:
            raise ValueError(f'base kind must be one of {KINDS}')
        return cls(level, {'kind': kind, 'sha1': sha1_of(base_path), 'file': os.path.basename(base_path)})

    @property
    def kind(self) -> str:
        return self.base.get('kind', 'navkit')

    def allowed(self, name: str) -> bool:
        return not (self.kind == 'dice' and name in REGION_OPS)

    def add(self, o: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        problems = validate(o, self.kind)
        if problems:
            raise ValueError('; '.join(problems))
        self.operations.append(o)
        self.redo_stack.clear()
        self.dirty = True
        return o

    def remove(self, index: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        o = self.operations.pop(index)
        self.redo_stack.clear()
        self.dirty = True
        return o

    def undo(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        if not self.operations:
            return None
        o = self.operations.pop()
        self.redo_stack.append(o)
        self.dirty = True
        return o

    def redo(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        if not self.redo_stack:
            return None
        o = self.redo_stack.pop()
        self.operations.append(o)
        self.dirty = True
        return o

    def base_changed(self, base_path: str) -> bool:
        """True when the file at base_path is not the one the edits were made on."""
        return bool(self.base.get('sha1')) and sha1_of(base_path) != self.base['sha1']

    def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {'format': FORMAT, 'version': VERSION, 'level': self.level, 'base': self.base,
                'operations': copy.deepcopy(self.operations)}

    def save(self, path: str) -> None:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), exist_ok=True)
        tmp = path + '.tmp'
        with open(tmp, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            json.dump(self.to_json(), f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write('\n')
        os.replace(tmp, path)                  # never a half-written side file
        self.dirty = False

    def summary(self, k: int) -> str:
        o = self.operations[k]
        name = o['op']
        if 'region' in o:
            r = o['region']
            where = f'polygon of {len(r["polygon"])} points, y {r["y"][0]:.1f}..{r["y"][1]:.1f}' if 'polygon' in r else \
                f'box {r["box"][3] - r["box"][0]:.1f} x {r["box"][4] - r["box"][1]:.1f} x {r["box"][5] - r["box"][2]:.1f} m'
        elif name == 'traversal':
            where = f'{o["kind"]}{" (two-way)" if o.get("two-way", True) else ""} {fmt(o["bottom"])} -> {fmt(o["top"])}'
        elif 'a' in o:
            where = f'{fmt(o["a"])} -> {fmt(o["b"])}' + (f' ({o["action"]})' if 'action' in o else '')
        else:
            where = fmt(o['at']) + (f': {o["text"]}' if 'text' in o else '')
        return f'{name}: {where}  [{o.get("by", "?")}, {o.get("when", "?")}]'


def fmt(p: Iterable[float]) -> str:
    return '(' + ', '.join(f'{v:.1f}' for v in p) + ')'


def load(path: str) -> NavTune:
    d = json.load(open(path, encoding='utf-8'))
    if d.get('format') != FORMAT:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: not a navtune side file')
    if d.get('version', 0) > VERSION:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: version {d["version"]} is newer than this tool reads ({VERSION})')
    t = NavTune(d.get('level', ''), d.get('base', {}), d.get('operations', []))
    problems = [f'operation {k}: {p}' for k, o in enumerate(t.operations) for p in validate(o, t.kind)]
    if problems:
        raise ValueError(f'{path}: ' + '; '.join(problems[:10]))
    return t


def default_path(root: str, lv: str) -> str:
    """Where the studio keeps a level's side file: OPFOR's work\\navkit\\<level>\\<level>.navtune.json."""
    return os.path.join(root, 'work', 'navkit', lv, f'{lv}.navtune.json')

```

`core/bfbc2core/pick.py`:

```py
"""A small level picker for the suite's 3D tools, shown when they are started without a level (a double-click,
or `python studio.py` alone): the levels of your BF1943 copy (game1943.find_game), double-click or OK to open one.

    lv = pick_level('BF1943 Navigation Studio')     # the level name, or None when cancelled
"""
import os

from . import game1943


def levels() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """[(level, state)]: each level of the game copy, and whether NavKit has built its navigation (work folder)."""
    out: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for lv in game1943.levels():
        built = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(game1943.level_work(lv), 'navkit', f'{lv}.hpd'))
        kind = 'multiplayer map' if lv in game1943.MP_LEVELS else 'other level'
        out.append((lv, kind + (', navigation built' if built else '')))
    return out


def pick_level(title: str) -> str | None:
    import tkinter as tk
    from tkinter import messagebox, ttk
    try:
        import ctypes
        ctypes.windll.shcore.SetProcessDpiAwareness(1)      # sharp on scaled displays
    except (AttributeError, OSError):
        pass
    root = tk.Tk()
    root.title(title)
    root.minsize(460, 420)
    try:
        ttk.Style().theme_use('vista')
    except tk.TclError:
        pass
    try:
        items = levels()
    except Exception as e:
        messagebox.showerror(title, f'No BF1943 game copy found: {e}')
        root.destroy()
        return None
    chosen: list[str] = []
```
