```py
        script('NavKit (both variants): Havok 4.6.1 meshes, and the collision reader on them', 'bf1943',
               NAVKIT_COMMON, 'test_havok461.py'),
        script('Level loader: every multiplayer map', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'level'),
        script('DbxEdit and LevelDiff on BF1943 partitions', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'dbxedit'),
        script('DbxEdit level check: BF1943 rules', 'bf1943', 'bf1943-dbx-tools', 'test_levelcheck1943.py'),
        script('Bundle tool command line', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'fbrb'),
        script('NavKit big-endian: navkit.py prepare', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'navkit'),
        script('the suite window (hub)', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'hub'),
        script('3D tools: Map Inspector, Navigation Studio', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'viewers'),
        script('NavKit big-endian: enclosure probe on Wake Island', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'probe'),
        script('NavKit big-endian: RSNV export of your builds', 'bf1943', NAVKIT_BE, 'test_navexport1943.py'),
        script('executable tools from the research workspace', 'bf1943', '', 'test_bf1943_tools.py', 'xex'),
    ]


def run_one(args: list[str]) -> tuple[str, str, str, list[str]]:
    """Runs one test as the runner does: (status, its last line, its output, its skip lines). status: 'FAIL' (a
    nonzero exit), 'SKIP' (its last line starts "skip": the whole test, its data is missing), 'ok* ' (passed, but
    some checks were skipped) or 'ok  '."""
    result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', cwd=SUITE,
                            # no __pycache__, their children too; output in UTF-8, as it is read (2026-10-30 second
                            # review: a test printing a path outside the ANSI code page died in the pipe)
                            env=dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1', PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8'))
    out = (result.stdout + result.stderr).strip()
    # the summary line is the test's own last line, not a warning it printed
    main_out = result.stdout.strip() or out
    lines = main_out.splitlines()
    last = lines[-1] if lines else ''
    skips = [line for line in lines if line.lower().startswith('skip')]
    if result.returncode != 0:
        status = 'FAIL'
    elif skips and last.lower().startswith('skip'):
        status = 'SKIP'
    elif skips:
        status = 'ok* '
    else:
        status = 'ok  '
    return status, last, out, skips


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if '--only' in argv and argv.index('--only') + 1 >= len(argv):
        # 2026-10-30: an IndexError before; a usage error like any other
        print('error: --only needs a part of a test\'s name')
        print(USAGE)
        return 2
    only = argv[argv.index('--only') + 1].lower() if '--only' in argv else None
    rest = list(argv[1:])
    if '--only' in rest:
        del rest[rest.index('--only'):rest.index('--only') + 2]       # its value is a name, not a tier
    tiers = [arg for arg in rest if arg in SELECT]
    unknown = [arg for arg in rest if arg not in SELECT and arg not in ('--list', '--strict')]
    if unknown or len(tiers) > 1:
        # a misspelled tier must not quietly run another one (and pass)
        problem = 'unknown tier or option ' + repr(unknown[0]) if unknown else 'more than one tier: ' + ' '.join(tiers)
        print(f'error: {problem}')
        print(USAGE)
        return 2
    tier = tiers[0] if tiers else 'quick'
    chosen = [test for test in tests()
              if test[1] in SELECT[tier] and (only is None or only in test[0].lower())]
    if only is not None and not chosen:
        print(f'error: --only {only!r} matches no {tier} test (see --list)')
        return 1
    if '--list' in argv:
        for name, test_tier, _ in chosen:
            print(f'{test_tier:6s} {name}')
        return 0
    strict = '--strict' in argv
    print(f'BF1943 Tool Suite tests: {tier}, {len(chosen)} test(s)' + (' (strict: a skip fails)' if strict else ''))
    failures: list[tuple[str, str]] = []            # (name, output)
    skipped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []             # (name, its last line)
    partly: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []        # (name, its skip lines)
    start = time.time()
    for name, _tier, args in chosen:
        test_start = time.time()
        status, last, out, skips = run_one(args)
        if status == 'FAIL':
            failures.append((name, out))
        elif status == 'SKIP':
            skipped.append((name, last))
        elif status == 'ok* ':
            partly.append((name, skips))
        print(f'{status} {name:42s} {time.time() - test_start:6.1f} s   {last[:90]}', flush=True)
    for name, out in failures:
        print(f'\n--- {name} (last 25 lines) ---')
        print('\n'.join(out.splitlines()[-25:]))
    if skipped or partly:
        print('\nnot fully run:')
        for name, why in skipped:
            print(f'  SKIP {name}: {why}')
        for name, why in partly:
            print(f'  ok*  {name}: ' + '; '.join(why))
    passed = len(chosen) - len(failures) - len(skipped)
    print(f'\n{passed} of {len(chosen)} passed' + (f', {len(skipped)} skipped' if skipped else '')
          + (f', {len(partly)} partly skipped' if partly else '') + f' in {time.time() - start:.0f} s')
    return 1 if failures or (strict and (skipped or partly)) else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
    from bfbc2core import errors
    errors.setup('run-tests', gui=False)       # a log; an unexpected error explained in words (exit code 1)
    with errors.guard():
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`tests/functions.py`:

```py
r"""Runs a pytest-style test file without pytest, as run_tests.py does (README "Tests"): each top-level function
whose name starts with "test", in the order the file defines them, one line each ("ok", "FAIL" with its traceback,
or "skip" with its reason), then a summary line ("all passed", "<n> failed", or "skip ..." when every test skipped:
run_tests.py shows that as SKIP). Exit code 1 if any failed.

What a test may use, so that it runs the same here and under pytest: plain `assert`; the `tmp_path` argument (a new
empty folder, removed afterwards); `raise unittest.SkipTest(reason)` to skip (its data is missing). Anything else
pytest offers (other fixtures, marks, pytest.raises) needs pytest, which run_tests.py does not require: write those
checks in plain Python.

The suite's folders are on sys.path as under pytest (conftest.py): the shared ones and both NavKit variants, so a
test imports any suite module plainly.

  python -B tests\functions.py <test file>
"""
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
import importlib.util  # noqa: E402
import inspect  # noqa: E402
import pathlib  # noqa: E402
import tempfile  # noqa: E402
import traceback  # noqa: E402
import unittest  # noqa: E402
from types import ModuleType  # noqa: E402

FIXTURES = {'tmp_path'}


def load(path: str) -> ModuleType:
    """The test file as a module of its own name (its folder is not put on sys.path)."""
    name = 'functions_' + pathlib.Path(path).stem
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f'{path} cannot be loaded as a Python module')
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run(module: ModuleType) -> tuple[int, int, list[str]]:
    """(passed, failed, skipped) after running and reporting each test function."""
    passed, failed = 0, 0
    skipped: list[str] = []
    for name, function in list(vars(module).items()):      # a list: a test may add a global (a warning registry)
        if not (name.startswith('test') and inspect.isfunction(function) and function.__module__ == module.__name__):
            continue
        params = list(inspect.signature(function).parameters)
        unknown = [param for param in params if param not in FIXTURES]
        if unknown:
            print(f'FAIL {name}: needs pytest (fixture {", ".join(unknown)}; here only {", ".join(sorted(FIXTURES))})')
            failed += 1
            continue
        try:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='bf1943test_') as tmp:
                function(**({'tmp_path': pathlib.Path(tmp)} if 'tmp_path' in params else {}))
        except unittest.SkipTest as e:
            print(f'skip {name}: {e}')
            skipped.append(f'{name}: {e}')
        except Exception:
            print(f'FAIL {name}')
            print('       ' + traceback.format_exc().strip().replace('\n', '\n       '))
            failed += 1
        else:
            print(f'ok   {name}')
            passed += 1
    return passed, failed, skipped


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) != 2:
        print('usage: python -B tests\\functions.py <test file>')
        return 2
    passed, failed, skipped = run(load(argv[1]))
    if failed:
        print(f'{failed} failed')
    elif skipped and not passed:
        print('skip: ' + '; '.join(skipped))
    elif not passed:
        print(f'FAIL: no test functions in {argv[1]}')
        return 1
    else:
        print('all passed')
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE, suitepath.NAVKIT_LE)
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

```

`tests/test_bf1943_data.py`:

```py
"""BF1943 data tests: the suite's readers on the game folder bf1943-xenia-kit extracts from your own package.

  python -B tests\\test_bf1943_data.py [bundles | dbx | terrain | apt | all]

  bundles  fbrb1943.py on every bundle: 82 of the 85 read (three use another layout), and each rebuilds with an identical
           directory and decompressed payload
  dbx      core dbx.py parses every .dbx partition of the readable bundles
  terrain  core terrain.py / water.py on every multiplayer level (big-endian): Wake Island's ground spawns stand on
           the terrain (within 1 m), and each level's water is flat
  apt      bf1943-apt-tools apt.py reads and validates the three menu movies the Xenia kit edits

BF1943_GAME overrides the game folder (default: bf1943-xenia-kit\\output\\title\\dist\\xenon); skipped when absent.
"""
import os
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
GAME = os.environ.get('BF1943_GAME', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-xenia-kit', 'output', 'title', 'dist', 'xenon'))
LEVELS = ['wake_island_s', 'guadal_canal', 'iwo_jima_s', 'coral_sea']
failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def bundle_paths():
    return sorted(os.path.join(dp, f) for dp, _, fs in os.walk(GAME) for f in fs if f.endswith('.fbrb'))


def bundles():
    from fbrb1943 import Bundle
    read, refused, differ = [], [], []
    for p in bundle_paths():
        raw = open(p, 'rb').read()
        try:
            b = Bundle(raw)
        except ValueError:
            refused.append(os.path.relpath(p, GAME))
            continue
        read.append(b)
        again = Bundle(b.build()[0])                  # compressed bytes differ (zlib is not DICE's encoder); the
        if again.directory != b.directory or again.payload != b.payload:      # directory and content must not
            differ.append(os.path.relpath(p, GAME))
    check(len(read) == 82 and len(refused) == 3, f'{len(read)} bundles read, {len(refused)} refused ({refused})')
    check(not differ, f'every readable bundle rebuilds with an identical directory and payload ({len(differ)} differ: {differ[:3]})')
    return read


def dbx_partitions():
    from bfbc2core import dbx
    from fbrb1943 import Bundle
    count, bad = 0, []
    for p in bundle_paths():
        try:
            b = Bundle(open(p, 'rb').read())
        except ValueError:
            continue
        for e in b.entries:
            if e['name'].lower().endswith('.dbx'):
                count += 1
                try:
                    dbx.parse(b.data(e['name']))
                except Exception as ex:          # any parse error is a failure of the reader
                    bad.append(f'{e["name"]}: {ex}')
    check(count > 1000 and not bad, f'{count} .dbx partitions parse ({len(bad)} failed: {bad[:2]})')


def terrain_water():
    import spawnmap
    from bfbc2core import terrain, water
    from fbrb1943 import Bundle
    for lv in LEVELS:
        b = Bundle(open(os.path.join(GAME, 'levels', lv, 'terrain-00.fbrb'), 'rb').read())
        names = {e['name'].lower(): e['name'] for e in b.entries}
        hf = terrain.read(b.data(names[f'terrains/{lv}/{lv}.heightfield-000.res']))
        mesh = os.path.join(SUITE, f'.test-{lv}-water.res')
        try:
            open(mesh, 'wb').write(b.data(names[f'terrains/{lv}/{lv}.water.mesh.res']))
            v, t = water.read_mesh(mesh)
        finally:
            os.remove(mesh)
        check(hf.size in (1024, 2048) and len(t) and float(v[:, 1].max() - v[:, 1].min()) < 0.01,
              f'{lv}: terrain {hf.size} samples per side, water flat at {float(v[:, 1].mean()):.1f} m ({len(t)} triangles)')
        if lv == 'wake_island_s':
            m = spawnmap.spawn_map(GAME, lv)
            flags = [s for o in m['objectives'] if o['role'] == 'flag' for s in o['spawns'] if s['kind'] == 'soldier']
            gaps = [round(s['position'][1] - float(hf.height(s['position'][0], s['position'][2])), 2) for s in flags]
            check(all(-0.1 <= g <= 1.0 for g in gaps), f'{lv}: flag spawns stand on the terrain (spawn - ground {gaps} m)')


def apt_movies():
    import apt
    from fbrb1943 import Bundle
    for bundle, entry in (('menu/main/mainmenu-00.fbrb', 'Menu/main_nav.res'), ('menu/main/mainmenu-00.fbrb', 'Menu/main_root.res'),
                          ('menu/hud/hud_multiplayer_cq-00.fbrb', 'Menu/igm_mp_cq.res')):
        b = Bundle(open(os.path.join(GAME, *bundle.split('/')), 'rb').read())
        a = apt.Apt(b.data(entry))
        problems = a.validate()[2]
        check(not problems and a.characters(), f'{entry}: {len(a.characters())} characters, {len(a.action_items())} action blocks, valid')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(GAME, 'levels')):
        print(f'skip: no BF1943 game folder at {GAME} (run bf1943-xenia-kit build first, or set BF1943_GAME)')
        sys.exit(0)
    what = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'all'
    if what in ('bundles', 'all'):
        bundles()
    if what in ('dbx', 'all'):
        dbx_partitions()
    if what in ('terrain', 'all'):
        terrain_water()
    if what in ('apt', 'all'):
        apt_movies()
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)

```

`tests/test_bf1943_tools.py`:

```py
"""The suite's tools on your BF1943 copy, as bf1943-xenia-kit extracts it (BF1943_GAME overrides; skipped when absent).

  python -B tests\\test_bf1943_tools.py [level | dbxedit | fbrb | navkit | hub | viewers | all]

  level    core level1943.py loads every multiplayer map: entities, collision, terrain, water, two bases and
           their flags, spawns with sides (a base's and a carrier's); Wake Island's 16 ladders
  dbxedit  DbxEdit and LevelDiff (built with their build.bat when missing or older than their sources, core
           csbuild.py) on Wake Island's partitions: every one
           round-trips byte for byte, DbxEdit's XML equals core dbx.py's, the level check passes, LevelDiff finds
           no change between a partition and itself
  fbrb     fbrb1943.py's command line: info, list and extract with a manifest; replace writes a copy whose entry
           reads back, and refuses to write into the game folder
  navkit   bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian navkit.py prepare on Wake Island, into a temporary work folder: the
           settings (sea level 215 m, sector offsets -11 / -11) and the object files
  hub      the suite window opens with your copy's levels in its Levels tab
  viewers  the Map Inspector draws Wake Island (a screenshot); the Navigation Studio draws it with a navigation
           build when there is one (work folder, or BF1943_HPD) and routes between two flags
  probe    NavKit's enclosure_probe1943.py on Wake Island's samples (when navkit.py has sampled it): from the Beach
           bunker's spawn the fill leaves the bunker
  xex      bf1943-xex-tools' ppcdis.py from the research workspace (BF1943_RESEARCH, else operation-rising-sun next to
           the suite; skipped without a decoded image)
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use(suitepath.NAVKIT_BE)
from bfbc2core import game1943  # noqa: E402

PY = sys.executable
failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def level():
    from bfbc2core import level1943
    for lv in game1943.MP_LEVELS:
        L = level1943.load(lv, log=lambda m: None)
        cats = {}
        for e in L.entities:
            cats[e.category] = cats.get(e.category, 0) + 1
        bases = [o for o in L.objectives if o['role'] == 'base']
        sided = {e.team for e in L.entities if e.category == 'soldier spawn' and e.team in (1, 2)}
        check(len(L.meshes) > 1000 and L.heightfield is not None and L.water is not None and len(L.water)
              and len(bases) == 2 and cats.get('flag', 0) >= 3 and sided == {1, 2},
              f'{lv}: {len(L.entities)} entities, {len(L.meshes)} with collision, terrain and water, {len(bases)} bases, '
              f'{cats.get("flag", 0)} flags, soldier spawns of both sides')
        if lv == 'wake_island_s':
            carrier = [e for e in L.entities if e.category == 'vehicle spawn' and e.team in (1, 2)]
            check(cats.get('ladder') == 16 and len(carrier) == 16,
                  f'{lv}: 16 ladders; the carriers\' 16 vehicle spawns take their carrier\'s side ({len(carrier)})')


def dbxedit():
    from bfbc2core import csbuild, dbx
    exe, ldiff = csbuild.ensure('dbxedit'), csbuild.ensure('leveldiff')      # rebuilt when older than their sources
    work = os.path.join(game1943.work_root(), 'test-dbx')            # short: .NET Framework's 260-character limit
    import shutil
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
    g = game1943.Game(None, 'wake_island_s')
    n = 0
    for name in g.names():
        if name.endswith('.dbx') and (name.startswith('levels/wake_island_s') or n < 600):
            p = os.path.join(work, *name.split('/'))
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
            open(p, 'wb').write(g.data(name))
            n += 1
    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'roundtrip', work], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace')
    check(f'{n} identical, 0 different' in r.stdout, f'DbxEdit round trip: {r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1] if r.stdout.strip() else r.stderr[-200:]}')
    subprocess.run([exe, 'xml', work], capture_output=True)
    same = bad = 0
    for dp, _, fs in os.walk(work):
        for f in fs:
            if f.endswith('.dbx'):
                p = os.path.join(dp, f)
                mine = dbx.to_xml(open(p, 'rb').read())
                theirs = open(p[:-4] + '.xml', 'rb').read() if os.path.isfile(p[:-4] + '.xml') else b''
                ok = (mine if isinstance(mine, bytes) else mine.encode('utf-8')) == theirs
                same, bad = same + ok, bad + (not ok)
    check(same == n and not bad, f'DbxEdit XML equals core dbx.py\'s on {same} of {n} partitions')
    lvp = os.path.join(work, 'levels', 'wake_island_s.dbx')
    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'check', lvp], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace')
    check(r.returncode == 0 and '0 error(s)' in r.stdout, f'DbxEdit level check on Wake Island: {r.stdout.strip()[-80:]}')
    r = subprocess.run([ldiff, lvp, lvp, '--summary'], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace')
    check(r.returncode == 0 and 'changed: 0' in r.stdout, 'LevelDiff: a partition against itself has no change')
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)


def fbrb():
    tool = os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-fbrb-tool', 'fbrb1943.py')
    game = game1943.find_game()
    b = os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'wake_island_s', 'terrain-00.fbrb')
    r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', tool, 'info', b], capture_output=True, text=True)
    check(r.returncode == 0 and '8 entries' in r.stdout, 'info: Wake Island\'s terrain bundle, 8 entries')
    r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', tool, 'list', b, 'heightfield'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    check(r.returncode == 0 and 'TerrainHeightfield' in r.stdout and len(r.stdout.strip().splitlines()) == 1, 'list with a filter')
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', tool, 'extract', b, d, 'water'], capture_output=True, text=True)
        man = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, 'fbrb.manifest.json')))
        check(r.returncode == 0 and len(man['entries']) == 2 and all(len(e['sha256']) == 64 for e in man['entries']),
              'extract with a filter: two water entries and their hashes')
        src = os.path.join(d, *man['entries'][0]['name'].split('/'))
        out = os.path.join(d, 'copy.fbrb')
        new = os.path.join(d, 'new.bin')
        open(new, 'wb').write(b'replaced')
        r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', tool, 'replace', b, out, f'{man["entries"][0]["name"]}={new}'], capture_output=True, text=True)
        from fbrb1943 import Bundle
        check(r.returncode == 0 and Bundle(open(out, 'rb').read()).data(man['entries'][0]['name']) == b'replaced'
              and os.path.isfile(src), 'replace: the copy holds the new entry')
        r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', tool, 'replace', b, os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'x.fbrb'), f'{man["entries"][0]["name"]}={new}'],
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        check(r.returncode != 0 and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'x.fbrb')), 'replace refuses the game folder')


def navkit():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        env = dict(os.environ, BF1943_WORK=d)
        r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'navkit.py'), 'prepare', 'wake_island_s'],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        w = os.path.join(d, 'levels', 'wake_island_s')
        s = json.load(open(os.path.join(w, 'navkit', 'navkit.json'))) if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(w, 'navkit', 'navkit.json')) else {}

              f'navkit.py prepare wake_island_s: sea level {s.get("sea_level")}, offsets {s.get("sector_offsets")}, {len(files)} of 5 files')

                           capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
```

`tests/test_cli_errors.py`:

```py
r"""Every command-line tool's error handling (no game data): each is run with input that must fail - a file that is
missing, or not the kind the tool reads - and must exit with an error code, tell the cause and what to do in
words, name its log, and record the error in that log (%LOCALAPPDATA%\bf1943-tool-suite\logs; a temporary folder
here). The BF1943 tools: the STFS reader, the spawn map, NavKit's BF1943 steps (level objects, the sampler, the
detailed sectors, the jump links, the navigation audit, the enclosure probe). The test runner's own errors: an
--only naming no test (its message, exit 1) and an --only without a name (usage, exit 2) - before 2026-10-30 this
case ran `--only` alone, which passed on an unhandled IndexError and never reached the unknown-name message.

Also every tool that once took --help for a file name: run with --help (and -h) in an empty folder, it must exit 0,
print its usage and write nothing.

Every Python it starts runs with -B, and none may leave a __pycache__ folder in the suite: the children run without
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, so the check holds however this test was started (2026-10-31: the tools ran without -B and
relied on run_tests.py's PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE; started directly, `python -B tests\test_cli_errors.py`, the test
left caches in core, the NavKit folders, the spawn map and bf1943-fbrb-tool, as -B does not pass to children).

  python tests\test_cli_errors.py
"""
import glob
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

SUITE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..'))
PY = sys.executable


def caches():
    """The suite's __pycache__ folders (outside work/ and .git)."""
    found = set()
    for folder, dirs, _ in os.walk(SUITE):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ('.git', 'work')]
        found |= {os.path.relpath(os.path.join(folder, d), SUITE) for d in dirs if d == '__pycache__'}
    return found


def main(argv):
    failed = 0

    def check(ok, what):
        nonlocal failed
        failed += not ok
        print(f'{"ok  " if ok else "FAIL"} {what}', flush=True)

    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cli_errors_')
    # no PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: each child must keep from writing caches by itself (-B)
    env = {**{k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE'}, 'LOCALAPPDATA': tmp}
    caches_before = caches()
    logs = os.path.join(tmp, 'bf1943-tool-suite', 'logs')
    junk = os.path.join(tmp, 'junk.bin')
    open(junk, 'wb').write(b'this is not any kind of game file')
    missing = os.path.join(tmp, 'missing.file')
    cases = [
        ('STFS reader, a missing package', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-console-readers', 'stfs', 'stfs.py'), 'info', missing], 'stfs', 'missing'),
        ('spawn map, a missing game folder', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-spawn-map', 'spawnmap.py'), missing, 'wake_island_s'], 'spawnmap', 'missing'),
        ('level objects, a missing game folder', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'levelobjects1943.py'), missing, 'wake_island_s', tmp], 'levelobjects1943', 'missing'),
        ('sampler, a level folder without objects', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'navsample1943.py'), tmp, missing, junk + '.out'], 'navsample1943', 'missing'),
        ('detailed sectors, a level folder without objects', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'detailed1943.py'), tmp, missing, '0', '0'], 'detailed1943', 'missing'),
        ('navigation audit, a level not built', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'navaudit1943.py'), 'audit', 'no_such_level'], 'navaudit1943', 'missing'),
        ('jump links, a level not prepared', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'jumplinks1943.py'), 'no_such_level'], 'jumplinks1943', 'missing'),
        ('vehicle navigation, a level without a soldier world', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'navexport_vehicles1943.py'), 'no_such_level'], 'navexport_vehicles1943', 'missing'),
        ('RSNV tool, a level not exported', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'rsnvtool.py'), 'info', 'no_such_level'], 'rsnvtool', 'missing'),
        ('navigation export, a level not built', [PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'navexport1943.py'), 'no_such_level'], 'navexport1943', 'missing'),
        ('enclosure probe, a level not sampled',[PY, '-B', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-auto-navkit-big-endian', 'tools', 'enclosure_probe1943.py'), 'no_such_level', '0', '0', '0'], 'enclosure_probe1943', 'missing'),
    ]
    try:
        for label, args, log_name, says in cases:
            r = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace', env=env, timeout=300)
            out = r.stdout + r.stderr
            log = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(logs, f'{log_name}-*.log')))
            text = open(log[-1], encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read() if log else ''
            ok = r.returncode != 0 and says in out.lower() and 'details' in out.lower() and 'ERROR' in text
            check(ok, f'{label}: exit {r.returncode}, the cause in words, the log ({os.path.basename(log[-1]) if log else "none"})')
            if not ok:
                print('       ' + out.strip().replace('\n', '\n       ')[:600])
        runner = os.path.join(SUITE, 'run_tests.py')
        for label, args, code_wanted, says in (('an --only naming no test', ['quick', '--only', 'no such test name'], 1,
                                                'matches no quick test'),
                                               ('an --only without a name', ['quick', '--only'], 2, 'usage')):
            r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', runner, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace', env=env,
                               timeout=120)
            out = r.stdout + r.stderr
            ok = r.returncode == code_wanted and says in out.lower() and 'traceback' not in out.lower() \
                and 'indexerror' not in out.lower()
            check(ok, f'test runner, {label}: exit {r.returncode}, its own message')
            if not ok:
                print('       ' + out.strip().replace('\n', '\n       ')[:600])
        empty = os.path.join(tmp, 'empty')
        os.mkdir(empty)
        helps = ['bf1943-apt-tools/apt.py', 'bf1943-dbx-tools/schema1943.py', 'bf1943-fbrb-tool/fbrb1943.py',
                 'bf1943-automated-map-and-bot-test-harness/xenia-run/udp_join_probe.py',
                 'bf1943-automated-map-and-bot-test-harness/xenia-run/xeniarun.py',
                 'bf1943-automated-map-and-bot-test-harness/xenia-run/guestmem.py']
        helps += [f'bf1943-auto-navkit-common/tools/{n}.py' for n in ('detailed', 'hpdcheck', 'hpdview')]
        for tool in helps:
            path = os.path.join(SUITE, *tool.split('/'))
            first = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('"""')[1].strip().splitlines()[0]
            for flag in ('--help', '-h'):
                r = subprocess.run([PY, '-B', path, flag], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace', env=env,
                                   cwd=empty, timeout=60)
                ok = r.returncode == 0 and first in r.stdout and not os.listdir(empty)
                check(ok, f'{tool} {flag}: exit {r.returncode}, its usage, nothing written')
                if not ok:
                    print('       ' + (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip().replace('\n', '\n       ')[:600])
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    new = sorted(caches() - caches_before)
    check(not new, 'no __pycache__ left in the suite by the tools run here' + ''.join(f'\n       {c}' for c in new[:10]))
    print('all passed' if not failed else f'{failed} check(s) failed')
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```

`tests/test_coverage_ratchet.py`:

```py
r"""The coverage threshold only goes up (tests/test_repo.py coverage_ratchet), on made-up histories

A git repository made here with a pyproject.toml per commit: a threshold that rises, stays or is first set passes;
one lowered in a later commit, or in the working copy only, is reported with the commit that set the higher value,
unless the commit's message gives "Coverage-threshold-lowered: <reason>" (then later commits are held to its value);
a file that does not read is reported, not skipped.

A pytest-style test (README "Tests"): python -B -m pytest <this file>, or run_tests.py.
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import subprocess

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def repo_rules():
    """tests/test_repo.py as a module of its own (its folder is not on sys.path)."""
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('ratchet_test_repo', os.path.join(HERE, 'test_repo.py'))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def pyproject(value):
    head = '[project]\nname = "x"\n\n[tool.coverage.report]\nprecision = 1\n'
    return head + (f'fail_under = {value}\n' if value is not None else '')


def history(root, values, working=None, messages=None):
    """A repository whose pyproject.toml took the given fail_under values, one commit each (None: not set), with the
    given commit messages; the working copy then gets `working` when given."""
    run = lambda *a: subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(root), *a], check=True, capture_output=True)  # noqa: E731
    run('init', '-q')
    run('config', 'user.name', 'test')
    run('config', 'user.email', 'test@example.invalid')
    path = os.path.join(root, 'pyproject.toml')
    for k, v in enumerate(values):
        with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            f.write(pyproject(v))
        run('add', 'pyproject.toml')
        run('commit', '-q', '-m', (messages or {}).get(k, f'commit {k}'))
    if working is not None:
        with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            f.write(working if isinstance(working, str) else pyproject(working))


def ratchet(root):
    rules = repo_rules()
    rules.SUITE = str(root)
    return rules.coverage_ratchet()


def test_rising_threshold_passes(tmp_path):
    history(tmp_path, [None, 60, 60.0, 65.5])
    name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert problems == [] and 'now 65.5' in name, (name, problems)


def test_no_threshold_yet_passes(tmp_path):
    history(tmp_path, [None])
    name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert problems == [] and 'now 0' in name, (name, problems)


def test_lowered_in_a_commit_fails(tmp_path):
    history(tmp_path, [60, 70, 69])
    _name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert len(problems) == 1 and 'fail_under 69 is below 70 (set in ' in problems[0], problems


def test_removed_threshold_fails(tmp_path):
    history(tmp_path, [70, None])
    _name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert len(problems) == 1 and 'fail_under 0 is below 70' in problems[0], 'removing it lowers it to 0'


def test_lowered_in_the_working_copy_fails(tmp_path):
    history(tmp_path, [70], working=65)
    _name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert problems == ['working copy: fail_under 65 is below 70 (set in ' + problems[0].split('(set in ')[1]], problems
    history_ok = tmp_path / 'ok'
    history_ok.mkdir()
    history(history_ok, [70], working=71)
    assert ratchet(history_ok)[1] == [], 'raised in the working copy: fine'


def test_unreadable_pyproject_is_reported(tmp_path):
    history(tmp_path, [70], working='[tool.coverage.report\nfail_under = 80\n')
    _name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert len(problems) == 1 and problems[0].startswith('working copy: pyproject.toml does not read'), problems


def test_lowering_with_a_reason_passes(tmp_path):
    lowered = 'remove the old viewer\n\nCoverage-threshold-lowered: its tests went with it\n'
    history(tmp_path, [70, 66, 67], messages={1: lowered})
    name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert problems == [] and 'now 67' in name, (name, problems)
    again = tmp_path / 'again'
    again.mkdir()
    history(again, [70, 66, 65], messages={1: lowered})
    problems = ratchet(again)[1]
    assert len(problems) == 1 and 'fail_under 65 is below 66' in problems[0], 'held to the lowered value from then on'
    plain = tmp_path / 'plain'
    plain.mkdir()
    history(plain, [70, 66], messages={1: 'Coverage-threshold-lowered:\n'})
    assert len(ratchet(plain)[1]) == 1, 'a marker without a reason does not count'


def with_branch(value, branch):
    """A pyproject.toml with fail_under = value and [tool.coverage.run] branch set (None: not given)."""
    run = '' if branch is None else f'[tool.coverage.run]\nbranch = {"true" if branch else "false"}\n\n'
    return '[project]\nname = "x"\n\n' + run + f'[tool.coverage.report]\nfail_under = {value}\n'


def history_texts(root, texts, working=None, messages=None):
    """history() with each commit's whole pyproject.toml text given."""
    run = lambda *a: subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(root), *a], check=True, capture_output=True)  # noqa: E731
    run('init', '-q')
    run('config', 'user.name', 'test')
    run('config', 'user.email', 'test@example.invalid')
    path = os.path.join(root, 'pyproject.toml')
    for k, text in enumerate(texts):
        with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            f.write(text)
        run('add', 'pyproject.toml')
        run('commit', '-q', '-m', (messages or {}).get(k, f'commit {k}'))
    if working is not None:
        with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            f.write(working)


def test_branch_coverage_turned_on_passes(tmp_path):
    # 2026-11-05: branch coverage on; the total (lines and branches together) stays above the old line threshold
    history_texts(tmp_path, [with_branch(80, None), with_branch(82, True), with_branch(83, True)])
    name, problems = ratchet(tmp_path)
    assert problems == [] and 'now 83' in name, (name, problems)


def test_branch_coverage_turned_off_fails(tmp_path):
    history_texts(tmp_path, [with_branch(80, True), with_branch(80, False)])
    problems = ratchet(tmp_path)[1]
    assert len(problems) == 1 and 'branch coverage turned off (on since ' in problems[0], problems
    removed = tmp_path / 'removed'
    removed.mkdir()
    history_texts(removed, [with_branch(80, True)], working=with_branch(81, None))
    problems = ratchet(removed)[1]
    assert len(problems) == 1 and problems[0].startswith('working copy: branch coverage turned off'), problems


def test_branch_coverage_turned_off_with_a_reason_passes(tmp_path):
    lowered = 'drop branch coverage\n\nCoverage-threshold-lowered: measured by lines again\n'
    history_texts(tmp_path, [with_branch(80, True), with_branch(80, False), with_branch(81, False),
                             with_branch(82, True)], messages={1: lowered})
    assert ratchet(tmp_path)[1] == []

```

`tests/test_fuzz_real.py`:

```py
r"""binary readers fuzzed from your BF1943 files (DBX, bundles, terrain, water, material map, APT, Havok, STFS, NavKit)

The bf1943 tier's variant of the fuzz tests (core/fuzzcheck.py; the quick tier's start from made-up files): the seeds
are real files, read where they are and never written - DBX partitions, a bundle and its directory, a height field,
a material map, a water mesh, a menu movie, Havok collision packfiles from your game copy (bf1943-xenia-kit's
output, BF1943_GAME overrides); the header, hash tables and file table of your BF1943 package (served from memory
over the read-only file: BF1943_PACKAGE, else operation-rising-sun's copy next to the suite); and NavKit's builds of
Wake Island (.hpd, .rsnv, samples) when they exist. On any input each reader returns or raises ValueError, within its
time and memory limits. Fixed seeds; BF1943_FUZZ=long for more (README "Tests").
"""
import gzip
import io
import os
import struct
import unittest

import numpy as np

import fuzzcheck

TIER = 'bf1943'
SUITE = fuzzcheck.SUITE
GAME = os.environ.get('BF1943_GAME', os.path.join(SUITE, 'bf1943-xenia-kit', 'output', 'title', 'dist', 'xenon'))
PACKAGE = os.environ.get('BF1943_PACKAGE') or os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(SUITE), 'operation-rising-sun', 'Battlefield 1943 (XBLA)', '5841097E', '000D0000',
    '945CD965D6B2B2584A9C06CE16F38A075A6D390558')
BUILD = os.path.join(os.environ.get('BF1943_WORK') or os.path.join(SUITE, 'work'), 'levels', 'wake_island_s')


def fuzz(*args, **kw):
    report = fuzzcheck.run(*args, **kw)
    assert report.ok, report.text()


_GAME = []


def game():
    """Wake Island's bundles (read once)."""
    from bfbc2core import game1943
    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(GAME, 'levels')):
        raise unittest.SkipTest(f'no BF1943 game folder at {GAME}')
    if not _GAME:
        _GAME.append(game1943.Game(GAME, 'wake_island_s'))
    return _GAME[0]


def test_dbx_partitions():
    from bfbc2core import dbx
    g = game()
    names = sorted((n for n in g.names() if n.endswith('.dbx')), key=lambda n: (len(g.data(n)), n))
    picks = [names[len(names) // 10], names[len(names) // 2], 'levels/wake_island_s.dbx'] if names else []
    seeds = [g.data(n) for n in picks if g.data(n)]
    fuzz('dbx.to_xml (BF1943)', dbx.to_xml, seeds[:2], iterations=600)
    fuzz('dbx.parse (BF1943 level)', dbx.parse, seeds[2:], iterations=60, limit=20.0)


def test_bundle():
    from fbrb1943 import Bundle
    game()
    path = os.path.join(GAME, 'menu', 'shared', 'fonts_us-00.fbrb')
    raw = open(path, 'rb').read()
    fuzz('fbrb1943.Bundle (BF1943)', Bundle, [raw], iterations=300)
    cut = struct.unpack_from('>I', raw, 4)[0]
    directory, body = gzip.decompress(raw[8:8 + cut]), raw[8 + cut:]

    def with_directory(d):
        z = gzip.compress(d, mtime=0)
        return Bundle(b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(z)) + z + body)
    strlen = struct.unpack_from('>I', directory, 4)[0]
    fields = [(4, '>I'), (8 + strlen, '>I'), (len(directory) - 4, '>I')] + \
        [(12 + strlen + 24 * k + 4 * w, '>I') for k in range(3) for w in range(6)]
    fuzz('fbrb1943 directory (BF1943)', with_directory, [directory], iterations=600, fields=[fields])


def test_terrain_water_material():

         [g.data('terrains/wake_island_s/wake_island_s-materialmap.res')], iterations=150, limit=10.0)

        fuzz('water.read_mesh (BF1943)', mesh, [g.data('terrains/wake_island_s/wake_island_s.water.mesh.res')],
             iterations=200)
    finally:

            os.remove(path)

def test_havok():
    import havok461
    import hkpack
    g = game()
    names = sorted(n for n in g.names() if n.endswith('_havok.res'))
    seeds = [g.data(n) for n in names[:: max(1, len(names) // 3)][:3]]

    def collision(d):
        pf = hkpack.Packfile(d, classes=havok461.CLASSES)
        out = []
        for off in pf.objects_of('hkStorageExtendedMeshShapeMeshSubpartStorage'):
            v, t = havok461.triangles(pf, off)
            if v and t:
                out.append(np.asarray(v, np.float32)[np.asarray(t)])
        for off in pf.objects_of('hkConvexVerticesShape'):
            out.append(havok461.convex_box(pf, off)[0])
        return out
    # prefix_ok: a packfile need not reach the end of its .res, and the reader reads no further than its sections
    fuzz('hkpack + havok461 (BF1943)', collision, seeds, iterations=300, prefix_ok=True, limit=10.0)


class Overlay(io.RawIOBase):
    """A read-only file whose first bytes are `head` (the case) and the rest the real file's from `skip` on."""

    def __init__(self, path, head, skip):
        self.f, self.head, self.skip, self.pos = open(path, 'rb'), head, skip, 0

    def seek(self, pos, whence=0):
        self.pos = pos
        return pos

    def read(self, n=-1):
        out = b''
        if self.pos < len(self.head):
            out = self.head[self.pos:self.pos + n]
        rest = n - len(out)
        if rest > 0:
            self.f.seek(self.pos + len(out) - len(self.head) + self.skip)
            out += self.f.read(rest)
        self.pos += len(out)
        return out

    def close(self):
        self.f.close()


def test_package():
    import stfs
    if not os.path.isfile(PACKAGE):
        raise unittest.SkipTest(f'no BF1943 package at {PACKAGE}')
    with open(PACKAGE, 'rb') as f:
        region = f.read(0x20000)        # header, the first hash tables, the file table
    pkg = stfs.Package(PACKAGE)
    try:
        small = sorted((e for e in pkg.entries if not e['dir']), key=lambda e: e['size'])[:4]
        names = [e['path'] for e in small]
        table = pkg._addr(pkg.ft_start)
    finally:
        pkg.f.close()

    def read(head):
        stfs.open = lambda path, mode: Overlay(path, head, len(region))
        try:
            p = stfs.Package(PACKAGE)
        finally:
            del stfs.open
        try:
            return [p.read(e) for e in p.entries if e['path'] in names]
        finally:
            p.f.close()
    fields = [(0x340, '>I'), (0x37B, 'B'), (0x37C, '<H'), (0x37E, '<H'), (0x395, '>I')]
    fields += [(table + 0x40 * k + o, fmt) for k in range(8) for o, fmt in ((0x28, 'B'), (0x29, '<H'), (0x2F, '<H'),
                                                                            (0x32, '>H'), (0x34, '>I'))]
    # prefix_ok: a cut of this region is a deletion inside the package (the rest of the real file follows it)
    fuzz('stfs.Package (BF1943 package)', read, [region], iterations=400, fields=[fields], prefix_ok=True, limit=10.0)
```

`tests/test_hub.py`:

```py
r"""The suite window (BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw) on a made-up game folder (no game data; its message windows replaced):

- a navkit.json that is valid JSON but not NavKit's record does not stop the window opening;
- an error while the output pane is filled (the game folder gone when a Levels run ends) is reported, and the pane
  goes on (2026-10-30: the 100 ms pump stopped for good, and no output reached the pane again);
- LevelDiff's exit code 1 (the files differ) is not a failure; its 2 (bad input, a crash) is;
- a Python tool's output is UTF-8: an extract into a folder named in Cyrillic finishes (it died on its last print);
- Stop is per process: another tool's failure is still told, and the stopped one is not called a failure.

  python -B tests\test_hub.py
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import shutil
import struct
import sys
import tempfile
import time
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def bundle(entries):
    """A stored FbRB v2 bundle of [(name, bytes)] (fbrb1943.py's layout)."""
    import fbrb1943
    strings, offs = b'', {}
    for s in [n for n, _ in entries] + ['RawFileAsset']:
        if s not in offs:
            offs[s] = len(strings)
            strings += s.encode('ascii') + b'\0'
    d = struct.pack('>II', 2, len(strings)) + strings + struct.pack('>I', len(entries))
    pos = 0
    for name, data in entries:
        d += struct.pack('>6I', offs[name], 0, pos, len(data), len(data), offs['RawFileAsset'])
        pos += len(data)
    d += b'\0' + struct.pack('>I', pos)
    z = fbrb1943.gzip_member(d, b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x0b')
    return b'FbRB' + struct.pack('>I', len(z)) + z + b''.join(x for _, x in entries)


def main():
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='hub_test_')
    saved_env = dict(os.environ)
    root = None
    try:
        os.environ['LOCALAPPDATA'] = tmp
        game = os.path.join(tmp, 'game')
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'lv'))
        with open(os.path.join(game, 'levels', 'lv', 'level-00.fbrb'), 'wb') as f:
            f.write(bundle([('a.res', b'a')]))
        os.environ['BF1943_GAME'] = game
        os.environ['BF1943_WORK'] = os.path.join(tmp, 'work')
        nk = os.path.join(tmp, 'work', 'levels', 'lv', 'navkit')
        os.makedirs(nk)
        with open(os.path.join(nk, 'navkit.json'), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            f.write('["not", "a", "record"]\n')
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('hub', os.path.join(SUITE, 'BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw'))
        hub = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(hub)
        hub.errors.setup('test-hub-quick', gui=False)
        import tkinter as tk
        root = tk.Tk()
        root.withdraw()
        shown = []
        hub.Hub.notify = lambda self, kind, title, text: shown.append(text.splitlines()[0])
        try:
            h = hub.Hub(root)
            opened = list(h.tree.get_children()) == ['lv']
        except Exception as e:
            h, opened = None, f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
        check(opened is True, f'the window opens with a navkit.json that is not a record ({opened})')
        if h is None:                                   # the other checks still run, on a window that opens
            os.remove(os.path.join(nk, 'navkit.json'))
            h = hub.Hub(root)
        shown.clear()

        def pane():
            return h.text.get('1.0', 'end')

        def drive(until, timeout=60):
            t0 = time.time()
            while not until() and time.time() - t0 < timeout:
                root.update()
                time.sleep(0.05)
            root.update()

        # the pump after an error: the game folder gone when a Levels run ends
        moved = game + '-moved'
        os.rename(game, moved)
        calls = []
        real_after = root.after
        root.after = lambda ms, fn=None, *a: calls.append(getattr(fn, '__name__', fn))
        h.lines.put(('done', 'Levels: navigation of lv', 0, True, (0,), -1))
        h.lines.put(('done', 'a malformed end'))            # an item that raises whatever the code
        h.lines.put('a later tool line\n')
        try:
            h.pump()
            raised = None
        except Exception as e:
            raised = f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
        root.after = real_after
        os.rename(moved, game)
        check(raised is None and 'pump' in calls and 'a later tool line' in pane(),
              f'an error while filling the pane is reported and the pump goes on (raised {raised}, rescheduled '
              f'{"pump" in calls})')

        # LevelDiff: 1 = the files differ (not a failure), 2 = bad input or a crash (a failure)
        a, b = os.path.join(tmp, 'a.dbx'), os.path.join(tmp, 'b.dbx')
        for p in (a, b):
            with open(p, 'wb') as f:
                f.write(b'made-up')
        for code, failure in ((1, False), (2, True)):
            fake = os.path.join(tmp, f'leveldiff{code}.bat')
            with open(fake, 'w', encoding='ascii', newline='\r\n') as f:
                f.write(f'@echo made-up LevelDiff\n@exit /b {code}\n')
            hub.tool = lambda name, fake=fake: fake
            shown.clear()
            h.ld_a.set(a)
            h.ld_b.set(b)
            h.diff()
            drive(lambda: h.proc.poll() is not None and h.lines.empty() and h.status.get() == 'Ready.')
            check(bool(shown) == failure, f'LevelDiff exit {code}: {"a failure" if failure else "not a failure"} '
                                          f'(windows: {shown})')

        # a Python tool's output is UTF-8: fbrb1943.py extract into a Cyrillic folder
        src = os.path.join(tmp, 'in.fbrb')
        with open(src, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(bundle([('a.res', b'a')]))
        out = os.path.join(tmp, 'Карта')
        shown.clear()
        h.run([hub.PYTHON, hub.SCRIPTS['fbrb'], 'extract', src, out], 'Bundle extract')
        drive(lambda: h.proc.poll() is not None and h.lines.empty() and h.status.get() == 'Ready.')
        check(h.proc.returncode == 0 and not shown and out in pane(),
              f'an extract into a Cyrillic folder finishes and its output is shown (exit {h.proc.returncode})')

        # Stop is per process: a launched tool fails, then the tab's tool is stopped
        shown.clear()
        h.launch([hub.PYTHON, '-c', 'import sys; sys.exit(3)'], 'Made-up window')
        time.sleep(1.5)                              # its end is queued first (the pane not pumped meanwhile)
        h.run([hub.PYTHON, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(60)'], 'Made-up long run')
        time.sleep(0.5)
        h.stop()
        drive(lambda: h.proc.poll() is not None and h.lines.empty() and h.status.get() == 'Ready.')
        check('Made-up window closed with an error' in pane() and not shown,
              f'Stop is per process: the other tool\'s failure is told, the stopped one is no failure (windows: {shown})')
    finally:
        if root is not None:
            try:
                root.destroy()
            except Exception:
                pass
        os.environ.clear()
        os.environ.update(saved_env)
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
```

`tests/test_hub_ended.py`:

```py
r"""The suite window's end of a tool (BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw Hub.ended, no window: a stand-in for the Hub's state)

Only the end of the tab's current tool (pid == self.proc.pid) frees the window (status Ready, Stop disabled): the end
of an earlier run, still queued when the next run started, leaves the running tool's status and Stop alone
(2026-11-05), while its line in the pane and its failure are still told; a launched window's end never frees it.

A pytest-style test (README "Tests"): python -B -m pytest <this file>, or run_tests.py.
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import sys
from types import SimpleNamespace

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SUITE = os.path.dirname(HERE)


def hub():
    """BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw as a module (its name has spaces; it is not on sys.path)."""
    name = 'test_hub_ended_hub'
    if name not in sys.modules:
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, os.path.join(SUITE, 'BF1943 Tool Suite.pyw'))
        assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[name] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return sys.modules[name]


class Var:
    def __init__(self, value=''):
        self.value = value

    def set(self, value):
        self.value = value

    def get(self):
        return self.value


class Button:
    def __init__(self):
        self.state = 'normal'

    def configure(self, state):
        self.state = state


def window(running_pid):
    """A stand-in for a Hub whose tab runs the process running_pid (status Running, Stop enabled)."""
    pane, failures, levels = [], [], []
    return SimpleNamespace(
        stopped_pids=set(), proc=SimpleNamespace(pid=running_pid), status=Var('Running: the new run'),
        stop_btn=Button(), pane=pane, failures=failures, levels=levels, write=pane.append,
        failed=lambda label, code, main: failures.append((label, code, main)), fill_levels=lambda: levels.append(1))


def test_stale_end_leaves_the_running_tool_alone():
    h = window(200)
    hub().Hub.ended(h, 'the earlier run', 2, True, (0,), 100)
    assert h.status.get() == 'Running: the new run' and h.stop_btn.state == 'normal', 'the running tool keeps its state'
    assert h.pane == ['finished with exit code 2: the earlier run\n'], 'its end is still in the pane'
    assert h.failures == [('the earlier run', 2, True)], 'and its failure is still told'


def test_current_end_frees_the_window():
    h = window(200)
    hub().Hub.ended(h, 'the run', 0, True, (0,), 200)
    assert h.status.get() == 'Ready.' and h.stop_btn.state == 'disabled' and h.failures == []


def test_no_tool_running_is_left_alone():
    h = window(200)
    h.proc = None
    hub().Hub.ended(h, 'a run', 0, True, (0,), 200)
    assert h.status.get() == 'Running: the new run' and h.stop_btn.state == 'normal'


def test_launched_window_end_never_frees_the_window():
    h = window(200)
    hub().Hub.ended(h, 'a window', 0, False, (0,), 200)
    assert h.status.get() == 'Running: the new run' and h.stop_btn.state == 'normal'


def test_stopped_stale_end_is_no_failure():
    h = window(200)
    h.stopped_pids.add(100)
    hub().Hub.ended(h, 'the stopped run', 1, True, (0,), 100)
    assert h.failures == [] and 100 not in h.stopped_pids and h.status.get() == 'Running: the new run'
```

`tests/test_import_opfor.py`:

```py
r"""tools\import_opfor.py --update on made-up trees only: a temporary git repository stands in for OPFOR's suite and
a temporary folder for this suite (the module's SOURCE_SUITE, SUITE and MANIFEST are pointed at them; the real
suites are never read or written). An updated single-file import (run_tests.py, and a renamed one) replaces that
file, not <file>\<file>; a folder import updates the changed file in the folder; a file changed here too is left
as a conflict; a file recorded as moved elsewhere in this suite (merged) is not brought back, and a change to it in
the source is a conflict naming its new place. The command line on runs that cannot finish (partial_runs): checked
before anything is written, and what a run stopped part-way wrote is recorded (marked incomplete).

  python -B tests\test_import_opfor.py
"""
import hashlib
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use('tools')
import import_opfor  # noqa: E402

failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', repo, '-c', 'user.name=test', '-c', 'user.email=test@example.invalid',
                           '-c', 'commit.gpgsign=false', *args], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout


def write(path, data):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(data)


def record(rel, data):
    return {'path': rel, 'bytes': len(data), 'git_blob': import_opfor.blob_id(data), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()}


def partial_runs(tmp, src):
    """The tool's command line (a copy of it in a made-up suite, so its SUITE and MANIFEST are there) on runs that
    cannot finish: a plan whose later item has no source, and an --update naming a destination never imported, write
    nothing; an update stopped part-way records what it wrote, marked incomplete (2026-10-30: such files were left
    without a record, and the next update took them for local edits)."""
    import importlib.util
    import json
    suite = os.path.join(tmp, 'cli-suite')
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(suite, 'tools'))
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(suite, 'provenance'))
    tool = os.path.join(suite, 'tools', 'import_opfor.py')
    shutil.copy(os.path.join(SUITE, 'tools', 'import_opfor.py'), tool)
    manifest = os.path.join(suite, 'provenance', 'opfor-imports.json')
    with open(manifest, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        json.dump({'imports': []}, f)
    env = {**os.environ, 'BFBC2_TOOL_SUITE': src}

    def run(*args):
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', tool, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        return r.returncode, (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()

    def imports():
        with open(manifest, encoding='utf-8') as f:
            return json.load(f)['imports']
    plan = os.path.join(tmp, 'plan.json')
    with open(plan, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        json.dump([{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'copied-tool'}, {'source': 'no-such-folder', 'destination': 'other'}], f)
    code, out = run('--plan', plan)
    check(code != 0 and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(suite, 'copied-tool')) and imports() == [],
          f'a plan whose later item has no source writes nothing (exit {code}: {out[-70:]})')
    code, out = run('tool', 'copied-tool')
    check(code == 0 and len(imports()) == 1, f'an import is copied and recorded (exit {code})')
    write(os.path.join(src, 'tool', 'a.py'), b'third a\n')
    git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-am', 'third')
    code, out = run('--update', 'copied-tool', 'never-imported')
    with open(os.path.join(suite, 'copied-tool', 'a.py'), 'rb') as f:
        kept = f.read()
    check(code != 0 and kept == b'new a\n' and len(imports()) == 1,
          f'an --update naming a destination never imported writes nothing (exit {code}, a.py {kept!r})')
    code, out = run('--update', 'copied-tool')
    last = imports()[-1]['items'][0]
    check(code == 0 and [f['path'] for f in last['files']] == ['a.py'] and not last['conflicts'],
          f'the update then brings the file and records it, no conflict (exit {code}: {out[-70:]})')
    # stopped part-way: the second blob read back wrong, after the first file was written
    write(os.path.join(src, 'tool', 'a.py'), b'fourth a\n')
    write(os.path.join(src, 'tool', 'c.py'), b'new c\n')
    git(src, 'add', '-A')
    git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'fourth')
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('import_opfor_copy', tool)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    mod.SOURCE_SUITE = src
    real_git, reads = mod.git, []

    def failing_git(*args):
        out_ = real_git(*args)
        if args[:2] == ('cat-file', 'blob'):
            reads.append(args)
            if len(reads) == 2:
                return out_ + b'damaged'
        return out_
    mod.git = failing_git
    saved_argv, sys.argv = sys.argv, ['import_opfor.py', '--update', 'copied-tool']
    try:
        mod.main()
        stopped = False
    except SystemExit:
        stopped = True
    finally:
        sys.argv = saved_argv
    last = imports()[-1]
    check(stopped and bool(last.get('incomplete')) and [f['path'] for f in last['items'][0]['files']] == ['a.py'],
          f'an update stopped part-way records the file it wrote, marked incomplete ({last.get("incomplete")!r})')


def second_review(tmp):
    """2026-10-30 second review, on a copy of the tool in its own made-up suite and a made-up source: a write that
    fails part-way (a full disk, made up by failing the write of one file's bytes, whichever way the tool opens it)
    leaves no cut file; a failure on the first file still records the import (its folder exists), and --update then
    finishes it with no conflict; a plan naming a folder and a folder inside it writes nothing; an update whose write
    fails leaves the old file whole."""
    import builtins
    import importlib.util
    import json
    src = os.path.join(tmp, 'sr-source')
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(src, 'tool'))
    git(src, 'init', '-q')
    data = {'a.py': b'a' * 300, 'b.py': b'b' * 300}
    for n, d in data.items():
        write(os.path.join(src, 'tool', n), d)
    git(src, 'add', '-A')
    git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'one')
    env = {**os.environ, 'BFBC2_TOOL_SUITE': src}

    def suite_copy(name):
        suite = os.path.join(tmp, name)
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(suite, 'tools'))
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(suite, 'provenance'))
        tool = os.path.join(suite, 'tools', 'import_opfor.py')
        shutil.copy(os.path.join(SUITE, 'tools', 'import_opfor.py'), tool)
        with open(os.path.join(suite, 'provenance', 'opfor-imports.json'), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
            json.dump({'imports': []}, f)
        return suite, tool

    def imports(suite):
        with open(os.path.join(suite, 'provenance', 'opfor-imports.json'), encoding='utf-8') as f:
            return json.load(f)['imports']

    def cli(tool, *args):
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', tool, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        return r.returncode, (r.stdout + r.stderr).strip()

    def in_process(tool, argv, fail_bytes):
        """main() with the write of fail_bytes failing after 10 bytes (through open or os.fdopen alike)."""
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('import_opfor_sr', tool)
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
        mod.SOURCE_SUITE = src
        real_open, real_fdopen = builtins.open, os.fdopen

        def wrap(f):
            class Failing:
                def __enter__(self):
                    return self

                def __exit__(self, *e):
                    f.close()
                    return False

                def write(self, b):
                    if bytes(b) == fail_bytes:
                        f.write(b[:10])
                        raise OSError(28, 'made-up full disk')
                    return f.write(b)

                def __getattr__(self, k):
                    return getattr(f, k)
            return Failing()

        def fake_open(file, mode='r', *a, **k):
            f = real_open(file, mode, *a, **k)
            return wrap(f) if ('w' in mode or 'x' in mode) and 'b' in mode else f

        def fake_fdopen(fd, mode='r', *a, **k):
            f = real_fdopen(fd, mode, *a, **k)
            return wrap(f) if 'w' in mode and 'b' in mode else f
        mod.open = fake_open
        saved_argv, sys.argv = sys.argv, ['import_opfor.py', *argv]
        os.fdopen = fake_fdopen
        try:
            mod.main()
            return None
        except BaseException as e:
            return e
        finally:
            os.fdopen = real_fdopen
            sys.argv = saved_argv

    for which in ('a.py', 'b.py'):
        suite, tool = suite_copy(f'sr-suite-{which[0]}')
        err = in_process(tool, ['tool', 'copied'], data[which])
        dst = os.path.join(suite, 'copied')
        cut = [n for n in (os.listdir(dst) if os.path.isdir(dst) else []) if open(os.path.join(dst, n), 'rb').read()
               != data.get(n)]
        rec = imports(suite)
        check(err is not None and not cut and rec and rec[-1].get('incomplete'),
              f'an import whose {which} write fails leaves no cut file and is recorded as incomplete '
              f'(cut: {cut}, entries: {len(rec)})')
        code, out = cli(tool, '--update', 'copied')
        got = {n: open(os.path.join(dst, n), 'rb').read() for n in os.listdir(dst)} if os.path.isdir(dst) else {}
        check(code == 0 and got == data and 'conflict' not in out,
              f'--update then finishes the import whose {which} write failed, no conflict (exit {code}: {out[-80:]})')

    suite, tool = suite_copy('sr-suite-nested')
    plan = os.path.join(tmp, 'sr-plan.json')
    with open(plan, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        json.dump([{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'x'}, {'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'x/inner'}], f)
    code, out = cli(tool, '--plan', plan)
    check(code != 0 and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(suite, 'x')) and imports(suite) == [],
          f'a plan naming a folder and one inside it writes nothing (exit {code}: {out[-80:]})')

    suite, tool = suite_copy('sr-suite-update')
    code, out = cli(tool, 'tool', 'copied')
    write(os.path.join(src, 'tool', 'a.py'), b'A' * 400)
    git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-am', 'two')
    err = in_process(tool, ['--update', 'copied'], b'A' * 400)
    kept = open(os.path.join(suite, 'copied', 'a.py'), 'rb').read()
    left = [n for n in os.listdir(os.path.join(suite, 'copied')) if n.endswith('.tmp')]
    check(code == 0 and err is not None and kept == data['a.py'] and not left,
          f'an update whose write fails leaves the old file whole, no temporary file ({len(kept)} bytes, {left})')


def main():
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='import_opfor_')
    saved = import_opfor.SOURCE_SUITE, import_opfor.SUITE, import_opfor.MANIFEST
    try:
        src, dst = os.path.join(tmp, 'source-suite'), os.path.join(tmp, 'this-suite')
        os.makedirs(src)
        os.makedirs(dst)
        git(src, 'init', '-q')
        old = {'run_tests.py': b'old runner\n', 'Old Suite.pyw': b'old hub\n', 'tool/a.py': b'old a\n', 'tool/b.py': b'old b\n'}
        for rel, data in old.items():
            write(os.path.join(src, *rel.split('/')), data)
        git(src, 'add', '-A')
        git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'first')
        first = git(src, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').decode().strip()
        # this suite as an import would have left it
        write(os.path.join(dst, 'run_tests.py'), old['run_tests.py'])
        write(os.path.join(dst, 'New Suite.pyw'), old['Old Suite.pyw'])
        write(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'a.py'), old['tool/a.py'])
        write(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'b.py'), b'changed here\n')
        manifest = {'imports': [{'commit': first, 'items': [
            {'source': 'run_tests.py', 'destination': 'run_tests.py', 'files': [record('run_tests.py', old['run_tests.py'])]},
            {'source': 'Old Suite.pyw', 'destination': 'New Suite.pyw', 'files': [record('Old Suite.pyw', old['Old Suite.pyw'])]},
            {'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'tool', 'files': [record('a.py', old['tool/a.py']), record('b.py', old['tool/b.py'])]}]}]}
        new = {'run_tests.py': b'new runner\n', 'Old Suite.pyw': b'new hub\n', 'tool/a.py': b'new a\n', 'tool/b.py': b'new b\n'}
        for rel, data in new.items():
            write(os.path.join(src, *rel.split('/')), data)
        git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-am', 'second')
        second = git(src, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').decode().strip()

        import_opfor.SOURCE_SUITE, import_opfor.SUITE = src, dst
        import_opfor.MANIFEST = os.path.join(dst, 'provenance', 'opfor-imports.json')
        for destination, rel, label in (('run_tests.py', 'run_tests.py', 'a single-file import'),
                                        ('New Suite.pyw', 'Old Suite.pyw', 'a renamed single-file import')):
            try:
                item = import_opfor.update_one(second, manifest, destination)
                got = open(os.path.join(dst, destination), 'rb').read() if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(dst, destination)) else None
                ok = got == new[rel] and [f['path'] for f in item['files']] == [rel] and not item['conflicts']
                why = f'{destination} holds {got!r}'
            except (Exception, SystemExit) as e:
                ok, why = False, f'{type(e).__name__}: {e}'
            check(ok, f'update of {label} replaces the file itself ({why})')
        item = import_opfor.update_one(second, manifest, 'tool')
        check(open(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'a.py'), 'rb').read() == new['tool/a.py'] and item['conflicts'] == ['b.py']
              and open(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'b.py'), 'rb').read() == b'changed here\n',
              'update of a folder import: the file changed only there is replaced, the one changed here too is a conflict')
        check(sorted(os.listdir(dst)) == ['New Suite.pyw', 'run_tests.py', 'tool'], f'nothing else written ({sorted(os.listdir(dst))})')
        # a file moved out of the folder import (2026-10-31: NavKit's shared modules to bf1943-auto-navkit-common)
        os.remove(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'a.py'))
        manifest['imports'].append({'items': [item]})
        manifest['imports'].append({'kind': 'move', 'destination': 'tool', 'paths': {'a.py': 'common/a.py'}})
        item = import_opfor.update_one(second, manifest, 'tool')
        check(not os.path.exists(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'a.py')) and not item['files'] and item['conflicts'] == ['b.py'],
              f'a moved file unchanged in the source is not brought back ({item["files"]}, {item["conflicts"]})')
        write(os.path.join(src, 'tool', 'a.py'), b'third a\n')
        git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-am', 'third (a moved file changed)')
        third = git(src, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').decode().strip()
        item = import_opfor.update_one(third, manifest, 'tool')
        check(not os.path.exists(os.path.join(dst, 'tool', 'a.py')) and not item['files']
              and item['conflicts'] == ['a.py (moved to common/a.py)', 'b.py'],
              f'a moved file changed in the source is a conflict at its new place ({item["conflicts"]})')
        git(src, 'reset', '-q', '--hard', second)
        partial_runs(tmp, src)
        second_review(tmp)
    finally:
        import_opfor.SOURCE_SUITE, import_opfor.SUITE, import_opfor.MANIFEST = saved
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
```
