`tests/test_import_opfor_main.py`:

```py
r"""tools\import_opfor.py's command line, in process, on made-up trees

import_opfor.main() and its helpers run in this process on made-up trees only: a temporary git repository stands in
for OPFOR's suite and a temporary folder for this suite (the module's SOURCE_SUITE, SUITE and MANIFEST point at them
for the test and are restored afterwards; the real suites are never read or written). Checked: a single-file import,
a plan, an --update (a changed file, a new file, a file removed here, a file new in the source that is already here),
what each records; each refusal before anything is written (a destination outside the suite, already there, named
twice or inside another, nothing committed at the source, nothing imported to an --update destination, no arguments);
symbolic links in the source are not copied; a blob read back wrong stops the copy; place() leaves no temporary file.
"""
import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

TOOL = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), 'tools', 'import_opfor.py')
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('import_opfor', TOOL)     # tools\ is not on sys.path
io_mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(io_mod)


def git(repo, *args, stdin=None):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), '-c', 'user.name=test', '-c', 'user.email=test@example.invalid',
                           '-c', 'commit.gpgsign=false', '-c', 'core.autocrlf=false', *args], input=stdin,
                          capture_output=True, check=True).stdout


def write(path, data):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(data)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def trees(tmp):
    src, suite = tmp / 'source', tmp / 'suite'
    src.mkdir()
    (suite / 'provenance').mkdir(parents=True)
    git(src, 'init', '-q')
    for rel, data in {'single.txt': b'one file\n', 'tool/a.py': b'a\n', 'tool/b.py': b'b\n',
                      'other/c.py': b'c\n'}.items():
        write(src / rel, data)
    git(src, 'add', '-A')
    blob = git(src, 'hash-object', '-w', '--stdin', stdin=b'a.py').decode().strip()
    git(src, 'update-index', '--add', '--cacheinfo', f'120000,{blob},tool/link.py')      # a symbolic link
    git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'first')
    manifest = suite / 'provenance' / 'opfor-imports.json'
    manifest.write_text('{"imports": []}\n', encoding='utf-8')
    saved = io_mod.SOURCE_SUITE, io_mod.SUITE, io_mod.MANIFEST, sys.argv
    io_mod.SOURCE_SUITE, io_mod.SUITE, io_mod.MANIFEST = str(src), str(suite), str(manifest)
    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            yield src, suite
    finally:
        io_mod.SOURCE_SUITE, io_mod.SUITE, io_mod.MANIFEST, sys.argv = saved


def run(*argv):
    """main() with argv: None, or the SystemExit's message (or code)."""
    sys.argv = ['import_opfor.py', *argv]
    try:
        io_mod.main()
    except SystemExit as e:
        return str(e.code)
    return None


def imports():
    with open(io_mod.MANIFEST, encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return json.load(f)['imports']


def test_import_plan_and_update(tmp_path):
    with trees(tmp_path) as (src, suite):
        assert run('single.txt', 'copied.txt', '--note', 'why') is None
        assert (suite / 'copied.txt').read_bytes() == b'one file\n'
        item = imports()[0]['items'][0]
        assert item['note'] == 'why' and item['destination'] == 'copied.txt' and item['files'][0]['path'] == 'single.txt'
        plan = tmp_path / 'plan.json'
        plan.write_text(json.dumps([{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'tools/tool'},
                                    {'source': 'other/', 'destination': 'other-copy', 'note': 'n'}]), encoding='utf-8')
        assert run('--plan', str(plan)) is None
        assert sorted(p.name for p in (suite / 'tools/tool').iterdir()) == ['a.py', 'b.py'], 'the link is not copied'
        assert len(imports()) == 2 and imports()[1]['items'][0].get('created')
        # the source moves on: a.py changed, d.py new, b.py removed here on purpose, e.py new there and here already
        write(src / 'tool/a.py', b'a two\n')
        write(src / 'tool/d.py', b'd\n')
        write(src / 'tool/e.py', b'e\n')
        write(src / 'tool/b.py', b'b two\n')
        git(src, 'add', '-A')
        git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'second')
        write(suite / 'tools/tool/e.py', b'mine\n')
        (suite / 'tools/tool/b.py').unlink()
        manifest = json.loads(open(io_mod.MANIFEST, encoding='utf-8').read())
        manifest['imports'].append({'kind': 'remove', 'destination': 'tools/tool', 'paths': ['b.py']})
        io_mod.save_manifest(manifest)
        assert run('--update', 'tools\\tool') is None
        last = imports()[-1]
        assert last['kind'] == 'update' and last['items'][0]['conflicts'] == ['e.py']
        files = {f['path']: f for f in last['items'][0]['files']}
        assert set(files) == {'a.py', 'd.py'} and files['d.py']['new'] and 'previous_git_blob' in files['a.py']
        assert (suite / 'tools/tool/a.py').read_bytes() == b'a two\n' and not (suite / 'tools/tool/b.py').exists()
        assert (suite / 'tools/tool/e.py').read_bytes() == b'mine\n'


def test_refusals_write_nothing(tmp_path):
    with trees(tmp_path) as (src, suite):
        (suite / 'there').mkdir()
        cases = [(('tool', '../outside'), 'destination is outside this suite'),
                 (('tool', '.'), 'destination is outside this suite'),
                 (('tool', 'there'), 'destination exists, refusing to overwrite'),
                 (('nothing-here', 'x'), 'nothing committed at nothing-here')]
        for argv, words in cases:
            why = run(*argv)
            assert why and words in why, (argv, why)
        for plan, words in (([{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'p'}, {'source': 'other', 'destination': 'P'}],
                             'destination named twice in the plan'),
                            ([{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'p'}, {'source': 'other', 'destination': 'p/q'}],
                             'lies inside')):
            path = tmp_path / 'plan.json'
            path.write_text(json.dumps(plan), encoding='utf-8')
            why = run('--plan', str(path))
            if os.name != 'nt' and words.startswith('destination named twice'):
                continue                                    # 'p' and 'P' are two folders there
            assert why and words in why, (plan, why)
        assert run() == '2', 'no source and destination: a usage error'
        why = run('--update', 'never-imported')
        assert why and 'nothing was imported to never-imported' in why
        assert imports() == [] and sorted(p.name for p in suite.iterdir()) == ['provenance', 'there']


def test_recorded_follows_renames_and_removals():
    manifest = {'imports': [
        {'items': [{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'old', 'files': [{'path': 'a.py', 'git_blob': '1'},
                                                                       {'path': 'b.py', 'git_blob': '2'}]}]},
        {'kind': 'rename', 'from': 'old', 'to': 'new'},
        {'kind': 'remove', 'destination': 'old', 'paths': ['b.py']},
        {'kind': 'move', 'destination': 'new', 'paths': {'a.py': 'common/a.py'}},
        {'items': [{'source': 'tool', 'destination': 'new', 'files': [{'path': 'a.py', 'git_blob': '3'}]}]}]}
    moves = {}
    source, files, removed = io_mod.recorded(manifest, 'new', moves)
    assert source == 'tool' and files['a.py']['git_blob'] == '3' and files['b.py']['git_blob'] == '2'
    assert removed == {'a.py', 'b.py'} and moves == {'a.py': 'common/a.py'}


def test_blob_read_back_wrong(tmp_path):
    with trees(tmp_path) as (src, suite):
        real = io_mod.git

        def damaged(*args):
            out = real(*args)
            return out + b'x' if args[:2] == ('cat-file', 'blob') else out
        io_mod.git = damaged
        try:
            why = run('single.txt', 'copied.txt')
            assert why and 'blob mismatch reading single.txt' in why
            assert not (suite / 'copied.txt').exists() and imports() == [], 'nothing written, nothing recorded'
        finally:
            io_mod.git = real
        assert run('tool', 'tool') is None
        write(src / 'tool/a.py', b'changed\n')
        git(src, 'commit', '-q', '-am', 'changed')
        io_mod.git = damaged
        try:
            why = run('--update', 'tool')
        finally:
            io_mod.git = real
        assert why and 'blob mismatch reading tool/a.py' in why
        assert (suite / 'tool/a.py').read_bytes() == b'a\n' and len(imports()) == 1, 'an update that wrote nothing is not recorded'


def test_place(tmp_path):
    data = b'payload'
    blob = io_mod.blob_id(data)
    target = tmp_path / 'sub' / 'file.bin'
    io_mod.place(str(target), data, blob, new=True)
    assert target.read_bytes() == data
    for args, words in (((str(target), data, blob, True), 'destination appeared while importing'),
                        ((str(tmp_path / 'other.bin'), data, '0' * 40, True), 'written file differs from its source')):
        try:
            io_mod.place(*args)
            why = None
        except SystemExit as e:
            why = str(e.code)
        assert why and words in why, why
    io_mod.place(str(target), b'new', io_mod.blob_id(b'new'), new=False)
    assert target.read_bytes() == b'new'
    assert sorted(p.name for p in tmp_path.rglob('*') if p.is_file()) == ['file.bin'], 'no temporary file left'
    assert io_mod.blob_id(b'') == 'e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391', "git's empty blob"


def test_run_recorded_part_way(tmp_path):
    """A run stopped after writing a file is recorded, marked incomplete with the error; one that wrote nothing is not."""
    with trees(tmp_path):
        manifest = {'imports': []}

        def wrote_one(items):
            items.append({'destination': 'tool', 'files': [{'path': 'a.py'}]})
            raise OSError(28, 'made-up full disk')
        try:
            io_mod.run_recorded(manifest, {'commit': 'c', 'items': []}, wrote_one)
            raised = False
        except OSError:
            raised = True
        assert raised and imports()[-1]['incomplete'].startswith('OSError: ')
        assert imports()[-1]['items'][0]['files'] == [{'path': 'a.py'}]

        def wrote_nothing(items):
            items.append({'destination': 'tool'})
            raise SystemExit('stopped')
        try:
            io_mod.run_recorded({'imports': []}, {'commit': 'c', 'items': []}, wrote_nothing)
        except SystemExit:
            pass
        assert len(imports()) == 1, 'nothing written: nothing recorded'
```

`tests/test_mutate.py`:

```py
r"""Mutation testing tool (tools/mutate.py): operators, keys, configuration and a run on a made-up module

tools/mutate.py on made-up sources (no game data): each operator finds its changes and leaves docstrings,
annotations, f-strings, `__main__` and TYPE_CHECKING blocks, `while True` and `# no mutate` lines alone; a mutant
applies to its own source only and compiles; keys repeat with #<n>; the configuration and its equivalents are read
(a reason is required); module names resolve; argv paths become {suite} however the folder is spelt (2026-11-05: a
work folder given with / ran every test from the first copy); and a whole run on a made-up suite of one module and
one test script scores it: killed, survived, timed out (an endless loop, killed with its process), not covered and
equivalent mutants each counted, the canary killed in every copy, and the suite itself never changed.

A pytest-style test (README "Tests"): python -B -m pytest <this file>, or run_tests.py.
"""
import ast
import contextlib
import importlib.util
import io
import os
import pathlib
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SUITE = os.path.dirname(HERE)


def tool():
    """tools/mutate.py as a module (tools/ is not on sys.path)."""
    name = 'test_mutate_tool'
    if name not in sys.modules:
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, os.path.join(SUITE, 'tools', 'mutate.py'))
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[name] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return sys.modules[name]


SOURCE = '''"""A docstring: 1 < 2 is left alone."""
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    LIMIT = 1

COUNT: int = 3


def f(a: int, b: list[int] = [1]) -> int:
    """Not mutated either."""
    if a < b[0] and a != 0:
        return a + 1
    while True:
        break
    x = not a
    y = a if a >= 2 else -a
    z = [v for v in b if v is None]
    assert a in b
    s = 'n' + str(a) + f'{a + 1}'
    a <<= 2
    q = a // 3 & 1  # no mutate
    if a == 5:
        raise ValueError('five')
    return a == 5 or x or y or z or s or q


if __name__ == '__main__':
    f(1 + 1)
'''


def test_operators_and_exclusions():
    m = tool()
    found = m.mutants(SOURCE, 'pkg/sample.py')
    changes = [(x.operator, x.before, x.after) for x in found]
    want = [
        ('constant', '3', '4'),                                           # COUNT's value, not its annotation
        ('constant', '1', '2'),                                           # b's default
        ('negate', 'a < b[0] and a != 0', 'not (a < b[0] and a != 0)'),
        ('boolop', 'a < b[0] and a != 0', 'a < b[0] or a != 0'),
        ('drop', 'a < b[0] and a != 0', 'a != 0'),
        ('drop', 'a < b[0] and a != 0', 'a < b[0]'),
        ('compare', 'a < b[0]', 'a <= b[0]'),
        ('constant', '0', '1'),
        ('compare', 'a != 0', 'a == 0'),
        ('constant', '0', '1'),
        ('arith', 'a + 1', 'a - 1'),
        ('constant', '1', '2'),
        ('not', 'not a', 'a'),
        ('negate', 'a >= 2', 'not a >= 2'),
        ('compare', 'a >= 2', 'a > 2'),
        ('constant', '2', '3'),
        ('negate', 'v is None', 'not v is None'),
        ('compare', 'v is None', 'v is not None'),
        ('negate', 'a in b', 'not a in b'),
        ('compare', 'a in b', 'a not in b'),
        ('arith', 'a <<= 2', 'a >>= 2'),
        ('constant', '2', '3'),
        ('negate', 'a == 5', 'not a == 5'),
        ('compare', 'a == 5', 'a != 5'),
        ('constant', '5', '6'),
        ('raise', "raise ValueError('five')", 'pass'),
        ('boolop', 'a == 5 or x or y or z or s or q', 'a == 5 and x and y and z and s and q'),
    ]
    assert changes[:len(want)] == want, [c for c in changes if c not in want][:5] or changes[len(want):len(want) + 3]
    rest = changes[len(want):]
    assert [c[0] for c in rest] == ['drop'] * 6 + ['compare', 'constant'], rest
    assert not any('str(a)' in c[1] and c[0] == 'arith' for c in changes), 'string joining is no arithmetic'
    assert not any(c[1] in ('True', '1 < 2', '2') and c[0] == 'negate' for c in changes)
    assert not any(c[1].startswith('a // 3') for c in changes), '# no mutate'
    assert all(x.function == ('f' if 9 < x.line < 27 else '<module>') for x in found), \
        [(x.line, x.function) for x in found]
    keys = [x.key for x in found]
    assert len(set(keys)) == len(keys), 'every key unique'
    assert 'sample.py:f:constant:0 -> 1 #2' in keys and 'sample.py:f:constant:0 -> 1' in keys
    assert keys[0] == 'sample.py:<module>:constant:3 -> 4'

def test_config(tmp_path):

    else:

    if x < lo:
        return lo
    if x > hi:
        return hi
    return x


def count_to(n):
    i = 0
    while i < n:

    return i


def check(x):
    if x is None:
        raise ValueError('none')
    return x


def unused(a):
    return a * 2
'''

TOY_TEST = '''import toy

assert toy.clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5
assert toy.clamp(-1, 0, 10) == 0
assert toy.clamp(11, 0, 10) == 10
assert toy.count_to(3) == 3
try:

except ValueError:

else:

print('all passed')
'''


def test_a_run(tmp_path):
    m = tool()
    suite = tmp_path / 'suite'
    suite.mkdir()
    (suite / 'toy.py').write_text(TOY, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')
    (suite / 'test_toy.py').write_text(TOY_TEST, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')
    (suite / 'work').mkdir()
    (suite / 'work' / 'big.bin').write_bytes(b'not copied')
    before = (suite / 'toy.py').read_bytes()
    equivalent = 'toy.py:clamp:compare:x < lo -> x <= lo'
    config = m.Config(modules=['toy.py'], timeout_factor=1.0, timeout_extra=4.0,
                      equivalents={equivalent: 'x == lo returns lo, which is x', 'toy.py:gone:raise:x -> pass': 'old'})
    lines = []
    tests = [('toy', [sys.executable, '-B', os.path.join('{suite}', 'test_toy.py')])]
    scores = m.run(str(suite), ['toy.py'], config, 2, str(tmp_path / 'work'), tests=tests, log=lines.append)
    assert (suite / 'toy.py').read_bytes() == before, 'the suite is never changed'
    assert not (tmp_path / 'work' / 'copy-0' / 'work').exists(), 'no work folder copied'
    [s] = scores
    found = {x.key: x for x in m.mutants(TOY, 'toy.py')}
    survived = {x.key for x in s.survived}
    not_covered = {x.key for x in s.not_covered}
    assert [x.key for x in s.equivalent] == [equivalent]
    assert 'toy.py:count_to:constant:0 -> 1' in survived, 'count_to(0) is not tested'
    assert 'toy.py:clamp:compare:x > hi -> x >= hi' in survived, 'clamp(10, 0, 10) is not tested'
    assert s.timeout >= 1, 'i -= 1 loops for ever'
    unused = {k for k in found if k.startswith('toy.py:unused:')}
    assert unused and unused <= (not_covered | survived), 'nothing tests unused()'
    import importlib.util as iu
    if iu.find_spec('coverage') is not None:
        assert unused <= not_covered, 'coverage shows no test runs unused()'
    assert s.total == len(found) == s.killed + s.timeout + len(survived) + len(not_covered) + 1
    assert abs(s.percent - 100.0 * (s.killed + s.timeout) / (len(found) - 1)) < 1e-9
    result = m.report(scores, config, set(found))
    assert result['stale_equivalents'] == ['toy.py:gone:raise:x -> pass']
    assert result['modules'][0]['equivalent'] == 1 and result['modules'][0]['mutants'] == len(found)
    assert any('toy.py: ' in line and '% killed' in line for line in lines), lines[-3:]

def test_a_run_by_short_path(tmp_path):
    """The run in a folder named by its 8.3 short path, as GitHub's runner temp (C:\\Users\\RUNNER~1): coverage records
    the long path, and before 2026-11-05 no measured file matched its copy ("no passing test runs it")."""
    if os.name != 'nt':
        return
    import ctypes
    long_dir = tmp_path / 'a folder with a long name'
    long_dir.mkdir()
    buffer = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(1024)
    ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetShortPathNameW(str(long_dir), buffer, 1024)
    if not buffer.value or os.path.normcase(buffer.value) == os.path.normcase(str(long_dir)):
        print('skip: this volume makes no 8.3 names')
        return
    test_a_run(pathlib.Path(buffer.value))

```

`tests/test_repo.py`:

```py
r"""The repository's own rules, checked before anything is pushed (no game data needed):

- no game file types and no large files anywhere in the history (EA / DICE content is never published);
- no co-author or generated-by lines in commit messages (the author is the only author);
- no build output or caches tracked (.exe, .pyc, __pycache__);
- a README in every tool folder, a LICENSE at the root;
- every Python file compiles;
- sys.path is changed only by the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py): no other edit in any Python file, and the
  bootstrap only where a script runs (under `if __name__ == '__main__':`); the folders it puts on sys.path share no
  module name, the two NavKit variants included (their shared modules are one copy in bf1943-auto-navkit-common
  since 2026-10-31), so the order a script names them in changes nothing it imports;
- the lint (ruff) leaves out exactly the VMX fingerprint's Python inputs, which are never edited, and the type check
  (pyright's include) covers none of them;
- the coverage threshold (pyproject.toml [tool.coverage.report] fail_under) never goes down: in no commit of the
  history (unless its message gives a "Coverage-threshold-lowered: <reason>" line) and not in the working copy; nor
  is branch coverage ([tool.coverage.run] branch), once on, turned off.

  python tests\test_repo.py
"""
import ast
import os
import py_compile
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

SUITE = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..'))
GAME_TYPES = re.compile(r'\.(dbx|res|fbrb|hpd|sb|raw|bik|fsb|fev|dds|tga|hkx)$', re.I)
OWNER = 'mathewsbinny <32554119+mathewsbinny@users.noreply.github.com>'
DEPENDABOT = 'dependabot[bot] <49699333+dependabot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>'
MAX_BLOB = 1_000_000
LARGE_ALLOWED = {'bf1943-dbx-tools/tests/fingerprints_795745.txt'}       # SHA-1 hashes only
LOWERED = re.compile(r'^Coverage-threshold-lowered: \S', re.M)     # a commit allowed to lower fail_under (its reason)
ATTRIBUTION = re.compile(r'co-authored-by|generated with \[?claude|noreply@anthropic', re.I)
TRACKED_NEVER = re.compile(r'(\.exe|\.pyc|\.dll|\.pdb)$|(^|/)__pycache__/', re.I)
BOOTSTRAP = ("sys.path.insert(0, str(next((p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents "
             "if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file())) / 'core'))")
# files allowed their own sys.path edits: the bootstrap's module, and the VMX language builder, an input of the VMX
# fingerprint (bf1943-xex-tools/vmx_inputs.py INPUTS), which must stay byte for byte as it is
PATH_EDITS_ALLOWED = {'core/suitepath.py', 'bf1943-xex-tools/build_vmx_language.py'}


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', SUITE, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding='utf-8',
                          errors='replace', check=True).stdout


def is_path(node):
    """sys.path, or sys.path under another name for sys (`import sys as _sys`)."""
    return (isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr == 'path' and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name)
            and node.value.id in ('sys', '_sys'))


def path_edits(tree):
    """(line, statement) of each change to sys.path that is not the bootstrap where a script runs."""
    guarded = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.If) and ast.unparse(node.test) == "__name__ == '__main__'":
            for stmt in node.body:
                if isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr) and ast.unparse(stmt) == BOOTSTRAP:
                    guarded.add(id(stmt.value))
    found = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        changed = None
        if (isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) and is_path(node.func.value)
                and node.func.attr in ('insert', 'append', 'extend', 'remove', 'pop', 'clear')):
            changed = node
        elif isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AugAssign, ast.AnnAssign, ast.Delete)):
            targets = node.targets if isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.Delete)) else [node.target]
            if any(is_path(t) or (isinstance(t, ast.Subscript) and is_path(t.value)) for t in targets):
                changed = node
        if changed is not None and id(changed) not in guarded:
            found.append((changed.lineno, ast.unparse(changed)[:100]))
    return sorted(found)


def shared_names():
    """Module names (a .py / .pyw file, or a package folder) found in more than one of the bootstrap's folders: the
    shared ones and both NavKit variants' (until 2026-10-31 the variants were let share 14 names)."""
    import suitepath
    seen, clashes = {}, []
    for rel in suitepath.SHARED + suitepath.NAVKIT_BE + suitepath.NAVKIT_LE:
        folder = suitepath.folder(rel)
        for n in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
            name, ext = os.path.splitext(n)
            if ext not in ('.py', '.pyw') and not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(folder, n, '__init__.py')):
                continue
            if name in seen:
                clashes.append(f'{name}: {seen[name]} and {rel}')
            seen.setdefault(name, rel)
    return clashes


def fail_under(text):
    """pyproject.toml's [tool.coverage.report] fail_under (0 when it has none), from the file's text."""
    import tomllib
    return float(tomllib.loads(text).get('tool', {}).get('coverage', {}).get('report', {}).get('fail_under', 0))


def branch_on(text):
    """pyproject.toml's [tool.coverage.run] branch (False when it has none), from the file's text."""
    import tomllib
    return bool(tomllib.loads(text).get('tool', {}).get('coverage', {}).get('run', {}).get('branch', False))


def coverage_ratchet():
    """(check, problems): the coverage threshold only goes up. Each commit that changed pyproject.toml (oldest first,
    the whole history: CI checks it out whole), then the working copy: a fail_under below the one before it is a
    problem, so a lowered threshold fails whether it is committed or not (README "Coverage"). The one exception: a
    commit whose message has a line "Coverage-threshold-lowered: <reason>" may lower it (a well-tested tool removed);
    the working copy never may. Branch coverage, once on, stays on under the same rule: with it the total counts lines
    and branches together (2026-11-05), and turning it off would raise the total without a test added."""
    log = git('log', '--reverse', '--format=%H%x00%B%x01', '--', 'pyproject.toml').split('\x01')
    commits = [entry.strip('\n').split('\x00', 1) for entry in log if '\x00' in entry]
    versions = [(sha[:10], git('show', f'{sha}:pyproject.toml'), bool(LOWERED.search(message)))
                for sha, message in commits]
    with open(os.path.join(SUITE, 'pyproject.toml'), encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
        working = f.read()
    if not versions or working != versions[-1][1]:      # an unchanged working copy is its last commit (reported once)
        versions.append(('working copy', working, False))
    problems, best, since = [], 0.0, None
    branch_since = None                                 # where branch coverage was turned on (None: it is off)
    for name, text, lowered in versions:
        try:
            value = fail_under(text)
            branch = branch_on(text)
        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:            # tomllib.TOMLDecodeError is a ValueError
            problems.append(f'{name}: pyproject.toml does not read ({e})')
            continue
        if branch_since and not branch and not lowered:
            problems.append(f'{name}: branch coverage turned off (on since {branch_since}); the total would count '
                            f'lines only')
        elif branch and not branch_since:
            branch_since = name
        elif not branch:
            branch_since = None
        if value < best and not lowered:
            problems.append(f'{name}: fail_under {value:g} is below {best:g} (set in {since}); raise coverage instead')
        elif value > best or lowered:
            best, since = value, name
    return (f'the coverage threshold only goes up (pyproject [tool.coverage.report] fail_under, now {best:g})',
            problems)


def main(argv):
    results = []

    blobs = git('rev-list', '--objects', '--all').splitlines()
    sizes = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', SUITE, 'cat-file', '--batch-check=%(objecttype) %(objectsize) %(rest)'],
                           input='\n'.join(l.split(' ')[0] for l in blobs), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    paths = {}
    for line in blobs:
        sha, _, path = line.partition(' ')
        if path:
            paths[sha] = path
    game_files, large = set(), set()
    for line, sha in zip(sizes.splitlines(), (l.split(' ')[0] for l in blobs)):
        kind, size, _ = (line.split(' ', 2) + [''])[:3]
        path = paths.get(sha, '')
        if kind != 'blob' or not path:
            continue
        if GAME_TYPES.search(path):
            game_files.add(path)
        if int(size) > MAX_BLOB and path not in LARGE_ALLOWED:
            large.add(f'{path} ({int(size):,} bytes)')
    results.append(('no game file types in the history', sorted(game_files)))
    results.append((f'no files over {MAX_BLOB:,} bytes in the history (allowed: {", ".join(sorted(LARGE_ALLOWED))})', sorted(large)))

    messages = git('log', '--all', '--format=%H%x00%B%x01').split('\x01')
    bad = [m.split('\x00')[0][:10] for m in messages if '\x00' in m and ATTRIBUTION.search(m.split('\x00', 1)[1])]
    results.append(('no co-author / generated-by lines in commit messages', bad))
    # who may author a commit (2026-11-03): the owner, under the GitHub noreply address; Dependabot's update commits;
    # and merges GitHub itself commits when the owner merges a pull request on the site (those carry the account's
    # web address, which the history should not have to name)
    others = []
    for line in git('log', '--all', '--format=%h%x00%an <%ae>%x00%cn%x00%p').splitlines():
        sha, author, committer, parents = line.split('\x00')
        if author in (OWNER, DEPENDABOT) or (committer == 'GitHub' and len(parents.split()) == 2):
            continue
        others.append(f'{sha} {author}')
    results.append((f'commits by the owner ({OWNER}), Dependabot, or GitHub merges of pull requests', others))

    tracked = git('ls-files').splitlines()
    results.append(('no build output or caches tracked', [t for t in tracked if TRACKED_NEVER.search(t)]))

    folders = [d for d in sorted(os.listdir(SUITE)) if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(SUITE, d)) and (d.startswith('bf1943-') or d == 'core')]
    results.append(('a README.md in every tool folder', [d for d in folders if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SUITE, d, 'README.md'))]))
    results.append(('LICENSE at the root', [] if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SUITE, 'LICENSE')) else ['LICENSE missing']))

    broken = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        for t in tracked:
            if t.endswith(('.py', '.pyw')) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SUITE, t)):    # not one deleted, uncommitted
                try:
                    py_compile.compile(os.path.join(SUITE, t), cfile=os.path.join(tmp, 'x.pyc'), doraise=True)
                except py_compile.PyCompileError as e:
                    broken.append(f'{t}: {str(e).strip().splitlines()[-1]}')
    results.append((f'every Python file compiles ({sum(t.endswith((".py", ".pyw")) for t in tracked)} files)', broken))

    edits = []
    for t in tracked:
        if t.endswith(('.py', '.pyw')) and t not in PATH_EDITS_ALLOWED and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(SUITE, t)):
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(open(os.path.join(SUITE, t), encoding='utf-8').read())
            except SyntaxError:
                continue                                    # reported above
            edits += [f'{t}:{line}: {what}' for line, what in path_edits(tree)]
    results.append(('sys.path changed only by the bootstrap (core/suitepath.py), and only where a script runs', edits))
    results.append(("the bootstrap's folders share no module name (the two NavKit variants included)", shared_names()))
    import suitepath
    import tomllib
    with open(os.path.join(SUITE, 'pyproject.toml'), 'rb') as f:
        dev_dirs = tomllib.load(f)['tool']['hatch']['build']['targets']['wheel']['dev-mode-dirs']
    results.append(('an editable install puts the shared folders on sys.path (pyproject dev-mode-dirs = suitepath.SHARED)',
                    [] if dev_dirs == suitepath.SHARED else [f'pyproject: {dev_dirs}', f'suitepath: {suitepath.SHARED}']))
    import vmx_inputs
    with open(os.path.join(SUITE, 'pyproject.toml'), 'rb') as f:
        lint_skips = set(tomllib.load(f)['tool']['ruff']['extend-exclude'])
    vmx_py = {i for i in vmx_inputs.INPUTS if i.endswith(('.py', '.pyw'))}
    results.append(("the lint skips the VMX fingerprint's Python inputs, and only those (pyproject [tool.ruff] "
                    'extend-exclude = vmx_inputs.INPUTS .py files, besides work and output)',
                    sorted(vmx_py ^ (lint_skips - {'work', 'output'}))))
    with open(os.path.join(SUITE, 'pyproject.toml'), 'rb') as f:
        typed = tomllib.load(f)['tool']['pyright']['include']
    results.append(("the type check covers none of the VMX fingerprint's Python inputs (pyproject [tool.pyright] "
                    'include)', sorted(i for i in vmx_py for d in typed if i == d or i.startswith(d.rstrip('/') + '/'))))

    results.append(coverage_ratchet())

    failed = 0
    for name, problems in results:
        failed += bool(problems)
        print(f'{"FAIL" if problems else "ok  "} {name}')
        for p in problems[:15]:
            print('       ' + p)
    print('all passed' if not failed else f'{failed} check(s) failed')
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use()
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))
```

`tests/test_run_tests.py`:

```py
r"""The test runner's command line (run_tests.py), with its test list replaced by two made-up tests (nothing else
runs): a known tier runs its tests; a misspelled tier or option is a usage error with a nonzero exit, never a run of
the quick tier; the value after --only is a name, not a tier. Pytest-style test files: found, named and tiered from
their source, and run by tests/functions.py with the runner's statuses (pass, fail, all or some skipped, a fixture
only pytest has).

  python -B tests\test_run_tests.py

import contextlib
import io
import os
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
if __name__ == '__main__':      # the suite's bootstrap (core/suitepath.py)
    import pathlib
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / 'core' / 'suitepath.py').is_file()) / 'core'))
    import suitepath
    suitepath.use('.')
import run_tests  # noqa: E402

PY = sys.executable
failures = []


def check(ok, what):
    print(('ok   ' if ok else 'FAIL ') + what)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(what)


def run(*args):
    buf = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
        code = run_tests.main(['run_tests.py', *args])
    return code, buf.getvalue()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_tests.tests = lambda: [('made-up quick test', 'quick', [PY, '-c', 'print("all passed")']),
                               ('made-up bf1943 test', 'bf1943', [PY, '-c', 'print("all passed")'])]
    code, out = run('quick', '--strict')
    check(code == 0 and '1 of 1 passed' in out, f'quick --strict runs the quick test (exit {code})')
    code, out = run('bf1943', '--list')
    check(code == 0 and 'made-up bf1943 test' in out and 'made-up quick test' in out, f'bf1943 --list lists both (exit {code})')
    code, out = run('--only', 'bf1943 test', 'bf1943')
    check(code == 0 and '1 of 1 passed' in out, f'--only takes a name that holds a tier\'s name (exit {code})')
    code, out = run('quick', '--only', 'no such test name')
    check(code == 1 and 'matches no quick test' in out, f'--only naming no test is an error, exit {code}')
    for args in (['bf19433', '--strict'], ['quik'], ['--strcit'], ['quick', 'bf1943'], ['quick', '--only']):
        try:
            code, out = run(*args)
        except Exception as e:                      # 2026-10-30: --only without a value raised IndexError
            code, out = f'{type(e).__name__}', ''
        check(code == 2 and 'usage' in out.lower() and 'passed' not in out, f'{" ".join(args)}: a usage error, exit {code}'
              + ('' if code == 2 else '\n       ' + out.strip().replace('\n', '\n       ')[:400]))
    # 2026-10-30 second review: a test's output reaches the runner in UTF-8 (it is decoded so), whatever the ANSI code
    # page: a test printing a Cyrillic path passed only when started from the hub
    for k in ('PYTHONIOENCODING', 'PYTHONUTF8'):
        os.environ.pop(k, None)
    text = 'made-up path C:/Users/\u041f\u043e\u043b\u044c\u0437\u043e\u0432\u0430\u0442\u0435\u043b\u044c caf\u00e9'
    run_tests.tests = lambda: [('prints outside the code page', 'quick', [PY, '-c', f'print({text!r})'])]
    code, out = run('quick')
    check(code == 0 and text in out, f'a test printing outside the ANSI code page passes and its line reads back (exit {code})')
    # 2026-10-31: pytest-style files are found (not listed), named by their docstring, tiered by TIER, and run by
    # tests/functions.py with the runner's statuses
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        def made_up(name, text):
            path = os.path.join(tmp, name)
            with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
                f.write(text)
            return path
        plain = made_up('test_plain.py', '"""made-up: plain functions\n\nmore"""\n\n\ndef test_one():\n    assert 1\n')
        later = made_up('test_later.py', '"""made-up later"""\nTIER = \'bf1943\'\n\n\ndef test_one():\n    pass\n')
        script = made_up('test_script.py', 'def test_x():\n    pass\n\n\nif __name__ == \'__main__\':\n    test_x()\n')
        wrong = made_up('test_wrong.py', 'TIER = \'bf19433\'\n\n\ndef test_x():\n    pass\n')
        check(run_tests.function_test(plain) == ('made-up: plain functions', 'quick'),
              f'a pytest-style file: named by its docstring\'s first line, quick ({run_tests.function_test(plain)})')
        check(run_tests.function_test(later) == ('made-up later', 'bf1943'), 'TIER = \'bf1943\' puts it in bf1943')
        check(run_tests.function_test(script) is None, 'a file with a __main__ block is a script, not found')
        try:
            run_tests.function_test(wrong)
            check(False, 'a misspelled TIER is an error')
        except ValueError as e:
            check('bf19433' in str(e), f'a misspelled TIER is an error ({e})')
        cases = [('pass', 'def test_a():\n    assert 1 + 1 == 2\n\n\ndef test_b(tmp_path):\n    assert tmp_path.is_dir()\n',
                  'ok  ', 'all passed'),
                 ('fail', 'def test_a():\n    assert 1 == 2, "made-up failure"\n\n\ndef test_b():\n    pass\n',
                  'FAIL', '1 failed'),
                 ('all skip', 'import unittest\n\n\ndef test_a():\n    raise unittest.SkipTest("no data")\n', 'SKIP', 'skip'),
                 ('some skip', 'import unittest\n\n\ndef test_a():\n    raise unittest.SkipTest("no data")\n\n\n'
                  'def test_b():\n    pass\n', 'ok* ', 'all passed'),
                 ('need a fixture only pytest has', 'def test_a(monkeypatch):\n    pass\n', 'FAIL', '1 failed')]
        for k, (what, text, status_wanted, last_wanted) in enumerate(cases):
            path = made_up(f'test_case{k}.py', text)
            status, last, out, _ = run_tests.run_one([PY, run_tests.FUNCTIONS, path])
            check(status == status_wanted and last.startswith(last_wanted),
                  f'functions.py, a file whose tests {what}: {status.strip()} ({last})')
    names = [name for name, _, argv in run_tests.function_tests() if argv[1] == run_tests.FUNCTIONS]
    check('water mesh reader: triangles past their vertices refused' in names
          and 'NavKit (both variants): headroom band' in names,
          f'the suite\'s pytest-style files are found ({len(names)})')
    print('all passed' if not failures else f'{len(failures)} failed')
    sys.exit(1 if failures else 0)
```
